title: Concerns for four NFL teams on the playoff bubble: Barnwell on the Cowboys, Patriots, Raiders, Texans
summary: The Cowboys' defense got lit up, the Patriots lost Drake Maye, the Raiders are adjusting to Fernando Mendoza, and the Texans can't find support for C.J. Stroud.
full_text:
If the trade deadline marks the beginning of the NFL's stretch run, there are four teams that might already be pulling up lame. In the first game after the deadline, with rosters essentially locked for the remainder of 2026, four franchises that were already facing difficult paths forward to the postseason looked overmatched in Week 10 losses.
The Cowboys, Patriots, Raiders and Texans all lost in Week 10, and while they each had serious playoff aspirations at one point or another this season. none of the four is currently a favorite to make it into the 14-team field, per ESPN's Football Power Index .
Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'
They're collectively down ... but are they out? I'll start in Big D, where the Cowboys spent most of the day chasing shadows on and off the field.
Note: All playoff chance percentages are via ESPN's Football Power Index.
Jump to: Cowboys | Patriots | Raiders | Texans
Peak playoff probability in 2026: 82.1% (after Week 4) Current playoff probability: 42.1% Week 10: Lost 46-40 to 49ers
The Cowboys allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 yards, the most they've allowed in a home game in the 67-year history of the franchise . And if there's a play that will come to stand as the example of how badly things have gone wrong for the Cowboys on defense since the ill-fated decision to trade Micah Parsons to the Packers, it would be the 66-yard Christian McCaffrey touchdown that essentially sealed up the game with 3:23 to go.
Under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker, the Cowboys have not been a blitz-happy team. They blitz at the league's third-lowest rate, in part to protect a shaky secondary and in part to align with the Vic Fangio-style defense that the Cowboys chose to install as they hired Parker, two years after it was at its peak. They still manage to get pressure at a top-10 rate, but when the Cowboys don't get home, they have the second-worst pass defense in the NFL by Total QBR.
Quarterback Brock Purdy had sliced the Cowboys blitz apart when Parker did send extra rushers to this point, going 5-of-5 for 131 yards with a touchdown, but also took two sacks on seven dropbacks. Blitzing turned the game into a boom-or-serious-bust situation for the Cowboys. Most defenses would prefer to major in what they do best with the game on the line, but with the 49ers averaging more than 7 yards per play with a 50% success rate when the Cowboys didn't blitz Sunday, Parker must have felt like he needed to throw a changeup to have any hope of stopping them.
So, facing a second-and-10 situation after a George Kittle false start, Parker sent the house. The Cowboys sent six defenders, twisting their three down linemen and blitzing an extra rusher to the weak side of the line, hoping that the pass rush would get home and force Purdy off his spot. Even if it didn't work, the blitz might push McCaffrey to come across the formation to try to block the free rusher, taking a key receiver out of the progression for the 49ers.
That didn't happen. McCaffrey immediately released vertically out of the backfield. The defender responsible for him was the edge rusher on that side of the field, who dropped off the line as a product of the Cowboys overloading the weakside rush to leave them with five coverage defenders against five eligible receivers. And that's how the Cowboys ended up with 37-year-old Von Miller in man-to-man coverage against the best receiving back in football with the game on the line.
It wasn't much of a contest, although Miller did manage to hit 18.5 mph as he tried to chase down McCaffrey, the first time he has reached that speed on a single snap since 2021, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. This was probably the easiest catch and run of McCaffrey's career and his second long touchdown reception of the game, having turned a catch against a blown coverage on a scramble drill into a 74-yard score earlier in the contest (two linebackers had attempted to chase down Purdy and neither ran with McCaffrey). It was the third touchdown of 60 or more yards the Cowboys had allowed in the game, too, marking the first time a defense has allowed three of those in a single contest since October 2007.
It's too simplistic to blame Miller, who should never be expected to hold up in man coverage against McCaffrey. It's not as simple as blaming Parker, who dialed up the sort of exotic pressure that other teams have pulled out in key situations for stops. It's just the reality of what happens in Dallas. Since this team traded Parsons, the Cowboys have spent the past 27 games throwing stuff at the wall on defense and hoping something sticks.
That's how you end up with Miller, an edge rusher at the very end of his career and nearly a half-decade removed from his last season as a full-time starter, with the game on the line needing a stop. It's how you end up with Parker sending an all-out blitz despite the 49ers picking those blitzes apart for most of the game, in the hopes of fooling one of the league's best offensive coaches. It's how you end up with Parker, as the Cowboys followed a disastrous year with an experienced-but-uninspiring defensive coordinator in Matt Eberflus by hiring what they hoped would be the league's next exciting young defensive mind.
And trying to chase down the problems with their defense, the Cowboys and Jerry Jones have desperately made personnel decision after personnel decision. They traded first- and second-round picks to the Jets for Quinnen Williams , and while he has been very good during his time in Dallas, he hasn't been able to singlehandedly fix the defense. It seemed like a microcosm when Williams literally ripped the ball out of Kaelon Black 's hands to try to force a game-altering fumble on San Francisco's next and final possession, only for the 49ers running back to fall on the football before any of Williams' teammates could react.
The Cowboys have traded for Kenny Clark , Rashan Gary , Joey Porter Jr . and Dee Winters . They used first-round picks on Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence . They signed Cobie Durant and Jalen Thompson in free agency. None of those moves is egregious in a vacuum. In the big picture, though, there's no identity, no coherent plan and no short- or long-term vision. The Cowboys traded Parsons because they wanted to save money and spread the cash and draft capital around the roster, then traded most of that capital away to land Williams, who signed a massive extension. They're spending $182.2 million in cash on their defense this season, the fifth most of any team in the league, so they aren't saving anything by the decision to move on from Parsons. They look and operate like an organization that desperately wants something to work on defense but has no idea how to make it happen.
And so, while wildly chasing down solutions on defense as a personnel philosophy, the Cowboys do the same thing on the field. Deebo Samuel Sr .'s 70-yard touchdown on an end-around was one of the most dramatic collective overpursuits you'll ever see on a single snap, as Samuel was expected to gain 35 yards from the moment he touched the ball by the Next Gen Stats model, the most by any runner on any play since 2022.
It's one thing to get fooled on misdirection, but edge rusher James Houston and defensive tackle Elijah Garcia were the two down linemen on the backside of the play who might have forced Samuel back to their help or at least slowed down the hybrid receiver. Instead, after Samuel takes the pitch, Houston and Garcia each take what appeared to be nine false steps in the wrong direction before realizing something's up. By the time they confirm Samuel has the ball, they're completely out of the play.
Porter's the cornerback on the backside of the field and the last line of defense. While Samuel has a convoy, Porter wasn't able to fight through Purdy to get to the sideline and force Samuel back to the inside, where help might have been able to stop Samuel from scoring. Instead, Samuel eluded a diving…
author: Bill Barnwell

title: Tiering all 32 teams' chances to make the playoffs, from the locks to the long shots
summary: We placed all 32 teams into tiers based on their likelihood of making the playoffs.
full_text:
The back half of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason , they don't tell us everything . Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.
So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between, because for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI), betting lines , metrics, health status and some instinct.
Walder ranked the teams within each tier too. All percentages and statistical rankings are through Sunday unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.
Jump to a team: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF SEA | TB | TEN | WSH
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.7% Chances to win the NFC West: 95.4% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 39.6%
Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is the FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and the Seahawks . Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR, and he is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far too.
Chances to make the playoffs: >99.9% Chances to win the AFC East: 99.7% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 29.3%
The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite, and nothing that has happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. Their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. Buffalo's defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen , running back James Cook III and the Bills' offensive line do more than enough damage on offense.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9% Chances to win the AFC South: 98.7% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 22.6%
The Jaguars were already playoff locks and clearly one of the top two teams in the AFC before the trade deadline, when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux . The Davis deal from the Jaguars' perspective is one of the worst trades in years , but there's also little doubt Jacksonville is better today than it was a week ago. And the Jaguars were great a week ago! The Jaguars rank in the top five in EPA per dropback on offense and EPA allowed per dropback as well as EPA allowed per designed rush on defense.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.5% Chances to win the AFC West: 45.1% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 16.1%
The Chiefs faced three major questions entering the season:
How would quarterback Patrick Mahomes fare after recovering from a torn ACL suffered last December?
What kind of impact would free agent running back Kenneth Walker III have on the offense?
Could the defense survive the loss of starting cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson ?
The answer to every question has been positive for Kansas City. In particular, Walker has helped transform the Chiefs' rushing attack into a strength. And coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has managed to keep the defense strong too: It ranks sixth in EPA per play.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8% Chances to win the AFC North: 93.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 19.1%
It's something we've wondered about for years: What would happen if the Bengals could manage to combine a peak Joe Burrow season with simply mediocre defense? Well, we're finding out. Burrow is in the MVP race, and Cincinnati's defense is ranked 11th in EPA per play. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been outstanding and provide a sky-high ceiling for the passing offense. Plus, the Bengals have a very easy schedule the rest of the way.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.2% Chances to win the AFC West: 54.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 9.0%
Somehow, it's working . Despite Bo Nix falling well short of expectations -- he entered Week 10 ranked 24th out of 31 qualifiers in QBR -- the Broncos are a virtual lock to reach the playoffs and have a great shot at winning the AFC West. The defense hasn't quite lived up to its reputation (13th in EPA per play), but Denver also hasn't had All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II for every game, either. If the offense can keep its recent momentum (the Broncos have put up 26 points in each of their past three games), Denver can be a threat in the postseason. The Broncos have a soft schedule the rest of the way, too.
Chances to make the playoffs: 96.1% Chances to win the NFC North: 45.0% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 14.4%
Minnesota's trade-deadline deal for quarterback Kirk Cousins breathed new life into its season. That move instantly increased the Vikings' playoff chances from 65% to 83% at the time of the deal, according to the FPI. But that deal was about what comes next. With Brian Flores' incredible defense leading the way, the Vikings can and should have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The moment Flores leaves, a real possibility in this upcoming offseason, the team's contention window vanishes, so the Vikings need to take advantage of this opportunity. Minnesota's 30-10 dismantling of the Packers on Sunday only reinforced what a good trade it was.
Chances to make the playoffs: 85.4% Chances to win the NFC North: 20.4% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 11.2%
Chicago entered its bye week as a near lock to reach the playoffs and very much a team that could go all the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a significant step forward, and the fact that the Bears are 7-2 despite Williams missing three games is a testament to the coaching staff and how strong this team is. Coordinator Dennis Allen was already getting the most out of a lacking defensive roster when the Bears acquired the best defensive tackle in the league in Jeffery Simmons as they prepare for what they hope is a Super Bowl run.
Chances to make the playoffs: 89.4% Chances to win the NFC North: 33.7% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 9.7%
If they played in a normal division, the Lions would be even safer than this, especially after the team's blowout win over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday -- albeit with New England missing quarterback Drake Maye for most of that contest . But Detroit's record has it on the verge of a playoff berth despite playing in a stacked NFC North and with the Seahawks and Rams looming as other wild-card threats. There's little doubt the Lions can score points. But the X factor down the stretch and in the postseason will be their defense, which ranks 23rd in EPA per play and now faces the possibility of a significant knee injury to star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson .
Chances to make the playoffs: 79.8% Chances to win the AFC North: 4.4% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 1.6%
The Steelers are barreling toward another playoff berth thanks to their running game and defense. No team in the league is more efficient (by EPA per play) on the ground than the Steelers -- hello, Jaylen Warren ! -- and the team's run defense hasn't allowed opponents to rush successfully against them. Getting past the Bengals to win the division will be a tall order, but the fall of the Ravens helps widen the Steelers' path to the postseason.
Chances to make the playoffs: 62.4% Chances to win the NFC South: 62.1% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.5%
The FPI believes the Bucs are the…
author: Seth Walder

title: Sources: Patriots fear QB Maye has broken ankle, could miss rest of season
summary: The Patriots are concerned that Drake Maye sustained a fractured ankle, sources told ESPN, an injury that could sideline the star QB for the rest of the season.
full_text:
MUNICH -- The New England Patriots are concerned that quarterback Drake Maye may have sustained a fractured ankle during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Maye will miss an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season, sources told Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Maye was knocked out in the first quarter of Sunday's 35-10 loss after he was sacked by Detroit defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , who suffered a serious knee injury while celebrating the play.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told WEEI radio in Boston that Maye stayed in Germany and did not travel home with the team.
"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back," Vrabel said Monday during an interview on "The Greg Hill Show."
"He'll be traveling back here shortly, but [we] just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. ... Just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel -- and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."
Maye, who wasn't in the locker room after the game when reporters were present, was replaced Sunday by backup Tommy DeVito .
The Patriots also have rookie quarterback Behren Morton , a seventh-round draft pick from Texas Tech, on the roster, and could look to add another quarterback to the team, potentially on the practice squad.
Maye's streak of 43 straight starts (including playoffs) is the third longest among NFL quarterbacks behind the Bills' Josh Allen (146) and Lions' Jared Goff (82).
Hutchinson sacked Maye on third down, ripping him down from behind with what appeared to be a possible hip-drop tackle. Hutchinson's right arm reached around Maye's right shoulder pad as he brought him down and landed on the quarterback's lower leg.
Sources told Rapoport that Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after initial tests revealed a torn ACL in his right knee. After leaping in the air to celebrate the sack, Hutchinson landed awkwardly and immediately clutched his knee.
On the Fox broadcast, rules analyst Mike Pereira said Hutchinson's tackle was "not a hip drop."
"Three things have to happen: you have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee," Pereira said. "This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse collar penalty."
Walt Anderson, the NFL's officiating rules analyst, confirmed Pereira's explanation through a league spokesman, noting it was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting.
It was also not a foul for a horse collar tackle, Pereira noted, because neither the collar nor the nameplate were grabbed. No penalty was called on the play by referee Clay Martin's crew.
Asked his view of the play, Vrabel said he wasn't going to assume there was any ill intent.
"However it happened, I don't think it was anything intentional. It's just part of the game," he said.
Maye was helped to his feet and limped to the sideline then later walked to the locker room for further evaluation as DeVito stepped in.
In other injury news, wide receiver A.J. Brown , who returned Sunday after missing two games with a knee injury, was ruled out in the fourth quarter after he sustained a hamstring injury.
"He wasn't able to finish. We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there," Vrabel said.
The Patriots are on a bye in Week 11.
author: Mike Reiss

title: Sources: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with torn ACL, possibly more knee damage
summary: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with what initial tests showed to be a torn ACL in his right knee, sources told NFL Network.
full_text:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with what initial tests showed to be a torn ACL in his right knee, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
The two-time Pro Bowl defensive end likely suffered additional damage in the knee, with concern about his meniscus, sources told Rapoport.
Hutchinson received an initial MRI in Germany and is set to have additional tests in the United States now that he has returned, according to sources.
Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack in the Lions' 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich on Sunday.
Hutchinson leaped in the air after his sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye on New England's first drive of the game but went straight to the ground after landing. He immediately grabbed his right knee. He stayed down and eventually was able to walk to the blue medical tent for evaluation. He then walked gingerly to the locker room and didn't return to the game.
He was seen walking out of the stadium with the aid of crutches after the game.
Maye suffered an ankle injury on the sack and also did not return. Sources told ESPN that the Patriots fear Maye suffered a fractured ankle and could also miss the rest of the season.
Hutchinson is second on the Lions with six sacks this season. He has 49 sacks since being selected by the Lions with the No. 2 pick in the 2022 draft.

title: Raiders TE Bowers avoided major ankle injury, source says
summary: Brock Bowers missed the entire second half of the Raiders' loss to the Seahawks with an ankle injury, but it is not believed to major in its severity, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
full_text:
Las Vegas Raiders star TE Brock Bowers , who did not finish Sunday's game, is not believed to have suffered a major ankle injury, source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Bowers is considered day to day and will have more tests Monday to determine the severity of his injury.
Bowers injured his right ankle on the opening drive of the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . He remained on the ground after Ashton Jeanty 's rushing attempt before walking off the field under his own power. Bowers went into the medical tent and then returned to the field for Fernando Mendoza 's 10-yard touchdown run.
Bowers then headed to the locker room after that play and was listed as questionable to return by the team.
However, he returned with 13:30 to go in the second quarter and made a 12-yard reception on third down. Later in the quarter, Bowers went back to the locker room, where he stayed for the rest of the first half before ultimately being ruled out.
Bowers finished with two catches for 18 yards, upping his season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns.
Bowers has battled injury issues and underwent a knee procedure in September that caused him to miss the Raiders' first two games this season.
Information from ESPN's Ryan McFadden was used in this report.

title: Burrow tight-lipped after joining elite QB club, but admits he played like 'a great one'
summary: Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday night, becoming just the third player in NFL history after Tom Brady and Peyton Manning to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Even after a performance that was reminiscent of some of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history and enhanced his case as the current best in the league, Joe Burrow was not in the mood to bask in his latest achievement.
During the Cincinnati Bengals ' 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers , Burrow became the third player in NFL history to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span, according to ESPN Research. He joined Tom Brady and Peyton Manning.
Burrow let his guard down only a couple of times after the game, including when he was asked what kind of quarterback he was Sunday night at Paycor Stadium.
"A great one," Burrow said with one of the few smiles he offered after the game.
Despite Burrow being tight-lipped after Cincinnati's fifth consecutive win, the numbers said plenty: He was 35-of-44 passing for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Per Next Gen Stats, Burrow was perfect against the blitz (completed all 12 passes) and led Cincinnati to its fifth straight game scoring 30 or more points, the longest such streak in franchise history.
"I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people who aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "Because if you are, it's really hard to say this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."
The Bengals (7-2) bludgeoned the Steelers from the outset. Cincinnati scored on five of its first six drives, the lone exception coming on kicker Evan McPherson 's first missed field goal attempt of the season.
Against a Steelers defense that ranked fifth in fewest points allowed per drive entering Sunday (1.57), the Bengals had 337 yards by halftime and a 21-point advantage that partially illustrated Cincinnati's dominance Sunday night.
Burrow wasn't the only Bengal who had a big night. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with 11 catches for a season-high 231 yards. He came within 26 yards of breaking his franchise record, which he set as a rookie in a 2021 win over Kansas City .
Chase has played with Burrow since they led LSU to a national championship in 2019. It's easy for Chase to see why Burrow is playing so well.
"He's confident in his craft right now," Chase said. "He's confident his receivers will be open, and that's what you want in a quarterback."
Burrow threw two touchdown passes to running back Chase Brown , one to tight end Drew Sample and one to first-year player Dohnte Meyers , the former CFL star who caught his first career NFL TD on Sunday night.
The Bengals' win avenged a 30-27 loss to the Steelers (6-3) in Week 3, when Burrow was sacked and lost a fumble on the final offensive drive.
Cincinnati is in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but that didn't mean much to Burrow.
"Nobody's winning the division with seven wins," Burrow said. "Nobody is making the playoffs with seven wins. We certainly aren't satisfied."
Burrow knows that feeling well. Last season, he missed nine games because of a turf toe injury. Even after his return later in the year, Cincinnati still sputtered and finished with its worst record (6-11) since his rookie season.
Cincinnati is off to its best start in Taylor's eight years as coach, including the 2021 season, when the Bengals went to the Super Bowl, and the following season that ended in the AFC Championship Game.
After Sunday's win, Burrow can boast something he couldn't in either of those seasons. He leads the NFL in Total QBR (82.1) heading into Week 11. As Burrow walked off the field, he was serenaded with the same "M-V-P" chants he heard at various points during the game.
Burrow didn't put too much stock in that opinion after nine games. But when do those things start to be taken more seriously?
"We'll see," Burrow said with a smile.
author: Ben Baby

title: Cousins emotional after win in Vikings return, reflects on 'tough three years'
summary: Kirk Cousins was emotional discussing his return to the Vikings after their victory over the Packers.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Kirk Cousins managed to hold back tears Sunday morning when he arrived at Lambeau Field. He didn't even try on the way out.
After the Minnesota Vikings ' 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers , Cousins' first game since the Vikings reacquired him at Tuesday's trade deadline, Cousins let it all out.
"It was emotional coming to the stadium," Cousins told ESPN's Lindsey Thiry, his voice catching several times before he headed into the locker room. "Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It's been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today, and grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible."
Cousins' six-season tenure as the Vikings' quarterback effectively ended Oct. 29, 2023, when he tore his right Achilles tendon during a 24-10 victory over the Packers. He signed that offseason with the Atlanta Falcons , only to see the Falcons use the No. 8 pick of the 2024 draft on quarterback Michael Penix Jr. After two years in limbo, Cousins signed last spring with the Las Vegas Raiders , who then selected quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 pick.
But the Vikings needed him to do nothing short of rescuing their season when they traded a 2027 third-round pick Tuesday to bring him back. Week 1 starter Kyler Murray is nursing a strained hamstring, and in Week 9, backup Carson Wentz had the worst outing by QBR of any NFL quarterback in a game this season. The Vikings had lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start.
On Sunday, Cousins became the first quarterback since at least 1950, when the NFL began tracking quarterback snaps, to start games for different teams in consecutive weeks. He completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns, including a season-high nine completions to receiver Justin Jefferson , and was particularly effective in critical moments of the NFC North matchup.
Cousins completed all eight pass attempts during a fourth-quarter drive that gave the Vikings a three-score lead. On third downs, he completed 9 of 12 passes for 110 yards and seven first-down conversions. Jefferson said afterward that with a defense that is playing as well as the Vikings' -- it sacked Packers quarterback Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers -- the Vikings' offense needs only to be "mediocre" to do its part."
"He did what we needed him to do," Jefferson said, "and that was just pitch and catch, just kind of getting it to the open guys and just letting them be the playmakers. It wasn't really too much of big shots down the field, but it was just dumping it off and getting those extra three, four yards after the catch. So it was definitely great for us. And his composure, his confidence in the huddle, all of that, it definitely created a positive vibe in the huddle."
Cousins arrived in Minnesota on Tuesday night, attended his first meeting Wednesday morning and participated in two practices Thursday and Friday. Right tackle Brian O'Neill said the Vikings changed most of their cadences to accommodate Cousins' preferences during the short week, and Cousins said that on a couple of occasions he let coach Kevin O'Connell know what playcalls with which he was most and least comfortable.
"He's always been mature," O'Connell said. "He's always been meticulous in his preparation. He's always done everything in his power to prepare himself for games. But there was a level of poise. It never felt like at any point from the time we talked on the phone [before the trade] all the way through to giving him a game ball today, where it was anything other than just rock solid, consistent."
Said O'Neill: "I can't say enough about what he did all week to prepare. I mean, he has been gone for a couple years, learned a language in Atlanta, learned a language in Vegas, and then in three days switched back to the language we talk about here. And he was running the show and he was in command. It was so awesome to see that. ... [and] a little bit of full circle to have a good feeling again in this locker room, but we got a lot of work to do and we'll keep going."
O'Neill was referencing the morose atmosphere in the visitors locker room after their game at Lambeau in 2023, knowing that Cousins would be lost for the season. The Vikings tiptoed around that coincidence this week, and O'Connell said he knew Cousins well enough to avoid the topic entirely.
"Kirk's not really wired like that," O'Connell said.
But Cousins had clearly thought about it himself.
"There's so much football up ahead," Cousins said, "but certainly it's gratifying to be able to come back here with the purple on. I think to come back here with another team isn't quite the same. To come back here with the purple on, similar time of year, three years later, it's a blessing, to be able to have a win like we had today.
"But there's just so much football ahead, and the story is going to get written much later."
author: Kevin Seifert

title: 49ers tout 'incredibly dangerous' offense after 584-yard showing vs. Cowboys
summary: The 49ers racked up 584 yards against the Cowboys on Sunday in a jaw-dropping offensive display led by Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel.
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Upon learning that his offense accounted for 584 yards against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle interjected to ask whether that was the most the team has ever had.
And though it wasn't -- the Niners record is 621, set Oct. 8, 2012 -- Kittle & Co. etched their name in the San Francisco and Dallas record books repeatedly in Sunday's 46-40 victory as they moved to 8-1 on the season.
"A lot of big numbers," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. "I'm proud of the guys for that. I mean definitely wasn't as clean as all those numbers and yards. A lot of plays that we'd like to have back, some penalties we'd like to have back, but everybody seemed to make a play on offense."
In a matchup pitting a Niners offense that ranks near the top of the league in most major categories against a Cowboys defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in many others, the 49ers hit plenty of big plays on a historic afternoon.
• The Niners' 584 yards were their most in a playoff or regular-season game since Shanahan took over in 2017, and the most by any team in a game since Week 11 in 2024.
• The 46 points were the most scored by any Niners team against Dallas in the history of the rivalry.
• Running back Christian McCaffrey 's 74- and 66-yard touchdown catches combined with receiver Deebo Samuel 's 70-yard scoring run made the 49ers the first team with three TDs of 65-plus yards from scrimmage in a game since the Rams in Week 4 of 2000. It was also the first time San Francisco has had a 70-plus-yard passing and rushing touchdown in a game since Week 13 of 1998.
• On the other side, the Niners' 584 yards are the most the Cowboys ever have allowed in a home game and the third most they've allowed in any game.
When it ended, Kittle said that even if it looked easy, the Niners had their share of struggles, including allowing five sacks on quarterback Brock Purdy and missing some third-down conversions that could have put the game away earlier.
"It's great to know that we have players who can score from anywhere," Kittle said. "That makes our offense incredibly dangerous, but we have to stay on the field more.
"But overall, we played really well."
Though others, such as Kittle, receivers Keenan Allen and Jordan Watkins and rookie running back Kaelon Black , made significant contributions, it was Purdy, McCaffrey and Samuel who did most of the damage.
Purdy finished 22-of-28 passing for a career-high 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Even while under pressure, Purdy found ways to do most of his damage when evading defenders, going 8-of-8 for 175 yards and a touchdown outside the pocket.
The first touchdown to McCaffrey came after Purdy escaped pressure, rolled out and found the running back after he finished a blitz pickup and leaked out of the backfield for a 74-yard score. Purdy and McCaffrey called it "backyard football."
"I promise he's the MVP of our league," linebacker Fred Warner said of Purdy. "He's the best quarterback, and I'm glad that he's on our side."
Christian McCaffrey's 8-game streak with a rushing touchdown is tied for the 3rd-longest streak by any player age 30 or older in NFL history:
Warner surely feels much the same about McCaffrey. In addition to the 74-yarder, McCaffrey found himself matched up against Cowboys pass rusher Von Miller on an all-out blitz. Purdy recognized it and found McCaffrey for a 66-yard score that provided the winning points.
For the day, McCaffrey had 13 carries for 62 yards and four catches for 161 yards and three touchdowns. It was the most receiving yards of his career and the most by a running back in a game since Jamaal Charles had 195 for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2013.
McCaffrey is the first player in NFL history with 160-plus receiving yards, two touchdown catches, 60-plus rushing yards and a rushing score in the same game. He also surpassed Keith Byars for fifth in career receiving yards by a running back (5,821) and became the first running back in the Super Bowl era with multiple receiving touchdowns of 65-plus yards in a game.
"You go into each game, you don't really predict anything," McCaffrey said. "You just have to have the right mindset that this is the play that's going to break and trust your instincts and play fast."
Samuel, in his first game back from a hamstring injury suffered in Week 5, made an immediate impact with an 11-yard touchdown catch on the Niners' opening drive before racing 70 yards for a score on a third-quarter reverse.
Samuel and McCaffrey are the first pair of 49ers teammates since the 1970 merger to each have a rushing and receiving touchdown in the same game.
With Samuel back and receiver Mike Evans closer to returning from Achilles tendinitis (Shanahan indicated it's possible as soon as next week against the Minnesota Vikings ), the 49ers suggested that Sunday's offensive explosion might be just a glimpse of what their unit can become.
Of course, with the Vikings and Seattle Seahawks -- two of the top defenses in the league -- next up, the Niners will get a chance to prove that Sunday was more than just feasting on a struggling defense.
"The ceiling is as high as we set it," Samuel said. "We've got a lot of playmakers on both sides of the ball, and we go out there and put up 40 points. It just shows you what we're capable of on offense."
author: Nick Wagoner

title: Steelers rally around McCormick after guard carted off with gruesome injury
summary: The Steelers' thoughts were with Mason McCormick after the guard suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury and was carted off the field Sunday night.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Pittsburgh Steelers left guard Mason McCormick was carted off the field with what appeared to be a serious ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals .
Coach Mike McCarthy declined to give details about McCormick's injury after the game.
"I think just the love for him is very evident and continues in the training room right now," McCarthy said. "So we'll speak on that when the time is right."
McCormick, a key part of the team's nucleus of young offensive linemen, suffered the injury as defensive tackle Jonathan Allen bulldozed him into quarterback Aaron Rodgers for a third-down sack. With McCormick still on the ground, Rodgers quickly waved for medical personnel.
"Made a lot of us sick to our stomach," left tackle Troy Fautanu said of seeing his teammate's injury. "I mean, seeing stuff like that. I had never seen anything like that before. But obviously prayers up for Mason. Just making sure we're checking on the person, not really the player right now."
An air cast was placed on McCormick's right ankle as teammates took a knee around the 26-year-old guard. Offensive linemen Dylan Cook and Ryan McCollum helped get McCormick into the cart, and McCormick briefly lifted a hand to wave to the crowd as he was driven off the field.
McCormick was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game.
"Seeing Mason go down was pretty tough," defensive tackle Cam Heyward said. "He has been kicking a lot of tail all year long, and on an offensive line, he's going to stand out. So it's going to be up to the guys to step up."
Selected in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL draft, McCormick has made 39 career starts after moving into the starting lineup as right guard in Week 4 of his rookie season. McCormick hasn't missed a game since becoming a starter, and this offseason, he switched to the left side of the line along with Fautanu, who was also drafted in 2024.
"The amount of work and just the presence that he brings to his offense and to this O-line room, it's a big loss, man," Fautanu said. "He's not going anywhere, but obviously being out there on the field, I know his presence is still going to be felt."
author: Brooke Pryor

title: JSN keeps up record pace with 144-yard 3rd quarter to spark Seahawks' offense
summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, finished with a season-high 171 yards on eight catches, with 144 coming in the third quarter to help the Seahawks turn a three-point halftime deficit into a 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
full_text:
LAS VEGAS -- Few defenders have been able to slow down Jaxon Smith-Njigba during what is shaping up to be a record-breaking season, and against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday, a slippery turf couldn't, either.
On a third-and-3 play midway through the third quarter, the Seattle Seahawks ' All-Pro wide receiver lost his footing coming out of his break on an in route past the line to gain. When he got back up and turned up field, Drew Lock hit him for a 71-yard touchdown.
The NFL's leading receiver finished with a season-high 171 yards on eight catches, with 144 coming in the third quarter to help the Seahawks (6-4) turn a three-point halftime deficit into a 21-13 win .
The touchdown was Smith-Njiba's 10th of the season, extending his NFL lead.
"When I slipped, I just look back to see what Drew was doing, and he rolled out to the left," said Smith-Njigba, still wearing a uniform covered in grass stains. "Just trying to find space. I was able to see the middle of the field open and take advantage of it."
According to ESPN Research, Smith-Njigba's 144 receiving yards in the third quarter were the most in a quarter since 2021, when Ja'Marr Chase had 147. Smith-Njigba's 160 yards in the second half were the most by any player in a half this season. Smith-Njigba has topped 100 receiving yards eight times this season, which is tied with four other players for most in NFL history through 10 games.
"The thing that stuck out today was he's making [plays] in all phases of the game," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. "There's some run solutions where he makes plays. There's some quick game where he made plays on catch-and-runs, the intermediate and the [deep] nine-balls, he made plays, and then on the extended plays, he's able to uncover and go become a target for our quarterback as well. So it's really in every stage of how we're playing offense.
"So it's pretty remarkable. He's a beast."
Smith-Njigba's 1,207 receiving yards this season are more than the rest of the team combined (1,122). According to Elias, he has the highest percentage of a team's receiving yards (52%) by any player through 10 games since 1966. As much as Seattle's coaches would like the ball to be spread around more, it continues to find its way to Smith-Njigba.
He's on pace for 2,052 yards, which would break Calvin Johnson's single-season record of 1,964. Smith-Njigba is ahead of his pace from last season, when he had 1,146 yards through 10 games before finishing with 1,793 -- eighth most all-time -- and winning AP Offensive Player of the Year.
According to ESPN Research, he's the sixth player in NFL history with at least 1,200 receiving yards through his team's first 10 games of a season, and the fourth to also have at least 10 touchdown catches along with that yardage total in the same span.
Smith-Njigba also pulled into the NFL lead in receptions Sunday at 79, one more than Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride .
"There ain't s--- you can do about it, bro," Pro Bowl cornerback Devon Witherspoon said. "I ain't going to lie. Nothing surprises me.
"The man can do everything. He can make all the catches," Witherspoon said.
Before his 71-yard touchdown, Smith-Njigba had a 29-yard score wiped out by a penalty for offensive pass interference, which he believed should not have been called.
It was about the only thing that could stop him Sunday.
"I tell people all the time, I've been watching Jax s   ince high school," said defensive tackle Byron Murphy II , a fellow Dallas-area native. "So the stuff that he's doing, I'm not surprised at all. He's been doing it. Just to see him at this level, it's even crazier. But he fires me up all the time. He scores, big catch, the whole sideline, the whole defense, we're fired up."
author: Brady Henderson

title: 🥨 Amon-Ra St. Brown explains Munich fit, TD celly
summary: Inspired by his mother, St. Brown paired a memorable performance with a coordinated Bavarian look alongside his Lions teammates.
full_text:
Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown set off the German gameday tunnel walk sporting traditional Bavarian attire: a lederhosen and a Bavarian jacket and hat in a return to his mother's homeland. Editor's Picks 'I thought he was speaking gibberish': Untold stories of Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing Eric Woodyard Amon-Ra St. Brown on celebrating Lions' win in Germany: 'Like a dream come true' 1 Related
St. Brown was joined by Lions receiver Isaac TeSlaa and long snapper Hogan Hatten , and the group carried beer mugs and offered a toast as they walked out prior to their 35-10 blowout win over New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
Asked after the game about the fit, St. Brown smiled while saying his mother suggested the look and told reporters, "I'm not going to put on some Amazon lederhosen." The @Lions have arrived in style! 🇩🇪

Amon-Ra St Brown, Hogan Hatten and Isaac Teslaa are repping traditional Bavarian outfits 👀 https://t.co/XQGjAjZAQt — NFL UK & Ireland (@NFLUKIRE) November 15, 2026
The @Lions have arrived in style! 🇩🇪

Amon-Ra St Brown, Hogan Hatten and Isaac Teslaa are repping traditional Bavarian outfits 👀 https://t.co/XQGjAjZAQt
St. Brown's mother was born in Leverkusen, and he spent a significant amount of his childhood living in Germany.
St. Brown scored two touchdowns Sunday and called his first score "one of the most memorable" of his career. The Lions added a memorable celebration following his second score to mark the occasion.
Rate the celebration from the @Lions... 😅 https://t.co/MfqzUFu6Qs
St. Brown said the "human centipede" celebration originated with Lions passing game coordinator Mike Kafka, who showed them an NFL Europe highlight as part of a pregame meeting. The NFL Europe players did the human centipede celebration after scoring a touchdown, and the Lions' skill players loved it.
"We were all laughing in the meeting room and said we've got to do it. I said first touchdown we got to do it," St. Brown said. "I scored the first TD, and I was too lit. I forgot to do it. So that was that. ... When I scored [my] second TD, I said now we need to do it. I was on the ground when they pushed me. I said TeSlaa, let's do the celebration. We all did it. It was lit."
Major love to St. Brown and the Lions for embracing the local culture in the NFL's second-to-last international game of the season.
author: Cameron Wolfe

title: Let's overreact to Week 10: Cousins changes the NFC North? Hardware for Mahomes, Shanahan?
summary: Will Kirk Cousins be the difference in the NFC North? The Browns are going to the playoffs ... but not the Patriots? Patrick Mahomes for MVP and Kyle Shanahan for COY?
full_text:
We did not do post- trade deadline overreactions last week, preferring to see at least one weekend's worth of NFL games before rushing to judgment about the immediate impact of any of the completed deals.
Now that we've seen the bulk of the Week 10 Sunday games, though? Well, as Dak Prescott would say if we hired him to introduce the weekly overreactions column: Here we gooooo ...
Let's look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the end.
Jump to: Cousins as the difference for the Vikings? Mahomes to win MVP? Browns going to the playoffs? But Patriots missing the playoffs? Shanahan to win COY? Fantasy overreactions
The biggest move at the deadline was Minnesota shipping a third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins, the former Vikings QB who was instantly installed as the starter to no one's surprise. Kyler Murray is still hurt (and wasn't playing well anyway), and Carson Wentz 's disastrous performance last Monday night was the main reason the Vikings decided they needed to make this deal. Fair to say the early returns are positive.
Cousins was 21-for-31 for 207 yards, two touchdown passes and an interception in a 30-10 victory over the Packers on Sunday. Solid numbers, nothing eye-popping, but there is important context here about team confidence and vibes in general. This Vikings team looked energized by the return of Cousins, who ran the offense with a proficiency that has eluded all Vikings quarterbacks for the past two seasons. And he did it with just one week of practice.
Minnesota scored the first 20 points of this game. The Vikings' all-world defense overwhelmed Packers quarterback Jordan Love , becoming the first NFL team in 11 years to record eight sacks and three takeaways in the first three quarters of a game. They finished with four takeaways for the game. On offense, star wideout Justin Jefferson set season highs in targets with 13 and catches with nine, finishing with 74 yards and the kind of smile he hasn't flashed since 2024.
The Vikings completed the two-game season sweep of the division-rival Packers and moved into a three-way tie for first place in the historically awesome NFC North. Minnesota, Chicago and Detroit are all 7-2, and Green Bay is 6-4. The Vikings have a 3-1 record in division games, having beaten the Bears in Chicago and losing to the Lions in Detroit .
Yeah, you probably could have guessed where I was going with this answer just by reading the last two sentences of the last paragraph. There is no way to predict anything with confidence with four teams in one division playing this well. Sure, the Packers are 1-3 in division games and their offensive line is struggling, but they're also getting Micah Parsons back at some point. The Lions have won five in a row but might have lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a knee injury in Sunday's victory over the Patriots in Munich. The Bears are off this week, so there's not a ton new to say about them, but they've won four in a row and are obviously quite good.
What we can say with confidence is that the acquisition of Cousins forces us to take the Vikings' chances very seriously, even in a division where everyone seems to be excellent. They just need a representative offense to pair with their elite defense, and Cousins right now appears to give them that.
Will it last? No way to know. Cousins is 38 years old and certainly not all he used to be. But he's also clearly better than what the Vikings have been working with since they let Sam Darnold walk after the 2024 season. And the way they looked Sunday tells us his impact has already been felt beyond the white lines. It's a major move -- it's just way too soon to feel sure about anyone's chances to win this NFC North.
Josh Downs also had a fun debut after being acquired by Kansas City , as the Chiefs cruised past the Falcons 35-13 . Running back Kenneth Walker III has been the Chiefs' MVP so far this season, Kansas City's big free agent acquisition from the spring. But Walker missed this game because of a groin injury , which left the Chiefs to rely on rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who had 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, and of course Mahomes, who had a vintage game.
The quarterback was 22-for-35 for 348 yards and five touchdown passes, including an 18-yarder to Downs that put the Chiefs up 14-3 just before halftime. Mahomes has 19 touchdown passes this season.
I think Mahomes is still the best player in the NFL, and he reminded us of that a bit Sunday. But he has also won this award twice. Based on how the voting tends to go, it will probably be harder for him to win again this year. Voters like to give it to someone new. (Before you ask: I am not an NFL MVP voter and never have been.)
Mahomes has also taken a back seat on the hype train to Walker, and Mahomes's overall numbers, though very good, lag behind the performances of Brock Purdy , Joe Burrow , Josh Allen , Trevor Lawrence , etc. Comeback Player of the Year might already be in the bag, and if he keeps throwing five touchdown passes every week, then yeah, MVP would be, too. But I think Mahomes and the Chiefs are very happy to build this season's offense around the running backs and focus on postseason success ahead of individual awards.
Rough day in Munich for the Pats. Not only did they get smoked 35-10 by the Lions , but they lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury after the first series. Wide receiver A.J. Brown 's injury-plagued Patriots debut season continued, as he returned from his ankle injury but had to leave in the second half because of a hamstring injury. New England came into the game already banged up at running back and on the offensive line.
Tommy DeVito relieved Maye and was ineffective, leading us to wonder if the offense can function if Maye has to miss much time -- especially if Brown also sits. New England is 5-5, 3½ games behind first-place Buffalo in the AFC East and a game behind Cleveland, which holds the final wild-card spot, in the AFC standings.
Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION
Twelve of the past 26 teams to lose the Super Bowl have missed the playoffs the following season, and the Patriots are in danger of making that 13 of 27. After making it through last season as one of the healthiest teams in the league, the Patriots are feeling the sting of regression in that area. They have a bye next week, so maybe that gives Maye and/or Brown enough time to get back in the lineup. (It does sound like Maye will be out an extended period of time .) But the problems range beyond that, including a defense that has given up 80 points during the past two weeks and has suddenly developed a disturbing propensity for allowing explosive plays.
It's not over yet, don't get me wrong. I'm not locking the Browns into that No. 7 spot just yet, and the Raiders, Ravens and Texans -- all of whom are in similar spots in the standings -- have plenty of issues. But it's absolutely possible that the Patriots miss the postseason, and if Maye is out for a while, it might even be likely at this point.
After falling behind the Texans 17-0 in the second quarter and still being behind 24-20 in the final minutes of the game, the Browns stormed back for an improbable 27-24 victory and improved to 6-4. After missing last week's game , Deshaun Watson had 312 passing yards and 50 rushing yards, leading a winning fourth-quarter drive for the sixth time this season. The blitzing Browns defense of first-year coordinator Mike Rutenberg made life tough for C.J. Stroud , and Cleveland wore down Houston and kept the score in range for the comeback win.
The Browns are half a game behind the Steelers and 1½ games behind the Bengals in the AFC North. And again, Cleveland occupies the third and final wild-card spot in the projected AFC playoff field.
All due respect to the job that first-year head coach Todd Monken and Rutenberg are…
author: Dan Graziano

title: Big questions: Are Bengals a Super Bowl threat? Could 49ers' offense be even better?
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 10.
full_text:
The Sunday slate for Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Munich between the Patriots and Lions. Detroit improved to 7-2 with a win after the Patriots lost Drake Maye early to an ankle injury.
Back in the United States, the Vikings comfortably defeated the Packers in quarterback Kirk Cousins ' first game since being traded from the Raiders . Without running back Kenneth Walker III (groin injury), the Chiefs started rookie Emmett Johnson , who coasted to 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Falcons. And the Jets went their second straight game without scoring a touchdown, losing to the Bills.
In the late window, rookie quarterbacks Carson Beck (Cardinals) and Fernando Mendoza (Raiders) made their debuts as NFL starters. Beck threw two interceptions and zero touchdowns in a loss to the Rams; Mendoza finished with a rushing score and zero turnovers in a loss to the Seahawks. Offense was not an issue in 49ers-Cowboys, as both teams combined for 86 points in a San Francisco win. Sunday night saw the Bengals put on a clinic in a blowout win over the Steelers and rise to first place in the AFC North.
Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.
Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.
Jump to: PIT-CIN | SF-DAL | SEA-LV LAR-ARI | HOU-CLE | MIA-IND CAR-NO | JAX-TEN | BUF-NYJ KC-ATL | MIN-GB | NE-DET
Catch up on Thursday's game: WSH-NYG
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap
Are the Bengals a true Super Bowl contender? With how the offense is playing, it definitely looks like it. For the first time in franchise history, Cincinnati has scored 30 or more points in five straight games. After a dazzling performance in Madrid, the Bengals carried that momentum into a big AFC North showdown at home. With quarterback Joe Burrow (35-for-44 for 409 passing yards and four TDs) playing at an MVP level and receivers Ja'Marr Chase (11 catches for 231 receiving yards) and Tee Higgins (five catches for 66 yards) also playing as well as they have in their respective careers, this offense is good enough to carry Cincinnati on a deep playoff run.
What to make of the QB performance: At this rate, Burrow will be the unquestioned front-runner to win Most Valuable Player. There was nothing he couldn't do Sunday night -- including hitting Chase in stride on multiple deep balls. Burrow is the first player since 2013 with at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span. -- Ben Baby
Next game: at Commanders (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)
Did the Bengals expose the Steelers' foundational weaknesses? Yes, in every way. The issues that lurked during the Steelers' 6-2 start were shoved into the spotlight in their primetime annihilation by a division foe. The defense, though stacked with some of the league's best and most highly paid defenders, has a talent deficiency in the secondary, significant tackling issues and coverage busts. With games against injured and flawed teams in the second half of the season, the Steelers might still finish with a winning record and even make the playoffs again. But Sunday night's loss showed that the Steelers aren't a serious contender as currently constructed.
What to make of the QB performance: Aaron Rodgers had a career-high eight incompletions to open the game before he finally connected with tight end Darnell Washington for a 5-yard gain late in the second quarter. Unlike the last time the Steelers played in Cincinnati in primetime, Rodgers looked every bit his age Sunday night. In addition to being sacked three times, the 42-year-old finished the game completing just 15 of 29 passes for 143 passing yards, 54 of which came on two long completions to DK Metcalf with the game well out of reach in the fourth quarter.
Best quote from the locker room: "We're not going to drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy and we're going to pour our energy into ourselves looking in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control," Steelers HC Mike McCarthy when asked how to keep the Steelers' loss from impacting the rest of the season. -- Brooke Pryor
Next game: at Eagles (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)
Fantasy football takeaway: Chase Brown posted a season-best 28.3 points in Sunday night's win. Brown had 10 carries for 44 rushing yards, but it was the receiving numbers that boosted his totals. He finished with eight receptions for 39 receiving yards, adding his first two receiving scores of the season. In the Bengals' pass-heavy system, Brown has the traits to produce on backfield releases, but managers shouldn't expect him to be a primary target inside the red zone at the rate he was Sunday. Brown fits as an RB2 for the Week 11 matchup versus Washington. -- Bowen
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap
As players get healthier, how good can the 49ers' offense be? The 8-1 Niners got WR Deebo Samuel Sr . back from a hamstring injury Sunday and the offense took off, averaging 9.8 yards per play and posting 584 total yards -- the most in any game under coach Kyle Shanahan (since 2017) -- against a bad Cowboys defense. Samuel had 109 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. But San Francisco is about to move up a few weight classes with showdowns against the Vikings and Seahawks defenses the next two weeks. That should offer a strong indication of where the offense is headed, especially if WR Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis for either or both of those games.
What to make of the QB performance: On a day when he was under pressure frequently and sacked five times, quarterback Brock Purdy was unfazed, leading San Francisco's outburst. He made plays on the move, including a 74-yard touchdown toss to RB Christian McCaffrey . More of that will be needed in the coming weeks. -- Nick Wagoner
Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET in Mexico City)
Is it time for the Cowboys to scoreboard watch? Anything is possible mathematically, but the only realistic way the 4-6 Cowboys will make the playoffs is by winning the NFC East. That means they will need help from the Giants (5-3-1). Five of New York's last eight games come against teams with a winning record (Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit). Whatever progress the Cowboys thought they were making defensively was exposed by the 49ers. The Cowboys have four games remaining against teams with a winning record (Seattle, Rams, Jacksonville, Giants). The Cowboys almost certainly have to win five of their last eight games to have a chance. And they have not won consecutive games this season.
Trend to watch: In the past three games, the Cowboys have given up six plays of at least 50 yards (four touchdowns). On Sunday, they gave up three touchdowns of at least 66 yards, a first in AT&T Stadium history. On the season, the Cowboys have allowed a league-high eight plays of at least 50 yards. -- Todd Archer
Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)
Fantasy football takeaway: 49ers RB Kaelon Black scored a career-best 14.6 points after 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, plus two receptions for 13 yards. He has now seen 11 or more touches in three straight games, with at least 10 points and a touchdown in two. Given his recent usage -- and the 49ers' attempt to reduce the overall volume for Christian McCaffrey -- Black has value as a flex option in deeper leagues. -- Bowen
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap
Is the Seahawks' defense ready for Round 2 versus the 49ers? Seattle allowed the Raiders to net only 163 yards, and it sacked Fernando Mendoza six times. Coach Mike Macdonald's unit has set the bar so high that such dominance was almost expected, especially with Mendoza making his first start and Brock Bowers missing much of the game. It will get harder when the Seahawks return from their Week 11 bye for a game against 49ers QB…
author: NFL Nation

title: Two games, 14 hours, 242 plays: Inside four NFL referees' unprecedented same-day doubleheader
summary: An inside look at the 14-hour day of four referees who worked an afternoon game in Indianapolis and the Sunday night game in Cincinnati.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- IT'S HARD to tell when an NFL referee is actually in a hurry because they're always jogging from here to there.
Jogging onto the field with a bag of footballs, jogging to take their position behind the quarterback, jogging over to the replay monitor to screen a review. But at 4:37 p.m. ET Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium, when referee Don Willard power-walks with his suitcase and bag through the concrete bowels of the stadium, led by a police officer and flanked by three other game officials and an NFL security staffer, it's clear that he is in a hurry.
"Next stop: Beep! Beep!" umpire Terry Killens yells as the group walks out of the official's locker room in street clothes.
Kickoff for their second NFL game of the day is less than four hours away, and Cincinnati is still two hours down the dark and construction-interrupted I-74. The crew has a police escort to the highway and then they'll be on their own. Willard, Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew hold their snack boxes in one hand and roll their small suitcases with the other. Willard totes a pink Pedialyte -- necessary for replenishing the 3 hours and 13 minutes of intense focus he had just put in during the Colts' 24-22 victory over the Dolphins. Larrew munches on a cookie while he walks and then accidentally drops it on the floor.
Two stadium security workers wave goodbye and yell, "Drive safe!" But these four VIPs won't be driving themselves anywhere. A black sprinter van waits for the entourage, tucked just behind the Dolphins' team buses. Another stadium security worker escorts a CBS videographer into the area to capture their departure. He backpedals to get the perfect shot: four officials boarding a van that will take them from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Bengals' Sunday night game against the Steelers -- pulling double-duty to officiate two NFL games on the same day.
The security worker tells another stadium worker, "Wow, this is really a big deal, huh?" He explains that the CBS camera he has shepherded into place is going to send its footage to NBC's "Sunday Night Football" broadcast (which will later highlight the feat).
The NFL declined ESPN's request to speak to the four officials and Ramon George, the league's head of officiating training and development, who was responsible for sorting through the travel disaster created by the FAA's nationwide ground stop Friday.
George worked through the night Friday to create new crews for each game based on geographic convenience so the game officials didn't need to use unreliable air travel. The result was flip-card changes for the game officials that were longer than the inactive players lists.
Each of the four double-duty referees work on different crews. At the Sunday night game, the inactives sheet handed out to the media pregame featured an entirely different crew of the seven on-field officials than what had been previously slated, with the parenthetical "the instant replay official still is Chad Adams."
The situation is likely unprecedented in NFL history because it's risky. The league intentionally arranges for officials to travel on the day before games (except in the case of international games, for which they travel further in advance), so they are settled and adjusted and can get good rest before they work.
Former NFL vice president of officiating and current Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino told ESPN that when he was running the department, having a game official work two games on the same day "would be the last resort," which shows how extreme the circumstances were. Typically an emergency alternate scenario would impact one crew and two officials, not the entire 17-crew system.
"I am sure they went through all the different iterations and exhausted every option," Blandino said.
• How Harbaugh, Minter aim to revive season • What is wrong with the Chargers' offense? • McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers • Patriots need to fix lack of defensive effort
Blandino said officiating two games in one day is the last resort because "it would be like playing two football games back-to-back. There's the physical aspect of running and the mental exhaustion after a game because you are doing a pre-snap routine for every snap, and then the eight-second play, and then a post-snap routine.
"The officials look like they are not exerting themselves the same way the players are, but they don't get breaks. They don't play one side of the ball. They are out there every snap and every kick. Then to say now I have to reset without any recovery time? That is a challenge."
"It's exhausting because you're looking for something on every single play," said Russell Yurk, ESPN's rules analyst and former VP of replay for the league office. "You're analyzing every single play. You're watching your players. You're watching your keys, you're making judgment calls, and it doesn't really let up the entire game."
Kickoff in Indianapolis. Willard, normally a side judge, has never refereed a regular-season NFL game before, only preseason games and Big Ten conference matchups before he began working for the NFL in 2018. So when he first speaks into the microphone at Lucas Oil Stadium to announce the coin toss, it sounds weird, because his voice is totally unfamiliar.
Following Willard's announcement of an illegal formation penalty that the Colts declined, CBS analyst Spero Dedes says, "I think we need to lower the volume on the officiating mic -- he is interfering with our call."
Walker, the field judge, calls two Miami field goals wide left, and an extra point is no good.
Willard and Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley have a spirited conversation with a lot of hand gesturing on Miami's sideline before the second half kicks off.
On the first play of the second half, Willard's instincts are tested. Colts cornerback Justin Walley hits Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord in the back of his throwing arm. McCord loses the ball with his arm drawn back, poised to throw. The Colts recover in the end zone for a touchdown. But is it a fumble or did he already start to move his arm forward? Willard throws his blue bean bag to mark the spot of the fumble and calls it a fumble recovery touchdown for Indianapolis.
"This is a tough play, because Walley comes behind Kyle McCord and it's the defensive arm that really hits the ball and makes it go forward. As an official you think that ball is going forward because of the pass," said Gene Steratore, a retired official and CBS rules analyst. "But Don has fumble all the way, and it's a great job by him."
Colts tight end Alec Ogletree gets to talking with Willard during a break. "Are you one of the ones going to Cincy after this?" he asks.
Yep, that's us, Willard tells him.
Ogletree knew there were going to be changes to the crew because on Friday, the Colts had gone over information about the officiating crew as a team, but it was all with an asterisk: it was only who they thought would be working the game.
"But we didn't really know who was going to be out there till we got out here," Ogletree said.
"I did ask [Willard], 'So how long you been the ref, like head ref?' He's like, 'First game.'"
Miami cornerback Chris Johnson picks off Daniel Jones at the 59-yard line and runs it back for a touchdown. Willard is standing at the Indianapolis 42, behind the quarterback as he throws, then runs that same distance back to the end zone to keep the play in front of him.
The first game ends after three hours and 13 minutes -- a long one because Miami kept it close. The double-duty refs shower and change into street clothes for their trip to Cincinnati. They've all packed a second uniform, this one for an outdoor game. It will be much colder at Paycor Stadium.
The weary travelers arrive at Paycor Stadium and bring their luggage straight into the security meeting at the 100-minute mark before game time. Willard carries a massage gun with him, hinting that his focus on the bus ride was as much about recovery…
author: Kalyn Kahler

title: Coaching commiseration: How Chargers' Harbaugh, Ravens' Minter aim to revive their seasons
summary: Los Angeles stands at 0-8 on the season while Baltimore deals with its worst three-game stretch in team history.
full_text:
In January 2022, Jesse Minter was hot on the recruiting trail as the Vanderbilt defensive coordinator when his phone rang with an unfamiliar number.
It was Jim Harbaugh, who was the head coach at Michigan.
"Hey, I'm pretty sure my brother's hiring Mike [Macdonald]," Harbaugh told Minter. "You want to come to Michigan and be the DC?"
Minter was stunned because he had never really spoken with Harbaugh. Their first real conversation started with a job offer.
There was an opening for the defensive coordinator job at Michigan because Macdonald was leaving to run the defense for John Harbaugh's Baltimore Ravens . Both Macdonald and John, Jim's older brother, knew Minter when he was a defensive assistant in Baltimore from 2017 to 2020. They strongly vouched for Minter, insisting that Jim should hire him.
"And Jim listened to them," Minter said.
Minter was sure he had spoken with Jim because it sounded like him. But he wasn't certain that he landed the biggest break of his career. He knows there are some coaches who will call with an offer and you still need to go through the interview process.
Minter quickly called Macdonald to ask if Jim had really just hired him as the next defensive coordinator at Michigan.
"I'm telling you, this is real," Macdonald said.
Jim Harbaugh and Jesse Minter formed one of the NFL's most successful coaching tandems over the previous four seasons. With Harbaugh as the head coach and Minter as his defensive coordinator, they won 50 of 63 games and captured a national championship at Michigan in 2023. And in 2024, Harbaugh and Minter were hired to be head coach and DC over the Los Angeles Chargers , where they earned playoff berths in each of their two seasons together, including last season.
Minter feels Harbaugh set his path to becoming an NFL head coach by not only hiring him but empowering him. Harbaugh let Minter have full control of the defense while building him up with "ridiculous positivity," as Minter described it. "Dude, I believe in you," Harbaugh once told Minter. "You're going to be the best coach I've ever hired."
In January, Minter was hired as the fourth head coach in Ravens history, replacing Jim's older brother. Jim Harbaugh then hired Western Michigan defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary to become the Chargers defensive coordinator.
In their first season apart, both Harbaugh and Minter are dealing with once promising seasons that have gone terribly wrong by the NFL's midway point. Monday's game between the Chargers and Ravens ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN/ABC ) has become a commiseration reunion for Harbaugh and Minter, both of whom are looking to live up to their reputations as problem solvers who instill confidence during tough times.
In Harbaugh's third season in Los Angeles, the Chargers (0-8) are the league's only winless team. In Minter's first season in Baltimore and his first as a head coach, the Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight to plummet into last place in the AFC North.
"He's a leader through adversity," Minter said of Harbaugh last week. "When you go through [a bad] stretch, I was always just really impressed with his ability to keep the team intact, keep them motivated, find improvement, find little things to get better at every day and hold players accountable. I mean, that's what Jim's doing."
The struggles for Harbaugh and Minter have reached historic proportions.
With ankle and wrist injuries to quarterback Lamar Jackson , the Ravens have lost three consecutive games by more than 20 points for the first time in their 31-year history. The Chargers, meanwhile, are tied for the fourth-longest losing streak by a playoff team from the previous season.
After starting the season with the third-best odds to win the Super Bowl, the Ravens currently have a 3.5% chance to make the playoffs, according to ESPN Analytics. The Chargers have gone from entering the season with a 68% chance to make the playoffs to now having a 74% chance of landing a top-5 pick in the 2027 NFL draft .
Each week, Harbaugh is asked about offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job security and the expectations laid upon QB Justin Herbert . And, each week, Minter is asked about the defensive breakdowns in the second half, the kicking struggles and Jackson's timeline to return.
On Monday night, the paths for Minter and Harbaugh converge again at a time when the questions outnumber their collective wins.
"He just figures it out," Harbaugh said of Minter. "He has got a great ability to make things right."
EIGHT DAYS AFTER the Chargers grabbed headlines for naming Harbaugh their new head coach, he touched down in Los Angeles on an atypical dark and rainy Southern California day.
Chargers owner Dean Spanos warned Harbaugh about the untimely storm he'd be arriving to.
Harbaugh's response? "Dean, we are the storm."
Two and a half seasons later, the Chargers have transformed from a franchise once infused with confidence to the worst team in the NFL following the offseason firing of offensive coordinator Greg Roman and Minter's departure.
After boasting the fifth-ranked defense in the NFL last season with Minter, Los Angeles has dropped to No. 21 at the midway point this season. The Chargers are coming off a loss to the Houston Texans in which they allowed a season-worst 44 points and 485 total yards.
It's been a swift change from the previous two seasons, when Los Angeles made the playoffs with 11-6 records in 2024 and 2025. In losing their first eight games in 2026, the Chargers are in the midst of the longest losing streak in 15 years by a team that had made the playoffs the previous season.
"There's fighting or there's slunking away," Harbaugh said this week. "That will never be a part of our culture, our organization. Any narrative that we're not hellbent on winning these games is completely wrong."
This is uncharted territory for Harbaugh. Entering this season, he ranked ninth among NFL coaches with the ninth-best all-time winning percentage (66-31-1, .678).
Before this disastrous start, Harbaugh had never had a losing season in six seasons as an NFL head coach. He had only lost eight games in a season once -- an 8-8 season in 2014 with the 49ers -- much less lose eight in a row.
"He's literally been the same," safety Tony Jefferson said about Harbaugh through their winless start. "He's been -- sometimes a little snappy, which I like, but he hasn't changed as far as there's no -- as a leader, he's doing exactly what we would want, is to see a motivated, highly spirited coach every day, regardless of the result, just trying to get it fixed."
While Harbaugh and Minter's on-field philosophies quickly produced results, Harbaugh and McDaniel have not experienced a similar dynamic.
Harbaugh, 62, is the old-school coach known for his buttoned-up polo shirts. McDaniel, 43, is the eclectic playcaller with a joggers-only wardrobe. Their identities have clashed as much on the field as they do in a photo lineup, with the offense, ranking last in points per game (15.1) and touchdowns scored (11). In last week's loss to the Texans, a third-quarter touchdown ended a 37-drive touchdown drought.
