Herbert, a two-time Pro Bowl quarterback, ranks last in the league with a 29.8 Total QBR. He has thrown nearly twice as many interceptions (11) as touchdown passes and has been sacked 31 times, the second most in the NFL.
"Just got to keep fighting," Herbert said. "As tough as it is, there's nothing else that we can do other than go out there and give our best effort throughout the week, understanding that it's only us in that locker room that can do anything about it. Obviously not where we want to be."
And, if there's any hope for salvaging the season, it seems to reside inside the locker room, where on a recent Friday afternoon, Mariah Carey blasted from linebacker Denzel Perryman 's DJ setup, as players milled jovially about and filled the adjacent barbershop in preparation for a game.
"Can I be honest?" Jefferson asked rhetorically when the surprisingly upbeat…
author: Jamison Hensley and Lindsey Thiry

title: What is wrong with the Chargers' offense this season? Bowen points to five major factors
summary: Are Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton both taking steps back? We looked at the tape for answers.
full_text:
Could it get any worse than this for the Chargers? After nine weeks, they are the only winless team in the NFL. They're the first team in NFL history to start 0-8 after winning 11-plus games in the previous season, per ESPN Research. And they haven't won a game since Week 16 of last season -- 331 days ago.
While last week's 44-22 loss to Houston featured plenty of poor defensive play, new coordinator Mike McDaniel 's offense is 30th or worse in an alarming number of stats this season: points, touchdowns, turnovers, efficiency, Total QBR, pass block win rate, red zone drives and fourth-down conversion percentage. The Chargers went 37 straight drives without scoring a touchdown, a streak they finally broke in the fourth quarter against the Texans.
So how did we get here after all the hype surrounding McDaniel, quarterback Justin Herbert and the rest of the Chargers' offense over the offseason? Ahead of their "Monday Night Football" matchup against the Ravens ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN ), I looked at the tape for some answers. Here are five reasons why Los Angeles' offense is off to such a horrific start.
Yes, injuries have played a role here. Left tackle Rashawn Slater has been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury , right tackle Joe Alt missed two games with a neck injury, and center Tyler Biadasz went down with an ACL injury during camp after signing a three-year deal .
But the interior of the front wasn't corrected over the offseason, as Cole Strange and Logan Taylor both rank in the bottom half of all qualifying guards in run block win rate. And overall, the Chargers currently own a 37.7% pass block win rate, the third lowest in the league.
Herbert must also take accountability in the pocket, but he has been sacked 31 times this season (second most in the league behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson ). Has the scheme clicked under McDaniel? No, and more on that later. But there is a general lack of execution on tape from the offensive line, which is devoid of quality talent in key spots.
Herbert's 11 interceptions, tied for the most in the league, show a regression in field vision. He has failed to identify second-level defenders in basic zone schemes. We're talking hook-to-curl drops and flat defenders, which has led to him to throw 10 interceptions and post a 17 QBR versus zone this season.
Herbert has also forced the ball into too many contested windows while taking unnecessary risks down the field. I see too many examples of Herbert playing hero ball, relying on his physical tools instead of taking the available throw. And his 19 QBR on pocket throws ranks dead last in the league.
Ladd McConkey 's availability is a major issue for this team. He has missed time in 2026 with rib, foot and back injuries, as well as a concussion in Week 6 . He has played just one full game, recording 17 receptions for 286 yards in total.
Besides McConkey, the Chargers don't have a receiver who alters defensive game plans. Quentin Johnston is an inconsistent straight-line speed target, while Tre' Harris would grade out as a No. 3 or No. 4 for most teams.
I don't see the Chargers' wide receivers creating separation at a consistent rate versus man coverage, plus opposing defenses are playing more zone (66.2% of Herbert's dropbacks) to cap vertical routes and force Herbert to read it out with late rotation in the secondary. He has completed only eight passes of 20 or more air yards in 2026. This isn't an offense that can create explosive plays in the pass game.
This summer, I was all-in on Omarion Hampton and the Chargers' run game under McDaniel. The use of 21 personnel (two RBs, one TE, two WRs) with fullback Alec Ingold and more motion/movement made perfect sense on paper. They had the tools to create advantages with numbers and blocking angles.
However, Ingold was put on IR ahead of Week 6 with a shoulder injury. And Hampton is now part of a backfield rotation featuring Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal .
The 2025 first-round pick is a volume runner who wins with short-area burst and contact balance when he can get on a downhill path. However, Hampton is averaging less than 4.0 yards per carry on outside and inside zone plays, which are core concepts in McDaniel's scheme. Based on the tape, Hampton isn't a great fit as a zone runner, as he lacks high-end vision as a ball carrier. And he doesn't display the one-cut ability to dart through creases of daylight.
As a team, the Chargers are also averaging 1.9 yards before first contact, fifth fewest in the league. That puts L.A. behind the sticks, impacts McDaniel's ability to influence second-level defenders with play-action, and sets up more third-down throws for Herbert.
Coaching does matter in this league. And I don't see the fit right now with McDaniel and Herbert.
This system is built on timing and ball location. Yet, Herbert is completing 61.3% of his throws, and I don't see a rhythm-based pass game on tape. McDaniel has put Herbert in a position to use play-action (55 attempts), but he has an 11.6 QBR on those throws (31st in the league).
What would I like to see? More boot off outside zone play-action. Let's move the pocket at a higher rate, as Herbert has just 18 attempts on designed rollouts in 2026. McDaniel could also use more schemed concepts that create leveled reads, especially on throws outside of the numbers. And the three-step passing game can improve with more defined reads for Herbert, using different formations and movement to clear the pre-snap picture.
But until we see more consistent play from Herbert, and improvements up front, this system will continue to produce poor results.
author: Matt Bowen

title: Patriots need to fix their lack of defensive effort -- especially if Drake Maye misses time
summary: New England has given up 80 points over the past two games. The bye week will allow the team to reset.
full_text:
MUNICH -- If quarterback Drake Maye misses time with the ankle injury he suffered on Sunday, the New England Patriots will likely need to rely more on defense to salvage the post-Week 11 bye part of their schedule.
That's not a comforting thought after what's unfolded the past two weeks, with Sunday's 35-10 bludgeoning by the Detroit Lions in Munich coming after the defense was sliced up by the Green Bay Packers in a 45-27 defeat the week before.
Yes, the Lions and Packers are two of the NFL's upper-echelon teams, playing in perhaps the best division, the NFC North. But that's no excuse for what the defense has produced in its past eight quarters. The unit hasn't met the most basic standard of what coach Mike Vrabel preaches as the No. 1 part of team identity. They aren't winning the "effort and finish" game.
Veteran safety Kevin Byard , one of six team captains, didn't sugarcoat it when dissecting how the Lions took it to them.
"They played harder than us. They played more physical than us," he said. "And as a defense, that feels like a slap in the face that we let them play harder."
Byard noted Lions receivers blocking way down the field on screen plays, and offensive linemen pushing the pile into the end zone for a touchdown. The Patriots provided little resistance -- allowing a season-high 4.5 yards before contact per rush (not including kneel-downs), per ESPN Research. The previous high was 2.85 yards per rush.
The Lions became the first team with 300 passing yards and 150 rushing yards in a game against the Patriots since the Chiefs did it in Week 1 of the 2017 season. It's part of a concerning trend: Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8 Tennessee Titans .
"We're not doing anything besides disrespecting ourselves," veteran outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones said. "We come out here, we work hard, and then to get blown out -- it's ridiculous. We got to make the game competitive. It shouldn't be 35-10, especially how we played so well in the first half of the season."
Christian Gonzalez , the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL, is among those on defense struggling recently. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, over the past two weeks, he has allowed 12 receptions for 271 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Gonzalez took responsibility for Amon-Ra St. Brown 's first touchdown, saying, "Obviously it starts with me. I can't miss that tackle."
Jones still believes there's time to recover, and one theme among Vrabel and players was that they are 5-5 at the bye week and still have a lot to play for. There's a Week 12 road game against the currently winless Los Angeles Chargers , followed by home games against the 8-1 Buffalo Bills and 7-2 Minnesota Vikings , road contests vs. the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs and 2-8 New York Jets before finishing the year with back-to-back home games against the 7-2 Denver Broncos and 1-8 Miami Dolphins .
"You have to go out there with the intention to do it. It has to be on the forefront of your mind to want to do more, want to give extra effort and show your identity," Jones said.
"What you show on tape is your résumé, so if you're loafing around, looking like some B.S., it's going to show. ... What you saw [in Munich] was a team showing more tenacity, more effort, way more than we did."
• How Harbaugh, Minter aim to revive season • What is wrong with the Chargers' offense? • McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers • Patriots need to fix lack of defensive effort
After the game, Vrabel was asked about the difference between execution breakdowns and not measuring up in the "effort and finish" category. He hinted there could be changes if he sees defenders not meeting what's required.
"I tried to reiterate as many times as I could that they were going to chase the ball, and they were going to try to push the receiver into the end zone -- just like they did. And if we weren't there, again, that's a choice," he said.
"I have to look at that and make sure that's something that's our standard. I'm not going to say that it was. That's what they were going to do, and it was no secret to anybody, especially me and to our team that got told that numerous times. Their first touchdown, the left guard's running 50 yards down the field and he's 5 yards behind the receiver, so give them a lot of credit."
That's the way Vrabel implores his teams to play, going as far as to paint the words "push the pile" and "finish longer than the guy with the ball" on wooden sleds that players use at practice.
The absence of it the past two weeks has been striking.
author: Mike Reiss

title: Giants QB J.J. McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers
summary: After only three starts and four games playing for New York, the quarterback's numbers are staggering.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Quarterback J.J. McCarthy played "very well" in Thursday night's 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders , according to coach John Harbaugh. He set a career high with 293 yards passing and had the New York Giants moving the ball the entire evening.
The night ended with McCarthy throwing his first interception since he entered the game in the fourth quarter last month against the New Orleans Saints . It still didn't come close to ruining the overall performance or change the impression that McCarthy has been impressive since becoming the team's starting quarterback.
It's not perfect, but it's promising.
"There were some plays made, he made some throws, scrambled. I thought J.J. played very well," Harbaugh said.
He later added that McCarthy "threw some dimes" and made some "great throws." McCarthy also seemed to be more comfortable in the pocket than last week against the Philadelphia Eagles , when he took five sacks, and did better getting through his progressions. In a lot of ways, he barely resembled the quarterback who struggled his first two seasons with the Minnesota Vikings , the first because of injury and then as he got acclimated to the NFL game.
McCarthy, the No. 10 pick for the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft, was traded to the Giants in late September for a fifth-round pick. He was pleased but not blown away with his performance Thursday night.
"There's things I could've done better," he said afterward.
That just goes to show how far McCarthy has come in such a short time. He was the third-stringer in Minnesota just six weeks ago.
It may be only three starts and four games playing for the Giants, but the numbers are staggering. They suggest a much different quarterback than the one who started 10 games for the Vikings last season.
McCarthy's QBR has skyrocketed from 36.1 to 56.3 this season. His completion percentage has gone from second to last among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts at 57.6% to 63.5% with the Giants. His completion percentage over expectation has risen from an awful minus-5.2 with Minnesota (second worst only to Chicago's Caleb Williams last year) to plus-5.0, which puts him fifth among all quarterbacks this season.
His off-target throw percentage has dropped from 19.3% to 13.5% and his yards per dropback has gone from a bad 5.71 to 8.04 with the Giants, which is fourth in the NFL. Even McCarthy's precision passing percentage has gone from 45.3% (dead last) to a more than respectable 53.5%.
The improvement in his accuracy has been among the most noticeable differences. It was on display against the Commanders. Perhaps McCarthy's best throw came when he was under pressure with a blitzer in his face early in the fourth quarter. He hit tight end Isaiah Likely in stride with a laser through a tight window over the middle for a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown.
"That's probably as good a play as you're going to see in the National Football League all season, honestly," Harbaugh said.
It has McCarthy and the Giants feeling confident about this season and his future. The 23-year-old quarterback has been a good fit with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy's scheme and in New York.
"I just feel really good in terms of my preparation going into every week. They are very detailed in terms of what they want from me, what the intent is every single play. There is no gray area going into each play and I just really appreciate the heck out of that," he said. "It is all about building, constantly growing, and that is what we are focused on. Being in the league for a little over two years now, seeing defenses that I have seen before and running concepts that I have run before, everything seems to be slowing down for me.
"Just being able to keep stacking and keep growing 1% every single day and I am just so blessed to be in this offense and so blessed to be a part of this organization."
The spike in numbers is not all apples to apples. McCarthy is a year older, with more experience and in a completely different situation. But there clearly has been progress, especially in understanding the professional game. It has been apparent when he faces zone defenses.
McCarthy is averaging 10.9 yards per attempt against zone defenses through four games as a Giants quarterback. That's second best of any quarterback behind only Houston's C.J. Stroud since McCarthy entered the lineup. He was at a paltry 6.8 yards per attempt against zone defenses last season, which ranked him near the bottom of the league.
In fact, McCarthy's expected points added against zone defense of 0.22 is tops among all quarterbacks this season. It seems to be a sign that his understanding of the game is improving under the guidance of Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan and trending in the right direction with more playing time and experience.
"I think he's done a great job," Harbaugh said Friday.
It's still early, but maybe, just maybe, the Giants hit on something here.
author: Jordan Raanan

title: Panthers 'talking about' penalties after nearly squandering win vs. Saints
summary: Breaking records for penalties isn't the usual path to victory, and coach Dave Canales says the issues will be addressed.
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Carolina Panthers defeated the New Orleans Saints , 20-17 , on Sunday at the Caesars Superdome. They also significantly outproduced their NFC South rivals in penalties and penalty yards in a game that was much closer than it needed to be on the road.
Carolina collected a franchise record 17 accepted penalties for 152 penalties yards in a walk-off win. And while coach Dave Canales was proud of the grit his team showed after several self-inflicted setbacks, he knows his squad won't always be able to overcome their tendency for miscues. The Panthers (4-5) have been flagged for 10 or more penalties four times in 2026, including their past two games. They are 2-2 in those matchups, including Sunday's win.
"I mean, some of the penalties that are judgment calls, they're going to call them how they see them," Canales said. "The things that I'm going to focus on are the ones we've got to take control on, which is offsides penalties, pre-snap deals, delay of game -- those types of procedural penalties. We've got to eliminate those.
• Sunday takeaways and big questions » • Highlights » | Scoreboard » | More »
"The competitive calls are going to happen. There's ways to talk about the technique but it's really the things we can control that we really have to focus on." The Panthers' defense was tagged with four penalties for 42 yards on the Saints' second touchdown drive of the game. That series forced Carolina to play from behind against the Saints (3-6) for the first time, which it ultimately recovered from by scoring 10 points in the final 3:43 of the game.
During interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash's second game in command, the Panthers held the Saints to 2.1 rushing yards per carry. They limited New Orleans to 222 net yards and produced two turnovers. With top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips returning from a three-game absence because of a lingering left hamstring injury, the unit also collected three sacks, seven tackles for loss, eight QB hits and four pass breakups.
That performance by the defense almost didn't matter, as the group squandered several stops with big penalties to bail out a struggling Saints offense.
"We've just gotta be more disciplined," Panthers outside linebacker Trevis Gipson said. "At the end of the day, we've gotta look ourselves in the mirror. We've got a new defense, this defense is really attack mode, but we're itching to make plays."
On offense, running back Chuba Hubbard took over, producing 92 rushing yards, 80 receiving yards and two rushing touchdowns. His all-around outing helped the Panthers overcome the plethora of penalties. Hubbard accounted for nearly 60% of Carolina's offense, and he made big plays when they mattered the most.
And yet, that output was almost spoiled.
"Proud of the group, proud of the way we stuck together and all that -- certainly, penalties, that's something we're going to be talking about for sure," Canales said. "And just finding a way to clean that stuff up because when the margins get tighter, it just makes it hard to win that way."
The Saints were only penalized three times on Sunday, losing 46 penalty yards in the process.
The third and final infraction helped the Panthers win the game on a 54-yard field goal from kicker Ryan Fitzgerald . Safety Kool-Aid McKinstry was whistled for a 30-yard pass interference penalty on wide receiver Jalen Coker . The flag set the Panthers up at the New Orleans 36-yard line with 21 seconds left on the clock. Following the walk-off winning field goal by Fitzgerald, Canales was asked about the disparity in penalty calls between the Panthers and the Saints. He declined to speak on the matter, even as his team has built itself a reputation on miscues through nine games.
Said Canales: "I'm not going to get into that."
author: Mike Kaye

title: Week 10 winners and losers: CMC, Gibbs dominate, Mahomes has biggest game in years
summary: Christian McCafffrey, Jahmyr Gibbs and Patrick Mahomes put fantasy teams on their back in Week 10, while Jonathan Taylor and the Packers and Panthers' passing games had quiet days.
full_text:
Week 10 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Christian McCaffrey , Jahmyr Gibbs , Patrick Mahomes and rookie Emmett Johnson . Meanwhile, Jonathan Taylor , Trey McBride , as well as the Green Bay and Carolina passing games, underperformed in a big way Sunday.
So, who were the big winners and losers around the league? Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.
Jump to a topic: Ranking winners | Ranking losers Biggest injuries and what's next
We have a new single-game high score for the season, as McCaffrey scored 46.3 fantasy points in a wild 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys. He was dynamic as a runner, but his receiving prowess in this game was extraordinary, as he had a career-high 32.1 points on catches. That's remarkable considering he has 121 games played and 12 games of 10-plus catches. By comparison, he had only four receptions in this game. The 49ers are doing a fine job keeping McCaffrey's 30-year-old legs fresh, though he does have two of his toughest matchups all season in the next two weeks (MIN, SEA). He's a clear RB1, but don't expect nearly the same ceiling for those games. -- Cockcroft
After a quiet Week 9, Gibbs roared back with a 44.2-point performance in Munich, reminding us why he's the No. 1 player in our game. He tore up a New England Patriots defense that has been reeling the past two weeks; the Patriots surrendered a combined 80 points and 972 total yards to the Green Bay Packers and Lions.
Gibbs has exceeded 40 fantasy points in three of his past 16 regular-season games and 35-plus in seven of his past 20. His 253.4 points for the season is the eighth-most ever by a running back through his team's first nine games. Gibbs' Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers might seem scary -- they entered the week the No. 1 defense against running backs -- but he's on too historic of a run to quibble about his clear overall RB1 fantasy stock. -- Cockcroft
The deadline acquisition of WR Josh Downs paid immediate dividends for Mahomes and the Chiefs as the veteran quarterback scored 35.42 fantasy points (his most in a game in five years) and the team totaled 461 yards of offense. Kenneth Walker III 's absence shifted the Chiefs' offensive philosophy more toward the pass, as fill-in running back Emmett Johnson has been excellent as a receiver.
Should Walker miss more time -- he's tentatively expected to play in Week 11 -- Mahomes could put up another big score in an extremely favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals . -- Cockcroft
Prescott's 34.42 points were a season high in the Week 11 shootout loss to the 49ers, and so were his 343 yards passing and the five touchdown throws. And it was Pickens who benefited from this pass-heavy game script, as he posted a career best 43.5 points. Pickens caught 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three scores. With a positive Week 11 matchup against a Tennessee defense that ranks at the bottom versus wide receivers, Pickens will be in my lower-tier WR1 ranks, while Prescott will stay in the QB1 mix. -- Bowen
Johnson, making his first pro start while filling in for an injured Walker, scored a career-best 35.1 points in the win over Atlanta. Johnson rushed for 101 yards on 22 carries as he showed that elusive running style from his college tape, but coach Andy Reid has unlocked his receiving ability in this offense. Johnson caught six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns Sunday. If Walker doesn't return for the Week 11 game versus Arizona, Johnson should be played as an RB1 with dual-threat upside. -- Bowen
In a prime matchup versus the Saints' defense, Hubbard had a season-best 34.2 points. Hubbard rushed for 92 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries, plus he had a season-high 80 receiving yards on five catches. The Week 11 tilt versus the Ravens' defense creates a tougher matchup for Hubbard, but with 20 or more touches in three straight games (and at least one touchdown in two), he'll be a fringe RB1 in my rankings. -- Bowen
Brown posted a season-best 28.3 points in the Sunday night win over the Steelers. Brown had 10 carries for 44 yards, but it was the receiving numbers that boosted his totals. He finished with eight receptions for 39 yards, adding two touchdowns on red zone targets (his first receiving scores off the season). In the Bengals' pass-heavy system, Brown has the traits to produce on backfield releases, but managers shouldn't expect him to be a primary target inside the red zone at a consistent rate. Brown fits as an RB2 for the Week 11 matchup versus Washington. -- Bowen
Burrow continued his run of high-level production in Sunday night's win over Pittsburgh, scoring 33.16 points. Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns, plus he added 8 yards rushing. Burrow has scored 22 or more points in his seven straight games, with at least four touchdown passes in four of his past five. Big-time production. Chase's 34.1 points were a season best, as he caught 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards (the third most in his career). Managers can lock in Burrow and Chase as elite fantasy starters regardless of the matchup. The Bengals get the Commanders' defense up next in Week 11, which bodes well. -- Bowen
With No. 2 quarterback Drew Lock getting another start for an injured Sam Darnold , Smith-Njigba scored 31.1 points, catching eight of 10 targets for a season-high 171 yards, plus he added a touchdown on a 71-yard, second-reaction catch. Smith-Njigba has now scored 31 or more points in two of his past four games, and he'll remain an elite WR1 when the Seahawks return from the bye in Week 12 versus the 49ers. -- Bowen
Purdy picked apart a bad Cowboys defense, scoring 31.66 fantasy points despite attempting only 28 passes and rushing just twice, as he accounted for two touchdown passes of greater than 60 yards. Samuel, meanwhile, had 25.9 fantasy points, thanks in large part to a 70-yard rushing touchdown on a reverse. These two have it much tougher in Week 11 against the Vikings, but Samuel's two-way ability could make him an important part of the game plan. Purdy is a back-end QB1, and Samuel a WR3, for that matchup. -- Cockcroft
Washington scored 28.2 points in Sunday's win over the Titans, catching seven of nine targets for a season-high 152 yards and a touchdown. Washington has now caught a touchdown in back-to-back games, with at least seven targets in each. Lawrence (26.78 points) threw for a season-high 352 yards with three touchdowns, and he added 27 rushing yards. Lawrence will be in my QB1 ranks for the Week 11 game versus the New York Giants , while Washington can be trusted as a WR2. -- Bowen
His 24.4 points surely pleased his fantasy managers as they represented his second-best total in 2026 and his 16 targets were easily his season high. Collins' day had its rough spots, as he collided with a pair of Cleveland Browns defenders en route to C.J. Stroud 's only interception late in the second quarter, he committed an unnecessary roughness penalty late in the fourth quarter and he failed to catch five of his final seven targets on the day in a game his Texans lost in the final minutes. Still, Collins' heavy usage continues to bolster his back-end fantasy WR1 value. -- Cockcroft
The slow but steady transition from Kyren Williams to Corum as the Rams' primary running back continued in Week 10, as Corum scored a season-high 20.9 fantasy points while playing 50% of the offensive snaps and handling 17 carries to Williams' 12. Williams, meanwhile, scored a season-low 5.2 points, the third time in his past five games that he has been held beneath 10. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, the Rams seem content with leaning heavily upon their running game while increasing Williams' work in the passing game (he ran 22 routes, second most on the team). Corum will be a fantasy RB2 when the Rams return from bye to play the Green Bay Packers in Week 12. -- Cockcroft

title: Aaron Rodgers passes HOFer Brees for second most fantasy football points all time
summary: With Aaron Rodgers' score on Sunday, he reaches another fantasy football accolade in his HOF-worthy career.
full_text:
Congratulations, Aaron Rodgers , on another significant career milestone!
With his 27-yard touchdown pass to tight end Pat Freiermuth in the fourth quarter of the Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals , Rodgers moved into second place all-time in fantasy football scoring. That play pushed his career total to 5,191.12 fantasy points, passing Drew Brees (5,188.92) on the all-time list.
Rodgers finished his day with 15.62 fantasy points, and he has 132.76 fantasy points for the season, 18th among quarterbacks.
This comes after Rodgers broke a tie with Peyton Manning (539) to move into third place exclusively in career touchdown passes, with 540.
Rodgers' career fantasy prowess is especially impressive if examining his contributions on a rate basis. He entered Week 8 having averaged 19.1 fantasy points across 271 career games, easily the most among any quarterback with at least 150 games played. In Rodgers' 264 career starts entering the week, he averaged 19.5 points, again easily the most among quarterbacks with at least 150 starts. Note, however, that among active quarterbacks, Josh Allen (22.4), Lamar Jackson (21.7) and Patrick Mahomes (21.3) comprise the top three in points per game as starters, if we lower the threshold to at least 100 career starts.
Rodgers' chances at reaching the top of the scoring list is long, to say the least. Tom Brady, who made 333 career starts (plus two relief appearances) over a 23-year NFL career, holds the all-time record for scoring , with 5,944.36.
Brady played until he was 45 years, 166 days old, or two years and 196 days older than Rodgers is today. To put the differential in their scoring into perspective, if Rodgers were to play until exactly the age that Brady was when he retired, he would need to play every one of 43 games -- assuming the league doesn't again expand the schedule during that time -- and average at least 17.6 fantasy points in them. That's a tall order, considering Rodgers has averaged 14.1 (2022), 15.1 (2024) and 14.1 (2025) fantasy points in his three most recent fully healthy seasons, as well as 16.0 over the first seven weeks of this season. Nevertheless, none of that should discount anything Rodgers has accomplished over his career. His resume includes four MVP awards (2011, 2015, 2020-21), a Super Bowl win (Super Bowl XLV), one fantasy football scoring title (2011), four seasons leading all quarterbacks in fantasy scoring (2009, 2011, 2014, 2016) and 10 seasons with at least 300 fantasy points scored (2009-12, 2014-16, 2018, 2020-21). Rodgers also joins Brady as the only players to score at least 250 fantasy points in a season played entirely after his 40th birthday (2024, 256.58).
It's yet another highlight in what's a clear Hall of Fame career, both on the gridiron and in fantasy football.

title: Betting buzz: What the numbers say about this improbable Browns season
summary: Only 10 games into the season, the Cleveland Browns have already hit the over on their preseason win total, and that's just one of several notable numbers surrounding this team.
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have been an underdog going into every single one of their games this season except for one. They have trailed at some point in every game. Before the season, sportsbooks assigned them a win total of 5.5, tied for the third-lowest in the league, per DraftKings lines.
And yet, against all odds, the Browns are 6-4 more than halfway through the 2026 NFL season, becoming the first team in the league to hit the over on their preseason win total in the process.
Even more remarkably, all six of their wins have been in comeback fashion, with Sunday's victory over the Houston Texans serving as perhaps the finest example yet. Cleveland trailed 17-0 in the second quarter, at which point, their live odds to win the game lengthened all the way to +1480 on the live moneyline from a pregame closing line of +164, per DraftKings odds.
The Browns' latest cardiac accomplishment put them into rare air: They are the first team in NFL history to win their first six games by four points or fewer, and the first team in the Super Bowl era to be underdogs and win their first four home games, according to ESPN Research.
In each of those six wins, Cleveland has trailed at some point in the game, naturally forcing sportsbooks to lengthen their in-play odds and provide lucrative opportunities for bettors. Week 10's nearly 15-1 live line against Houston was the longest so far, but the Browns have been at least +365 at some point in every game, and were +1060 before coming back to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2, per DraftKings lines.
"The Browns have turned live long shots into a weekly feature," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "Bettors are starting to recognize the pattern, and we have seen more interest in Cleveland when the Browns fall behind and their live price grows. There is still a little hesitation because repeatedly relying on fourth quarter comebacks is difficult, but bettors are becoming more willing to take a chance at the longer numbers."
To that point, Hard Rock Bet said that Cleveland's early season wins against the Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers attracted live ticket shares in only the 30% range, but Sunday's latest victory got an 89% share.
The Browns are still a long shot to win the Super Bowl and AFC at 180-1 and 96-1, respectively, but other futures are starting to become more realistic, according to DraftKings odds movement. Cleveland entered the season at 21-1 to win the AFC North and have cut that almost in half to +1050, passing the preseason favorite Baltimore Ravens at 38-1.
Feazel says that Caesars has some liability on the Browns to win the division due to some "handsome prices," and BetMGM reported them as their third-most bet division winner since Week 1 by tickets. At both books, though, more bettors focused on Cleveland's win total under, allowing for a nice win relatively early in the season for the house.
Still, if the championship odds are any indication, bookmakers are not getting too ahead of themselves when approaching the Browns, noting that these miraculous wins, while entertaining, are not necessarily sustainable for long-term success.
"While our rating and view of the team is certainly well improved from what it was going into the season (they've already exceeded their preseason win total), we still do not view this as a top 20 team in the NFL from a power rating perspective," a senior NFL trader at Hard Rock Bet said in an email. "While their ability to win close games has certainly been impressive thus far, we expect some variance to swing the other way going forward in these results."
Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds | Sports betting home | DraftKings
It has been a banner season for big underdogs in the NFL, as underdogs of seven or more points have won at least one game outright in each of the first eight weeks -- the first time that has happened since 1971, according to ESPN Research. Underdogs of at least seven points are now 20-7-2 against the spread (ATS) with nine straight-up wins.
Of all the big underdogs, though, one has stood above the rest: the Arizona Cardinals .
With their dramatic, come-from-behind overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the Cardinals notched their third outright victory of the season ... all of which have come when they were underdogs of seven or more points.
Arizona is the only team in the league to be 4-0 against the spread when coming in as an underdog of seven or more points and, oddly enough, their three ATS losses have come when they've been smaller underdogs (they have not been dubbed a favorite yet this season). They were responsible for the largest upset of the 2026 NFL season when they defeated the Los Angeles Rams as 13.5-point underdogs in Week 6.
In general, the big underdogs' winning and covering has been a welcome development for bookmakers: It's a well-known axiom in sports betting that the public tends to back favorites, both on the spread and as featured in moneyline parlays.
"Bettors still tend to be hesitant to trust big underdogs, which makes those occasional outright upsets especially valuable for the book," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football, Joey Feazel, told ESPN over email. "That has been a welcome change compared to 2024, when it often felt like the public's preferred teams continued to find a way home. Bettors are beginning to show more interest in taking the points with these underdogs, but we have not seen a widespread shift away from favorites on the moneyline just yet."
Feazel said that "Arizona was comfortably the most important decision in the book's favor" on Sunday, and DraftKings noted that neither team was heavily backed either way.
This most recent Cardinals win was particularly improbable. Down by 14 in the fourth quarter, Arizona was as long as 28-1 on DraftKings' live moneyline. Feazel said that some Caesars customers grabbed them in the 12-1 range, but not with significant enough money to cause too much of a problem for the sportsbook, while BetMGM called the Cardinals a "small loser" for the book due to live betting.
Seven-point underdogs trailing by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter are now 5-977 since 2000, according to ESPN Research. The Cardinals are also the first team in the Super Bowl era to have three road wins as at least seven-point underdogs in their first eight games.
Arizona began the season with the shortest odds to have the fewest regular-season wins (+250) and was tied with the Miami Dolphins with a preseason win total of 3.5, the lowest in the NFL since 2017. Less than halfway through the season, the Cardinals need just one more win to cash that futures ticket for faithful bettors.
Their first chance to do so will be in Week 9 when they go on the road to face the Seattle Seahawks ... as 11.5-point underdogs, per DraftKings lines.
In 2018, the Supreme Court struck down the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, clearing the way for states to legalize sports betting nationwide. That same year marked the beginning of another momentous occasion that has become a stalwart of NFL betting every season.
On the fourth Sunday in October -- Oct. 25 in 2026 -- the NFL celebrates National Tight Ends Day, a tongue-in-cheek commemoration of football's most underappreciated skill position. Since San Francisco 49ers tight ends Garrett Celek and George Kittle helped bring the honorary day to life eight years ago, it has become a staple of the betting world, with bookmakers taking extra notice and bettors staking extra cash backing players of the position.

title: Ranking the top 10 Super Bowl performances by a defender: From Aaron Donald to Richard Dent
summary: Not all Super Bowl MVPs were quarterbacks or offensive stars. We listed 10 standout individual defensive performances.
full_text:
Super Bowls are mostly remembered for offensive fireworks, miraculous fourth-quarter drives, gravity-defying catches and MVP quarterbacks who hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy in victory.
Yet, as the old adage in football reminds us, offense sells tickets while defense wins championships.
While team defenses such as the 1985 Chicago Bears , 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 2013 Seattle Seahawks dominated as collective units, a select group of defenders delivered singular, dominant, game-altering performances on the NFL's biggest stage.
Here are 10 of the best individual defensive performances in Super Bowl history, including four defenders who earned the game's Most Valuable Player award.
COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February. We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series , featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, which will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027.
Score : Broncos 24, Panthers 10
Stats : 2.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 pass defended
Miller set the tone with a strip-sack of Cam Newton in the first quarter that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown to give the Broncos a 10-0 lead. With Denver up 16-10 late in the fourth quarter, Miller once again jarred the ball loose from Newton when he sacked the quarterback deep in Carolina territory to put the Broncos in position to score the game-sealing touchdown four plays later.
Miller's performance was so dominant he earned unanimous Super Bowl MVP honors, becoming the 10th defensive player and fourth linebacker in NFL history to win the award.
Score : Raiders 27, Eagles 10
Stats : 3 interceptions, 5 tackles
Martin created the standard for ball-hawking dominance on the biggest stage when he set the Super Bowl record for interceptions -- a record that is shared but still stands -- by picking off Ron Jaworski three times.
The linebacker staved off any chance of a Philadelphia comeback when he intercepted Jaworski in the first, third and fourth quarters of the Raiders' eventual 17-point win. He also added five tackles in Oakland's second Super Bowl victory.
Score : Bears 46, Patriots 10
Stats : 1.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 blocked pass, 3 tackles
The "Sack Man" in Chicago's legendary "46 defense" led the NFL with 17.5 sacks during the 1985 season and gave a master class in pass rushing during Super Bowl XX. Dent wreaked havoc in the backfield with 1.5 sacks, three tackles two forced fumbles while constantly ripping through blocks to keep Patriots quarterback Tony Eason under pressure.
Dent earned Super Bowl MVP honors and is the last true defensive end to win the award.
Score : Packers 35, Patriots 21
Stats : 3 sacks, 4 QB hits, 1 tackle for a loss
White established the Super Bowl record by sacking Drew Bledsoe three times.
After a quiet first half, White lived up to his "Minister of Defense" nickname when it mattered most. With Bledsoe and the Patriots trying to mount a comeback after pulling within a touchdown in the third quarter, White took over and recorded three second-half sacks, which included back-to-back sacks that flipped the game's momentum.
Score : Buccaneers 48, Raiders 21
Stats : Only player in Super Bowl history with 2 pick-sixes
While his teammate Dexter Jackson captured MVP honors for setting the tone in a rout of the Raiders, Smith delivered the decisive knockout blows against league MVP Rich Gannon when he returned two interceptions for touchdowns.
Smith picked off a third-quarter pass and took it 44 yards for a touchdown to extend Tampa Bay's lead to 34-3. He then punctuated the win with a 50-yard pick-six in the final seconds. Smith capped off a dominant five-interception defensive clinic by Monte Kiffin's "Tampa 2" unit and cemented his place in postseason lore.
Score : Rams 23, Bengals 20
Stats : 2 sacks, 2 tackles for losses, 4 tackles, 3 QB hits
Donald's second-half takeover came after fighting through constant double-teams and triple-teams. With Cincinnati trailing by three after just crossing into LA's territory with less than a minute to play, Donald blew up a run play on third-and-1 for no gain. He sealed the victory by pressuring quarterback Joe Burrow on fourth down and forcing an incomplete pass.
The Rams took over in victory formation, and many believed Donald's effect should have earned him game MVP honors over Rams' wide receiver Cooper Kupp .
Score : Colts 16, Cowboys 13
Stats : 10 tackles, 2 interceptions and a fumble recovery
Howley made history as the first non-QB and player from the losing team to win Super Bowl MVP.
The linebacker was a bright spot in a sloppy game that was nicknamed "The Blunder Bowl" due to 11 combined turnovers. He recorded two interceptions and recovered a fumble while single-handedly terrorizing Johnny Unitas and the Colts' passing game.
Score : Cowboys 30, Bills 13
Stats : 1 interception, forced fumble and fumble recovery, which he returned for a TD
Trailing 13-6 at halftime, the Cowboys desperately needed a spark, and Washington provided it 54 seconds into the third quarter when he recovered a fumble from Bills running back Thurman Thomas and returned it 46 yards for a game-tying touchdown.
The safety anchored Dallas' secondary with a team-high 11 tackles and terrorized Buffalo's offense by adding a crucial interception and another forced fumble later in the second half. He played a direct role in three turnovers that fueled Dallas's second-half takeover.
Score : Broncos 24, Panthers 10
Stats : 3 sacks, 2 tackles for a loss, 3 QB hits, an interception, pass defended, fumble recovery and forced fumble
Despite the Panthers' loss, Ealy delivered the most stat-sheet stuffing defensive performance in Super Bowl history. While logging only 23 defensive snaps (38%) as a rotational edge rusher, the second-year defender harassed Broncos quarterback Peyton Manning all night and matched the Super Bowl single-game sack record.
Ealy's efforts kept the game close. He intercepted Manning in the second quarter and forced a fumble in the fourth to put the Panthers within a touchdown. He became the only player in Super Bowl history to record multiple sacks and an interception in the game.
Score : Seahawks 43, Broncos 8
Stats : An interception, touchdown, fumble recovery and 10 tackles.
Smith was at the center of the Legion of Boom's dominant defensive performance. He racked up a team-high 10 tackles, recovered a forced fumble and blew the game open in the second quarter when he intercepted an errant Peyton Manning pass and returned it 69 yards for a touchdown. His opportunistic play made him just the third linebacker at the time to win Super Bowl MVP.
Miami Dolphins S Jake Scott, Super Bowl VII (Dolphins 14, Redskins 7): 2 interceptions, MVP
New England Patriots CB Stephon Gilmore, Super Bowl LIII (Patriots 13, Rams 3): 1 interception, 3 passes defended, 1 forced fumble
Dallas Cowboys CB Larry Brown, Super Bowl XXX (Cowboys vs. Steelers) 2 interceptions, 77-yard INT return, MVP
Pittsburgh Steelers DE L.C. Greenwood, Super Bowl X (Steelers 21, Cowboys 17): Unofficially 3 sacks (before it was an official stat), 1 forced fumble
Patriots S Rodney Harrison, Super Bowl XXXIX (Patriots 24, Eagles 21): 2 interceptions, 1 sack, 7 tackles, 2 passes defended

title: 'Brought the star power': 49ers' petty posts aimed at Cowboys tops NFL Week 10 trolls
summary: NFL teams kept it petty in Week 10, led by the San Francisco 49ers poking fun at the Dallas Cowboys.
full_text:
The NFL's oldest rivalries bring plenty of history, memories and gut-wrenching wins and losses. It's what makes the games more valuable -- and the trolls follow suit.
The San Francisco 49ers put on an offensive show against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in a 46-40 victory.
San Francisco had 584 total yards of offense, the most yards Dallas has allowed in a home game in franchise history, according to ESPN Research. 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey had 262 yards, plus three total touchdowns. He's the first 49ers player with at least 200 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns in a regular season game since Jerry Rice in 1995.
The 49ers poked fun at the Cowboys multiple times with Texas- and Dallas-specific posts, including cowboy boots outside of AT&T Stadium with a 49ers cowboy hat on top of them. In one post, lyrics from country star Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" were in the caption, while another caption read: "Brought the star power."
A post shared by San Francisco 49ers (@49ers)
A post shared by San Francisco 49ers (@49ers)
A post shared by San Francisco 49ers (@49ers)
Here are the top trolls from Week 10.
The Buffalo Bills have won five in a row after their victory over the New York Jets .
Buffalo kept New York out of the end zone and scored four touchdowns -- three total from quarterback Josh Allen , and running back James Cook III had the other. The Bills' 8-1 record ties their second-best nine-game start in franchise history. Five of Buffalo's wins have come on the road, including Sunday.
The Bills play in the western New York area, not far from Canada, and have embraced that region by including the Canadian national anthem at their home opener this season. title: NFL draft standouts, notes off Saturday's college games: Jackson Harris, Boubacar Traore rising?
summary: Is Jackson Harris the WR3 in the class? And has Boubacar Traore emerged as the No. 3 edge rusher? Here's our weekly draft spin, including top standouts.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 college football season isn't quite over -- we have Ole Miss and Oklahoma on Sunday . But we've already seen Utah hold off Arizona, Texas come back against LSU, Indiana take down USC, Arkansas top South Carolina, Florida edge Kentucky and Colorado upset Houston. Fun slate of games.
What about the top 2027 NFL draft prospects? Who stood out? Yes, the draft is still about five months away, but our analysts are always looking down the road, taking early notes on top players and starting to stack their rankings for an exciting class.
With that in mind, Mel Kiper Jr. and Jordan Reid will size up college football action through a draft-centric lens on Sundays all season long. They are answering lingering questions on the best 2027 prospects , sharing insights from scouts, picking out risers to watch and pulling back the curtain on their evaluation process. Here is what they saw and heard through Week 11.
Jump to: Week 11 | Week 10 | Week 9 | Week 8 Week 7 | Week 6 | Week 5 | Week 4 Week 3 | Week 2
Jeremiah Smith and Charlie Becker are WR1 and WR2 on most boards. But who is emerging as WR3?
Reid: LSU's Jackson Harris . His name keeps coming up when speaking to evaluators out on the scouting trail. The 6-foot-2, 202-pound playmaker transferred first from Stanford to Hawaii and then from Hawaii to LSU, and he has emerged as a go-to option for the Tigers this season. With nine touchdown catches -- including two on Saturday against Texas -- Jackson is a reliable route runner who just understands how to create separation and get open. He has strong hands to make catches in traffic and when defenders are crowding his frame. And Harris also has the savvy to leave defenders behind against press coverage.
On my latest board , Harris made a major leap, jumping to No. 17 overall after not even being on my radar coming into the season. Harris is firmly in the Round 1 picture now, and considering the WR need of many NFL teams potentially picking early, he could be a top-15 selection.
Likewise, Dylan Stewart and Colin Simmons seem like the clear top two edge rushers. So who is No. 3 right now?
Reid: Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore . After a standout performance against Miami last week , his positive play continued with a sack and forced fumble against Boston College . At 6-foot-5 and 253 pounds, Traore is an explosive and heavy-handed edge rusher who can consistently generate pressure on the QB. He has an expansive set of tools in his pass rush arsenal, and he's much improved as a run defender. Traore is No. 23 on my board, and it shouldn't come as a surprise if he ends up as a top-20 pick.
What else are you hearing this week?
Kiper: With six catches for 94 yards and a touchdown against SMU , Wake Forest receiver Carlos Hernandez stood out to me this weekend. His TD was for 44 yards, marking yet another long gain on the season. He is super dynamic, with strong route running, solid after-the-catch production and sure hands. At 6-foot and 190 pounds, he divides his time between the slot and out wide, and he has punt return experience, too. Hernandez produced at Washington State in 2023 and 2024, and then caught 40 passes last season after transferring to Wake Forest. But his game has really taken off with Gio Lopez at QB this year. I had a late-Day 3 grade on him coming into the season, but he could certainly go early-Day 3 now. I'm curious to see how he tests.
Reid: Texas safety Jelani McDonald had a career game against LSU with three interceptions. McDonald is a versatile player on the back end; he can play on the roof of the defense, but his best moments come when he's allowed to roam on the second level. His combination of savviness and ball skills was on full display, as he was the Longhorns' most consistent defender Saturday. McDonald was No. 45 on my board that came out last week. The 6-foot-2, 201-pound senior is not only playing himself into Round 1 contention; there's even a chance for him to be the first safety off the board.
Kiper: Abu Kamara might be the best player to ever play for Yale. He was all over the field once again against Princeton . The 6-foot, 208-pound safety had eight tackles, an interception return for a touchdown and a blocked punt. I don't know what more he could have done. And it's nothing new. Kamara hit 70-plus tackles in 2024 and 2025, and he already has 36 this season, along with 9.5 tackles for loss. In coverage, he has seven interceptions and 23 pass breakups over his career, and he has added 5.5 sacks and seven forced fumbles.
With his versatility, instincts and production, Kamara could make for a really good Day 3 pick. And with his special teams upside, he could make an impact for an NFL team, too. He's another player that I want to see in testing, but I really like his game.
Reid: Kiper mentioned him in last week's notebook: I'm calling out Georgia running back Nate Frazier here. Back and finally healthy, he had a three-touchdown performance against Missouri . At 5-foot-10, 205 pounds, Frazier is a sudden runner who has easy speed and contact balance to slice through defenses. Finishing with 72 yards Saturday, Frazier is beginning to look like the player we saw in spurts last season. And in a jumbled running back class outside of Florida's Jadan Baugh , Frazier is in contention to be a Round 3 pick.
Kiper: USC's Elijah Paige just missed the top five at offensive tackle on my Big Board . The 6-foot-7, 315-pound left tackle has really, really good technique. I love his footwork as the blindside pass protector, and he shows good hand placement. Paige can take away inside rushers, handle secondary moves and mirror well. He definitely needs to get stronger and show more punch and power; that will help him anchor against NFL pass rushers. And I'd like to see his run blocking improve. But Paige looks like a good developmental OT with a Day 2 grade.
Reid: Texas Tech defensive tackle A.J. Holmes Jr . continues to play like a Round 1 player. Scouts had his matchup against Oklahoma State circled this week. And with a half sack on the first drive of the game, he now has 5.5 sacks over the past five contests. Holmes is a true upfield penetrator with high-level finishing power. With a ton of knock-back strength at 6-foot-3 and 300 pounds, Holmes can disrupt plays in a hurry, and we saw that against Oklahoma State. Xavier Gilliam (Tennessee) and Will Echoles (Ole Miss) are my top two interior defenders, but Holmes has at least joined them in the "best defensive tackle of this class" conversation.
Kiper: Yeah, Holmes wreaked havoc Saturday. With cat-like reflexes, explosiveness and quicks out of the blocks, he gets in the backfield regularly. He makes plays down the line of scrimmage and is just straight-up disruptive. I have Holmes in the second-round mix right now, but he could jump into Round 1.
Kiper: One more quick shoutout: Miami's Cooper Barkate continues to impress in Malachi Toney 's absence. He caught eight passes for 134 yards against Duke , showcasing hands and after-the-catch traits. Barkate is comfortable making plays in traffic, and he can block. He clearly has good chemistry with Darian Mensah , and while he's still a Day 3 guy, he is ascending.
How would you restack the QB rankings after this weekend?
Reid: Week 10 was one of the more important weeks for this QB class. I'd rank the top quarterbacks as ...
Drew Mestemaker , Oklahoma State
LaNorris Sellers , South Carolina
Trinidad Chambliss , Ole Miss
Carr was the most impressive of the bunch, finishing 29-of-40 for 319 yards and three touchdowns against Miami. He showed poise and executed timely throws. Carr's best moment of the night was a two-minute drill to close out the second quarter, when he went 6-of-7 for 79 yards and capped it off with an impressive 18-yard TD pass. Carr came in as my QB4 and certainly helped his stock ... I have him at QB2 now just behind Mestemaker.

title: Reid ranks the top 50 prospects in the 2027 NFL draft class
summary: Jordan Reid updated his rankings for the 2027 NFL draft class with 50 players -- including eight quarterbacks and an elite wide receiver prospect.
full_text:
With the 2026 college football season in full swing, it's time to start stacking the top prospects in the 2027 NFL draft class, which begins on April 29 in Washington, D.C. I've been watching and evaluating these players for a couple of years in some instances, and these rankings are a compilation of my scouting (both on film and in person) and conversations I've been having with scouts and evaluators around the NFL.
We're going to start these rankings with 50 players, with scouting reports on the top 25, but this list will expand as the draft gets closer and closer. And these rankings will evolve -- some players will shoot up boards, others will fall and still more will ultimately return to school for another year. But this is how I currently see things in the 2027 class.
Let's get to it, starting with arguably the best wide receiver prospect of the past 15-20 years. Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk, and the top names at every position are listed at the bottom.
Jump to: Rankings by position
Stats through Nov. 7: 69 receptions for 1,200 receiving yards (17.4 yards per catch) and 14 touchdowns
Smith could have All-Pro potential early in his NFL career as a true No. 1 receiver. He immediately changes the offensive outlook for the team that adds him. He is sure-handed and can glide past defenders with ease. And he's equally as capable of winning with strength at the catch point. Smith's change of direction in routes needs to become sharper, as he can take too many choppy steps when working back toward passers. But he is tough to stop when allowed to attack defenses vertically.
Stats through Nov. 7: 16 tackles, five passes defensed, 43.8% completion percentage allowed
With excellent length, speed and technique, Moore is the prototypical cornerback prospect. His length and physicality allow him to excel when getting hands on receivers in press man coverage. He also has the awareness to identify and defend route concepts in zone coverage. Moore has the ball skills to match receivers, routinely tracking and attacking the ball out of the air. But he needs to improve his discipline and hand timing at the top of routes.
Stats through Nov. 7: 12 tackles, two sacks, 4.5 tackles for loss, three forced fumbles, 20% pressure rate
With a slender frame, Stewart has rare burst and closing speed as a pass rusher. That allows him to wreak havoc on twists and stunts, though the tools have yet to lead to high-end production at the college level. Stewart must also become more consistent with using his length and shedding against the run.
Stats through Nov. 7: 25 tackles, 10.5 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery, 20.5% pressure rate
Simmons is an energetic and high-effort pass rusher, with a quick first step to explode past blockers. He has a nifty combination of hesitation moves and shoulder fakes. But he still needs to develop consistent counter moves, as he can get stuck if his initial move isn't effective. Simmons is a powerful run defender, using a strong base and powerful hands to keep his frame clean when setting the edge.
Stats through Nov. 7: 206-of-309 passing (66.7% completion percentage) for 2,962 passing yards, 29 touchdowns and eight interceptions; 36 carries for 177 rushing yards (4.9 yards per carry) and three touchdowns
Mestemaker is my top quarterback prospect despite this being only his second season as a starter in high school and college. He has an unconventional style, holding the ball at his waistline before ripping a fiery, three-quarters release. Mestemaker has the confidence to test the tightest of windows from various platforms, but that can get the best of him and lead to turnovers. Plus, he can be oblivious to underneath defenders. Mestemaker is bit of a streaky passer, though his hot streaks feature plenty of "wow" moments. And he is capable of being a running threat.
Stats through Nov. 7: 58 tackles, five sacks, 11 tackles for loss, three fumble recoveries, three passes defensed
Cole is an easy moving, urgent defender from the second level. He has excellent lateral agility and pursuit speed to close on ball carriers in a hurry. But his ability to read and react to run concepts is still a work in progress, as his eyes can get fixated in the wrong spots. And he can be slow at recognizing concepts in zone coverage, leading to easy catches in his area. Cole is frequently used as a blitzer, which he does effectively.
Stats through Nov. 7: 50 receptions for 875 receiving yards (17.5 YPC) and nine touchdowns
Becker is primarily used as a vertical threat, and there are few college players who can match his straight-ahead speed. But he is more than just a threat with his legs; he's similar to an NBA rebounder with the way he wins 50-50 passes. That ability comes from a combination of elite body control at the catch point and A-plus hand-eye coordination, which helps him see the ball in slow motion. Becker does need to round out his route tree, showing NFL teams that he has more branches on it than just vertical patterns.
Stats through Nov. 7: 35 tackles, two interceptions for 2 yards, 12 passes defensed, 26.8% completion percentage allowed
Hampton is a physically imposing cornerback who strives to humiliate receivers at the line of scrimmage by getting his hands on them. Since most receivers struggle to untangle from his coverage, he would be ideal for press man coverage schemes at the next level. Hampton is also a forceful tackler on the perimeter, with lots of knockback strength when coming into contact with ball carriers. But he does need to be more disciplined with his timing in coverage.
Stats through Nov. 7: 19 tackles, two interceptions for 8 yards, six passes defensed, 48.1% completion percentage allowed
Robinson is an ultra-athletic cornerback whose quick feet and sudden change of direction helps him stay connected in man coverage. But there are times when Robinson gives up big gains because his technique tends to be abandoned. His best reps come in zone coverage, where he has a great feel for concepts unfolding. Robinson has excellent awareness with attacking the ball in flight, and he has a linebacker-like appetite for contact in run support.
Stats through Nov. 7: 22 tackles, 2.5 sacks, four tackles for loss, five passes defensed
An explosive 3-technique, Echoles is one of the most versatile and well-conditioned interior defenders in the country. He has energetic hands that help him accelerate past blockers, and reliable lower body strength helps him be a malleable run defender. Echoles still needs to make major improvements in his counter moves, as he can get stuck on blockers when his power and initial moves are matched. Plus, he can get caught not being firm on contact and get moved off his spot.
Stats through Nov. 7: 612 snaps, 0.9% pressure rate allowed, 1.2% blown run block rate
Seaton combines a good blend of awareness, quick hands and lower-body suddenness to be a high-level pass protector. He's also an easy mover in space, which allows him to excel as a puller or on screen plays. Seaton can be trusted on an island, but his biggest area of improvement must come as a run blocker. His hands and feet are inconsistent when driving on blocks to the second level.
Stats through Nov. 7: 531 snaps, 0.3% pressure rate allowed, 0.5% blown run block rate
Johnson is a hulking interior blocker whose strength helps him latch and sustain at the point of attack. He has a reliable anchor that helps him tether his feet and quickly stall pass-rush moves. In gap run schemes, Johnson has shown quickness when pulling. In zone run schemes, Johnson can be fluid enough to climb and cover up linebackers on the second level. A lot of Johnson's losses are a result of him relying solely on his upper body to generate torque and movement. His recovery athleticism is average, and he can face challenges when forced to readjust after being beaten quickly around either shoulder.
