title: Jaguars improve to 7-2 with 40-23 win over Titans
summary: The Jaguars didn't play their best game of the season today in Tennessee, but they didn't need to to beat the Titans.
full_text: The Jaguars didn't play their best game of the season today in Tennessee, but they didn't need to to beat the Titans. In a game the Jaguars sleepwalked through for some long stretches, Trevor Lawrence still ended up with 352 passing yards and three touchdowns, and the Jaguars still covered the 10.5-point spread in a 40-23 win. Lawrence hit Parker Washington in the end zone for a touchdown on the first possession of the game, and it looked like it would be a cakewalk for the Jaguars. But Cam Ward made some plays both running and passing, and Tony Pollard turned a short pass into a 32-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, and the Titans kept it to within one score for much of the game. Ultimately, however, the Titans just couldn't hold this Jaguars team in check for 60 minutes. Few opponents have managed to hold the Jaguars in check for 60 minutes. Today's win improves their record to 7-2, and they're poised to make a run for the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs. The Titans fall to 1-8, and they're poised to make a run for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Josh Downs "excited to keep building" connection with Patrick Mahomes
summary: Chiefs wide receiver Josh Downs didn't waste any time making an impact for his new team.
full_text: ' Chiefs wide receiver Josh Downs didn't waste any time making an impact for his new team. Downs joined the Chiefs in a trade with the Colts on Tuesday, which meant that he had limited practice time with quarterback Patrick Mahomes ahead of Sunday's game in Atlanta. Their lack of familiarity with one another didn't get in the way of Downs hauling in an 18-yard touchdown pass from the quarterback in the second quarter and he finished his Kansas City debut with four catches for 53 yards. "Pat gave me a chance, and I went up and made a play ," Downs said, via Nate Taylor of ESPN.com. "I'm excited to keep building off of that. First game and first touchdown, you can't write it better than that. Playing with a guy like him is incredible. Doing anything you can to get open for him and making plays is what I want to do." Downs only played 10 offensive snaps in the 35-13 Chiefs win, which makes his production stand out all the more. It also leads to thoughts of what his connection with Mahomes will look like once they've had more time working with one another and those thoughts will be pleasant ones for Chiefs fans to ponder heading into Week 11.
author: Josh Alper

title: Geno Smith getting tests on ankle, will start in Week 11 if healthy
summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith was forced out of Sunday's loss to the Bills with an ankle injury and his status for Week 11 is still to be determined.
full_text: '' Jets quarterback Geno Smith was forced out of Sunday's loss to the Bills with an ankle injury and his status for Week 11 is still to be determined. Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters at a Monday press conference that Smith is having tests on his ankle on Monday. Smith missed one series earlier in the game to have a concussion evaluation and left the game for good after hurting his ankle in the third quarter. Glenn confirmed that Smith will remain the team's starter against the Chargers if he is cleared medically. Rookie Cade Klubnik made his regular season debut on Sunday and will make his first NFL start if Smith is unable to play. Rookie wideout Omar Cooper also left Sunday's game with an ankle injury and he'll go for tests on Monday as well.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with torn ACL, likely additional damage
summary: Hutchinson suffered the season-ending injury while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye, who was also injured.
full_text: '' Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season with a serious knee injury he suffered while celebrating a sack on Sunday. Hutchinson has a torn ACL in his right knee and probably additional damage, according to Ian Rapoport. The torn ACL was seen on the MRI he had in Germany after leaving Sunday's game, and the team plans to give him additional tests now that he's back in Detroit. There are concerns that he also injured his meniscus. Hutchinson is one of the best defensive players in the NFL and his loss is devastating to the Lions, who are 7-2 and have legitimate Super Bowl hopes. They also had legitimate Super Bowl hopes two years ago, when Hutchinson suffered a season-ending broken leg, and their defense wasn't the same without him. The injury came moments after Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye. Hutchinson got up, jumped in the air celebrating, and landed awkwardly, with his right knee seeming to buckle. He immediately went to the ground and grabbed his leg. Maye was also injured on the play, missed the rest of the game and is likely out for a significant period of time.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Joe Burrow becomes the MVP favorite
summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is having a potentially historic season.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is having a potentially historic season. And, to no surprise, his performance has vaulted him past Bills quarterback Josh Allen as the favorite for the NFL MVP award. After registering a fifth straight game with four or more total touchdowns — matching Peyton Manning (2004) as the only two players to ever do that — Burrow has surged to a +105 favorite to win the MVP trophy. Along the way, the Bengals blasted the Steelers, 38-18. Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, as Cincinnati outgained Pittsburgh, 484 to 222. Allen is second in the current odds, at +310. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy lurks at +400, with Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence at +500. There's a gap after those four, with Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes at 16-1. (Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who arguably best fits the official Associated Press definition of the term, remains an 80-1 long shot.) The voting, which happens in the days after Week 18, will undoubtedly be influenced by the final configuration of the AFC and NFC playoff trees. Getting the top seed will give the quarterbacks of those teams a boost. In the AFC, rhat could be the Bengals. Or the Bills. Or the Jaguars. Or the Chiefs. In the NFC, it could be the 49ers. For now, Burrow has laid the foundation for a stretch run that earns his first career MVP award.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers pull out 20-17 win in New Orleans, take lead in NFC South
summary: NFC South football has earned a negative reputation over the last few years and Sunday's game between the Panthers and Saints didn't do much to change that, but it did push one of the teams into first place in the race to represent the division in the playoffs.
full_text: NFC South football has earned a negative reputation over the last few years and Sunday's game between the Panthers and Saints didn't do much to change that, but it did push one of the teams into first place in the race to represent the division in the playoffs. After the Saints rallied to tie the game on a Charlie Smyth field goal with 41 seconds left to play, the Panthers took over on their own 34-yard-line. Bryce Young threw an incompletion and then uncorked a deep shot to wide receiver Jalen Coker. Saints corner Kool-Aid McKinstry was flagged for pass interference and that set up a 54-yard field goal as time expired. Ryan Fitzgerald had missed from 48 yards in the first half, but he nailed this kick and the Panthers are in first place after a 20-17 win. There's some irony in the fact that a penalty helped put the Panthers in position to win the game. Carolina committed 17 penalties during the contest, including a facemask call on linebacker Tyrel Dodson that helped set up Smyth's game-tying kick. The Saints did their best to match that sloppiness with a pair of turnovers in the first half and they focused on the running game well beyond the point when it became clear that they weren't going to generate the kind of production needed on that front. Travis Etienne, Audric Estime, and Alvin Kamara combined to pick up 24 yards on 17 carries on Sunday. Their offense picked up a bit once they leaned on throwing the ball and rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson wound up with 11 catches in his second game of the year, but the overall approach was still lacking against a Panthers team that has not been very stout defensively this season. New Orleans will be in Chicago next Sunday and they'll need a win there to try to keep themselves in stalking distance of the Panthers heading into the stretch run. Carolina improved to 4-5 with the win and they will host the Ravens in Week 11. They'd be wise to continue leaning on Chuba Hubbard in that contest. Hubbard had 27 carries for 92 yards and two touchdowns along with five catches for 80 yards. That accounted for 172 of the Panthers' 283 total yards, so Carolina's best chance of winning games appears to be relying on their workhorse running back.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Glenn could become sixth coach to start 0-9 in division
summary: Jets coach Aaron Glenn has a 5-21 record during his one-and-a-half-year tenure with the team.
full_text: Jets coach Aaron Glenn has a 5-21 record during his one-and-a-half-year tenure with the team. That's bad. Here's something worse: Glenn is 0-8 in AFC East games. That's the longest active losing streak in the division by any team. And it's one game short of putting Glenn in a small club that no one wants to belong to. A loss on Sunday to the Bills would make Glenn the sixth head coach since the 1970 merger to start his career 0-9 in division games. The others were Jim Schwartz (0-10), Matt Eberflus (0-9), Pat Shurmur (0-9), John McKay (0-9), and Jim Ringo (0-9). With each additional loss, the question becomes whether it will be Glenn's final loss. The clock seems to be ticking toward an in-season termination. Or, if owner Woody Johnson doesn't decide to make a move before Week 18, an abrupt parting of ways after the season ends.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deshaun Watson found it "definitely special" to beat the Texans
summary: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson led a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter on Sunday, which isn't surprising given the way the 2026 season has unfolded in Cleveland.
full_text: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson led a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter on Sunday, which isn't surprising given the way the 2026 season has unfolded in Cleveland. All six of the team's wins have come thanks to Watson's efforts in the final minutes and the Browns are the first team in league history to win its first six games of a season by four points or fewer. Sunday's 27-24 win did have a different wrinkle for the quarterback, however. It came against the Texans, who drafted Watson in 2017 and then traded him to the Browns in 2022 after Watson sat out the 2021 season amid sexual misconduct allegations and a trade request. Watson said that the opponent meant that beating his former team was "definitely special" for him. “I think people know the history behind it," Watson said, via a transcript from the team. "Didn’t leave on a good note, but it’s all love for the city of Houston, the fans there, the players there, some of the staff there, most definitely, that I got to see today. And even the older ownership. So, it was good to see a lot of people, familiar faces, but it’s still love. But it’s definitely a good win.” Watson's time with the Texans is in the past and the present is exciting for the Browns. They head into their bye week with a 6-4 record that has them firmly in playoff contention and Sunday's win gave them their first 4-0 home start to a season since 1963. Faster starts would likely help their chances of both staying unbeaten at home and making it to the postseason, but knowing that they're never out of a game isn't a bad lesson to take from the first 10 weeks of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Burrow: Sunday night was great, but you're not winning anything after nine games
summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow entered some rare company in Sunday night's romp over the Steelers.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow entered some rare company in Sunday night's romp over the Steelers. Burrow's four touchdown passes gave him 20 over the last five games and that's something that only Tom Brady and Peyton Manning have accomplished over the history of the league. Both of those players have won MVP awards and Burrow is now the frontrunner for that award for the current season. The crowd in Cincinnati picked up on that and chanted "MVP" for Burrow during the 38-18 win and Burrow acknowledged the run he's been on during a postgame press conference. Burrow said "a great one" when asked what kind of quarterback he was on Sunday, but noted it's "a long season" when asked about the MVP conversation and that the team's goals are equally unrealized at this point in the year. "No one is winning the division with seven wins," Burrow said, via a transcript from the team. "Nobody's making the playoffs with seven wins, and we're certainly not satisfied." Burrow may not want to look ahead at this point, but others will do it for him and the Bengals' schedule is set up for them to continue stacking wins as long as they remain in the groove they've been in on their current five-game streak. If they do that, there will likely be a lot of people who believe Burrow can join Brady and Manning as both MVPs and Super Bowl champs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots currently expect QB Drake Maye to be out "a while"
summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye left Sunday's game against the Lions in Germany after the first drive, due to an ankle injury.
full_text: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye left Sunday's game against the Lions in Germany after the first drive, due to an ankle injury. And while the specific nature of the injury has yet to be diagnosed via the available imaging technologies, the organization is bracing for not-great news. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, the current expectation is that Maye will be out "a while." They have a bye in Week 11, before facing the Chargers in L.A. on Sunday night in Week 12. (That game could be flexed out of prime time in the coming days.) After that, the Patriots host the Bills in Week 13 and the Vikings in Week 14. In Week 15, they face the Chiefs on Monday night in Kansas City. The season ends with a game at the Jets, followed by home games against the Broncos and Dolphins. The Patriots are currently 5-5. They'd miss the playoffs, if the playoffs started today. Without Maye, the starter is Tommy DeVito and the backup is Behren Morton.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kirk Cousins, Vikings dominate, lead 17-0 at halftime
summary: Kirk Cousins is back, and so are the Vikings.
full_text: Kirk Cousins is back, and so are the Vikings. The quarterback, acquired by the team last week, threw for 126 yards and a touchdown in a first half dominated by the Vikings. Minnesota leads 17-0 at halftime. Since late in the third quarter of the Week 1 game between the Vikings and Packers, Minnesota has outscored Green Bay 46-0. The Vikings outgained the Packers 170 to 57 in the first half, forced two turnovers and sacked Jordan Love five times. Cousins' first touchdown came on third-and-23, a 38-yard throw to Myles Price. His second came on an overturned interception when Cousins' knee was on the ground for a sack before Lukas Van Ness picked him. Cousins then hit Tai Felton for a 24-yard gain to Tai Felton to the 1 on third-and-15. Aaron Brooks scored on a 1-yard run. Cousins is 10-of-17, with Price catching three passes for 45 yards and Felton contributing three receptions for 33 yards. Jordan Mason has seven carries for 26 yards. Jordan Love is 7-of-12 for 72 yards and an interception, a Harrison Smith pick with the Packers at the Minnesota 18. Matthew Golden has two catches for 30 yards and two drops, giving him nine drops for the season. Tight end Mark Redman had the ball taken away from him by Andrew Van Ginkel at the Green Bay 10, and the fumble led to four-play, minus-6 yard field goal drive. Packers kicker Trey Smack missed a 53-yard field goal.
author: Charean Williams

title: Emotional Kirk Cousins: "It's been a tough three years. There's more to the story being written."
summary: In first game at Lambeau Field since tearing his Achilles tendon there, Cousins fights back tears.
full_text: ' Three years ago, quarterback Kirk Cousins played the last game of his first stint with the Vikings at Lambeau Field, tearing an Achilles tendon during a Week 8 game. The first game of his second stint happened on Sunday. At Lambeau Field. The Vikings won, 30-10, completing the season sweep of the Packers and moving to 7-2 on the season. And Cousins was visibility emotional during his an-field interview after the win with Lindsey Thiry of ESPN. "It was emotional, you know, coming to the stadium, three years ago, tearing my Achilles here," Cousins said, voice breaking multiple times. "It's been a tough three years," Asked whether he thought it would be this emotional, Cousins said, "It's been a tough three years. There's more to the story being written." It's easier to write the story when the defense is serving up an endless supply of pens, inks, and paper. The Vikings sacked Packers quarterback Jordan Love eight times and forced three turnovers. (The Packers also had a special-teams fumble.) And while the Minnesota defense did its job (as it always does), Cousins displayed accuracy, velocity, and force on his passes that none of the other quarterbacks on the team could ever match. He also made good decisions in key moments, helping the Vikings' offense convert eight of 15 third-down situations. It all happened after Cousins showed up only four days before the game. He now has a full week to prepare for a game against the 49ers — the last team he played during his nine-game run in Las Vegas.
author: Mike Florio

title: Drake Maye remained in Germany as ankle injury continues to be evaluated
summary: Maye was injured early in Sunday's game and is expected to miss extended time.
full_text: '' Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was knocked out of Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich early in the first quarter and he did not return to the United States with the team after the game. Head coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update on Maye's outlook during a Monday morning appearance on WEEI, but he did share that Maye remained behind as the team continues to evaluate his injury. "The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back ," Vrabel said. "He'll be traveling back here shortly, but just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around with injuries, just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly." PFT reported on Sunday night that Maye is expected to be out a while and multiple reports on Monday morning have indicated fear that he may not be back on the field this season. An update on that from the team may not come until Maye is back from Europe, but it looks like the 5-5 team's chances of staying in the playoff hunt are going to rely on backup quarterback Tommy DeVito for the indefinite future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brock Bowers "should be good to go next week"
summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was limited to 11 snaps on Sunday, due to an ankle injury that knocked him out of the game against the Seahawks.
full_text: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was limited to 11 snaps on Sunday, due to an ankle injury that knocked him out of the game against the Seahawks. Current indications are that Bowers will be back in Week 11. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, the initial assessment was that there seemed to be nothing structural and nothing serious, and that he "should be good to go next week" at the Broncos. The Raiders, who are hanging around the outer fringes of playoff contention at 4-6, could pull themselves into the chase for a wild-card berth. At some point, however, the current 1-6 slide needs to end. Sunday's annual return to Denver provides a perfect opportunity to do that. But it won't be easy; the Broncos are 7-2 and they'll be well rested for the game, given that they were off in Week 10.
author: Mike Florio

title: Travis Hunter now has two games with a catch and an interception. Deion Sanders had nine.
summary: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter intercepted a pass on Sunday against the Titans, and doing his part-time job as a wide receiver, he also caught two passes.
full_text: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter intercepted a pass on Sunday against the Titans, and doing his part-time job as a wide receiver, he also caught two passes. It was the second time Hunter has both caught and intercepted a pass in the same game. That's a rare feat in the modern NFL, where few players play both ways. It's been four years since any player other than Hunter had both a catch and an interception in the same game. The last player to do it was New England's Marcus Jones, who did it twice in 2022. Since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, the player who has had both a catch and an interception in the same game the most times is Hunter's college coach, Deion Sanders, who did it nine times. Sanders did it three times while playing for the Falcons and six times while playing for the Cowboys. Hunter is primarily a defensive player: He played 56 defensive snaps and only six offensive snaps on Sunday, and that's been typical for him this season. Overall in 2026, Hunter has played 84 percent of the Jaguars' defensive snaps and 9 percent of the Jaguars' offensive snaps. But the Jaguars say they view Hunter as a two-way player for the long term, so there's a good chance that he'll have more games with both a catch and an interception, and perhaps eclipse Sanders' modern-era record of nine such games. But Hunter is unlikely to break the all-time record of Packers Hall of Famer Don Hutson, who had 21 games with both a catch and an interception between 1940 and 1945. Hutson had some statistics that don't look possible, such as the game when he outscored the Chicago Cardinals all by himself with six catches for 86 yards and two touchdowns, plus two interceptions for 84 return yards and a pick-six, in a 35-14 Packers victory. Hutson was by far the best receiver of his era and one of the best defensive players of his era, and he was also a pretty good kicker by the standards of the 1940s. There will never be another Don Hutson. What Hunter is doing in 2026, however, is a special accomplishment that also deserves celebration. There's no one else playing the game in quite the same way Hunter is playing it.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Seahawks' team doctor OK after getting hit in the face by a Fernando Mendoza pass
summary: Seahawks team physician Dr.
full_text: Seahawks team physician Dr. Ed Khalfayan took a Fernando Mendoza fastball to the face on Sunday, but he emerged OK. With the Raiders backed up deep in their own territory, Mendoza dropped back into his own end zone and fired a bullet toward the sideline. It sailed out of bounds near the 20-yard line, where Khalfayan was standing on the sideline. Khalfayan didn't see it coming, and it hit him hard in the head. Khalfayan dropped to the ground and for a moment it appeared that he was knocked unconscious, although he was able to get back up quickly. Reporters asked Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald after the game, and Macdonald said the sideline was alarmed by the sight of it. " I was worried about him ," Macdonald said. "That was scary, so we'll check on him. Thanks for asking." Fortunately, Khalfayan told the Seahawks' website he was doing well after the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Macdonald praises Tory Horton's "tremendous play" on late kickoff return
summary: After the Raiders cut the Seahawks' lead to 21-13 by kicking a field goal with 2:04 left in Sunday's game, they wanted to force a touchback that would allow them to use the two-minute warning as a third timeout in hopes of getting the ball back.
full_text: After the Raiders cut the Seahawks' lead to 21-13 by kicking a field goal with 2:04 left in Sunday's game, they wanted to force a touchback that would allow them to use the two-minute warning as a third timeout in hopes of getting the ball back. Seahawks wide receiver Tory Horton made sure that didn't happen. Horton perfectly timed a leap that allowed him to bat a kickoff that was sailing long into the end zone. Horton stepped out of bounds upon coming down, so he motioned for Rashid Shaheed to return it into the field of play and Shaheed was tackled with 1:59 left to accomplish the Seahawks' goal of burning the Raiders' extra chance to stop the clock. Horton was flagged for an illegal bat of the ball, but the Raiders declined the penalty as it would have forced a re-kick that took more time off the clock and head coach Mike Macdonald praised Horton's quick thinking in his postgame press conference. "It was a tremendous play ," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "Tory's actually trying to catch that ball, albeit with one hand. Just an incredible play. With George Holani going down, we had to take [Jadarian Price] off of kickoff returns, so those are guys that haven't necessarily practiced a bunch in a while, especially with this game plan. So to be able to step in and be able to execute some of those critical situations is some great stuff by them, great job by our coaches, and it really helped us close the game out. . . . We told them that was the situation going. Now, there's a difference between catching it 8 yards deep in the end zone and making a play like that, which is just some really, really great stuff." The Seahawks were likely to win the game regardless of how the kickoff played out, but Horton made closing things out easier and his effort will be on the minds of many people around the league if they find themselves in a similar situation.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fernando Mendoza: It's good to learn from getting punched in the face
summary: Fernando Mendoza didn't look overmatched early in his first NFL start, but the road got tougher for the Raiders' rookie quarterback over the final three quarters of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
full_text: Fernando Mendoza didn't look overmatched early in his first NFL start, but the road got tougher for the Raiders' rookie quarterback over the final three quarters of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. Mendoza capped the team's first offensive possession with a touchdown run and led the Raiders to a field goal on their second possession, but the Raiders would pick up just 68 yards and three points over the rest of their 21-13 home loss. Things got particularly bad in the second half as the Raiders failed to pick up a first down while losing 17 yards over their first five post-halftime possessions. Mendoza was sacked six times and hit 12 times over the course of the game, but found a way to put a positive spin on the experience when he spoke to reporters after the game. "The Seahawks have a fantastic defense, we've seen it all season ," Mendoza said, via the team's website. "A lot of credit to them. . . . It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and [become] a future hopeful leader of this offense." The Broncos are next up for the Raiders, which means Mendoza will face another experienced and accomplished defense that could teach him some painful lessons that he uses to steel himself for future success as an NFL quarterback.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jahmyr Gibbs in Hall of Fame company with a long list of statistical achievements
summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had another phenomenal game on Sunday, and in his fourth NFL season he has hit a long list of statistical milestones that only Hall of Famers have reached before him.
full_text: '' Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had another phenomenal game on Sunday, and in his fourth NFL season he has hit a long list of statistical milestones that only Hall of Famers have reached before him. In Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots, Gibbs carried 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns, and added seven catches for 99 yards. After the game, the NFL distributed a list of Gibbs' stats that show him either equaling or exceeding the accomplishments of some of the greatest running backs ever to play the game. Among Gibbs' milestones: Gibbs has the most touchdowns in NFL history in a player's first four seasons. He has now scored 62 touchdowns (50 rushing and 12 receiving), breaking the previous record of Hall of Famer Terrell Davis, who had 61 touchdowns in his first four seasons. Gibbs' 50 career rushing touchdowns make him the third player in NFL history to run for 50 touchdowns before turning 25. The other two are Hall of Famers Barry Sanders with 52, and Emmitt Smith with 50. Gibbs doesn't turn 25 until after this season, so he's a near-lock to move ahead of Sanders and into first place on the all-time list. Gibbs and Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson are the only players in NFL history to have multiple games with at least 250 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns before turning 25. Gibbs, Tomlinson and Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson are the only players to have four games of at least 200 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in their first four seasons. Gibbs has topped 1,200 scrimmage yards and 10 rushing touchdowns in each of his first four seasons. The only players who have done that before are Tomlinson, Dickerson, Hall of Famer Earl Campbell and future Hall of Famer Adrian Peterson. Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown have played 24 games together in which they've both scored touchdowns, surpassing Bills Hall of Famers Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed, who both scored in 23 games, for the fourth-most games in which running back-wide receiver teammates both score. All the players ahead of Gibbs and St. Brown are Hall of Famers: Emmitt Smith and Michael Irvin did it 32 times for the Cowboys, Lenny Moore and Raymond Berry did it 31 times for the Colts, and Edgerrin James and Marvin Harrison did it 25 times for the Colts. Only three and a half seasons into his NFL career, it's too early to put Gibbs in the Hall of Fame. But everything about the way he has played so far indicates that some day he'll have a bust in Canton.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike McCarthy: "That's clearly not to the standard of the Pittsburgh Steelers"
summary: "I was very disappointed. We're all disappointed," McCarthy said after a 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
full_text: ' Steelers coach Mike McCarthy did not mince words about his team's performance in Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals. "That's clearly not to the standard of the Pittsburgh Steelers. It's not to any of our expectations," McCarthy said. "I was very disappointed. We're all disappointed." Heading into the game, the Steelers and Bengals were tied atop the AFC North at 6-2. Now the Bengals have a one-game lead and currently would have the tiebreaker edge over the Steelers as well. The Bengals are now the overwhelming betting favorites to win the division at -600, with the Steelers far behind at +700. But as badly as McCarthy's team played, he said he can't overreact to one game. "It's one loss and it will be dealt with," McCarthy said. "I'm more focused on the details, the fundamentals, and the things we need to do. We're not gonna drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time, it's a waste of energy. We're going to pour our energy into ourselves, looking in the mirror and focusing on the things we can control." The Steelers were not even competitive on Sunday night, and now it's time for McCarthy to search for answers.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sunday Night Football: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase torch Steelers in 38-18 Bengals victory
summary: Burrow threw for 409 yards and four TDs while Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards.
full_text: The Bengals wanted to create a special "white out" environment for Sunday's game, with the home team wearing its "White Bengal" uniform and helmet. After the performance against the Steelers, they may want to make that alternate kit permanent. Quarterback Joe Burrow and receiver Ja'Marr Chase were stellar on Sunday night, with Cincinnati defeating division-rival Pittsburgh 38-18. In just the first half, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns before finishing the contest 35-of-44 for 409 yards with four TDs. Joe Flacco came in for mop-up duty midway through the final period. Burrow also tied Peyton Manning's record streak of five consecutive games of at least four touchdowns . As he often is, Chase was Burrow’s favorite target, catching 11 passes for 231 yards. While Chase didn’t have a touchdown himself, he caught deep bombs of 53 and 43 yards that helped set up scores. It was the third-highest output of Chase’s career and the fourth time he’s gone over 200 yards in a regular-season game. The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions, and would have made it all five if Evan McPherson had hit his 43-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide right. That was McPherson’s first missed kick of the season. But McPherson had opened the scoring with a 24-yard field goal to cap the opening drive. Drew Sample had a 3-yard TD catch, Chase Brown had a 2-yard score, and Dohnte Meyers had a 15-yard touchdown reception to give the Bengals a 24-3 halftime lead. Brown caught his second touchdown in the third quarter to make it 31-3. And Samaje Perine closed the Bengals’ scoring with his 1-yard touchdown run with 10:08 left in the fourth quarter. As well as Cincinnati’s offense played, the defense may have been better. Aaron Rodgers started the contest 0-of-8 passing, with his first completion not coming until there was 4:31 left in the second quarter. Pittsburgh had just four first downs and 40 total yards at halftime. Rodgers ended the night 15-of-29 for 143 yards with two touchdowns, both of which came in the fourth quarter after the game was out of reach. Rodgers was also sacked three times. With the win, the Bengals are now 7-2 on the season and have sole possession of first place in the AFC North. They will have an extra day to prepare, as they’ll face the Commanders next Monday night. The Steelers fall to 6-3 and will be on the road to face the Eagles next Sunday afternoon.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Joe Burrow matches Peyton Manning's record for consecutive games with at least four TDs
summary: Joe Burrow has accomplished something that had not been done for over 20 years.
full_text: Joe Burrow has accomplished something that had not been done for over 20 years. With his 4-yard touchdown to Chase Brown in the third quarter, Burrow became the first since Peyton Manning in 2004 to have at least four total touchdowns in five consecutive games, which is the longest streak in NFL history. That score gave the Bengals a commanding 31-3 lead with 4:12 left in the third period. Burrow has been excellent all season, but that’s particularly been the case on Sunday night. So far, he’s completed 32-of-41 passes for 359 yards with four TDs. The one difference between Manning’s streak and Burrow’s is that Manning did it with all passing touchdowns. Between Weeks 8 and 12 in 2004, Manning threw for five, four, five, four, and six TDs with the Colts. Manning would win his second MVP award for his 2004 season. Burrow has thrown for four, four, five, three, and now four in his last six games. He’s also had a rushing touchdown in each of the last two weeks before Sunday’s matchup against Pittsburgh.
author: Myles Simmons

title: CeeDee Lamb is 96 yards from becoming first Cowboys' player with six straight 1,000-yard seasons
summary: It may not happen today, but it'll happen at some point.
full_text: ' It may not happen today, but it'll happen at some point. Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb, with only 96 receiving yards over the next eight games, will become the first player in franchise history with six straight 1,000-yard receiving seasons. It's an amazing stat, given the great receivers the Cowboys have had — starting with those who, like Lamb, have worn No. 88: Dez Bryant, Michael Irvin, and Drew Pearson, most notably. Tight end Jason Witten had four in six years, with 952 and 942 peppered between them. For the season, Lamb has a league-high 108 targets. He has made 70 catches for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. More importantly, the 4-5 Cowboys have an opportunity to gain ground on the 5-3-1 Giants atop the NFC East. It won't be easy against the 7-1 49ers. Especially since quarterback Dak Prescott has lost his last four starts against the 49ers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deebo Samuel scores on 49ers' first drive for 7-3 lead
summary: Deebo Samuel hadn't played since Oct. 11.
full_text: ' Deebo Samuel hadn't played since Oct. 11. He hadn't scored since Oct. 4. Samuel started and caught a touchdown pass on the 49ers' first drive Sunday. His 11-yard reception started chants of "Dee-bo!" at a red-clad AT&T Stadium. The 49ers lead 7-3. Keenan Allen, acquired in a trade last week, caught a 6-yard pass in the eight-play, 78-yard drive. Brock Purdy went 4-for-4 for 59 yards and the touchdown to Samuel. Kenny Clark sacked Purdy early in the drive, but Caleb Downs was cited for defensive holding. The Cowboys drove 35 yards in eight plays on their opening drive, settling for Brandon Aubrey's 52-yard field goal.
author: Charean Williams

title: George Pickens' TD has Cowboys with a 10-7 lead
summary: George Pickens is back and has his first touchdown since Oct. 26.
full_text: ' George Pickens is back and has his first touchdown since Oct. 26. The Cowboys wide receiver caught a 35-yard touchdown from Dak Prescott, a play after Javonte Williams recovered his own fumble. Pickens, who missed Week 9 with a hamstring injury, has the Cowboys leading 10-7. He has four catches for 51 yards after two possessions. Dak Prescott is 4-for-9 for 51 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys went 71 yards in 11 plays for their touchdown after an eight-play, 35-yard field goal drive. The Cowboys list cornerback DaRon Bland as questionable to return with an ankle injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers lead Cowboys 17-16 at halftime
summary: The 49ers and Cowboys are in a shootout at AT&T Stadium.
full_text: ' The 49ers and Cowboys are in a shootout at AT&T Stadium. In an entertaining first half, the difference is an extra point. Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed one, giving the 49ers a 17-16 halftime lead. Christian McCaffrey scored on a 74-yard catch-and-run touchdown after Brock Purdy rolled to his right to buy time. Eddy Pineiro's PAT gave San Francisco a lead with 2:26 remaining in the first half. The 49ers' other points came on Deebo Samuel's 11-yard touchdown catch and Pineiro's 28-yard field goal. The 49ers outgained the Cowboys 244 to 165, with Purdy going 12-of-17 for 217 yards and two touchdowns. McCaffrey has two catches for 81 yards and a touchdown and eight rushes for 21 yards. The 49ers can't cover George Pickens, who returned from a one-game absence with a hamstring injury and has touchdowns of 35 and 39 yards. He has six catches for 97 yards. Dak Prescott is 7-for-17 for 104 yards and two touchdowns, with Ryan Flournoy having the only other catch besides Pickens' six. Aubrey kicked a 52-yard field goal on the team's first drive.
author: Charean Williams

title: Deebo Samuel's 70-yard TD run gives 49ers 31-19 lead
summary: Welcome back, Deebo Samuel.
full_text: ' Welcome back, Deebo Samuel. The 49ers have missed you. The wide receiver, who hadn't played since Oct. 11, scored his second touchdown. His first came on an 11-yard reception. His second came on a reverse. Quarterback Brock Purdy flipped to Kaelon Black, who was running right, and the running back flipped it to Samuel running left. Trent Williams and Purdy were among the caravan of blockers Samuel had in front of him. The 49ers lead 31-19 with 6:59 remaining in the third quarter. Samuel has three carries for 78 yards and two catches for 22 yards. The Cowboys also allowed Christian McCaffrey to score on a 74-yard catch-and-run in the first half. The 49ers have 405 yards. It is the 17th consecutive game the Cowboys have allowed at least 20 points.
author: Charean Williams

title: Christian McCaffrey, 49ers run past Cowboys 46-40
summary: The 49ers had 584 yards, the third-most the Cowboys have allowed in their history.
full_text: ' 49ers fans took over AT&T Stadium on Sunday, out-drawing and out-yelling Cowboys fans. They booed the Cowboys running onto their own field, and they loudly celebrated a 46-40 San Francisco win. In an entertaining game, the 49ers moved to 8-1, and the Cowboys fell to 4-6. Christian McCaffrey had a career-high 161 receiving yards on four catches, two of them touchdowns, and ran for 62 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown. The 49ers led 38-19 with 11:26 remaining in the fourth quarter. But George Pickens caught a 5-yard touchdown pass, which was followed by a missed 2-point conversion. Ryan Flournoy's 11-yard score with 3:42 left cut the Cowboys' deficit to 38-32. The 49ers burned only 2:26 on their possession in between, punting after four plays. The 49ers showed the Cowboys who they are, though, when Brock Purdy hit McCaffrey across the middle of the field. Von Miller, who was covering McCaffrey, and his teammates had no chance of catching the running back, who went 66 yards to the end zone. The Cowboys didn't go away quietly, scoring once more on CeeDee Lamb's 1-yard reception. Dak Prescott ran in the 2-point conversion. Dallas tried an onside kick despite having three timeouts and did not convert. Kaelon Black, who had 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled on the second-down play. Quinnen Williams forced it, but Black was able to get back on the ball. The 49ers punted, and the Cowboys were left with only 9 seconds and in need of 91 yards and a miracle. They didn't get it. McCaffrey's other touchdowns were a 74-yard reception and a 16-yard run. The 49ers had 584 yards, the third-most the Cowboys have allowed in their history. It was not far from the 49ers' team record of 621. Purdy set a career-high with 389 passing yards and threw three touchdowns, completing 22 of 28 passes. George Kittle had six catches for 74 yards, and new addition Keenan Allen five for 61. Deebo Samuel had three catches for 31 yards and a touchdown and three carries for 78 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys couldn't keep up, even with 439 yards. Prescott was 30-of-51 for 343 yards with five touchdowns and an interception. Pickens had 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns, and Lamb seven for 72 yards and a touchdown. Flournoy added six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown.

title: Christian McCaffrey on career-high receiving yards: You just catch it and run as fast as you can
summary: Christian McCaffrey had a day.
full_text: ' Christian McCaffrey had a day. The 49ers running back had never had more than 121 receiving yards in a single game. He had 161 receiving yards on four catches Sunday against the Cowboys, scoring on catch-and-runs of 74 and 66 in the 49ers' 46-40 win. "You never know," McCaffrey said. "You go into each game. You don't really predict anything. Again, you just have to have the right mindset on a play that's going to break. You trust your instincts and play fast." His first receiving touchdown came when Brock Purdy rolled to his right to buy time and found McCaffrey running free on the scramble drill. "It really is backyard football at that point," McCaffrey said. "We all played it as kids at recess, and you draw up plays on your hand, and it never happens. You ever tell a 5-year-old to run a post route, and he just runs a corner and something else, but he's open? That's kind of what that was. Again, I think those little decisions that you make in games, from Brock to scramble, not to just surrender the play but to keep it alive. That's a big deal. There's no planning that goes into that. It's just him doing a great job playing ball." What turned out to be the game-winning touchdown came with 3:23 remaining when Purdy found McCaffrey, who was matched up against Von Miller, over the middle. "They brought pressure," McCaffrey said. "They dropped a D-end on me, so that's a perfect look for that play. Again, it was a great job by Brock getting the ball where it needed to be. It made it easy for me. "You just catch it and run as fast as you can to try to score. Don't overthink it. You hope that nobody catches you, and you hope that you're really fast so your teammates don't catch up to you to celebrate, because it makes you look slow. We'll have to check the tape." McCaffrey had a 16-yard touchdown run and 62 yards rushing. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown.

title: Dak Prescott: 49ers fans "were more present than ours"
summary: On Sunday, America's Team wasn't even Dallas's Team. 49ers fans showed up in big numbers for the game against the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
full_text: ' On Sunday, America's Team wasn't even Dallas's Team. 49ers fans showed up in big numbers for the game against the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. After the game, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott was asked whether the home team had to use the silent count. "No, we didn't go on the silent count," Prescott said. "[We] anticipated it. I think y'all even potentially asked me on Thursday about it, having this many 49er fans there. Tricked myself and told myself early on that the red was for my high school. "And at the end of the day, all I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours, but it created a great atmosphere. So, we take the good out of it one way or another." For owner Jerry Jones, the colors worn by the fans don't matter; their money is the same shade of green. Still, it's always a bad look when too many fans of the opposing team show up for a road game. On Sunday, 49ers fans found their way to buy tickets and infiltrate the venue. And their fans got to see the Niners move to 8-1 on the season.

title: Joe Burrow strengthens MVP case with four more TDs; college football rankings projections
summary: Plus why Kayla Harrison should retire after UFC 334
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The nationwide ground stop the FAA issued Friday could not have come at a more disruptive time for football teams since it was a travel day for numerous squads. The NFL schedule went off without a hitch save for some referee reassignments and a rare instance in which four officials worked multiple games in one day . Travel hiccups were much more defined in the college game and impacted countless games , some of which were delayed multiple hours to accommodate teams' late arrivals.
Of the 14 highest-profile games that featured programs which experienced travel issues, those teams went 9-5 , so it's hard to say the flight disruptions were to blame for any poor play.
The biggest snag came in the matchup between Ole Miss and Oklahoma . A handful of challenges including a timed-out flight crew and a small airport left the Rebels grounded until Saturday and led the SEC to push the game to Sunday.
The conference's decision was highly unpopular among Oklahoma stakeholders. Sooners athletic director Roger Denny put the league on blast for forcing his program to comply with the schedule change. Legendary former Sooners coach Bob Stoops chimed in with his own criticism of commissioner Greg Sankey .
In the end, the Sooners pulled off a 24-17 win anyway. Their revitalized offense controlled the game flow in a victory over a ranked opponent and provided proof of concept that Jason Witten could be the answer as the team's potential full-time offensive coordinator. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott even said Witten could be an NFL coach .
LSU 's last chance to secure a resume-building win was dashed by Texas . The Tigers led by as many as 11 points in a marquee matchup and were two seconds away from closing it out when Arch Manning connected with Raleek Brown on a game-winning swing pass for the Longhorns . From the Tigers' standpoint, it was the most devastating loss for a CFP bubble team in Week 11 and another stain on Lane Kiffin 's young tenure. He was the biggest individual loser of the week .
Manning's heroics came in another clutch moment for college football's most polarizing quarterback , who relished in the fact that his team dealt the decisive blow to LSU's playoff hopes . On the opposing sideline, Kiffin watched his championship expectations come crumbling down in that moment. Our Chris Hummer was on site to tell the story.
In the Big Ten, Indiana has a quarterback controversy. Seventh-year senior Grant Wilson might just be the key to the Hoosiers' search for a second consecutive national championship, not Josh Hoover , the expensive transfer they brought in to lead them back to glory. Wilson guided Indiana to a 27-13 win over USC and left Lincoln Riley to tell the same old story to Trojans fans.
In the ACC, Miami turned in a "B" performance in its second game without Malachi Toney , and Wake Forest obliterated SMU in a statement game .
Week 11 also dialed up the heat on the hot seat . For now, the pressure is off Deion Sanders . He orchestrated Colorado 's first top-15 win since 2007 in a stunner against Houston . Dabo Swinney , on the other hand, reached a new low . Clemson has now lost nine of its last 11 home games against Power Four opponents.

title: Drake Maye injury update: Patriots reportedly fear QB fractured ankle, could miss rest of season
summary: Maye remained in Germany for additional testing after injuring his ankle against the Lions
full_text:
The New England Patriots may have to finish the 2026 season without their franchise centerpiece. Quarterback Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a significant lower-leg injury that is poised to sideline him for an extended period of time, according ESPN . The report notes that the injury has the potential to keep Maye out for the remainder of the year. Specifically, ESPN reports that the team fears Maye fractured his ankle.
Maye suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of New England's opening drive against the Detroit Lions during their Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany. The third-year quarterback was sacked by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a third-and-goal play and was in noticeable discomfort after the hit. After being looked at on the sideline, Maye gingerly walked to the locker room where he was eventually ruled out with what the team called an ankle injury.
Immediately after the game, coach Mike Vrabel didn't have much of an update on Maye's status. However, Vrabel told WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday morning that Maye stayed back in Germany.
"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,' Vrabel said, via the Boston Herald . "He'll be traveling back here shortly. But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries, and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."
Given that Maye was unable to travel back with the team following the international contest, this lends credence to this latest report on the severity of the injury. ESPN's report highlights that Maye stayed in Germany to undergo additional tests to determine whether he needs surgery.
Maye -- along with the entire Patriots team -- has come back down to earth a bit in 2026 following his MVP runner-up season last year as New England made a surprise Super Bowl run. Through 10 games, Maye was 5-5 as the starter, completed 65.6% of his passes, averaged 233.0 passing yards per game, and threw for 18 touchdowns. He's also thrown 11 interceptions, which are already a career high.
Of course, it's never a good time for your franchise quarterback to endure a potential season-ending injury, but Maye going down comes at a critical juncture of New England's season. The club is reeling after losing three of its last four games, dropping it back to .500 on the season.
This latest loss to Detroit pushes them further behind the Buffalo Bills (8-1) in the AFC East race, and they are now on the outside looking in on the AFC playoff picture. Coming into Week 10, they were slotted as the No. 7 seed, but are now sitting as the No. 8 seed and looking up to the Cleveland Browns (6-4), Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3), and Denver Broncos (7-2) for the three wild card spots.
The Patriots will have the bye to collect themselves in Week 11, but the road ahead doesn't get any easier, particularly in December, when they'll face the Bills, Vikings , and Chiefs (road) over a three-week span. Not having Maye for those matchups would make New England significant underdogs, even with two of those games at Gillette Stadium.
With Maye on the shelf, the Patriots will first turn to top backup Tommy DeVito . He stepped in during their contest with Detroit in Germany on Sunday. In that game, DeVito put up less-than-stellar numbers, completing 12-of-24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He also rushed four times for 19 yards on the ground.
DeVito has been with New England for the past two seasons after being claimed off waivers in August of 2025 following his release from the New York Giants . Last offseason, he signed a two-year, $7.4 million extension with the team and became the primary back to Maye entering 2026.
The 28-year-old has starting experience, having logged eight starts over his career since entering the NFL in 2023 as an undrafted free agent out of Illinois. DeVito is 3-5 over those starts and has a 63.4% completion percentage to go along with an 84.6 passer rating for his career.

title: NFL Week 11 early odds: Bills, Chiefs favored by 16.5 points; Bengals line jumps after blowout
summary: Buffalo and Kansas City are each favored by 16.5 points as four teams enter Week 11 laying double digits
full_text:
Week 11 is one of the smallest slates that we'll have during the 2026 season. With six teams on the bye, that leaves us with just 13 games on the docket next week. While small, the slate packs a punch with several heavy favorites. In all, there are four double-digit favorites in Week 11, two of which are above two touchdowns.
The Buffalo Bills are one of those favorites, opening as a 16.5-point favorite over the Miami Dolphins when they host their AFC East rival. Meanwhile, the Kansas City Chiefs are also laying 16.5 points after initially opening as a 14-point favorite at home against the Arizona Cardinals . These are true David vs. Goliath matchups, but it'll be fascinating to see how the public feels about laying such massive numbers, even with both Buffalo and Kansas City 3-1 ATS at home.
Those are just a couple of early lines that we'll sink our teeth into. Below, we're diving into all of the early lines for Week 11 and seeing who the oddsmakers project coming out on top.
Note : Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, Los Angeles ( Rams ), New England, and Seattle are on the bye in Week 11.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Colts at Texans (Thursday)
Dolphins +900, Bills -1587
Steelers -198, Eagles +164
Ravens +110, Panthers -130
Cardinals +850, Chiefs -1449
Buccaneers +195, Lions -238

Despite these teams coming out on opposite ends of the scorecard on Sunday, it hasn't disrupted the line for this divisional matchup. Despite falling to 3-6 with a loss to the Browns , Houston is a 10-point favorite at home over the Colts. The Texans are 3-6 ATS and are still looking for their first ATS win at home (0-4). Indianapolis is 2-2 ATS on the road. When it comes to the 44.5 total, the Over is 12-7 between these two this season.
Buffalo is a huge favorite at home as they host the Dolphins, with the line opening at 16.5. The Bills are tied for an NFL-best 7-2 ATS record, and their average margin of victory sits at 9.8 (third-best in the NFL ). That figure is even better at home, as they own a 10.8 average margin of victory and are 3-1 ATS at Highmark Stadium. As for the Dolphins, they've been a solid bet on the road, coming into Week 11 with a 3-2 ATS record away from Hard Rock Stadium. The Over is 10-8 between them.
Chicago is emerging from its bye as a 10-point favorite, which is up from the 9.5 points they were laying at the open. The Bears are 6-3 ATS so far in 2026, which includes a 3-2 ATS mark at Soldier Field. While the Saints fell to the Panthers at the Superdome, they've fared much better on the road for bettors. New Orleans is a perfect 3-0 ATS as the away team. They are the only team in the NFL without an ATS road loss so far.
Pittsburgh opened as a 4.5-point favorite on the road against the Eagles, who were on the bye in Week 10. Philadelphia is 0-5 ATS at home this season, and four of those ATS defeats have come as a home underdog. The Steelers are 1-1 ATS as a road favorite.
Carolina is up to a 2.5-point favorite after initially opening as a 1.5-point favorite at home as they face the Ravens. Baltimore still has its Week 10 matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, so this line could see some movement depending on how that game unfolds. That said, the Ravens playing on a short week is a tough turn of events. This season, Baltimore is 0-2 ATS when at a rest disadvantage. Carolina will hope that continues as they look to improve their 1-3 ATS record at home.
Kansas City has jumped out as a 16.5-point favorite after this line first opened at -14 when they host the Cardinals. The Chiefs are coming off a dominant win over the Falcons , in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdowns. They head back to Arrowhead Stadium where they are 3-1 ATS and have an average margin of victory of 15.8 (second-best in the NFL). Arizona is 4-2 ATS on the road.
The Lions are now a 5.5-point favorite at Ford Field after initially opening as a 6-point favorite over the Buccaneers. That could be due to a couple of factors, including star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffering a serious knee injury in the win over the Patriots in Germany. Speaking of Germany, Detroit will also be at a disadvantage in rest. As they come off the international game, the Bucs are coming out of their bye week. The Lions are 1-2-1 ATS at home this season, while Tampa Bay is 3-1 ATS on the road.
Dallas is a 7.5-point favorite as they host the Titans and look to bounce back following a loss to the 49ers on Sunday. AT&T Stadium hasn't been kind to Dallas so far this season, as the team is 1-3 ATS at home. That'll be tested against a Tennessee team that is 3-1 ATS on the road. Points are expected in bunches in this game as well, as the total has jumped to 53.5 after opening at 51.5. The Over is 3-1 in Cowboys home games so far in 2026.
The Chargers opened as a field goal over the Jets. New York may have some questions at quarterback for this game after Geno Smith was unable to finish Sunday's loss to Buffalo due to injury. If he cannot go, Cade Klubnik , who came in under duress for Smith on Sunday, would get the start. If/when that becomes official, this line could move even more. On top of that, this line could move depending on how Los Angeles' game against the Ravens on Monday night goes. The Jets are 4-5-1 ATS, which includes a 2-2-1 ATS record on the road.
Denver is a 9.5-point favorite as they come out of their bye week and gear up to host Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders. That's up from the 8.5 points they were laying at the open. The Raiders are 3-2 ATS on the road this season, but 0-1 ATS so far in the Mendoza era after failing to cover at home against the Seahawks . Meanwhile, Denver is a perfect 4-0 ATS at Mile High.
Jacksonville has opened as a 6-point favorite. The Giants will have a rest advantage after playing on Thursday, but the Jaguars have been one of the season's juggernauts so far. They are 6-3 ATS on the year, which includes a 3-1 ATS record on the road (2-0 ATS as away favorite). New York is 3-2 ATS at home (2-1 ATS as a home underdog). The total is up to 46.5, up from 44.5 at the open.
The NFL heads outside of the country yet again as the Vikings and 49ers will square off in Mexico City. On this neutral site, the 49ers are a 3-point favorite after initially opening as a 3.5-point favorite. That movement towards the Vikings could be faith in the offense now that Kirk Cousins is at quarterback. The Niners are 5-3 ATS, while the Vikings are 5-4 ATS on the year. The total is down to 45.5 after opening at 46.5. The Under is 8-1 in Vikings games.
Cincinnati is up to a 3.5-point favorite after opening as a 1.5-point favorite on the road against the Commanders. Washington is 2-2 ATS at home, which includes a 1-1 ATS record as a home underdog. The Bengals are 2-2 ATS on the road, but 1-2 ATS as a road favorite. The total is also down to 51.5, having opened at 52.5.
