title: Steelers' receiver problem proves they made a massive NFL trade deadline mistake
summary: Pittsburgh declined to add a receiver at the trade deadline, leaving Aaron Rodgers without the help he needed
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers lost Sunday night's game to the Cincinnati Bengals days before the game even started. OK, that might be a stretch. But the Steelers' decision not to acquire a receiver before the trade deadline has aged faster than milk on a hot summer day.
Hours after Josh Downs -- whom the Steelers were reportedly interested in acquiring before the deadline -- scored a touchdown in his Kansas City Chiefs debut, Pittsburgh fans were forced to sit through another game of watching DK Metcalf play dodgeball and Aaron Rodgers desperately looking for Jaylen Warren in the flat with no open options downfield.
Rodgers did not complete a pass until late in the first half. At that point, it was already 17-0 Bengals, a lead that swelled to 24-3 before intermission. It was 31-3 in the third before the Steelers finally found the end zone early in the fourth quarter. Ironically, the score was courtesy of Metcalf, but it was way too little, too late. Pittsburgh later tacked on another late score in garbage time in what was a 38-18 loss.
There was plenty of evidence before the deadline that the Steelers needed help at receiver. Metcalf entered Sunday with just one touchdown and only 33 catches on 64 targets. Germie Bernard has played well for a rookie, but he's not a No. 2 receiver, at least not now.
Despite their lack of weaponry, the Steelers were 6-2 heading into their bye week, which coincided with the trade deadline. Pittsburgh reportedly discussed trades involving Downs, Brian Thomas Jr. , and Calvin Ridley . Thomas and Ridley were not traded, but Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick were sent to Kansas City in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks. A very reasonable trade that the Steelers should have tried to make.
There are two likely reasons why the Steelers didn't trade for a receiver. Pittsburgh probably didn't want to give up too many future draft picks that could be used to acquire its next franchise quarterback, and it still has confidence in its receiving corps.
Let's address the second reason first. Pittsburgh had an eight-game sample size to assess their situation at receiver. It was clear before the deadline that reinforcements were needed, even with the prospect of Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman 's possible returns from injuries (Pittman, an expensive offseason acquisition, has seven catches this season and hasn't played since Week 4).
Regarding future draft picks, that's the price the Steelers continue to pay for not having found their long-term solution at quarterback. The Steelers have three other quarterbacks on their roster (including rookie Drew Allar ), so there's a good chance that Pittsburgh won't spend a high pick on a quarterback in 2027, anyway. Pittsburgh's current 2026 projection suggests they won't have a high draft pick again. That has been an ongoing issue for a team that still hasn't found Ben Roethlisberger's long-term successor.
Regardless of the reason, the Steelers' lack of movement at the deadline raises the following question: what was the point of bringing back Rodgers? If the Steelers were serious about maximizing their strong start (like the Chiefs and Jaguars did) in Rodgers' final season, they would have gotten a receiver at the deadline, among other things. Instead, the Steelers stood pat and were blown out on Sunday night by a Bengals team that moved past them for first place in the AFC North.
Pittsburgh's situation at receiver is a mess, but that's not its only issue. The defense was a disaster on Sunday night. They had no answer for Joe Burrow , who sliced and diced Pittsburgh's zone coverage.
Cincinnati, winners of five straight games, appears to be not only the front-runner to win the North, but possibly the entire AFC. Conversely, the Steelers are a decent team that has benefitted from an easy schedule.
Pittsburgh faces only two teams with winning records from here on out, so it's very possible that the Steelers can get to 10 wins for a fourth straight season. That's far from a guarantee, however. The Steelers suffered a serious loss Sunday night when guard Mason McCormick was carted off the field in the second quarter. While the severity of his injury wasn't immediately known, it appears that Pittsburgh will have to move forward without him.
Even if the Steelers reach 10 wins and earn a fourth straight playoff berth, their season appears headed for a disappointing finish. Rodgers deserved better than that in his final season.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Aidan Hutchinson injury: Lions star joins bizarre list of NFL players hurt while celebrating
summary: Aidan Hutchinson's sack celebration ended with a significant knee injury, recalling some of the strangest and most painful mishaps in NFL history
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' win in Germany came at a high cost. Lions' talented pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a "significant" knee injury in the first quarter that was sustained during his post-sack celebration.
Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF
Despite Hutchinson's absence, Detroit rolled to a 35-10 win over the Patriots . The Lions received a big game from Hutchinson's backup, rookie Derrick Moore , who had two of Detroit's five sacks.
Hutchinson has joined the list of NFL players who have sustained injuries after celebrating. Here's a look at some of the others.
Greenlaw wasn't celebrating, but he joins the conversation because his injury occurred on a non-contact play during the Super Bowl . The 49ers ' linebacker was enthusiastically jumping in place before he tore his Achilles as he was in the process of jogging back on the field.
Dre Greenlaw appeared to injure himself jogging back onto the field pic.twitter.com/p3nwmTUsfO
The 49ers ultimately lost to the Chiefs in the second Super Bowl, which was decided in overtime. Greenlaw missed most of the following season while recovering from the injury.
Houston tore his ACL after celebrating his sack of Jimmy Garoppolo near the end of Chicago's blowout loss to New England in Week 8 of the 2014 season. Houston, who had signed a big contract before the start of that season, apologized to his teammates the following day.
THROWBACK: Lamar Houston tears his ACL celebrating a sack with Chicago trailing by 3 touchdowns pic.twitter.com/rXcsgAPKlc
Houston moved from defensive end to linebacker the following season and recorded a career-high 8.0 sacks. His last season was in 2017.
Five weeks prior to Houston's incident, Tulloch tore his ACL after celebrating a sack of Aaron Rodgers . In just the season's third week, Tulloch was lost for the season.
Former Detroit Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch tore his ACL in his left knee in 2014 while doing a similar celebration. https://t.co/TYxFD2PPRr pic.twitter.com/fOZUR95F5d
Tulloch returned from the injury and had 107 tackles, a forced fumble and two fumble recoveries in 2015. In 2016, he appeared in just 12 games for the Eagles in what was ultimately his final NFL season.
Gramatica tore his ACL after celebrating a 42-yard field goal during the first quarter of a Week 14 game against the Giants .
At the time, no one knew the seriousness of Gramatica's injury. Iconic Cardinals safety Pat Tillman handled the kickoffs for the remainder of the game, and Gramatica hit a short field goal and a point-after attempt in Arizona's eventual 17-13 loss.
Gramatica missed the remainder of the 2001 season. His replacement, Cedric Oglesby, made five field goals on six attempts. Those were Oglesby's only NFL regular season appearances.
Haven’t seen a worse Celebration injury since Gramatica! Prayers up for Aiden Hutchinson! pic.twitter.com/SwJDNA9wpU
A rookie at the time, Gramatica played four seasons in the NFL. He clarified the cause of his injury during a 2010 interview.
"You guys got it wrong," Gramatica said at the time . "You said I got hurt jumping. My jump was excellent. It was my landing I needed to work on. It was funny. It was part of my career. I talk about it all the time. You have to laugh about it."
Maybe the most infamous celebratory injury in NFL history. In Week 13 of the 1997 season, Frerotte -- a Pro Bowler the previous season -- suffered a sprained neck and a concussion after headbutting a padded cement wall after a short touchdown run against the Giants late in the first half.
With Aiden Hutchinson’s celebration injury, couldn’t help but think about Gus Ferrote concussing himself by headbutting the wall 😅 pic.twitter.com/i4HjiKB0EJ
Frerotte returned for Washington's next possession, but he was replaced in the second half by veteran backup (and former Giants Super Bowl-winning quarterback) Jeff Hostetler. Washington's offense didn't score another point and had to settle for a 7-7 tie.
Frerotte played a week later and sustained a season-ending hip injury. With Hostetler back under center, Washington won two of its last three games but missed the playoffs with an 8-7-1 record.
Frerotte played another decade in the NFL, but he never matched the level of success he had enjoyed prior to his injury against the Giants.
"You know, it didn't define me, and it still doesn't define me," he said back in 2017 . "And that's what's great. I think if I didn't laugh about it, I wouldn't have been able to go on and play another 10 years after that."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Ravens vs. Chargers: Can LA get its first win on 'MNF' against the injury-plagued Ravens?
summary: Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup
full_text:
In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers .
Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently-acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley .
Los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season.
Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes.
Justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston , Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options.
Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton , Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries — an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry.
Other than all that, though, things are going really well!
That said, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change.
It's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago.
We know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling.
We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson , but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns . The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers , and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here.
Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside.
Still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry , so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle.
Henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season.
The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to big plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews .
I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board.
Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20
author: Jared Dubin

title: Bengals' blowout win over Steelers makes NFL history with 1,100th 'scorigami'
summary: Cincinnati's 38-18 victory became the 1,100th unique final score in NFL history
full_text:
It took 107 years, but the NFL has finally produced its 1,100th final score of all time, and it came on Sunday night in Cincinnati. In an AFC North showdown, the Bengals topped the Steelers 38-18, marking the first time that a game ended with that exact final score.
The scorigami only happened because the Steelers scored a garbage-time touchdown in the fourth quarter. With Pittsburgh trailing 38-11, Aaron Rodgers threw a 27-yard TD pass to Pat Freiermuth , and at that point, the Steelers could have gone for two, but instead, they decided to kick the extra point. If the kick had missed, there wouldn't have been a scorigami, because 38-17 has happened before, but Boswell's kick went through and that ultimately gave us the 1,100th final score in NFL history.
PIT 18 - CIN 38 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1100th unique score in NFL history, and the 5th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/jIo0wxFPxX
For a game to end in a scorigami, you need a few bizarre things to happen and the Steelers definitely provided those.
With the Bengals leading 31-3 in the fourth quarter, the Steelers scored a touchdown and decided to go for two, even though it didn't make much sense at that point. They ended up getting the two-point conversion, bringing the score to 38-11. Surprisingly, that final score has actually happened before, so the scorigami didn't become official until Freiermuth got his touchdown later in the fourth quarter. On the second touchdown, the Steelers did NOT go for two, which was a bit bizarre considering they had gone for two on their first score.
The Bengals did their part of the scorigami by lighting up the scoreboard at Paycor Stadium. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns to help the Bengals get to 38 points.
The Bengals actually had a missed field goal in the game from Evan McPherson and if that would have gone in, we also would have gotten a scorigami, because 41-18 has never happened before in NFL history. The missed kick ended McPherson's franchise-record streak for 25 consecutive field goals.
When it comes to scorigamis, the Bengals are the hottest team in the NFL right. This is the second straight home game where they've had a scorigami. Before Sunday night, their last home game came in a 43-36 win over the Titans that gave us the 1,098th different final score in NFL history .
As for the Steelers, this marks the first time they've been involved in a scorigami since a 48-37 playoff loss to the Browns back in January 2021.
This turned out to be a banner week for scorigamis. Not only did the Bengals and Steelers give us a new final score, but the 49ers ' 46-40 win over the Cowboys was also a scorigami .
This actually marks the second time this season that we've had two scorigamis in one day. It also happened back in Week 1 . And I already know what your next question is: This marks the first time since 2017 that we've had two scorigamis in one day happen TWICE in the same season.
Overall, there have been five scorigamis this year, tied for the most in the 2025 season. Basically, this is turning into the year of the scorigami.
author: John Breech

title: Cover 32: Two NFL awards already in the bag, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 10
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all of the biggest items from Week 10 in the NFL, including a historic day from Jahmyr Gibbs and statement return to Minnesota for Kirk Cousins
full_text:
In lockstep with Week 10 kicking off, the second half of the regular season is underway. Naturally, there's going to be plenty of twists and turns as we barrel down the stretch run. Teams will jockey for playoff positioning while players and coaches look to put themselves in contention for awards such as MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and more. When it comes to awards, two are already in the bag.
Even with seven weeks left to go in the regular season, I'm ready to call two awards right now:
What we saw from both of them in Week 10 only bolsters their case, if not outright putting the final nail in the coffin to eventually go home with the awards when we get to the NFL Honors during Super Bowl week.
When it comes to Monken, who opened at +1400 to win the award at DraftKings Sportsbook , he has remarkably put the Browns in the AFC playoff picture after jumping out to a 6-4 record. That record includes a 4-0 mark at home, the first time the franchise has done so since 1963.
He's also coached through some tightly contested games. In fact, Monken's Browns are the first team in NFL history to have their first six wins each come by four points or less. To his credit, Monken named Deshaun Watson the starter this summer, which is a move that has borne fruit. Watson has been solid this season, notching six game-winning drives. He's also thrown for at least 300 yards in each of his past three games, making him just the third Browns quarterback to do so.
Sunday's win over the Texans also inched Cleveland closer to securing a playoff spot. Even as they entered Week 10 with a 3-5 record, Houston was a dark horse to possibly oust the Browns from a playoff spot. However, after knocking them down to 3-6 and claiming the head-to-head tiebreaker, they've largely killed that possibility in its crib.
BROWNS WIN pic.twitter.com/mQGRiqo4mM
Moreover, when you look at the rest of the competition in the wild card race, there's not much to speak of.
The Ravens (4-5 before Monday night) are starting a backup after Lamar Jackson went down with a fractured right thumb. Meanwhile, the Patriots (5-5) could be starting a backup for the foreseeable future depending on the severity of Drake Maye's ankle injury. Then, you have the Raiders , who are 4-6 and are working in a rookie quarterback. The Browns host Las Vegas in Week 12 following their bye week, putting themselves in a strong position to pick up yet another key head-to-head tiebreaker.
The path is quite clear for them to secure a wild card spot. If/when that happens, Monken is the runaway favorite for Coach of the Year. Right now, he's +370 at DraftKings Sportsbook, tied with John Harbaugh for the second-best odds, as they both look up to Kyle Shanahan (+300). The smart money should be on Monken.
As for Mahomes, he was the favorite to win Comeback Player of the Year from the jump, but was still +185 to win i t at the start of the season. While they were short odds at the time, getting it at plus money feels like stealing right now.
After suffering a torn ACL and LCL last season, Mahomes has come back and helped Kansas City to a 7-2 record. Prior to Sunday, Mahomes largely managed games and leaned on the likes of Kenneth Walker III for the burst on offense. Week 10 was a different animal, however. Mahomes exploded for 348 passing yards and five passing touchdowns in a dominant win over the Falcons .
MAHOMES FIVE TOUCHDOWN PASSES 🔥 pic.twitter.com/G1ZClQomml
This was Mahomes' first game with at least five passing touchdowns since Week 1 of the 2022 season.
Sunday's win put Kansas City back atop the AFC West and in prime position to return to the playoffs in some capacity after a one-year absence in 2025. All that has Mahomes as a shoo-in to win Comeback Player of the Year.
So, even though we have plenty of time before these awards are handed out, you can start engraving COY and CPOY now.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Gibbs was a man amongst boys in Detroit's Week 10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He finished with 252 yards from scrimmage, which were the second-most in a game in his career. It was also the second-most scrimmage yards in an international game all-time. Moreover, his 28-yard touchdown run (his second of the day) was his 62nd of his career, which is the most by any player in his four seasons in NFL history.
Penei leads the way for another Jahmyr Gibbs tuddy! pic.twitter.com/EuBi7Y2U4c
Jacksonville continues to roll and moved to 7-2 after a 40-23 win over Tennessee. Amid the winning effort, Parker Washington dazzled with some circus catches en route to 152 receiving yards for the day. That set a new career high for the Jags wideout. Dating back to last season, Washington has tallied 992 receiving yards over his last 12 games. That's the most in a 12-game span by a Jaguars player since 2015.
Parker Washington or Peter Parker? JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/l02kcfOngG
Chase may not have found the end zone, but he was the catalyst for the Bengals offense in a dominant win over the Steelers. The Cincinnati wideout hauled in 11 of his 14 targets for 231 yards. This marks the third time in Chase's career that he's recorded at least 10 catches and 225 receiving yards in a game, which is tied for the most in NFL history.
Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3
Kenneth Walker III, who? The Chiefs rookie back filled the shoes of the star back perfectly as he was inactive for Week 10 due to a groin injury. If you didn't look too hard, it was hard to tell the difference between Johnson and Walker in this game. The fifth-round pick out of Nebraska erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and was a key outlet for Mahomes in the passing game, particularly in the red zone. Johnson became just the second player since 1970 with at least 100 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in his first career start.
Emmett Johnson is too quick 💨 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/sY1oGo45zY
Hubbard was the straw that stirred the drink of the Panthers offense as they outlasted the Saints in New Orleans. The veteran back accounted for both of Carolina's touchdowns and led the team in rushing as well as receiving. He's just the second player in franchise history to have at least 80 yards rushing and receiving and two rushing touchdowns in a single game, joining Christian McCaffrey (twice). Hubbard helped the Panthers notch their first road win against the Saints since 2023.
Chuba Hubbard for the lead with 1:49 to play! CARvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H1nYzGJl8G
McCaffrey became the first running back in NFL history with two 65-yard touchdown receptions in a game. The 49ers back was doing it all as San Francisco fended off the Cowboys in Dallas to move to 7-1 on the season. Amid a 21-point fourth quarter by the Cowboys, McCaffrey helped keep them at bay with two touchdowns of his own. The final was a 66-yard catch-and-run that proved to be the dagger.
Don't leave CMC in the open field 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/hGnsBSY5V5
Aidan Hutchinson has reportedly suffered a serious knee injury that could knock him out for the foreseeable future. To make matters worse, the injury didn't even come during a play. Instead, Hutchinson was celebrating a third-down sack of Drake Maye during Detroit's opening defensive possession of the afternoon in Germany. After taking down the Patriots quarterback, Hutchinson leaped in the air and then came down awkwardly on his knee.
The Lions have ruled out star DE Aidan Hutchinson for the game with a knee injury. pic.twitter.com/jR365USNf2
He limped off the field and into the locker room before being ruled out for the rest of the game. Now, it appears that the rest of his season could be in jeopardy.
One of the dagger moments of Minnesota's victory…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 10 grades: Packers fail in showdown with Vikings, Patrick Mahomes catches fire
summary: We're handing out grades for every team that played in Week 10
full_text:
Welcome to the Week 10 grades!
It was a day of statement wins around the NFL and the biggest statement was made by the Minnesota Vikings .
In their first game since trading for Kirk Cousins , the Vikings pounded the Packers 30-10, and the impressive part is that they did that at Lambeau Field. Combined with their 39-22 win in Week 1, they became the first team since 1987 to beat the Packers by at least 17 points twice in a season.
Patrick Mahomes also made a statement on Sunday and that's the Chiefs offense can still function just fine without Kenneth Walker . In Kansas City's 35-13 win over Atlanta, Mahomes threw five TD passes in a game for the first time since 2022. He also threw for 348 yards, and a big reason was that he finally had the long ball working. Mahomes, who had gone 20 straight games without throwing a touchdown pass that traveled at least 20 yards in the air, produced two of those against the Falcons .
Deshaun Watson also made a statement. The Browns quarterback led ANOTHER fourth-quarter comeback and just became only the third QB in NFL history with a game-winning drive in each of his team's first six wins in a season (1990 Troy Aikman and 2016 Matthew Stafford ).
And then there was Joe Burrow. The Bengals QB made a statement on Sunday night against the Steelers with four touchdown passes in a dominating 38-18 win. Burrow now has at least four total touchdowns in five straight games, which is tied with Peyton Manning (2004) for the longest streak in NFL history.
And now, it's time for the Week 10 grades, and we're going to start with the Vikings, who are starting to look pretty super.

title: Scorigami: Cowboys-49ers ends with score never before seen in NFL history thanks to Dak Prescott
summary: Dak Prescott's otherwise meaningless two-point conversion helped make history
full_text:
Fill in your charts, Scorigami fans: We have yet another score that had never happened before in 107 years of NFL history. The 49ers ' 46-40 win over the Cowboys is the first 46-40 game on record.
It took some oddities and some late-game madness to get there, as is pretty much always the case when looking for a unique score. There were five touchdowns, a failed two-point conversion and two successful two-point conversions in the fourth quarter alone!
SF 46 - DAL 40 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1099th unique score in NFL history, and the 4th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/qW3tfAiLSJ
Entering the fourth quarter, the 49ers led 31-19, not a super common score, but nothing too absurd: That score has happened 17 times before. A missed Brandon Aubrey extra point earlier in the game created the strange number for Dallas.
Then all hell (or, for Scorigami fans, heaven) broke loose. Christian McCaffrey scored on a 16-yard run. Dallas answered with a long touchdown drive but failed on the two-point conversion. At 38-25, the scoring chances rose. As a general rule, as the score rises astronomically, so, too, do the chances for a unique score. The Cowboys got a stop and scored again, this time kicking the extra point to make it 38-32. That score has happened before, albeit only three times.
It took just two plays for the 49ers to find the end zone, with Brock Purdy finding McCaffrey jetting off for a 66-yard touchdown. Purdy also found McCaffrey for the two-point conversion. That was big, because 44-32 and 45-32 have both happened before (once each). But 46-32 had never happened before.
Luckily, one final Dak Prescott touchdown pass and, crucially, a successful two-point conversion didn't ruin things, either. The two-point conversion was actually crucial, because 46-38 has happened before. So, everyone, please applaud Dak Prescott's effort here.
Dak converts the two-point conversion! We've got a six-point game 👀 SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SjVjt43GD9
The next Scorigami will be the 1,100th unique score in NFL history, and hopefully, it will be half as fun as this game was. This was also the fourth Scorigami this season, a rare feat in itself.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 10 winners and losers: Texans crumble against Browns, Kirk Cousins trade pays dividends for Vikings
summary: Houston squandered a three-score lead while Minnesota won by a three-possession margin of its own
full_text:
Week 10 in the NFL offers the first look at most teams in the wake of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Early returns are in on the majority of the 17 in-season transactions. A couple of newcomers have yet to debut with their new squads, but there is already a clear frontrunner for the most impactful trade of the year after Kirk Cousins ' first game with the Minnesota Vikings .
Other deals have not aged nearly as well. For instance, Marvin Harrison Jr . was inactive for the Houston Texans on Sunday, was not all that productive in his first three games with the franchise and watched his teammates take a bad loss when they threw away a 17-point lead to the Cleveland Browns .
Not all of this week's top takeaways revolve around trade deadline fallout, though. Division races and injuries are, as always, a large part of the picture.
Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday's NFL Week 10 action.
As winners of three of four games heading into Week 10, and with a 17-0 first-half lead over the Browns, the Houston Texans were in an ideal position to climb back into the playoff race after a 0-4 start to the season. Surely, with C.J. Stroud playing the best football of his career and Will Anderson Jr . pinning his ears back against the trailing Browns, that three-possession lead had to be safe, right? Not so fast.
The Texans and a defense that has been a disappointment all year surrendered 20 unanswered points in the second and third quarters. The lead evaporated. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson threw for 312 yards and a touchdown and tacked on another 49 yards and a score on the ground. He orchestrated yet another comeback—the Browns have trailed or been tied in every fourth quarter this season—and helped Cleveland improve to 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. Watson did all that against what was supposed to be the NFL's best defense.
That unit's inability to carry its 2025 dominance into 2026 has been the primary factor behind Houston's underwhelming season. Nothing the Texans have done to address it has worked, including a change of play-caller. Each of their last four opponents scored at least 21 points.
In turn, Houston is three games back of .500 at 3-6 and has practically no margin for error remaining in its hunt for a postseason berth. That is why only one team in NFL history has ever started a year at 0-4 and still made the playoffs. The climb out of the hole is steep, and the reasons behind a poor start are usually season-defining. They certainly are for the Texans.
The Vikings were so universally celebrated at the trade deadline because if Cousins could deliver even a modicum of improvement to an anemic offense, the team's ceiling would skyrocket. One game into his reunion with the franchise, he already delivered exactly what was envisioned . Minnesota's top-ranked defense did its thing in a 30-10 beatdown of the Green Bay Packers , and instead of just skating by on the other side of the ball, the Vikings finally pulled away from an opponent.
Cousins went 21-for-31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He freed Justin Jefferson from his season-long frustration, finding the superstar wide receiver nine times for 74 yards. As a result, the Vikings turned in their second 30-point outing of the campaign and the first since they exploded against that same Packers team in the season opener.
Minnesota's trade deadline transaction helped snap a two-game losing skid. It also solidified a head-to-head tiebreaker over the Packers in the NFL's most competitive division. The Cousins deal is already a home-run trade.
Other familiar faces in new places this week included Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Josh Downs and Buffalo Bills safety Amani Hooker . They also did their front offices proud in blowout wins. Downs hauled in his longest touchdown since 2024 to help the Chiefs score 35 points for the second consecutive week, while Hooker racked up seven tackles to rank third on the Bills defense.
It was the same old song and dance with the Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 10. The maligned unit wasted a tremendous offensive performance that included five passing touchdowns from Dak Prescott , three of which went to George Pickens , in a 46-40 loss to the NFC's best team: the San Francisco 49ers . The 584 yards they allowed were the most in a home game in franchise history, and the 46 points were the fourth most.
Explosive plays were easy to come by for the 49ers in a game that set series records for combined points and yards. Christian McCaffrey recorded the longest receiving touchdown of his career with a 74-yarder and followed it up with a 66-yard catch-and-run later in the game. Deebo Samuel broke loose for a 70-yard run on a reverse that completely confused Dallas' defense.
DEEEEEEBOOOOOOO SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3RwQ4dNchJ
For context on McCaffrey, a few notes from CBS Sports research and ESPN Insights :
The Cowboys had a tremendous opportunity to capitalize on the New York Giants ' loss and move closer to the NFC East lead. Their defense blew it.
The same week most of the NFL's top trade deadline movers debuted with their new teams, Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III watched theirs win without them. The former Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle and ex-Falcons safety hadn't hit their bye weeks yet when the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for them, so coach Liam Coen gave them the week off to rest while they acclimated to their new surroundings.
The Jaguars did not need them anyway. They rolled to a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans . They would have been better off with both newcomers in the lineup, since they are standouts at positions that have thinned out in Jacksonville in recent weeks, and the squad gave up its second-highest point total of the year without them. But it should be a promising sign that the Super Bowl contenders can cruise past a bottom-dwelling opponent with a couple of glaring holes on their defense. Just imagine what Jacksonville will do to Tennessee at home in two weeks when Davis and Bates are active.
There might not be a more unfortunate way to sustain a serious injury in the course of an NFL game than while celebrating. Detroit Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson experienced that harsh reality firsthand in Munich. He went down with a non-contact knee injury in the Week 10 international game after landing awkwardly while celebrating a sack on New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye .
Aidan Hutchinson just got hurt celebrating a sack pic.twitter.com/bz1CY4G4Av
The Lions reportedly fear that Hutchinson sustained a significant injury that will sideline him for the foreseeable future. He and the team are seeking second opinions following the initial tests in Germany, but early indications suggest his season may be over.
Beyond the unfortunate freakiness of how the injury occurred, this is also a devastating blow to a Lions defense that seems to be turning a corner for the better. What has all season been a bottom-tier unit in limiting opposing teams' yardage has not allowed more than two touchdowns in a game since Oct. 11. It will be hard-pressed to keep that streak going much longer without its most disruptive player.
Patrick Mahomes was already the leading candidate for Comeback Player of the Year and boosted his chances even higher with his best game of the season. In a 35-13 demolition of the Atlanta Falcons , Mahomes passed for 348 yards and five touchdowns and set a new NFL record for passing touchdowns (328) by a player in his first 10 seasons. He passed Peyton Manning on that leaderboard.
The most impressive part of Mahomes' monster performance was that he and the Kansas City Chiefs torched Atlanta's defense even without star running back Kenneth Walker III in the lineup. Instead, rookie Emmett Johnson picked up the slack on the ground and turned into Mahomes' favorite option in the passing game. They linked up six times for 70 yards and a pair of touchdowns…

title: Bengals vs. Steelers prediction: First place in AFC North up for grabs in rivalry battle on 'SNF'
summary: Pittsburgh won the first matchup between the two teams back in Week 3. Plus, how to watch, what to know, and a prediction
full_text:
The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division.
Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh.
Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown.
The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred.
Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception.
Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns.
Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain.
It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury.
Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally.
Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe .
This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers.
The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night.
In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. Pick: Bengals 23, Steelers 20

title: NFL Week 10 overreactions: Patriots to miss playoffs? Texans' DeMeco Ryans on the hot seat?
summary: Drake Maye got hurt, and New England got blown out in Germany as the Pats playoff hopes slip away
full_text:
On a week defined by flight issues, the teams with the longest flights home aren't feeling particularly great.
Yes, the Lions would normally be feeling excellent after blowing out the Patriots for their fifth straight win. But Aidan Hutchinson suffered what appears to be a serious knee injury , casting a very dark cloud over the result.
But at least the result went in Detroit's favor. The defense is coming around after an awful start, and the offense continues to just shred opponents. The Lions are 7-2. It's not perfect; the Hutchinson loss is a massive one. But it's 7-2.
The Patriots, meanwhile ... Well, let's start there.
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
During the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Germany ...
This game was a microcosm of the entire season. There were massive expectations around the Brown addition. He has fallen woefully short, first with a knee injury, then an ankle injury, and now a hamstring injury. With Romeo Doubs also on IR, the wide receiver corps looks nothing like New England envisioned.
The defense also looks nothing like New England hoped. The Patriots are allowing 8.1 yards per attempt, a bottom-five rate in the NFL . Big plays are a huge reason behind that. Through the early-afternoon games Sunday, only the Colts , Titans and Falcons had allowed more explosive plays than the Patriots have, and New England's 30 passes of 20+ yards allowed is tied for most in the league.
This, simply, isn't a playoff team. Even the standings say that: The Patriots are currently the No. 8 seed in the AFC after the Browns beat the Texans . The bye — followed by a game against the winless Chargers — will help New England. But the schedule gets really hard thereafter: Bills , Vikings , at Chiefs . We don't know how long Maye will be out, or at least affected, because of the ankle injury. Other players are dropping like flies. The offensive line looks especially flimsy. The reigning AFC champions look like they won't even get a chance to defend their conference crown.
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
The Vikings' 30-10 destruction of the Packers showed, once again, just how good this defense is. Not just good — great. The type of defense you cannot waste. And the Vikings' trade for Kirk Cousins showed the Vikings won't waste it.
Cousins went 21-for-31 for 207 yards and a pair of touchdowns and an interception. It wasn't amazing by any stretch, and the Packers turning the ball over four times helped. But perhaps that's the point here. Minnesota doesn't need amazing quarterback play. It just needs not-awful play. Even Cousins admitted as much post-game, speaking to the Fox broadcast.
"With this defense, we're always gonna have a chance," Cousins said.
There was a lot to like. Cousins completed two passes at least 20 yards downfield. That's the same number the Vikings had connected on, combined , over their previous three games. Cousins' opening touchdown pass was a 38-yard touchdown to Myles Price . That was Minnesota's first touchdown on a throw 20+ yards downfield since Week 3!
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
Justin Jefferson had a season-high nine catches (on a season-high 13 targets) for 74 yards, with a couple of narrow misses in the end zone. Cousins leaned heavily on his superstar wide receiver, and that connection should continue to grow.
Cousins also converted seven third downs with his arm, including the Price touchdown above on third-and-23, a 24-yard connection with Tai Felton on third-and-15 and a 16-yard screen to Jefferson that Cousins audibled to on third-and-12.
All the Vikings needed was capable quarterback play. They got it from someone who only joined the team five days ago. Outstanding work all around.
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
The Texans have lost a bunch of games they absolutely cannot lose this year, and Sunday's was the most "can't lose" loss yet. Houston was up 17-0, and Cleveland had lost 61 straight games when trailing by 17 or more entering Sunday. That streak is no longer.
It started with a 65-yard connection between Deshaun Watson and Jerry Jeudy to set up Cleveland's first touchdown. Houston has given up way, way too many big plays this season. Cleveland cut the deficit from 17-0 to 17-10 at halftime.
Houston went three-and-out on four straight possessions in the second half. It was outgained 109 to -1 (NEGATIVE ONE!) in the third quarter and 200 to 35 in the second half.
After going up 24-20 late, the Texans failed to hold on. On the game-winning drive, Kamari Lassiter , who has had a rough year, got called for a brutal unnecessary roughness. I'm not sure what he's supposed to do here.
Kamari Lassiter Tries To Make A Play On The Ball. Instead He Makes Contact With Tylan Wallace Right To The Head As He Has The Ball. A Flag Comes Out On This One. pic.twitter.com/4xakXExU5O
But then the Texans, instead of responding, gave up a 30-yard catch to Harold Fannin and a 5-yard touchdown run to Quinshon Judkins . The inability to make winning plays in winning moments has defined this team all year.
The Browns ground up 379 yards on 5.7 yards per play. The Houston defense has been arguably the most disappointing non-Chargers unit in the NFL this year, currently in the bottom 10 in expected points added per play and explosive play rate. And guess who took over defensive play-calling recently? DeMeco Ryans .
Ryans has had his fair share of coaching blunders this year, from poor time management to extremely conservative decisions. The Texans had legitimate Super Bowl hopes entering this year but have frankly been nowhere near it. Houston is now 1-5 in one-score games. Ryans belongs on the hot seat, maybe not in-season, but certainly by the end of it unless there's a miraculous turnaround coming.
Overreaction or reality check: Overreaction
Michael Penix Jr . looked awful in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs. He was all over the place with his accuracy en route to completing just 23 of his 43 pass attempts. He threw an awful pick late. He looked completely flustered when he got pressured — and even before he got pressured. What is this?
Stefanski: Come on Mike let’s get a 1st down here and keep the ball away from Pat. Michael Penix: pic.twitter.com/5CyIlCs0ld
Penix went 5-of-13 for 34 yards on plays he was blitzed. That's atrocious. Unsustainable, especially in today's blitz-heavy NFL.
Penix's play has taken a nosedive since his three-touchdown Week 7 against the 49ers . He threw four interceptions in monsoon-like conditions against the Buccaneers in Week 8. Last week, he threw another bad pick against the Bengals . This week was another brutal outing.
Unfortunately, the Falcons don't have a better option. Tua Tagovailoa has looked terrible in the few moments he has actually been available, and his penchant for turnovers, poor arm strength and lack of movement skills are near non-starters. It's pretty bleak in Atlanta, which will certainly have a new quarterback next year.
Overreaction or reality check: Overreaction
Meanwhile in the lowly NFC South, the Panthers beat the Saints 20-17 — a game that was equal parts entertaining and, simply, bad. Neither team hit 300 yards of offense. They combined for 20 penalties. Tyler Shough had two bad turnovers, one off a deflected pass, another when he fumbled an exchange with his running back. Ultimately, a huge pass interference on New Orleans set up Ryan Fitzgerald's game-winning kick late.
At 4-5, Carolina currently leads the NFC South. It's hard to envision it finishing that way, though. The offensive line is in rough shape, and the passing game might be even worse. Bryce Young was 17-of-30 for 200 yards. He completed just two of his eight passes 10+ yards downfield, and his three biggest gains were on short throws that gained yards after the catch. Remember, this was a pretty bad defense he was facing. Carolina ran the ball 32 times for 97 yards. Again, this is not a…

title: Chiefs trade deadline move for Josh Downs unlocks MVP Patrick Mahomes of old
summary: Mahomes' MVP is back thanks to his new downfield deep threat: NFL trade deadline WR addition Josh Downs
full_text:
Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs ' deep-strike passing game appeared dead and gone through nine weeks of the 2026 season.
However, Chiefs general manager Brett Veach's NFL trade deadline acquisition of Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs Tuesday afternoon brought the two-time NFL MVP version of Mahomes and the team's downfield passing attack back to life in Week 10.
Entering Week 9, Mahomes was averaging an NFL-worst 5.6 air yards per pass attempt and had become the only quarterback in the last 20 years to average under 5.0 air yards per pass attempt in four consecutive games in the same season, per Pro Football Focus. That four-game dry spell coincided with the ankle dislocation for deep threat wide receiver Tyquan Thornton in Week 4. A week ago, Mahomes was grabbing his right elbow in pain after the New York Jets bent it backward, and on Sunday, the Patrick Mahomes of old returned.
The introduction of Downs and his ability to threaten defenses out of the slot and down the field changed everything. Downs' 1,995 receiving yards out of the slot were the second-most in the NFL in his career since he entered the league in 2023 at the start of Week 10, trailing only Detroit Lions All-Pro wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (2,160).
Mahomes, as a result, marched into Atlanta like Union General William T. Sherman in 1864 and burned the Falcons ' secondary to the ground at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, completing 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards, 5 passing touchdowns, and no interceptions in a 35-13 win for the visiting Chiefs. Sunday marked Mahomes' first game with at least five passing touchdowns since the opening week of the 2022 NFL season, the year of his second and most recent league MVP season. He averaged 9.3 air yards per pass attempt, his most since Week 4 at the Las Vegas Raiders , the game Thornton went down.
Mahomes had not one but two touchdown passes of 20-plus air yards, which snapped a 20-game drought without a passing touchdown of 20-plus air yards. That was the second-longest such streak of his career. Downs' arrival coincided with a number of different droughts ending for the three-time Super Bowl MVP on Sunday.
300-plus pass yards and 4-plus pass TD
Multiple TD of 20-plus air yards
It was clear Mahomes was throwing with a different level of confidence with Downs on the field. He rifled a dart of a back-shoulder touchdown to Downs from 18 yards out, and that set the tone for the rest of the afternoon. He finished with 4 catches on 5 targets for 53 yards, including that 18-yard receiving touchdown. The box score doesn't fully capture the gravity he brought to the Chiefs' passing game, which is more apparent on some of Mahomes' other highlight throws from Sunday's demolition in Atlanta.
"It [was] good to see guys step up and make plays, especially against man coverage," Mahomes said in an understatement postgame, via Fox 4 News Kansas City .
Mahomes steps up and drops a dime to Josh Downs for a TD! KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dwTMy1qZYC
His next touchdown toss was a 39-yard effortless throw to fifth-round rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen , and the Falcons had no safety help on the play.
3rd touchdown pass for Mahomes! Cyrus Allen scores on a 39-yarder. KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Nijm7zG3lT
That was just a warm-up for Mahomes' 50-yard rocket launch of a pass down the middle of the field to wide receiver Rashee Rice , his longest pass of the day.
Mahomes & Rice connect deep for 50 yards! KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZFDULxVq7n
His final touchdown throw of the day came on a classic Mahomes roll out into a deep strike score from 43 yards out to undrafted wide receiver Andrew Armstrong .
348 yards & 5 TDs for @PatrickMahomes 👏 pic.twitter.com/WUMyRQsznx
The rest of the AFC, and the NFL at large, for that matter, are now on notice because the arrival of Downs awakened MVP Mahomes once again.

title: LOOK: Fernando Mendoza scores first NFL TD on opening drive vs. Seahawks
summary: Fans had planned to sit during the QB's first TD to honor Mendoza's mother, Elsa, utilizes a wheelchair because of her multiple sclerosis
full_text:
With Kirk Cousins traded back to the Minnesota Vikings , Las Vegas Raiders fans' wait to see 2026 first-round pick Fernando Mendoza start is over. Some waited to jump for joy upon Mendoza scoring a touchdown at home against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 until he scores his second touchdown.
The time to celebrate didn't take long. Mendoza capped Las Vegas' 11-play, 46-yard opening drive with a 10-yard touchdown run reminisicent of his national championship scoring scramble against the Miami Hurricanes in January.
Fernando Mendoza rushes it in for his first career TD 🗣️ SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gcKUNMIZUH
The reason behind this is a wholesome one. Mendoza's mother, Elsa, utilizes a wheelchair while dealing with multiple sclerosis (MS), so fans are trying to organize a tribute to her, Mendoza, and his family by remaining seated if/when he scores against Seattle on Sunday. For those who watched Mendoza's college career, TV cameras often cut to his family celebrating, and Mendoza's father, Fernando Sr., would often be seen seated and hugging Elsa after touchdowns. Fernando Sr. also remained seated as he and Elsa's son was drafted first overall in the 2026 NFL draft .
"I see her fighting every single day, and with a smile on her face," Mendoza said of his mother during a pre-draft appearance on The Rich Eisen Show. "So there's no excuse for me to have a bad day, bad play or bad game. I'm always trying to have an optimistic approach, give the best and serve the best to my teammates."
Obviously, there will still be Raiders fans who got so excited that they left their seats when Mendoza scored his first NFL touchdown, but it's a thoughtful gesture.
Listen, everyone going to Allegiant Stadium this Sunday. Stay seated when Fernando scores his first touchdown. Will be an epic gesture from fans to player. Pass it along.
Mendoza is the first No. 1 overall quarterback in NFL history to make his first career start versus the defending Super Bowl champions. Either way, many Raiders fans are glued to their seats at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

title: With Kirk Cousins back, the Vikings really can win the Super Bowl and here's how
summary: From the 2000 Ravens to the 2015 Broncos, history offers plenty of reasons to believe Minnesota can win with Kirk Cousins
full_text:
Three weeks ago, the Minnesota Vikings were 6-0, a remarkable achievement given their offense was among the worst in the NFL . Brian Flores' defense was playing at a historically dominant level, and the question wasn't whether they could win games this way – it was whether they could keep doing it all the way to the Super Bowl .
I know, that seems like a silly thing to write – forget about even saying it out loud – but there's precedent !
But since winning six straight to start the season, the Vikings have lost two in a row, the offense has somehow gotten worse, and following one of the most historically inept quarterback performances in 35 years, the team traded a third-round pick for 38-year-old Kirk Cousins .
According to TruMedia, NFL QBs have attempted at least 25 passes in a game 14,463 times since 1990. Carson Wentz's performance on MNF vs. the Bills ranks: • 15th-worst passer rating (8.9) • T-27th-worst completion rate (32%) • 12th-worst EPA/dropback (-0.85, since 2000)
A year ago, such a move would've seemed supremely desperate because Cousins was still in Atlanta sharing time with Michael Penix Jr. , the quarterback the Falcons drafted not long after signing Cousins to a huge deal in 2024.  And during those two seasons, Cousins barely resembled the version we had seen in Minnesota, the one who made Justin Jefferson look like he actually enjoyed playing football. (I suppose it didn't hurt that Jefferson averaged 98 receiving yards per game when Cousins was the Vikings QB throwing the passes.)
Now, that very same trade just seems … moderately desperate, and that has everything to do with the trifecta of ineffectiveness that was JJ McCarthy , Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz . And after Cousins helped the Vikings get back in the win column Sunday against Green Bay – at the same stadium where he tore his Achilles in his final game with Minnesota three years ago – that Super Bowl question suddenly sounds much less ridiculous.
Because here's the thing: The Vikings don't need Cousins to play like an MVP. They don't even need him to lead a top-10 offense. Hell, above average – even average – could be good enough. History is full of teams that won championships with replacement-level offenses and dominant defenses, and Minnesota is unequivocally closer to joining that group than they were a week ago.
When we first wrote about the Vikings' Super Bowl chances in late October , they ranked 31st in offensive efficiency, averaging just 18.8 points per game despite that 6-0 start.
Two games later … they're still 31st in offensive efficiency, and their scoring average has somehow fallen (it was 18.3 coming into Week 10). Meanwhile, Flores' defense continues to carry this team. They're allowing just 14.5 points per game, and opponents have struggled to move the ball consistently against a defense that blitzes on 74% of dropbacks, more than twice the league average (32.8%) and easily the highest rate in the NFL.
That formula has been good enough for six wins in eight games. But there's a difference between surviving the regular season and winning three or four consecutive playoff games against the NFC's best teams.
In his first game back with the Vikings, Cousins led the team to 30 points Sunday. The last time this group scored 30? Week 1 … against these very same Packers . This time around, Cousins tossed two touchdowns (good luck finding someone – anyone – happier than Justin Jefferson, who finished with 9 catches for 74 yards).
It's like Kirko Chainz never left!
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
Kirk Cousins to Gavin Bartholomew for the TD pic.twitter.com/g1YUgVp8nr
But the defense was even more impressive, sacking Jordan Love eight times — the most by any team in a game this season — and forcing three turnovers.
Cousins looked like a shell of himself during his time in Atlanta, which ain't unreasonable for a quarterback in his mid-30s coming off Achilles surgery. That said, he had manifested 2023 Pre-Injury Kirk this season for the Raiders . Through nine games, he'd thrown 20 touchdown passes against eight interceptions, with a 97.1 passer rating.
More importantly, he's been substantially more efficient than the QBs Minnesota had trotted out through the first two months (admittedly, it would be hard to be less efficient). So, how much of a difference could that make over the next 2-3 months?
Based on how Cousins has played this season compared to Murray and Wentz, Minnesota's offense could go from averaging just 18.3 points per game to as many as 27 when you look at expected points added per dropback (which is just a measure of how much a quarterback helps or hurts his team's chances of scoring). That's the best-case scenario, but even a more modest improvement could mean the Vikings score 4-6 more points per game.
And we don't even have to assume Cousins will replicate everything he's done in Las Vegas. Here's what Minnesota's offense could look like if he's something less than that.
How much better could the Vikings offense be with Cousins?
With Cousins - modest improvement
With Cousins - solid improvement
Additional expected points/game
Projections use Cousins' 2026 passing efficiency compared with Minnesota's previous quarterbacks.
The "solid improvement" projection puts Minnesota at 25 points per game, nearly seven more than it's averaging now. Even "modest improvement" gets the Vikings to 22.7, which might not sound all that impressive until you consider what some previous Super Bowl champions managed offensively.
And there's another obvious reason this could work and it doesn't require advanced stats, just eyes and common sense: Cousins has already shown he can run Kevin O'Connell's offense at a high level. In 2022, he threw for 4,547 yards and 29 touchdowns and Minnesota finished 13-4. He was playing well again the following season before tearing his Achilles. Now, some three years later, time is a flat circle.
Look, it's easy to win a Super Bowl with a Hall of Fame quarterback – at least easier than winning one with a replacement-level passer leading an average offense. There's a reason Patrick Mahomes , Tom Brady and Peyton Manning have a combined 12 rings.
But there is more than one way to crack an egg. (I reflexively wrote 'to skin a cat,' but then spent 15 minutes figuring out whether people still say that, and if it's even acceptable. I went with the egg idiom instead. Getting old is weird.) And for the Vikings, that means a lights-out defense and something approaching an average offense.
Luckily, history has plenty of such success stories that ended in hoisting the Lombardi Trophy.
Super Bowl champions that won without dominant offenses
Five of the Super Bowl champs averaged between 20.8 and 22.2 points per game. Even if we go with "modest improvement" for the Vikings and Cousins, it would put them above all five.
So what lessons does history give us about how Minnesota could win the whole thing?
Baltimore might be the most famous example of a defense carrying an offense to a title. Ray Lewis and company allowed just 10.3 points per game, the fewest ever in a 16-game season, while their offense went five consecutive games without scoring a touchdown. Five! The Ravens eventually replaced Tony Banks with Trent Dilfer, who was a game manager in the best sense of the phrase. Baltimore finished 12-4 and won Super Bowl XXXV, beating the Giants 34-7. Minnesota's defense isn't quite at that level, but Cousins is a considerable upgrade over Dilfer.
Tampa Bay's defense, led by Derrick Brooks, Warren Sapp, John Lynch and Ronde Barber, allowed just 12.3 points per game. Brad Johnson threw 22 touchdowns and only six interceptions during the regular season, but the Bucs still ranked 18th in scoring. They didn't need an explosive passing game because their defense consistently put them in position to win. In the Gruden (Super) Bowl, Tampa Bay intercepted Raiders quarterback…

title: Jets' Geno Smith ruled out with ankle injury: Rookie QB Cade Klubnik makes NFL debut
summary: Rookie Cade Klubnik stepped in to open the second half, leading a 10-play, 61-yard scoring drive on his very first NFL possession
full_text:
New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith left for the locker room in the third quarter of Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills after he suffered an ankle injury. He had returned to the lineup for one drive in the second half after clearing concussion protocol, and led the Jets to a field goal. However, he exited again, pushing rookie Cade Klubnik into the game to complete his first NFL action.
Smith's second injury of the day came in the third quarter after just one full drive following his concussion evaluation. As he threw, he took a hit that seemed to fall on his right ankle. The Jets initially ruled him questionable to return before downgrading him to out in the fourth quarter.
Earlier in the game, on a third-and-9 with 25 seconds remaining in the second quarter, Smith was sandwiched between defenders Terrel Bernard and TJ Parker . He remained on the turf for several moments as trainers attended to him. He was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared after halftime.
Check out what happened here:
Geno Smith is down after taking this big hit.  Jets could kick the FG and hope Geno bounces back during the half. pic.twitter.com/sjqLI4oFVE
When the Jets took the field in the second half, it was the rookie Klubnik under center. On the very first drive of his NFL career, he marched the Jets 61 yards downfield on 10 plays and set up a 22-yard field goal. Klubnik completed two of four passes for 39 yards and rushed twice for 19 yards. His first completion went to star wideout Garrett Wilson for 29 yards.
first NFL completion for Cade Klubnik is a 29-yard completion to Garrett Wilson 📺: #BUFvsNYJ on @NFLonCBS | @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/OKrWLPwutf
When Klubnik entered the game for his second possession in the third quarter, he threw an interception to Davison Igbinosun , who fumbled the ball back to the Jets. New York didn't take advantage of its second chance, going three-and-out.
Jets throw an INT but get it back on a fumble on the return BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/f5vRx8b3m1
The fourth-round pick out of Clemson ranked top five in the FBS in completions (855), passing yards (9,426) and passing touchdowns (71) from 2023-25, and came in and beat out Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe for the backup job.
Prior to exiting the game, Smith completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards.

title: Drake Maye, Aidan Hutchinson injured on same play: Injury updates for Patriots QB, Lions DE
summary: Maye and Hutchinson both went down on the final play of the first drive
full_text:
Two of the game's biggest stars went down on the same play in Germany, as New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson headed to the locker room following injuries on a third-down sack on the first drive.
The Patriots announced that Maye was downgraded from questionable to out with an ankle injury, and the Lions announced that Hutchinson was downgraded to out with a knee injury. Patriots backup QB Tommy DeVito took over for Maye and played the remainder of the 35-10 loss for New England. He finished 12-for-24 with 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception.
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said he didn't have an update on Maye after the game but did say they would run more tests back in the United States to determine the severity of the injury. He called it a "lower leg" injury.
When asked why Maye was ruled out despite not knowing the full extent of the injury, Vrabel said , "He couldn't function, couldn't play, couldn't run, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play QB to protect himself to execute, or function at that level."
Vrabel initially said there were a lot of issues he didn't believe Maye's absence affected, but then said it "may have, but I highly doubt it" when asked what his concern is without his QB1 on the offense.
The head coach said the team as a whole needs to do the little things better on all three phases and work on fundamentals. He listed tackling, creating turnovers, preventing turnovers on offense, running the football, getting open, protecting the quarterback, and special teams needing to create some momentum as areas the team needs to work on, regardless of who is at QB.
According to reports , Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a significant knee injury , and there "does not appear hope that he returns this season." The DE immediately had an MRI and will get a second opinion, per the report.
After the game, Lions coach Dan Campbell said he had "nothing new" in terms of injury news surrounding Hutchinson, and that the team will "know more when we get back in the States."
"Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy. I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out ... but knowing Hutch for who he is, he doesn't stay down long," Campbell said. "... but certainly you don't want to know that a player like that is down."
He emphasized how well the team adjusted and made up for a big defensive loss.
On third-and-goal, Hutchinson got to the quarterback, who was limping after the play. Maye was able to walk under his own power to the sideline, but was hunched over, seemingly in pain, and eventually went to the locker room.
Here is a look at the final play of the opening drive and the last play before Maye went to the locker room:
This was Drake Maye's final play before leaving the game questionable with an ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/Yi1rQYpMeW
Hutchinson appeared to injure his knee during the celebration of the sack. Here is a closer look at the celebration:
Oh boy. #Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson got hurt celebrating a sack. He’s now in the medical tent. pic.twitter.com/DnPLvjm7qL
The Patriots' opening drive ended in a successful field goal attempt. The Lions immediately responded with an Amon-Ra St. Brown touchdown on their first offensive drive of the game.
Fortunately for the Patriots, they have a bye in Week 11, so they will have time to nurse these injuries before they take the field again in Week 12, when they visit the Los Angeles Chargers . The Lions will return to Detroit to host the Tampa Bay Bucanneers in Week 11.
CBS Sports will continue to update this article as more news becomes available.

full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals passes for his first career completion during the first quarter of a game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cardinals unfortunately did not provide a sturdy foundation for rookie quarterback Carson Beck to work off of in his first NFL start. Beck threw a pair of interceptions and was sacked five times in a lopsided 34-6 loss at home against the Rams. There truly wasn’t much in the way of positives to cling to in this one, which is why CBS Sports’ John Breech gave the Cardinals a big fat “F” for their most recent performance. Here’s what he hadto say: “ Carson Beck’s first career start was a total disaster. When you’re a rookie QB, it helps when you have a ground game that can take some pressure off you and/or an offensive line that can protect you, but Beck had neither of those. Beck got sacked five times and he threw two interceptions, including one that Devin Duvernay practically handed to the Rams. The Cardinals had a big first quarter with 71 yards, but they never really moved the ball after that, totaling just 52 yards for the rest of the game. If this is what the Cardinals are going to look like for the second half of the year, don’t expect many fireworks from this team for the rest of the season. ” Was this the right grade for the Cardinals?
