title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Rams Winners & Losers: Arizona taken to the woodshed
summary: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win. They already defeated the Los Angeles Rams earlier this year with six Chad Ryland field goals. Can they defeat this divisional rival again? This one is completely different from the first contest. For one, instead of 10-year veteran Jacoby Brissett under center, rookie Carson Beck will be starting his […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win. They already defeated the Los Angeles Rams earlier this year with six Chad Ryland field goals. Can they defeat this divisional rival again? This one is completely different from the first contest. For one, instead of 10-year veteran Jacoby Brissett under center, rookie Carson Beck will be starting his very NFL game. Is he ready? Prior to Week 1, the answer from Beck was a resounding yes. His coaching staff agrees. For another thing. All-World EDGE rusher Myles Garrett made his Rams debut. Yikes. RELATED: BECK STARTS OFF STRONG The Rams came into this game 5-4-0 while Arizona is 3-6-0. Both clubs need a win badly. When the contest finished, Arizona was taken to the woodshed by Los Angeles to the tune of 34-6. What is odd is that in two games against the Rams this year, kicker Ryland has scored every point. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS First quarter offense – Things sure did begin well. Two drives: two scores. But like what mostly this offense has done all year, the points ended up as two field goals instead of touchdowns. The first drive was eight plays highlighted by a 10-yard completion to TE Trey McBride followed by a 21-yard gain by WR Simi Fehoko. But a third-and-two at LA’s 24 became a sack instead and a three-point lead. On the Cardinals next possession, it was also unicorns and lollipops that began on their own 35 with a huge 31-yard gain by WR Devin Duvernay’s and short runs by RB Tyler Allgeier to the Rams’ 26. Then a false start, coupled with an incomplete pass made it fourth-and-10, and out trotted Chad Ryland as Arizona led 6-3 going into the second quarter. Unfortunately for the Cardinals, there were three more quarters to play. First career INT for @Cody_Simon30 🙂‍↕️ #LARvsAZ on @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/cnQKQoX5JE — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 15, 2026 LB Corey Simon – Holding a three-point lead, the Rams gave it up on their next possession. What a great play by Simon on the pick as Los Angeles had driven to the 24-yard line. The play was intended for WR Konata Mumpfield, but Simon made an acrobatic catch and the defense averted a costly score. He nailed TE Colby Parkinson after just a one-yard gain in the second quarter. Six total tackles. Kickers – When your kicker and punter are in the running for offensive MVP, you know the offense is a complete disaster. K Ryland nailed both field goals, each from 49 yards. P Blake Gillikin had a great game, booting three kicks for a 50.0 average per punt, with one downed inside the 20 with a long of 56 yards. One of the league’s best punters. And with that, we must give a big shout out to long snapper Casey Kreiter who consistently passes the ball exactly where the punter likes it, and a swift spiral right to the holder. S Andrew Wingard – The talented safety came off an injury and was everywhere. On a third-and-10 in the first quarter, Wingard stopped RB Blake Corum for a nine-yard gain as he broke free to the third level. On the 22-yard completion to WR C.J. Daniels late in the first quarter, Wingard left his man and raced all the way over to the opposite side to assist in the tackle. Led all defenders with 11 total tackles. LB Mack Wilson – Wilson was also an active tackler with so many runners coming to the second level. Had 10 tackles with one tackle for loss and one pass defense. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Offensive line – Well, did anyone in the Cardinals fanbase expect anything different than what happened along the offensive line? Pretty much jailbreak all game. Poor QB Carson Beck. The rookie never had a chance all game. Agent 0 on the move! 💪 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/K04597Uvcf — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 The Rams had five sacks, while the rushing attack had a grand total of 34 yards. Geez. Can’t run and no time to throw. Back in the origins of American Football, if the offense didn’t get anywhere, oftentimes they would punt on second or third down and try to work on field position. Our next poll: Should the Cardinals punt on third downs? WESLEY BAILEY RIPPED IT AWAY FOR HIS FIRST NFL INTERCEPTION 😤 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/upvqsq5djk — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 QB Carson Beck – The best thing to happen to the rookie in his maiden NFL start, was that at no time was the cart summoned. Beck was flushed from the pocket for most of the contest, and he had no run game to depend on. Which meant after a while, the defense no longer thought about runners and was all out for the pass. Miserable day, and a miserable game. The second pick wasn’t his fault. Went 11 for 18 for 108 yards, a 6.0 average per pass completion, zero TDs, two picks, sacked five times (which could have been double digits), and a QB rating of 38.4. Welcome to the NFL. Defense three quarters – The Rams were stymied in the first quarter being held to a field goal. Then the first drive in the second quarter was the Simon pick. But the wheels fell off from there. The Cardinals could not stop the run, and were burned repeatedly with accurate passing from QB Matthew Stafford who completed passes for 31 yards, 22, 18, 27, 10, 22 (TD), 44, 10, and 19 (TD). BRADEN BRINGIN' THE BOOM 💥 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/ebyDOeJVKB — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 Offense final three quarters – When it was apparent that the Cardinals could not run the ball, and the offensive line wasn’t going to keep their pass rushers out for long, the Rams began stacking the box with seven and eight defenders. Final numbers for this offense: 142 total yards, 6 first downs, 0 for 6 third down efficiency, 0 for 1 on fourth down, 3.6 yards per play average, 34 rushing yards, allowed five sacks, zero Red Zone appearances, two turnovers, 3.9 yards per pass completion average, and time of possession: 17:37. Yes, it was that bad. Can you imagine how tired the Arizona defense was today? Cardinals’ drives beginning with Quarter 2: punt, punt, INT, half, INT, downs, punt. CB Kalen King – On the Rams first possession, King allowed WR T Atwell to gain 31-yards to the Cardinals’ nine which eventually set up a field goal. King was way off Atwell and then missed the tackle before scoring the TD. In the second quarter on a second-and-10, King lost WR Xavier smith who rambled 22-yards to Arizona’s 46. FIRST NFL TOUCHDOWN FOR XAVIER SMITH!! 🙌 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/ZIhTbMxp7i — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 With 9:37 left before halftime, King played off Smith who gained 18-yards. After the Cardinals were intercepted, the Rams were back in business at Arizona’s 32. On their third play, King was way off Smith and then missed the tackle before scoring the TD with just 13 seconds left in the half. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – Is it wrong that only one company makes the game Monopoly? DT L.J. Collier – Had the sack in the second quarter, but the Rams ran up the gut too many times to count. Three tackles with one sack, one tackle for loss, and one QB hit. Cookin' in the Kinchens 👨‍🍳 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/D0hbu0qVOR — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 WR Devin Duvernay – He had the 31-yard gain in the first quarter, but with 37 seconds to play in the first half, Beck rolled out and found an open Duvernay who tipped the ball up instead of securing the rock, and Rams’ S Kamren Kinchens not only got the interception, but Los Angeles scored another touchdown with just ticks left in the first half. But yet Beck got the negative stat.

title: Carson Beck starts off strong, then the Arizona Cardinals get blown out by Los Angeles Rams
summary: It did not start too bad for Carson Beck. In the Arizona Cardinals rookies first two drives he lead the team to two field goals. So, in two scoring drives Beck was 5/6 for 69 yards. After that Beck was 6/12 for 39 yards, two interceptions and a fumble and the Arizona Cardinals did not […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals greets teammate Tyler Allgeier #22 before a game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images It did not start too bad for Carson Beck. In the Arizona Cardinals rookies first two drives he lead the team to two field goals. Beck was 3/3 for 34 yards 2-3 for 35 yards So, in two scoring drives Beck was 5/6 for 69 yards. After that Beck was 6/12 for 39 yards, two interceptions and a fumble and the Arizona Cardinals did not score again. First off, none of this is on Carson Beck. The second interception, egregious, but he was in a position where he is trying to make a play. However, it was 10-6 and the Cardinals were about 5-7 yards away from kicking a makeable (albeit very long) field goal. Instead, Devin Durvenay causes an interception off a drop, the Rams go down and score and we get a 17-6 game at the half instead of at worst a 10-6 game. From there, it was the flood gates. Rams touchdown drive to make it 24-6. Beck interception… 14 yards on offense. Rams touchdown drive to make it 31-6. Arizona Cardinals go four and out, gain nine yards. Field goal, 34-6. Five play, 13 yards, and a punt!!! At this point, the game is already out of hand, you are down 4 scores, just go for it. Instead, the Rams get the ball back and run 12 minutes and 15 seconds off the clock with former Cardinals great Ronnie Rivers accounting for 81 yards rushing, and ending the game. This was a nightmare… disaster… expected? We are onto the Chiefs… Oh god, we are onto the Chiefs.

title: Is Sunday the beginning of the Carson Beck era?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals opened training camp with four good quarterback prospects. Jacoby Brissett was listed as the starter, and after the team couldn’t sign Jimmy Garoppolo for the backup role, they settled on seasoned veteran Gardner Minshew. 2025 holdover Kedon Slovis was already under contract. Then, the team selected Carson Beck of Miami in the […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up before the game against the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. The Broncos defeated the Cardinals 30-16. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals opened training camp with four good quarterback prospects. Jacoby Brissett was listed as the starter, and after the team couldn’t sign Jimmy Garoppolo for the backup role, they settled on seasoned veteran Gardner Minshew. 2025 holdover Kedon Slovis was already under contract. Then, the team selected Carson Beck of Miami in the third round in April’s NFL Draft. RELATED: GET TO KNOW CARSON BECK It appeared to be a solid position group. Fast forward to this week. This room has just one of the four listed on the main roster, and is now comprised of Minshew headed to IR, a 40-year-old who collects NFL game-used helmets, and two rookies. Journeyman Josh Johnson was signed on Monday. He has played 11 years in the NFL, despite coming into the league in 2009. He has been a roster member of 19 NFL clubs, as well as three other teams in other leagues. He has played in 50 NFL games with 11 starts and is a lifelong backup. Johnson has thrown for 2,669 career yards, which shows he is strictly a backup. Cardinals officially named rookie QB Carson Beck their starter for Sunday’s game vs. the Rams. pic.twitter.com/AvRfj4ISvo — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 11, 2026 On the heels of inking Johnson, the front office also signed rookie Joey Aguilar off the Jacksonville Jaguars practice squad as the new QB3. On Wednesday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur named his starting quarterback for the game against the Rams. His choice is Beck. And that should be his choice. Carson Beck… your time is NOW, kid. https://t.co/EINPxJ9Pef — John Frascella (Football) (@NFLFrascella) November 9, 2026 Beck has been to every function Arizona offered since being drafted. Every mini-camp, every OTA, every training camp practice, and he has been situated as QB3 for his entire time as a member of the Cardinals, except for this past weekend against the Seattle Seahawks, when he was elevated as the backup. The coaching staff needed to determine what they had in Beck this season anyway. There has been talk about how Arizona should draft a quarterback high in the 2027 NFL Draft and should be picking in the Top-10. But if Beck is suitable, why would they waste that selection on yet another rookie quarterback? Offensive and defensive lines are more positions of need. But Beck seems ready. If you ask him, he was ready Week 1 to step in. What a choice for the youngster to start his first official NFL game. The Cardinals defeated the Rams 18-16 in Week 6 on six Chad Ryland field goals when the offense could not finish drives. LA was supposed to be one of the NFC’s elite clubs, but has fallen to a 5-4-0 record in one of the toughest divisions in the league. The Rams are currently on a three-game winning streak. They have beaten a lot of bad-to-mediocre teams, and lost to every good club on their schedule. This weekend, All-World EDGE rusher Myles Garrett is supposed to start his first game as a member of the Rams. He will be paired with another future gold-jacket defender, DT Aaron Donald. That in itself is terrifying. To add to the horrific situation, Arizona’s offensive line is missing OT Paris Johnson, who would be the perfect match to wall off Garrett. Johnson is on IR after he tore his left biceps in Week 4 and is gone for the year. The game could have been an epic battle between Superman and Batman, although Garrett can’t shoot laser beams from his eyes. Arizona’s offensive line now consists of their third left tackle, Josh Fryar, and the return of RG Isaiah Adams. Overall, this group has struggled mightily and is ranked #31. That’s out of 32 teams for those scoring at home. They are weak at pass blocking, but that’s okay because they are also feeble at run blocking, so they have mastered consistency. Here is more bad news. Center Hjalte Froholdt is on concussion protocol from the Seahawks game. That usually takes 10 days to get clearance, which most likely means he won’t be available for the home contest this weekend against Los Angeles. Yikes. The depth chart lists Kingsley Eguakun as his backup, who has played in seven NFL games with two starts. Can it get any worse? Yeah, one of Beck’s main playmakers, receiver Michael Wilson, is also gone for the year. He fractured his neck on the fourth play of last weekend’s loss to Seattle but he remained in the game and finished. This comes off the heels of trading away WR Marv Harrison, plus injuries to receivers Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks. Both are now on IR, spending their days rehabbing and playing “Call of Duty.” Not piling on here, okay, we are piling on. Arizona has struggled with a running game. They rank #19 in yards gained and #19 in average yards per carry at 4.1. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is more of a distant memory and is sitting on IR. So are James Conner and Trey Benson. Tyler Allgeier is sitting in the pole position at RB, but he has been a roller coaster this year. Behind him are Bam Knight and former practice squad player Evan Hull. After gaining 147 yards on 11 carries and scoring two touchdowns against the Dallas Cowboys, this past weekend Allgeier had just 46 yards on 17 attempts and no scores in the loss to the Seahawks. Establishing a rushing attack is critical; otherwise, the defensive linemen fly off the snap and don’t concern themselves with the running back as they head straight to the quarterback. Is Beck ready? The more important question is: Can Beck survive his first official NFL game?

title: Falcons – Chiefs recap: Wilting away in Mercedes-Benz Stadium
summary: If you were daydreaming about an improbable run, simply hoping for a miracle, or just looking for something enjoyable as the season very slowly winds down, the Falcons were determined to ensure your Sunday left you bereft. The quality of the opponent aside—the Chiefs are very good, obviously—this was the bottom for the Falcons, and […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Downs #12 of the Kansas City Chiefs carries the ball after a reception defended by DeMarcco Hellams #23 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you were daydreaming about an improbable run, simply hoping for a miracle, or just looking for something enjoyable as the season very slowly winds down, the Falcons were determined to ensure your Sunday left you bereft. The quality of the opponent aside—the Chiefs are very good, obviously—this was the bottom for the Falcons, and the point at which team and fanbase alike need to fully accept certain hard truths about the Atlanta Falcons of 2026. Those truths? The first and most obvious one is that this is a bad football team at the moment. Despite some promising signings and trades, the talent level is not good enough across the board to make them a playoff-caliber team even in a weak NFC South, something the Falcons appeared to accept when they traded away Jessie Bates and Ryan Neuzil. Also, while this team has more resources than just any other team in the NFL, they are going to need every dollar and draft pick just to overhaul what they have in a way that brings their talent level up to where it needs to be and exorcises all the weird ghosts that have been awkwardly floating around this team for most of the last decade. And finally , there are very few positions on this roster that are actually settled with 2027 looming, meaning this team could look very, very different than it does now by May of next year. There is a Sunday every year in this miserable stretch of losing seasons where the terrible weight of losing lands especially heavy on my shoulders, and this is the one for 2026. More than likely, I’ll come out of the bye ready to joke about the Falcons reeling off some unlikely wins and finishing this year with a losing record for the ninth straight season, and we’ll all lock arms and head into a pivotal offseason daring to dream of something better. But I’ll tell you with naked honesty that this Sunday got to me in a way the previous nine games did not, as I saw the this team continue a frankly brutal three game slide and make it fully clear just how limited their ceiling for this season really is. At 3-7 and driving that stake into this team’s hopes with relish, the Falcons ensured I can fully give up on 2026 and just try to find the bright spots in what’s to come, and I do intend to take full advantage. I hope you will, as will. For now, though, we’ll be digesting a game where Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and the Chiefs ran all over Atlanta despite not having Kenneth Walker, and the defense was still the more impressive unit. Atlanta’s offense has now scored 17 or fewer points in three straight games, which begs the question of whether Tommy Rees is the right coordinator, Penix is the right quarterback, and almost every player on that side of the ball is going to be part of the next great Falcons offense outside of Bijan Robinson, Chris Lindstrom, and Drake London. That seems like an overreaction to one game—and perhaps even three games—but this is an evaluation year for a regime with the resources to make substantial changes in 2027, and an offense studded with talented players looking this crummy will give them genuine pause. The Chiefs are a good, well-coached team, but the gulf between them and a frankly hapless Falcons team should give them further pause. The bye week will give these Falcons a chance to reset and try to make something of the rest of this year, but the fate of this team seems beyond obvious at this point. As we have so many times over the past decade, we Falcons fans are left to look ahead to better days after the last bloom has fallen off the rose. May this coming offseason finally bring those long-elusive days to us, so that we may put games like in the past where they belong. On to the full recap. The Good He hasn’t looked superhuman very often lately, but Bijan Robinson remains a player defenses fear and a back capable of breaking some jaw-dropping runs. His best carries in this game were like that, where through sheer will, balance, and power he managed to reel off 10-plus yards despite the at-times nonexistent threat of the Falcons passing game working against him. Someday the offense will sputter to life again and he’ll look like the Bijan of old. Jahan Dotson would ideally be your third receiver, but even with his ups and downs he’s been a very credible receiving threat for this team, and has had some really good weeks. He was a better pass away from a touchdown today and finished second on the team with three receptions for 63 yards, and is on his way to a career year in an offense that can and wants to get him the ball. Drake London deserves a medal of some kind. His career has been defined by a revolving door of play callers, quarterbacks, and surrounding personnel, and yet he continually blocks his ass off and shows out as the team’s best receiver. He somehow had over 100 yards in this one despite the passing game being dormant much of the day, and London deserves better than the results this team sees in the win and loss columns weekly. Harold Perkins had a couple of ugly reps on the first defensive drive, and that must have galvanized him because he was a man possessed after that point. Perkins was fantastic against the run, a demon as a pass rusher, and more stingy in coverage after that point, standing out over and over again no matter what he was asked to do. There’s little question Perkins is a player the Falcons plan to count on in 2027 and beyond, and he showed why on Sunday. Brandon Dorlus and Gervon Dexter remain one of the best duos on the interior in the NFL, and Dexter in particular was a man possessed with five pressures, three run stops, and multiple plays where he rampaged through the overmatched Chiefs offensive line like Godzilla through the financial district. If the Falcons can bring more consistent pressure off the edge to help out D&D, quarterbacks will be miserable. The defense did the heavy lifting on Sunday against a good Chiefs team minus key pieces, and reminded us they’re the unit that is much closer to being a finished product, even if the overall results were still rough. It’s not that difficult to talk yourself into Billy Bowman Jr., Xavier Watts, Kendal Daniels, Perkins, Dorlus, Dexter, and company just getting better a year from now with better complementary pieces around them. Jake Moody came uncomfortably close to missing an extra point, but otherwise he was excellent. Moody hit both short field goal tries and had the NFL’s first successful onside kick attempt, with a major assist from Chris Blair, in his Falcons debut. Hopefully he can prove to be the team’s long-term solution at kicker, and the early returns were promising, even if the kicks weren’t particularly challenging. Blair, as mentioned above, had a phenomenal play. He wasn’t quite there on a potential touchdown pass from Penix, but the onsides kick recovery was flawless, as Blair very confidently grabbed it away from a sleepwalking Xavier Worthy and kept his feet inbounds to give Atlanta a last gasp chance they couldn’t take full advantage of. The Ugly Yes, the offense has holes and weaknesses that need to be addressed in the offseason, but it’s not so bereft of talent that it should look like it did on the first four drives. The Falcons started this game with one productive Bijan Robinson carry, one eight yard catch for Kyle Pitts, and a whole lot of incompletions, penalties, and ineptitude that led to four straight three-and-outs. That represented all four drives in the first quarter, and was evidence enough that this team selling at the deadline was an accurate read of their potential. It was, as the broadcast noted, the first time since 2000 that the Falcons started the game with four…

title: Week 10 Snap Reactions: We’re on to 2027
summary: The Atlanta Falcons are 3-7 after getting lit up by the Kansas City Chiefs. The offense looks worse than ever, and the defense is out of adjustments. Here are the Week 10 snap reactions. Did they healthy scratch the wrong Terrell? After getting torched by the Bengals, the Falcons made A.J. Terrell captain of the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Downs #12 of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a catch for a touchdown against Billy Bowman Jr. #33 of the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons are 3-7 after getting lit up by the Kansas City Chiefs . The offense looks worse than ever, and the defense is out of adjustments. Here are the Week 10 snap reactions. Did they healthy scratch the wrong Terrell? After getting torched by the Bengals, the Falcons made A.J. Terrell captain of the game as a vote of confidence; it did not matter. Terrell got smoked by the Chiefs WR4 on a simple double move. Later, it looked like he busted his zone coverage, letting Emmitt Johnson skip into the end zone. The cornerback is having one of the worst seasons of his career, and there’s still a lot of football left. Atlanta needs to figure out its DB shuffling cause what they are currently doing isn’t working. Filthy route from Cyrus Allen 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/YNh2IdJZjU — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Tommy Rees is no wunderkind Even Zac Robinson wasn’t this bad. Rees calls plays like he’s never seen a football game before. His best player on offense is an afterthought until it’s too late; his screen game has benefited opposing defenses, and moving to the sideline won’t fix any of these issues. Kevin Stefanski has given Rees years to figure it out. He couldn’t do it in Cleveland, and he can’t do it with a fleet of top-10 picks. He is not the guy. Penix struggles continue Pre-game, Matt Ryan said growth isn’t linear and that Penix has shown he can play; he also ended the interview by saying the quarterback has to stack good performances. He’s stacking bad ones. You can’t miss a wide-open Drake London to start the game; slow starts will always catch up to you. Missing Austin Hooper in the end zone was even more inexcusable. Penix is auditioning for his 5th-year option, and it isn’t going well. The garbage time numbers won’t save him, especially when there’s an interception mixed in there. Tommy Rees deserves fair criticism, but there has been many times this season where we have seen this from the #Falcons offense pic.twitter.com/9Dd4q1NeUp — Miles Garrett (@MilesGarrettTV) November 15, 2026 Jeff Ulbrich is out of moves The defense gave up an opening-drive touchdown but tightened up afterward. However, that didn’t last long, as the offense couldn’t give them any support. It was nice to see Harold Perkins Jr. have a great day after an early red zone mishap, but CJ Henderson picked the worst time to turn in a bad performance. The effort overall was not good enough. Emmitt Johnson looked like Emmitt Smith, and wide receivers you’ve never heard of torched the defense. The unit has come undone, and Ulbrich can keep hitting shuffle on his lineup, but that isn’t going to fix the systemic issues. They can’t stop the run and therefore become vulnerable to the pass. Injuries have taken their toll, but this scheme needs more than talent; it needs legitimate adjustments. 348 yards & 5 TDs for @PatrickMahomes 👏 pic.twitter.com/WUMyRQsznx — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Eyes on 2027 The Falcons are gonna put up a united front in the presser, but the truth lies within their actions; this team is focused on the offseason. They stripped it down as much as they could, and this is the result. Players are auditioning for their 2027 roster spots, and they shouldn’t be the only ones. The Falcons have now lost three in a row and dropped to 3-7. Enjoy the bye week; it’ll be your first Sunday without disappointment since October.

title: Falcons – Chiefs instant recap: It’s over
summary: Even in lost seasons, you wait for the Falcons to make it official. Atlanta had shown enough life in the recent past to think they might have a surprise or two left in them at 3-6, and so while I counseled that you should leave your expectations behind for the rest of 2026, I did […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs breaks up a pass intended for Jahan Dotson #4 of the Atlanta Falcons during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Even in lost seasons, you wait for the Falcons to make it official. Atlanta had shown enough life in the recent past to think they might have a surprise or two left in them at 3-6, and so while I counseled that you should leave your expectations behind for the rest of 2026, I did indulge in a little hope. No longer. This season is over. The 3-7 Falcons, who can do nothing on offense despite the presence of a top ten selection at quarterback in Michael Penix Jr., maybe the best running back in football in Bijan Robinson, a great receiver in Drake London, and a well-paid tight end room and offensive line, are cooked. Their defense is far more game and has the foundation of a really good unit, but as the afternoon wore on, they devolved into frustration and sloppiness. This is a team that is not ready to be great, and aside from a couple of beautiful weeks, they don’t even look ready to be competent. We know how this goes. The coaching staff is not getting fired after one year, the front office is just beginning to piece this team together, and there’s still seven games to go. The Falcons must play out the string and try to figure out what they want to be, and it will be up to this still-fresh regime to make 2026 and the years preceding it a distant memory. We have put our hope in that outcome over and over again and have gotten nothing from it, so we are bucking history when we assume things will be different in 2027. What choice do we have, though? For the moment, it is beyond clear that this team is going nowhere this season, and we are left to watch them play out the string. The bye week allows us to heal up a bit and try this thing again, but there is Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. Please don’t read it. 1st Quarter The Chiefs deferred and kicked off, with Khalil Herbert getting it to the 29 yard line. Michael Penix Jr. threw it too high for Drake London to come down with it on first down. Penix then tried Dotson and missed again. Penix then hit Kyle Pitts for eight yards. Jake Bailey’s punt rolled into the end zone for a touchback. Emmett Johnson’s first carry went for a first down. Then a defender slipped working against Travis Kelce and he got a huge gain. Johnson then picked up six yards and then 12 more on the ground. Mahomes took a shot to the end zone intended for Cyrus Allen working against Billy Bowman Jr. but Bowman was right on him. Mahomes then scrambled and slid for nine yards. Johnson then plowed ahead for a first down. Johnson rolled through contact for four yards. Justin Fields tried a carry and was stopped by Cameron Thomas. A swing pass to Johnson went for a touchdown after multiple missed tackles. 7-0 Chiefs. Herbert took it almost to the 50 yard line. Bijan took it nine yards on first down. Penix was then sacked on second down by George Karlaftis. On third down, Penix got away from pressure and had to throw it away. Punt, and after the Chiefs returner muffed it, Sydney Brown got him at the four yard line. 2 The Chiefs got out as Mahomes threw a short pass the receiver took for close to 20 yards. Mahomes then skipped it into the turf on the next play. On a delayed handoff, Johnson ran into his lineman and Dexter for a yard. A quick pass to Johnson went for seven yards on the screen. Punt, and Zaccheaus took it to about the 25 yard line. Bijan lost a yard on first down. Then Penix missed on a deep ball and Jake Matthews got called for holding. A quick pass to Jahan Dotson went for seven yards. A false start on Jawaan Taylor followed. A swing pass to Khalil Herbert fell incomplete. Punt, and there was a Chiefs hold on the return. Mahomes hit Josh Downs over the middle for a first down and 11 more. Rashee Rice then dropped a screen pass. A quick swing pass to Johnson went for three yards, with Harold Perkins Jr. on the tackle. Pressure got to Mahomes on the next play and he threw it up to Johnson, who dropped a difficult catch attempt. A hold on the play was declined. A false start on the punt attempt backed Kansas City up further. Punt. A swing pass to Bijan lost two yards. A pass to London went for seven yards. Penix then fired one down the sideline to London and it was incomplete. 2nd Quarter Punt, and a fair catch around the 10 yard line. Johnson carried it for five yards. Johnson was stopped cold by Perkins on second down. Mahomes missed on third down under pressure. Punt, and it wasn’t a great one. Bijan rolled through the middle for 17 yards. Bijan tried to dance and got three yards. A bad exchange from a late Corey Levin snap resulted in Penix fumbling and falling on the ball for a four yard loss. With pressure coming in, Penix hit Dotson over the middle for a first down. Bijan was then hit early for a minimal gain, but a neutral zone infraction gave Atlanta five yards. Bijan then showed nice patience, stutter stepped, and picked up close to 15 yards again. Penix scrambled away from pressure for a few yards, but a holding call backed the Falcons up. Bijan tried to cut it back but the Chiefs smothered it for a minimal gain.A quick pass to Zaccheaus got seven or eight yards. Penix then tried to run away from pressure and was taken down. Jake Moody hit the 28 yard field goal try to make it 7-3 Chiefs. Perkins drilled the return just past the 25 yard line. Johnson then went right and picked up a first down. Then Mahomes scrambled away from pressure and hit Rice for a first down. Johnson was tackled for a five yard loss by Zach Harrison and LaCale London. Xavier Worthy dove to try to make the catch and missed it. On third down, Mahomes tried to fake and scramble, but was hit after a gain of a few yards by Perkins and then a holding call on the Chiefs that the Falcons accepted. On third down and a mile, Mahomes did hit Rice for about 10 yards, but the Chiefs still had to punt, with Zaccheaus getting to about the 25. Bijan picked up five yards on a plunge. Penix then threw it away on second down, for some reason. Then Penix hit Pitts on the sideline for maybe a yard. Punt. Johnson took it two yards. Then a screen to Johnson went 39 yards after he picked up speed and nobody was near him. Mahomes then found Downs for a first down. Mahomes then threw it into the dirt looking toward Downs. Noah Gray then caught one for eight yards. The Chiefs then picked up a flag for 12 men on the field. Rice was tackled after getting within a couple of yards of a first down. Harrison Butker’s kick was good, but there was a flag on Atlanta, and the Chiefs decided to keep going for it. Mahomes then hit Downs for a touchdown. 14-3 Chiefs. Penix fired one to London, who took a big hit and had it jarred loose. Penix then hit London down the sideline for 37 yards, but time expired as London rolled out of bounds. 3rd Quarter A quick run up the middle went for a couple of yards for Emmett Johnson. Then Mahomes was sacked by like four dudes, with Brandon Dorlus getting there first. A screen to Kelce went for a few yards, but the Chiefs had to punt, with no return. Bijan picked up 13 yards and a first down, following that up with seven yards. Jawaan Taylor then had a false start, and Bijan was stonewalled on second down. Penix’s pass was then batted down by Karlaftis. Punt. Mahomes threw it away with pressure closing in on first down. Rice caught a screen and got about four yards. The blitz then got home and Mahomes had to throw it away. Zaccheaus took the punt return to the 33 yard line. Penix finally hit London over the middle for a first down. Bijan plunged ahead for two yards, and then evaded two tackles for five yards. Bijan then went into the teeth of the defense and was tackled for a loss of a yard. On fourth and 4, the Falcons went for…

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Chiefs
summary: The Atlanta Falcons host the Kansas City Chiefs, looking to bounce back with a win against one of the decade’s most successful teams. With the Chiefs in the thick of contention at the top of the AFC, they’re a litmus test for whether the Falcons can knock off another top team and pull off a […]
full_text: Falcon's RB #7 Bijan Robinson celebrates a touchdown during the 2026 NFL Madrid Game American football match between Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, on November 8, 2026. The National Football League return to Madrid with this 2026 NFL regular season game for the second time following 2025 first edition at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons host the Kansas City Chiefs , looking to bounce back with a win against one of the decade’s most successful teams. With the Chiefs in the thick of contention at the top of the AFC, they’re a litmus test for whether the Falcons can knock off another top team and pull off a home upset like they did three weeks ago against San Francisco . Five Falcons will be among the most tested in this matchup. Michael Penix Jr. The formidable Chiefs defense will be another big test for Michael Penix, thanks to defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. Spags’ strategy will likely lean on blitzing Penix to exploit his struggles under pressure and using disguised coverages to confuse the young quarterback. For Penix’s evaluation, it’s important to see how he handles one of the NFL’s most challenging defensive schemes and stays poised amid the controlled chaos. Bijan Robinson Bijan Robinson, along with the Falcons’ run game, will be tasked with taking pressure off Penix, but will be tested against one of the NFL’s best run defenses. Whatever category you want to measure, whether it’s yards, yards per carry, EPA, or yards before and after contact, the Chiefs rank among the top 10 teams across the board . Facing four other Top 11-ranked run defenses so far this year, Robinson has averaged 76.5 yards per game and 4.6 yards per carry. That looks impressive at face value, but his success rate in those games was 36 percent, which ranks among the bottom 5 in the NFL, according to NextGenStats . As the NFL’s leading rusher, Robinson has racked up most of his production against lesser defenses, averaging 115 yards per game, 5.6 yards per carry, with a second-ranked 52 percent success rate in his five other outings. Essentially, the numbers show that the quality of competition dictates the Falcons’ success when establishing the run. Given the Chiefs’ stout defense, it’s another huge trial to see whether this trend continues. Corey Levin With Ryan Neuzil’s surprising departure at Tuesday’s trade deadline, Corey Levin now has to fill the void at center. The Falcons likely moved Neuzil due to declining play as of late, and expect there to be minimal dropoff to career backup Levin. However, that will be thoroughly tested on Sunday against the Chiefs’ pressure looks and the formidable presence of defensive tackle Chris Jones. One area where Neuzil struggled was with protection calls against various blitzes. Expect Spagnuolo to challenge whether Levin proves an upgrade in that area. Kendal Daniels After a solid performance against the 49ers in Divine Deablo’s stead, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels has been less impactful in the last two games. With Deablo out for this Chiefs game , Daniels will once again be forced to take over the mantle as the leader in the middle of the Falcons’ defense. Even with Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker out of the lineup , the Falcons’ run defense will still be challenged by explosive rookie replacement, Emmett Johnson. With many doubting if Deablo will return to Atlanta in 2027, this is another opportunity to see how ready Daniels is to take over calling the defense. DeMarcco Hellams Stepping into the void left by Jessie Bates’ departure will be backup safety, DeMarcco Hellams. Hellams took over for Bates during training camp, when the latter was sidelined with a back injury for multiple weeks. But since then, Hellams has barely seen the field on defense, with just 24 snaps over nine games. However, he’ll see a lot more this week as a starter. Hellams is known for his hard-hitting style, but his biggest challenge against Kansas City may be covering tight end Travis Kelce. Coverage has been Hellams’ biggest vulnerability since arriving in Atlanta, making his assignment against Kelce a trial by fire before the Falcons hit their bye week and potentially reshuffle the secondary. At 3-6, the Falcons need to pass this high-stakes exam to keep pace in the NFC South playoff race and take some momentum into their bye week. Beating heavyweights like the Chiefs is a trial they’ve already passed in 2026, but they’ll need to do it again to prove it wasn’t a fluke. Can you name other Falcons who will be important in this Week 10 battle?
author: Aaron Freeman

title: Falcons vs. Chiefs: What will Week 10’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: The Falcons cap off a very eventful week which saw them trade away major contributors on both offense and defense in Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil, with a meeting against the team that built the dynasty of the modern NFL in the Kansas City Chiefs. Atlanta is currently in a unique situation, sitting in […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 22: Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons runs the ball after a catch during the fourth quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons cap off a very eventful week which saw them trade away major contributors on both offense and defense in Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil, with a meeting against the team that built the dynasty of the modern NFL in the Kansas City Chiefs. Atlanta is currently in a unique situation, sitting in between playoff contention due to their pathetic division and a top 10 pick, and their decision to ship out contributors indicates that they have no delusions on the present as one eye firmly stays looking toward the future. With the bye week ahead, the Birds have an opportunity to really lock in on having the best of both worlds with a victory, and possibly a more gleaming future with continued losses. It’s a rare scenario where the perspective can be that of glass half full either way. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 10, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They’ll stamp in another victory against an opponent they were wholly unlikely to defeat, as their resume will have very impressive victories over the Packers, 49ers and now Chiefs up until this point. Their continued identity of showing up against the good teams will be solidified. It’s hard to believe, sitting here at 3-6 and in the basement of the NFC South, but the Falcons would put themselves in a decent position in their division going into the bye week. With Tampa on a bye, Atlanta would move ahead of them and they would jump the loser of the Saints – Panthers matchup this weekend to control sole possession of second place, just 0.5 games back of first. The odds won’t shift much in either direction for Atlanta as far as the playoffs are concerned, according to playoffstatus.com. They currently sit at 17%, a win would increase that to 21% regardless of other outcomes around the NFL. The Falcons would break a three game losing streak at the hands of the Chiefs, earning their first victory in this matchup since 2012. If the Falcons lose They would go into the bye week likely with an even greater eye toward the future. I would predict that coming out on the other side we would see the likes of Aveion Terrell, Billy Bowman and other young pieces be given more of an opportunity over veterans. They would remain in play in the division no matter what, sitting at 1.5 games back of either the Saints or the Panthers. If Panthers are victorious and if they win their matchup again next week while Atlanta is on the bye, the Birds would find themselves at a full 2.0 games back with no tiebreaker essentially needing to make up three full games in the second half of the season. With games against the Lions and Vikings on the other side, the playoff dream is likely to be slipping quickly. The playoff odds would decrease from 17% to a meager 13% and then even lower than that depending on what happens next week during the bye. As unlikely as it may be, a Cardinals victory against the Rams would see Atlanta’s pick at minimum reach as high as 8th at the end of this week.
author: Adnan Ikic

title: Ravens discussion: loss to Chargers would be most embarrassing since…?
summary: The Ravens have some bad losses on their ledger over the last several years. Some bad losses. But even with all the blown leads and second-half collapses in recent years, falling to the Chargers – the winless Chargers – on Monday night might be a new low. The following is true of Jim Harbaugh’s squad this […]
full_text: Nov 25, 2024; Inglewood, California, USA; Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry (22) carries the ball against Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Kristian Fulton (7) and cornerback Elijah Molden (22) in the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Ravens have some bad losses on their ledger over the last several years. Some bad losses. But even with all the blown leads and second-half collapses in recent years, falling to the Chargers – the winless Chargers – on Monday night might be a new low. The following is true of Jim Harbaugh’s squad this year: Ranks 32nd in scoring Ranks 28th in points allowed -98 point differential through eight games… …good for a 12.25-point average margin of defeat 18.9% of offensive drives end in a turnover The Chargers will also be without star wide receiver Ladd McConkey on Monday night, while a few other key players are questionable. All of these factors should tip the scales in the Ravens’ direction, even with Jacoby Brissett set to make his debut. But there is a reason winless seasons are rare. This is an Any Given Sunday league, wherein last week’s defeat is forgotten in the fog of a new war. The Chargers are probably going to beat someone eventually. Wouldn’t it be so spot-on for the Ravens’ 2026 season if it happened in Baltimore on Monday night? That would almost certanily be the Ravens’ most embarrassing loss this season. That’s saying something after off three straight defeats of 22 points or more, but those came against three of the best teams in the AFC with a combination of Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano under center. Last year’s 44-10 loss to the Texans looms large given the margin, but what more were you expecting from Cooper Rush, a bad O-line against a fiercesome Houston front, and a suddenly banged-up defense? My pick: Week 10 of the 2021 season, a 22-10 loss to the Dolphins. The Ravens had no answers for Brian Flores’ defense. Lamar Jackson could not summon his usual magic to dance away from pressure and make plays downfield, and Baltimore’s offense walked on the field like lambs to the slaughter every drive. A solid showing from the defense – ironically, against Brissett for much of the game – was not enough to rescue one of the worst showings of Jackson’s career. Dishonorable mention: Come to think of it, Week 2 of the 2022 season – Mike Macdonald’s second game as defensive coordinator – was an embarrassing loss, too. The Ravens seem to only throttle the Dolphins or melt down in spectacular fashion.

Unlike some of the league’s international games this year, including the Ravens’ thrilling win in Rio, this morning’s matchup in Munich between the Patriots and the Lions was effectively over before halftime. Detroit took a commanding 21-3 lead with Tommy DeVito replacing an injured Drake Maye. This afternoon presents a number of intriguing faceoffs with major playoff implications, including several between division rivals. With Cousins back in the fold after a solid start to the year in Las Vegas and Brian Flores’ defense demolishing opposing offenses, the Vikings could round into one of the league’s most complete teams. Cousins’ Vikings (re)debut will take place against a Packers defense that quietly ranks 11th in yards and points allowed this year despite season-ending injuries to Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargave. Micah Parsons is still working his way back from last year’s ACL tear, too, so the unit should get a major boost down the stretch. Green Bay has a massive run/pass disparity on the offensive side of the ball with the league’s worst rushing game dragging down Jordan Love’s explosive aerial attack. He threw for 353 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, the most of any opposing passer this year, but committed two turnovers that contributed to a 39-24 loss. Tune in for what will probably be some ugly football. Top 4:00 p.m. game: Seattle Seahawks (5-4) @ Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) The Seahawks are 6.5-point road favorites in an inter-conference matchup, so this game is more about the storylines than the competitiveness or playoff implications. Raiders No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza is making his first career start, just in time for his head coach Klint Kubiak’s first game against his former team. As for the other two late afternoon matchups…let’s just say I won’t be glued to the television. The Los Angeles Rams should be able to take care of the Carson Beck-led Arizona Cardinals, and the San Francisco 49ers offense could drop 50 points on the Dallas Cowboys defense. And then there’s Sunday night. Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Cincinnati Bengals in a primetime faceoff that has massive implications for the Ravens and the AFC North. Again, it’s too early for Baltimore’s postseason odds to sway wildly based on tonight’s result, but it may be important later in the year. Baltimore Beatdown will have a separate game thread for Steelers-Bengals, so be sure to check back in closer to the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff!

title: Takeaways from Bills win over Jets
summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the Jets 31-12 in Week 10 on inside MetLife Stadium, in a game that went from defensive slugfest in the first two quarters to blowout in the second half. At 8-1, the Bills are out to their best start since 1991. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. I’m glad we […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills beat the Jets 31-12 in Week 10 on inside MetLife Stadium, in a game that went from defensive slugfest in the first two quarters to blowout in the second half. At 8-1, the Bills are out to their best start since 1991. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. I’m glad we saw some pass-game pop within structure During the Bills’ four-game win streak entering this game, which included dominance after the bye week, it felt natural to narrow focus on Buffalo’s entire operation, checking for any component of the team that could improve. And in wins over the Rams, Raiders, Ravens, and Vikings, Buffalo seemingly lacked efficiency from the pass game in a classic sense. You know, Josh Allen standing in the pocket and completing the football to pass catchers within the intended design of the play. It hadn’t happened at the frequency one would expect in games in which the Bills scored 37, 33, 36, and 23 points (against the No. 1 defense in football on the road). But in the second half against the Jets, the Bills demonstrated their ability to move the ball through the air in a normal, rhythmic way… at all levels of the field. And there was an explosive element that’s been mostly missing over the past four outings. For as good as Allen has been creating this season, and for as reliable as Buffalo has been on the ground, this team needs to be able to win with classic dropback passing too, and in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets, the Bills did just that. Defensive depth shines The turf at MetLife Stadium has one of the most notorious reputations in the NFL. And a handful of Bills were dinged with injuries in this game, unsurprisingly. Here’s to hoping the likes of Christian Benford, Dorian Williams, and Dee Alford are OK. In their absence, Buffalo’s defensive depth was immediately tested. And it shined. The Bills defense didn’t skip a beat with Kaleb Elarms-Orr, Jordan Hancock, and Maxwell Hairston on the field. But it wasn’t just that trio making relief appearances for those sidelined in-game with injury. Rookie T.J. Parker played the second-most snaps of his NFL career to date (38) and had five pressures with two sacks on 26 pass-rush snaps. Javon Solomon chipped in 12 snaps and registered a pair of pressures in his two pass-rush opportunities. As we’ve come to know during the Allen era, depth can be vital in the playoffs, and Buffalo’s backups are not only getting a decent amount of run this regular season but they’re playing respectable football. Hats off to Spencer Brown Brown was listed as doubtful going into this game. Ankle injury. He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday. Then he told reporters while warming up pre-game he was going to play. And I don’t think anyone would’ve blamed him if he struggled against surging rookie, No. 2 overall pick David Bailey, on the edge. But that didn’t happen. Per Next Gen Stats , Brown squared off with Bailey 13 times and didn’t allow a single pressure of Allen. He was also the blocker attached to star veteran linebacker DeMario Davis 10 yards downfield on James Cook’s 74-yard touchdown run that put the game away in the fourth quarter. It was such a gutsy performance from Brown, who is still getting better in Year 7 at right tackle. With his height, agility, explosiveness, balance, and power, he’s one of the most unique players at his position in football. And this game was the latest piece of evidence that Brown is incredibly tough too. James Cook is special So maybe not a takeaway just from this game, but I was reminded of just how tremendous of a football player Cook has become in his 157-yard performance in Week 10 that was capped with the long touchdown sprint. Cook isn’t Bijan Robinson or Derrick Henry. He’s not regularly jump-cutting the opponent’s entire linebacker group or running it over. He’s incredibly flexible in his lower half with outstanding vision as he works through blocks from his offensive line and one of the most dynamic open-field running backs in the game. Only Jahmyr Gibbs has more 10-plus yard runs (34) than Cook (27). And Gibbs is the only back in football with more 15-plus yard runs (16) than the Bills feature back (14). Cook is up to 971 yards on the ground this season at 5.2 yards per. He can wear down a defense three or four yards at at time — like vs. Vikings — on 31 carries, or hit explosive plays on the ground like he did against the Jets in this one. Bills linebacker group… a defensive strength? Through the first month of the 2026 campaign, this specific subheading would’ve been insane. But it’s a testament to how things can change for a team — and a position group — throughout a long season in the NFL. Terrel Bernard is 27 years old. Prime of his career. Dorian Williams is playing for a second contract. Elarms-Orr looks as ready to go in Year 1 as a team can expect from a fourth-round pick at linebacker. In this contest, that trio had 19 tackles, two tackles for loss, three total pressures, and a sack without any missed tackles. And it aligned with how the those three have played over the past month or so and certainly since the bye week. And Bernard, Williams, and KEO aren’t simply thriving downhill. In this game, they allowed five catches for 30 yards in their coverage area. And that aligns with how well the group has collectively covered this season.

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: Head coach Joe Brady and Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrate after Allen's touchdown pass against the New York Jets in the third quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets on Sunday and with the Denver Broncos on a bye, the Bills have now opened a full one-game lead in the AFC. The Kansas City Chiefs actually pass the Broncos thanks to a superiors record in the AFC West, so Buffalo’s lead is over K.C as well as the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars. In the AFC East, the New England Patriots lost in Germany, which drops them to 5-5. The Bills have a 3-game lead in the division and the Patriots have games against the Bills, Vikings, Chiefs, and Broncos still upcoming. With so many games going on still here, we will update but the headline won’t change; the Bills have a playoff picture stranglehold. Explaining the 7-2 tiebreakers in the AFC The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker at 7-2, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beat all the others, so it heads to AFC record. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed. Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card. title: Bills at Jets Week 10 postgame analysis: Buffalo dominates in New Jersey
summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets 31-12 at MetLife Stadium to improve to 8-1 and 5-0 on the road. Buffalo’s defense kept New York out of the end zone for the second straight week. Things started slow, but the Bills surged late to grind out an important AFC East win against the New […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: Keon Coleman #0, DJ Moore #2, and Khalil Shakir #10 of the Buffalo Bills celebrate after Moore's receiving touchdown against the New York Jets in the third quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets 31-12 at MetLife Stadium to improve to 8-1 and 5-0 on the road. Buffalo’s defense kept New York out of the end zone for the second straight week. Things started slow, but the Bills surged late to grind out an important AFC East win against the New York Jets in Week 10 There were plenty of thoughts running through my head as this one played out. We’ll dive into all that and more below. 1st Half This “you gotta play Josh Allen in the 1st drive” thing hasn’t worked. If Joe Brady wants to continue to do that, he gotta have a better script for the 1st drive. Too many fails so far to justify it. I like starting with some screens and run/pass options, and not just the heavy dose of running game and play action from under center. DJ Moore got good yardage on one of those. Josh can’t throw it right at a DE when he’s there, though. Run play from under center on 3rd and 2 ain’t it. I get that you call it thinking of going for it on 4th down, but still, I don’t like it. Weird pass by Josh on the following 3rd down. Very short. Defense will be under pressure to start the game well again. Great 1st defensive drive. Containing the run, forcing 3rd down, getting off the field. (Breece Hall: 11 carries, 41 yards) Adonai Mitchell had Christian Benford beat deep. Thankfully, Geno Smith threw it short, allowing Buffalo’s CB to recover. Long methodical drive by the offense. A pass to Dalton Kincaid drew a flag in the endzone. Didn’t look catchable to me. After some plays (and other defensive flags), third Tush Push conversion on the day, 7-0 Bills. 2nd defensive drive is a good one so far, forcing another 4th down (4th and 6) after Geno misses Garrett Wilson, with good aggressive press man coverage by Davison Igbinosun. Jets go for it trying to draw a penalty, and when everybody in the world knows they’re trying to make you jump, Ed Oliver falls for it. A TE tush push after it, and it’s a new set of downs for New Jersey. Nice simulated pressure by Jim Leonhard here, with Bradley Chubb dropping in coverage and Dorian Williams getting the sack. It essentially kills the Jets’ drive. Their FG is good, 7-3 Bills. (Dorian Williams: 9 tackles, 1 sack, 2 QB hits) Run/PA game at its best on this drive. Josh finds Keon Coleman on a curl after the PA for a 1st down, and it sets up the next two big runs by James Cook. Then a great crossing route vs man to Moore for another 1st. Bills in the red zone. James Cook drops a perfect pass by Josh on 2nd down. He’d have the 1st down easily if he catches it. After another pass goes incomplete (and another penalty), Tyler Bass kicks it. 10-3 Bills. Geno Smith completes 2 good passes in a row, but a holding penalty sets the Jets back. Welcome, Amani Hooker. The former Titan almost picks him off. After another penalty, Buffalo’s D does its job again and gets off the field on 3rd down. Isaiah Williams got absolutely leveled by Kaleb Elarms-Orr. Oh boy, haven’t seen a Bills linebacker hit this hard since prime Matt Milano. Brandon Spikes level hit stick. Cook opens the new drive with a five-yard run and gets a new 1st down with the 2nd run, both from shotgun. I’d like to see the Bills using gun formations more often. Another run on an RPO. Jets’ safeties are playing too aggressively, making Josh hand the ball off. Something to keep an eye on. I wouldn’t be surprised by one of those fake screen/deep pass attempts later in the game. High pass to Dawson Knox on 3rd down, could’ve hauled it in, but those ribs exposed to the hit cost him the 1st down conversion. Jets open their 2-min drill with a big pass play, but penalties negate the play. He tries it again next and hits Wilson deep for a 1st down. Jordan Hancock, filling in for the injured Dee Alford, in the blue tent. Wilson is getting hot, and Geno is taking advantage of it. Jets inside the 10. (Garrett Wilson: 7 receptions, 106 yards) 3rd down and Geno buys time, can’t find anybody and throws it away, just to get absolutely destroyed by Terrel Bernard. What’s going on with our LBs today? Well, whatever is happening, keep it up. I love those (completely legal) big hits. (Bernard last Monday vs. Minnesota: 6 tackles, 1 INT, 2 pass breakups) Geno seems hurt. TB hit him hard, but I think it’s more related to his fall, hitting his head on the ground. 3rd week in a row taking on a backup QB? Geno in the blue tent. Jets FG is good. 12 seconds left in the 1st half, 10-6 Bills. (Geno Smith: 13/21, 148 yards) Josh takes a knee, end of the 1st half. Jets will get the ball to start the 2nd. Dangerous game. I get that nobody has been able to survive the Bills’ run game for 4 quarters, but still. I’d like to see Brady mixing it up more, unleashing Josh and the passing game a bit more, especially at the beginning of the game, and daring the Jets to keep up with them, before turning to the ball-control run game, but it hasn’t been his strategy recently. Now the defense will need to start the 2nd half with a stop, or the Jets can start to make this one extremely complicated. 2nd Half Cade Klubnik in, Geno out. He starts finding Wilson on a beautiful corner route, and the Jets are already on the Bills 30. People lost faith in him, but the truth is, Bernard has looked great recently. Aggressive play, tackling the running back in the backfield. The rookie has got wheels. Klubnik scrambles for 2 consecutive 1st downs. 1st and goal Jets. Thankfully, another penalty. (Cade Klubnik: 3 carries, 26 yards) Klubnik tries Wilson in the endzone, and it’s a good pass. Alford, with an even better play, almost intercepts it. Unfortunately, he hit his head on the ground as he fell, and it doesn’t look good. The rookie seems to be a boost for the Jets, but almost blows it with a forced pass in the endzone. Williams hits his arm, and Hooker, for the 2nd time in this game, almost intercepts it. FG Jets, 10-9 Bills lead. (Klubnik: 11/20, 137 yards, 1 INT) Josh Allen for the rescue. 54-yard completion, a hope in the Turkey hole to Kincaid. Bills 1st and goal. (Kincaid: 2 receptions, 58 yards) TD Bills, Superman is in the building. Josh with a QB keeper from empty. Extra point is good, 17-9 Bills. (Josh Allen: 2 rushing TDs, both from 1 yard) After an impressive 1st drive, Klubnik is out, and Geno is back. Honestly, not sure if it’s bad. Nice curl route by AD Mitchell, even better burst after the catch. Benford barely could tackle him, he was almost gone. I’m ok with Coleman, but AD was my guy in that draft, I wish we had him. He’s the kind of guy Josh would take advantage of. (Adonai Mitchell: 3 receptions, 59 yards) 3rd down and Leonhard sends the house, forcing Geno to get rid of it. 4th down. Jets FG is good, 17-12 Bills. Gotta keep riding Allen. Scoring TDs as they score FGs is what will win games for us. No need to take the foot off the gas now. Control the clock later. (Jets: 4-for-4 on field goals, 0 touchdowns) One run and one bomb from Allen to Moore for a 45-yard TD. That’s what I’m talking about. All gas, no brakes. 24-12 Bills. Dare the Jets to keep up with them, they can’t. (Moore: 4 receptions, 90 yards, 1 TD) Klubnik is back with Geno hurting his ankle now, and, under duress, he throws an INT. IGB with the pick, but was too greedy on the return, took a hit, and fumbled it back to NY. (Igbinosun: 1 INT, 17 return yards, 1 fumble) End of the 3rd, defense does its job, and Josh will get the ball back. Josh is surprised by Connor McGovern’s snap, but still puts it on the money for Keon to plug it in beautifully before getting a big hit. Coleman to the tent and a penalty negates the play. 3rd and 12, Josh forces it deep to Greg Dortch, intercepted.…

title: Buffalo Bills ground New York Jets, improve to 8-1 with Week 10 win
summary: The Buffalo Bills earned their first AFC East divisional win this season thanks to a persistent attack that gradually wore down an overmatched New York Jets team in all three phases of the game. The Bills were once again held in check until halftime, but the offense came out with an aggressive swagger after the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball against the New York Jets in the third quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills earned their first AFC East divisional win this season thanks to a persistent attack that gradually wore down an overmatched New York Jets team in all three phases of the game. The Bills were once again held in check until halftime, but the offense came out with an aggressive swagger after the break that broke most of the Jets’ prior momentum. You might say that head coach Joe Brady has put together a masterclass in his first season at the helm, lulling opponents into a false sense of hope through the first two quarters, only to pull the rug out from under them when it counts. Buffalo again started the game on offense, thanks to another lost coin toss. It didn’t work out as Brady probably planned for in New Jersey, though the choice wasn’t his to make this weekend. The Jets’ forced a punt that soon ushered in a mid-tempo battle in the trenches for the duration of the half. The Bills eventually found the end zone in the first quarter thanks to another goal-line carry by Allen. The Jets’ defense caused plenty of early confusion and frustration for Allen and the passing game, ultimately holding them to just 10 points at halftime. Thankfully, Buffalo’s defense was ready for a slugfest and limited the Jets to just two field goals through two quarters while having to defend two different quarterbacks in starter Geno Smith (who was injured before the break), and rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik. If you caught his quick interview after the half, it was clear Brady was annoyed at his mostly stagnant first-half offense. They responded to what must have been an epic challenge speech in the locker room, which led to three second-half touchdowns and a 31-12 blowout win. A defense that’s been ranked as low as last and currently resides in the middle of the pack held an under-the-radar and (yes) talented Jets offense out of the end zone. These are the sorts of building blocks that matter when it comes to postseason discussions. The Bills can’t control their schedule or who suits up, but in watching the defense it’s clear things have begun to click and they’re responding far better to in-game adversity. It was a banner day for the pass rush, which claimed four more sacks. The unit was led by rookie edge rusher T.J. Parker, who notched a pair to increase his total to three on the season. It’s true that it wasn’t Allen’s finest day at the office, with him completing just 11-of-21 passes for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception. His numbers were propped up by two longs passes: a 54-yard catch and run by tight end Dalton Kincaid, and a 45-yard deep shot to wide receiver DJ Moore. Importantly, the Jets were unable to stop Allen’s threat as a short-yardage runner, which allowed the offense to stay on the field and gave him another pair of rushing touchdowns. With 90 rushing touchdowns, Allen is now just nine touchdowns shy of tying Pro Football Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders. As for running back James Cook III? What a tremendous game, which sounds like a broken record at this point. Cook had 13 carries for 56 yards at halftime. He finished with 18 carries for 157 yards and a career-long 74-yard touchdown run late in action. Do the math and you’ll see that he had just five carries and 101 yards with that touchdown in the second half. He probably would have had a receiving touchdown as well, if not for a dropped catch. Cook is on a mission in 2026, and Bills Mafia should enjoy every second of his play. The rushing attack is again the story on offense, out-gaining the passing attack and finishing with a total of 201 yards on 32 carries. That’s a machine built for winter football, and Buffalo has an offensive line filled with aggressive run blockers. If they can cut down on the pre-snap penalties, teams may struggle getting the Bills’ offense off the field. Improving to 8-1 was the Buffalo’s ultimate goal in Week 10, which allows them to maintain their first-place lead in the AFC playoff race. Just over half of the 2026 NFL season is now in the books, and the contenders have begun to separate from the pack. The Bills have a still-undefeated road record this season, improving to 5-0 Sunday afternoon. Most teams facing Buffalo seem incapable of holding them under 30 points, which often spells doom in professional football. The Bills have scored 31 or more points in six games, each of those coming in winning efforts. For as dominant as the Bills have been this season, it feels like their best is yet to come. They’ll need to continue willing teams to submission via the ground attack while trying to improve efficiency in the passing game. In Week 11, Buffalo gets its first crack at this year’s version of the Miami Dolphins. Despite a losing record, Miami is likely to have some things up its sleeve in an effort to frustrate the Bills. Buffalo needs to remain focused and avoid any scent of a letdown before their game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.
