title: Buffalo Bills stock report in big victory over New York Jets
summary: The Buffalo Bills and the New York Jets played a hard-fought game this afternoon. Truthfully, it was typical of games between these two clubs, as the feisty Jets played tough against a heavily-favored Bills team. Any time a divisional game is happening, you can throw out the Vegas line, and that was exactly what happened […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills looks on before a game anyat MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and the New York Jets played a hard-fought game this afternoon. Truthfully, it was typical of games between these two clubs, as the feisty Jets played tough against a heavily-favored Bills team. Any time a divisional game is happening, you can throw out the Vegas line, and that was exactly what happened today. The Jets kept things close early on, as the score was 10-9 in favor of the Bills early in the third. Buffalo answered quickly, scoring a touchdown on their first possession of the second half to extend their lead to 17-9. While the Jets fought hard, their inability to score touchdowns eventually came back to bite them, as Buffalo continued to expand their lead as the game progressed. Ultimately, Buffalo prevailed, winning 31-12 in a game that featured quite a few injuries for both sides. Here are our horns up and horns down for Buffalo in today’s game against the Jets. _____________________________________________________________________________ Horns Down: Pre-snap Discipline Throughout this season, false start penalties have been a problem. Early on today, it was jumping offside that proved to be an issue. After the Jets’ first possession, Michael Hoecht jumped offside while the Jets lined up to punt. While it did not give the Jets a first down, it gave them five extra yards to set up a more comfortable punt. Later, on a fourth-down on the Jets’ second drive, Ed Oliver jumped on a fourth-and-six where it was fairly clear that the Jets weren’t going to run a play. That gave New York a fourth-and-one, which they converted en route to what became a field goal drive. Pre-snap penalties are a matter of discipline, and too often this year, the Bills have not passed the test. Well, all we had to do was wait for the second quarter for the false start penalties to kick in. Dawson Knox and Dion Dawkins were each called for one on what became a field goal drive. Four pre-snap penalties in the first half alone is maddening. Alec Anderson committed a fifth one with a false start in the fourth quarter. Heck, Hoecht tried to read the snap count and jumped offside for a second time in the game while the Jets were driving in the fourth quarter. Horns Up: James Cook III Another week, another game where Buffalo’s top running back looked great. Cook found holes, was decisive throughout, and gained plenty of yardage on the ground. If there was a negative, it was that he dropped what would have at least been an easy completion, and potentially could have been a first down or more, while Buffalo was in the red zone during the second quarter. Cook is a dynamic receiving threat, but he just has too many concentration drops to be considered a reliable threat in that area. Cook’s 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter put the game away, as well. Overall he had exactly the kind of game that we’ve come to expect from him, totaling 157 rushing yards and the aforementioned touchdown on 18 carries. Horns Up: Dorian Williams The former Tulane Green Wave standout had another solid day. He was the one who notched Buffalo’s first sack of Geno Smith, timing a blitz perfectly to take down the Jets’ signal caller in the second quarter. Williams has been playing quite well over the last month or so, and he led the Bills in tackles through the first half of play this week. He also was able to put a hit on Cade Klubnik to force an incomplete pass that Amani Hooker nearly intercepted on New York’s first possession of the second half. Williams left the game in the fourth quarter with a calf injury, and here’s hoping that it was mostly precautionary that he didn’t return. He finished with a team-high nine tackles, including five solo stops, one sack, one pass breakup, and two quarterback hits. Horns Up: The Kicking Game Tyler Bass nailed a PAT and yet another field goal in the first half. That field goal extended his franchise-record streak of made field goals, as it was the 24th straight kick he’s made. Tommy Doman Jr. hit some great kickoffs and good punts, as he seems to have mastered the concept of “hangtime” on his punts. Focusing on the punter is ever a good thing, but in an ugly first half, Doman was a bright spot. He pinned another one deep in Jets territory in the fourth quarter, bouncing a high boot inside the ten-yard line. Bass finished with just that one field goal and four made PATs, while Doman landed all three of his punts inside the Jets’ 20-yard line, averaging 46.3 yards per punt in the process. Horns Down: Pass Rush Early For much of the early going, there was little pressure on either Jets quarterback. Geno Smith had time to throw, completing 9 of the 16 passes he attempted in the first half before he was forced out of the game with an upper-body injury. When rookie Cade Klubnik entered the game, the Bills still couldn’t create pressure, and the mobile 23-year old was able to make them pay on the Jets’ first possession out of the half. The pass rush plan can’t be “let’s hope Greg Rousseau makes a play.” Sometimes, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard needs to dial up some different looks, especially when the front four or five players aren’t creating enough pressure. In the second half, Leonhard started to dial it up a notch, and whether that was due to Smith’s injury or not is irrelevant. Buffalo was able to create some pressure through blitzes when the rookie Klubnik was in the game. After a slow start, Buffalo finished with four sacks and 12 QB hits on the day. Horns Up: Red Zone/Third Down Defense While the Bills allowed the Jets to drive quite a bit, they were very efficient when it came to keeping the Jets out of the end zone. Part of that could be because the Jets are among the NFL’s worst red zone offenses, but it doesn’t change the fact that Buffalo kept holding the Jets to three points instead of six when Gang Green was close to scoring touchdowns. The Jets were just 3-for-13 on third downs, and Buffalo held their opponents out of the end zone once again. The Bills haven’t allowed a touchdown in 11 quarters, dating back to their victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Horns Up: DJ Moore Buffalo’s top wideout made a couple of big plays in this one. In the first half, Moore caught a pass on a crossing route to convert a first down, traveling 34 yards to set up the Bills’ first touchdown. Then, on the Bills’ second possession of the second half, Moore caught a 45-yard touchdown pass on a beautifully thrown ball from Josh Allen. On the former, Moore was slammed hard to the turf, and for a moment, I was worried that he injured his left shoulder after dealing with an injury to his right shoulder for most of this season. On the latter, Moore lost the football while crossing the goal line, and it wasn’t immediately clear that the pass was caught. However, both plays worked out for the Bills. Moore finished his day with four catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on six targets. All of those numbers led the Bills today. Horns Up and Down: Davison Igbinosun The rookie continued his streak of solid play, as he was strong in coverage regardless of which Jets wideout he was covering. Igbinosun also notched his second career interceptions, picking off Klubnik in the third quarter. Unfortunately for Igbinosun, he was absolutely smoked on the return by Jets tight end Jeremy Ruckert. Igbinosun fumbled, and the Jets recovered it, negating the big play and giving the Jets the ball back. New York eventually punted, but Buffalo forfeited plenty of field position. He finished with four tackles and two pass breakups. He was once again excellent in coverage. Horns Down: The Injury Bug MetLife Stadium is a house of horrors for many, as its turf is notorious for causing injury. By the end of today’s game, Buffalo was without Dorian William…

title: Josh Allen breaks Peyton Manning’s NFL touchdown record
summary: Josh Allen no longer has to share the top spot with Peyton Manning.  The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially moved ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Famer, becoming the NFL’s all-time leader in combined touchdowns by a quarterback through his first 10 seasons. And Allen has done it before completing his ninth year.  Allen […]
full_text: Nov 25, 2021; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) gestures after throwing a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports Josh Allen no longer has to share the top spot with Peyton Manning. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially moved ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Famer, becoming the NFL’s all-time leader in combined touchdowns by a quarterback through his first 10 seasons. And Allen has done it before completing his ninth year. And he did it in nine seasons. 😏 @JoshAllenQB | #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/5PKNI0B5aX — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 Allen entered Sunday’s game against the New York Jets tied with Manning at 322 career touchdowns. One more touchdown was all he needed to claim the record for himself. On Buffalo’s second possession of the day, Allen methodically moved the Bills down the field. After a defensive holding call gave the Bills a first and goal at the one-foot line, Allen called his own number and used the opportunity to pass Manning. Josh Allen calls his own number. 😤 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/9Fj8amAJvc — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 With that touchdown, Allen’s career total climbed to 323, passing the mark Manning established during his first decade with the Indianapolis Colts. But the difference between the two quarterbacks isn’t just the number of touchdowns. It’s how quickly Allen got there. Manning needed 160 regular-season games to reach 322 touchdowns. Allen matched that total in just 136 games, throwing his record-tying touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings last Monday night. That’s 24 fewer games, the equivalent of nearly a season and a half of football. Allen has also taken a different route to the record. While Manning’s touchdowns came almost exclusively through the air, Allen has been just as dangerous with his legs. His career total entering Sunday included 232 passing touchdowns, 88 rushing touchdowns, and two receiving touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes is the only other active quarterback in the top 10 who can still add to his total. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback entered Week 10 with 301 touchdowns and will spend the remainder of the season chasing Allen. But Mahomes is already in his 10th NFL season, meaning his final number will be set when the regular season ends in January. Allen, meanwhile, will have all of 2027 to keep adding to a record Mahomes will no longer be eligible to chase.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: The Optimist: What the Turducken was that, refs?
summary: Despite the closeness of yesterday’s 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints, the Panthers established themselves as the team to beat in the NFC South. A dubious honor, to be sure, but it’s where we are now. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are the only thing that resembles a threat in this division and I’m not […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS - OCTOBER 07: Quarterback David Carr #8 of the Carolina Panthers successfully argues with referee Gene Steratore #114 and head linesman Paul Weidner #87 after being called for an intentional grounding against the New Orleans Saints at the Superdome on October , 2007 in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Panthers defeated the Saints 16-13. (Photo by Doug Benc/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite the closeness of yesterday’s 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints, the Panthers established themselves as the team to beat in the NFC South. A dubious honor, to be sure, but it’s where we are now. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are the only thing that resembles a threat in this division and I’m not confident that what we saw against them in Week 7 will happen again in Week 12. I guess we’ll see. The Panthers overcame aggressively one-sided officiated, middling quarterback play from Bryce Young, baffling editorial and marketing decisions by Fox Sports, and inconsistent kicking from Ryan Fitzgerald to do something they couldn’t manage last season: they won a game to take control of the division. They also snapped a three game losing streak, extended their streak of not sending anybody to injured reserve to two weeks, and are set to keep bringing key players back from injuries over the next several weeks. That said, it’s not all sunshine and beignets for the Panthers after conquering the Saints in New Orleans. We can’t pretend like that wasn’t a rough game even outside of the liberal interpretations of several rules that the officials were using. There are four things that need to be addressed coming out of Week 10 that need to be addressed more than anything else if the Panthers want to win any more games this season. Coaching and short yardage situations Play-calling and execution in the red zone and in short yardage situations have been a challenge all season. The Saints opening drive ended with an interception that, after one offensive play, became first and ten at the New Orleans 11 yard line. The Panthers walked away with zero points. They traded three punts with the Saints on subsequent drives before missing a field goal. The Panthers were managed to convert a first down or touchdown on four of eleven attempts with four or fewer yards to gain. On those attempts, they called seven running and four passing plays. That’s a better balance than I thought it was going to be after the game, but the truth remains simple: the Panthers need to find a way to consistently convert in these situations or they are going to have a disappointing end to an already middling season. “Discipline” You’re going to hear the word “discipline” this week as a critique of Dave Canales and his coaching staff about as often as you saw a flag thrown on the field yesterday. There were a couple of false starts and neutral zone infractions that were, indeed, characterized by a lack of discipline. However I would wager that the bulk of the 17 flags thrown for 152 penalty yards (only seventy fewer yards than the Saints total offensive output) were flags that most fans would describe as “bullshit.” When you lose and you point at one sided officiating, it’s called being a sore loser. I guess the Carolina Panthers are in danger of making me a sore winner. Let’s take a moment to consider the penalties that keyed the Saints three scoring drives. 1st & 10 at New Orleans 48, 8:46 3rd quarter , Panthers 7 Saints 0 Quarterback Tyler Shough found a wide open Jordan Tyson for an 18 yard pass. So far so clean. Tyson fell to the ground untouched while making the catch. Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd fell onto and over Tyson in an effort to make sure he was downed by contact. This was flagged as unnecessary roughness. The NFL rule book, under Rule 12. Section 2. Article 8 states that unnecessary roughness can be defined as the following: running, diving into, or throwing the body against or on any player on the ground either before or after the ball is dead; It’s possible that Lloyd’s momentum qualified under the letter of this law. It is also possible, to revive a quote from last week, that this could have been described as a “bang-bang play.” Unfortunately, that term is not defined in the rule book. The fifteen yards from that penalty, added to the reception, put the Saints into the red zone for the first time in the game. Unlike during the rest of the game, the Saints did proceed to score from there under their own power. 1st & 5 at Carolina 42, 6:18 4th quarter, Panthers 10 Saints 7 Jaelan Phillips, unheld, pursued Shough and brought him down for a 17-yard sack. This should have brought up second & 22 from the Saints’ 39 yard line. Well out of field goal and certainly an uphill climb to get another first down. Instead, a selective interpretation of Rule 12. Section 2. Article 16 was enforced, calling Phillips for a horse-collar tackle and giving the Saints 15 yards instead of them losing 17. The text of the rule is below with one part highlighted for emphasis. No player shall grab the inside collar of the back or the side of the shoulder pads or jersey, or grab the jersey at the name plate or above, and pull the runner toward the ground. This does not apply to a runner who is in the pocket area or in the area defined by close-line play. If his knees are buckled by the action, it is a foul, even if the runner is not pulled completely to the ground. Your next reasonable question is “how does the NFL define the pocket area?”. Fortunately, that is easily answered by Rule 3. Section 25. “Pocket Area”: The pocket area is the area between the outside edges of the normal tackle positions on each side of the center extending backward to the offensive team’s end line. A player who is in possession of the ball is out of the pocket area, and the pocket area no longer exists, if any part of his body or the ball is outside of the pocket area. Where was Shough tackled? Between the inside hip of the right tackle and the center, 17 yards behind where the ball was snapped. Is 17 yards behind the line of scrimmage outside of the pocket area? No, the pocket area extends back to the offensive team’s end line (the back of the end zone, in NFL parlance). Were Shough’s knees buckled by the action? No, he fell to his side. He did not fall directly backwards in the way this rule was meant to penalize and prevent. After this penalty, the Saints ran a total of four plays for an average of 1.2 yards per play. Unfortunately, a poorly timed neutral zone infraction by Trevon Moehrig (five-yard penalty) and a ticky-tack pass interference penalty on Corey Thornton (17-yard penalty, but I couldn’t find a replay last night) added insult and further injury to the pile. Penalties, dubious penalties, accounted for 42 of the Saints 70 yards on this touchdown drive. 2nd & 7 at the New Orleans 37 , 1:10 4th quarter, Panthers 17 Saints 14 Tyler Dodson tackled Jordyn Tyson high. His hand was clearly around the upper chest to neck area of Tyson and replay showed that not even a single finger contacted or snared Tyson’s face mask. Nonetheless, Dodson was flagged for grabbing Tyson’s facemask. We return to Rule 12. Section 2, this time Article 15 holds our answers: If a player grasps an opponent’s facemask or helmet opening, he must immediately release it. He shall not grasp and control, twist, turn, push, or pull the facemask or helmet opening of an opponent in any direction. The only part of the rule that Dodson failed to comply with is that he did not immediately release Tyson’s facemask. That is because he never grabbed it in the first place. He did not grasp and control, twist, turn, push, or pull the facemask or helmet opening of Tyson. So it must be Dodson’s failure to release that which he did not ever grasp that gifted the Saints 15 yards on their tying field goal drive. Keep in mind that the Saints only advanced the ball six yards after this penalty before kicking their 55-yard field goal. Yes, there are legitimate things to…

title: Panthers vs Saints: Recap and reaction
summary: The Carolina Panthers overcame an avalanche of penalties, some justified and a lot not, to defeat the New Orleans Saints on a last second field goal, 20-17. First Quarter Ryan Fitzgerald started the game out right by kicking the opening kickoff out of bounds. After a few stops, the defense forced the Saints into a […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Chuba Hubbard #30 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after his rushing touchdown in the second quarter of a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers overcame an avalanche of penalties, some justified and a lot not, to defeat the New Orleans Saints on a last second field goal, 20-17. First Quarter Ryan Fitzgerald started the game out right by kicking the opening kickoff out of bounds. After a few stops, the defense forced the Saints into a 4th and 1. Tyler Shough tried to find Chris Olave, but the pass was tipped and picked off by Devin Lloyd. He ran it all the way back to the New Orleans 23. Chuba Hubbard broke off a nice run to start the drive. The Panthers inched closer to the goal line but ended up in their own fourth and short. Bryce Young tried to scramble out of a collapsing pocket, but he stumbled when trying to make a cut and was touched down just short of the line gain. The defense took the field with the Saints backed up against their own goal line. They made three straight stops and forced a punt. Trevor Etienne let the punt bounce which added a bunch of extra yardage to it, but he was able to pick it up and get a few of those yards back on the return. The offense rode Chuba Hubbard into Saints territory. The offense picked up a 3rd and 9 on a pass to Darren Waller, but he was called for a phantom offensive pass interference to end the drive. Sam Martin pinned the Saints inside the five with his punt. The defense had the Saints in a 3rd and 4, but Derrick Brown jumped offsides. It was the team’s fifth penalty of the first quarter. It didn’t hurt though. The defense got off the field three plays later after Jaelan Philips got a fingertip on Tyler Shough’s third down pass. Second Quarter The Chuba show continued into the second quarter. He caught a check down to pick up a first down into Saints territory then broke a big run down to the 30. On the next play, Bryce Young had Darren Waller wide open down the sideline, but Waller dropped it. McMillan also failed to reel in a catchable ball on third down. Ryan Fitzgerald took the field to miss a field goal and keep the score knotted at zero. Tyler Shough found Juwan Johnson with a third down pass to get into Panthers territory. On the next play, he and Audric Estime dropped the exchange on a handoff, and Jaelan Phillips scooped it up. Tommy Tremble took a screen pass into the red zone. A couple plays later, Hubbard ran it in for a touchdown. However, it was called back for a late holding call that also seemed questionable. Dave Canales used a Saints timeout to give the refs a hard time while the broadcast team discussed the second time the officials screwed over Carolina. Young found Waller to eventually pick up the first down. Chuba Hubbard ran it down to the one. Two incompletions set up another nervous fourth down, but Hubbard ran it in, and the officials couldn’t find anything to flag. The Saints picked up a few quick first downs while the broadcast talked about turduckens for an extended period of time. When they stopped talking about turduckens, the defense stuffed a couple of runs. On 4th and inches, they tried a fullback dive, but Lee Hunter broke through the line to stuff the run deep in the backfield. Young found Tetairoa McMillan to move the offense out to midfield. That’s as far as they’d get though. On third down, Young checked it down to a heavily covered Hubbard for no gain. After the punt, Jaelan Phillips got pressure and forced Shough into a sack by Pat Jones. A couple plays later, he got his own sack to end the half with the Panthers up 7-0. Third Quarter The Panthers got the second half kickoff and immediately got backed up 15 yards because Trevis Gipson tapped a Saints player on the back of the helmet. Dave Canales made a gutsy call to go for it on fourth and short deep in New Orleans territory. It worked, but the offense ultimately had to punt a few plays later anyway. The Saints picked up a long gain on a diving catch and Devin Lloyd was flagged 15 yards for diving on the un-downed wide receiver. A few plays later, Alvin Kamara checked into the game for his first touch, and he punched it in for a touchdown to tie the game. The Panthers responded with a field goal drive. Their two biggest gains were a short completion to McMillan and a defensive pass interference on another pass to McMillan. It wasn’t much, but it got the offense into long field goal range. Dave Canales trusted his guy, and Ryan Fitzgerald drilled the 55 yard field goal right down the middle. The Saints went to the air three straight times on their ensuing drive, and the Panthers stopped each one. On third down, Jaelan Phillips collapsed the pocket and forced Shough to step into the waiting arms of Derrick Brown. Feleipe Franks got called for a 15 yard penalty for blocking someone apparently? The drive went nowhere and ended in a sack of Young. It also ended the third quarter. Fourth Quarter The defense kept up their strong play and got off the field quickly once again. They forced Shough into a one yard gain on a near sack and forced two incompletions to force a quick three and out. The offense didn’t fare any better. They got one first down on a completion to Darren Waller but otherwise didn’t do anything and punted the ball right back. Shough made a couple of completions to move the Saints into Panthers territory. Jaelan Phillips appeared to set the drive back with a huge sack of Shough, but he was called for a horse collar tackle. The Saints moved to the goal line with a pass interference on Corey Thornton on an underthrown ball. Two plays later, Kamara scored his second touchdown of the day to put the Saints up 14-10. It felt like nearly the entire drive was picked up via penalty yards. Chuba Hubbard broke a couple of tackles on the first play of the ensuing drive and scampered down the sideline for a 29 yard gain. Two plays later, he did the same thing for another 33 yards to get the players down to the one yard line at the two minute warning. Two plays later, Hubbard extended to reach for the goal line. He was ruled short, but the play went to review. It looked pretty clear on replay that the ball was the first thing to touch the ground, and it did so on the goal line, but the call stood somehow. Fortunately, Hubbard was able to punch in the score on the next play. The Saints got a boost by a defensive face mask in which the defender grabbed the Saint’s shoulder pad. That penalty was enough to put the Saints into field goal range, and they made a 55 yarder to tie the game. The Panthers had 41 seconds to manufacture a game winning drive. In a bit of poetic justice, the Saints were called for a defensive pass interference on a heave from Bryce Young to Jalen Coker. That was enough to get the Panthers into field goal range. Ryan Fitzgerald drilled the 54 yard field goal as time expired. Overview It’s normally pretty lame to complain about the officiating, but this game was an exception. The Panthers out-penalitied the Saints 17 to 3 and out-penalty yardaged the Saints 152 to 46. A number of the calls were questionable to outright bad, and the vast majority of those were significant, game altering penalties. There was an offensive pass interference, offensive holding, two personal fouls, and horse collar tackle that all could easily be argued were very incorrect. They also incorrectly rule Hubbard short of the goal line before he ultimately scored his second touchdown of the game. I don’t know if it had the same effect on the players, but as a spectator, it felt like the Panthers had to walk on eggshells to avoid flags, and it’s hard to play football that way. On the football side of things, the defense looked really, really good under Todd Wash. They lived in the backfield on both run and pass plays. Tyler Shough was the…

title: ESPN likes the Bears to repeat as division champs, but it won’t be easy
summary: Well, that division lead was fun while it lasted. The Chicago Bears (7-2), after entering their Week 10 bye at the top of the NFC North, are now suddenly third in the division following Sunday’s games. Minnesota (7-2), who’s beaten Chicago already this year and just dispatched Green Bay (6-4), and Detroit (7-2) now share […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Devin Bush #12 and Tyrique Stevenson Sr. #29 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a fourth down stop against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that division lead was fun while it lasted. The Chicago Bears (7-2), after entering their Week 10 bye at the top of the NFC North, are now suddenly third in the division following Sunday’s games. Minnesota (7-2), who’s beaten Chicago already this year and just dispatched Green Bay (6-4), and Detroit (7-2) now share the same record as the Bears but own tiebreakers (for now). Still, a number of experts think the Bears remain the best team in the North—or at least they did before the Vikings and their newly re-acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins put the beats on the Packers 30-10 yesterday. In a pre-Week 10 pundit poll of the NFC North’s ESPN beat writers , three of four put the Bears atop their ultimate NFC North rankings. “The Bears’ runway coming out of the bye is favorable with the Saints in Week 11 and the lowly Dolphins in Week 14, but Chicago has four division opponents (after an 0-2 start in NFC North play) and two potential Super Bowl previews with the Jaguars and Bills. Still, the Bears have proved they can win ugly and coach Ben Johnson is 7-0 in November since arriving in Chicago. With the most complete team in the division and an offense scoring 30.7 points per game when Williams has been under center, the Bears are in position to capture the division crown again,” said Courtney Cronin. “The Bears have the most well-rounded team in the division, and maybe the conference, following the trade for Simmons. But the one thing to watch is that both of their losses this season were in the division. That could be detrimental in a division tiebreaker if that is how the season ends,” Kevin Seifert, a Vikings insider, added. Rob Demovsky, notably of the Packers beat, even gave the Bears their props. “The Bears are the best team in the division despite being 0-2. They ran into Minnesota’s red-hot early-season defense in Week 2 and played without their quarterback in Week 5 at Green Bay. They haven’t even played the Lions yet, and Green Bay still has to go to Soldier Field as part of the three-game finishing stretch for the Bears that goes Packers at home, Lions at home and Vikings on the road,” he said. Only Lions writer Eric Woodyard shot down the Bears hype, saying—you guessed it—the Lions were the better squad. “The Bears might be the most well-rounded team in the division, but the Lions beat them twice last season, as Campbell could be one of the few coaches who knows how to counter the attack of Johnson—his former offensive coordinator. The division is certainly up for grabs, but Detroit’s explosive offense could be the game-changer in the division title race,” he wrote. Though this year is not last year, of course, it’s not hard to see how much trouble Detroit has given these Ben Johnson-led Bears. Even with Chicago adding Jeffery Simmons and the Lions now likely to lose Aidan Hutchinson for an extended period of time—maybe even the season—Detroit has been too good to dismiss. And while none of the writers envisioned Cousins putting Minnesota over the top, watching his performance in his first game back with Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings makes one curious. As for the Packers? See you at Soldier Field on Christmas. Payback time. The Bears will have every opportunity to prove those writers right with four division games in the back stretch of their season. If they can so much as break even against their North opponents for the season, it would get them to 10 wins. But who knows? 10 wins might not be enough to keep their crown. Time to see what Johnson, Caleb Williams, and this squad are made of.

title: 5 Bears Takes: Grading The First Half and Dissecting The NFC North
summary: Following a fast and furious nine games, the Chicago Bears enjoyed their bye over the weekend. In the process, they watched two divisional foes beat each other up and got a live look at their Week 11 opponent as the Panthers beat them at home. The playoff picture continues to take shape, and the Bears […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Rome Odunze #15 celebrates with Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears after scoring a touchdown during the first quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a fast and furious nine games, the Chicago Bears enjoyed their bye over the weekend. In the process, they watched two divisional foes beat each other up and got a live look at their Week 11 opponent as the Panthers beat them at home. The playoff picture continues to take shape, and the Bears will start practice early next week as they gear up for a second-half run. We’ll cover all of that, and more in a special installment of 5 Bears Takes. 1. Grading out the offense over the first nine games of the season. Before the season, head coach Ben Johnson spoke about wanting to set the NFL’s scoring record. While some took those words and ran with them, the Bears were well on pace after a Week 1 that produced 59 points on the road. Since that point, the offense has yet to break the 40-point mark again, but they’ve eclipsed the 30-point mark four separate times. All of which were with starting quarterback Caleb Williams under center. Through nine games, the offense ranks within the Top 5 in yards per game (383), Top 10 in points per game (26.8), 11th in EPA/play, and 10th in success rate. In total, their numbers are right around where they sat for the majority of last season, with one major caveat: They missed their starting quarterback for a third of the season (so far). They’ve also faced four of the Top 10 defenses in the league through that stretch. Overall, there’s still plenty of meat left on the bone when looking at this unit’s production and what it could (or should) be. With better health at the quarterback position and no clunkers in the second half of the season, the Bears have a real opportunity to finish as a Top 5 offense. Part of that will depend on health at key positions like running back and receiver, but the offensive line will play a key part, too. We’ve seen multiple flashes of dominance, but there’s still plenty to clean up, especially when it comes to penalties and self-inflicted mistakes. With a better-than-expected defense, they’ve been able to control most games, but for them to take the next step and be scarier down the stretch, the offense must be more consistent. Grades: Quarterback: A Running Backs: C+ Wide Receivers: B Tight Ends: C- Offensive Line: B+ 2. Grading out the defense over the first nine games of the season. Coming into the season, the defense felt like the Achilles’ heel of what could be a Super Bowl contender. During the offseason, the front office did very little to improve the defensive line, and through the first month and a half of the season, it seemed clear the interior defensive line wouldn’t be good enough. Despite what their depth chart has looked like on paper, they’ve performed better than expected, even before the acquisition of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Through nine games, the defense ranks 1st in third-down percentage (22.8%), Top 5 in fourth-down percentage (30.8%), Top 10 in EPA/play, yards per game, and sacks, and gives up just 20.4 points per game. It’s also worth mentioning that they were 9th in pressure percentage coming into Week 10. With Simmons in the mix on the interior, the biggest hole this group has is at cornerback. The hope is that with a healthy Malik Muhammad, either Jaylon Johnson or Tyrique Stevenson can step into the spot opposite the rookie and provide consistency and stability. With any luck, they’ll get Coby Bryant back at some point in December. It’s worth pointing out how well Cam Lewis has played since taking over the starting spot opposite first-round rookie Dillon Thieneman. With the divisional defenses starting to shake out, this group must continue its upward trajectory. Getting back Dayo Odeyingbo should help the defensive line, but Austin Booker, Montez Sweat, and even Grady Jarrett have been noticeably better since the arrival of Simmons. Many expected the Bears to make another move or two before the deadline, but with nothing materializing, they’re stuck with what they have. Similar to the offense, health will be key down the stretch, but overall, the team should feel pretty good about where they stand. The only real concern heading into the second half is how well their cornerbacks can perform against top offenses. Grades: Defensive Line: A- Linebacker: B Cornerback: D- Safety: B- 3. Dissecting the NFC North after another hectic week that saw the Bears drop from first to third place. With the Bears’ bye week, they were the only team in the division that was not in play on Sunday. The Detroit Lions took their crack at the piñata that has become the New England Patriots in the early-morning slot, and outside of the opening drive, it wasn’t much of a game. The Patriots lost quarterback Drake Maye early, and, to put it nicely, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was ineffective. For as impressive as the Lions were, they lost another star defender when Aidan Hutchinson went down with what appeared to be a serious knee injury following a sack of Maye on the first drive. The play (and subsequent celebration) took two of the most impactful players out of the game before it could really even get going. Although the Lions have been playing much better defense as of late, losing their top two leaders, Jack Campbell and Hutchinson, will wear on them as the season goes on. During the next time slot, the Packers hosted the Kirk Cousins-led Vikings. What looked like a good matchup on paper turned into a season sweep for Minnesota, following a 30-10 drubbing. The Vikings’ defense continues to be one of the best overall units in the league, and with Cousins under center, the offense looked more cohesive, even if it wasn’t a perfectly played game. Cousins has plenty of familiarity with the offense, so it’s fair to assume that he’ll continue to hit the ground running. For the Packers, it’s hard to know whether Sunday’s 20-point loss was simply a bad day at the office, or a sign of things to come. Green Bay has shown clear holes all season, and although they’ve looked considerably better over the last month, there are still ways to attack them. All in all, the division once again had another winning week. With the Lions and Vikings both winning, there’s a three-way tie at the top with all three teams sitting at 7-2. The Packers will go on an abbreviated bye week before going to Los Angeles to face a red-hot Rams team on Thanksgiving Eve. Ultimately, their bye week will amount to the same number of days off as it would if they played on Thursday night and then played a Monday night game the following week. It’s clear that all four teams are playoff-caliber, but it remains to be seen if all four can make the playoffs come January. With Sunday’s results, the Packers have now fallen a game and a half behind everyone else, while sporting a 1-3 record within the division. Even more troubling is that their 4-4 conference record won’t help them much in tie-breakers once more games are played. Heading into Week 11, all four teams fill out the seven teams that would comprise the NFC playoff picture, but with plenty of head-to-heads remaining (both in the division and the conference), this is still a long way from a resolution. Heading into Week 11, here’s how the divisional standings look: Detroit Lions (7-2) Minnesota Vikings (7-2) Chicago Bears (7-2) Green Bay Packers (6-4) Here’s how the tie-breakers come out: Lions win the head-to-head tie-breaker against the Vikings and have a better divisional record than the Bears. Vikings win the head-to-head tie-breaker against the Bears. After Week 11, each team will have seven games remaining. Both the Bears and Lions have favorable matchups, while the Vikings will play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football. Barring a surprise,…

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ uplifting win over the Steelers
summary: It’s good to sometimes take a step back and appreciate how far the Cincinnati Bengals have come since drafting Joe Burrow. The lead-up to primetime games used to be filled with anxiety. Bengals fans knew the likelihood of getting embarrassed was high, But now, primetime is where the Bengals shine. And last night’s game might […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Ja'marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals catches a pass against Asante Samuel Jr. #22 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the second quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s good to sometimes take a step back and appreciate how far the Cincinnati Bengals have come since drafting Joe Burrow. The lead-up to primetime games used to be filled with anxiety. Bengals fans knew the likelihood of getting embarrassed was high, But now, primetime is where the Bengals shine. And last night’s game might be the best example. Cincinnati went head-to-head with their heated rivals, who were tied with them for the division lead. And they absolutely destroyed them. Here are three things we learned from the clinic Burrow and the Bengals put on against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The pass blocking isn’t just serviceable; it’s great Amarius Mims dominated T.J. Watt, making him look like a child. Amarius Mims vs. T.J. Watt tonight 👀 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WYtWQuZ29j — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 And Orlando Brown Jr., considered to be the weak link at the start of the season, just delivered the best pass protection game of any left tackle this year , not allowing a pressure on 44 dropbacks. Burrow had clean pockets almost the entire game, similar to the game against the Atlanta Falcons. And, as a result, he methodically picked those defenses apart. There’s no more playing scared on offense In the past, the Bengals would fall behind early, trying to force a run game that wasn’t there. Against the Steelers, they used the short game to get the pass in a flow, and sprinkled in deep shots down the field. Burrow and the offense came out firing, confident in their ability to have their way with any defense, even one as intimidating as Pittsburgh’s. Ja’Marr Chase is in the zone He’s probably been the best receiver in the league for a couple of seasons, but he’s somehow reached another level. After a slow start, Chase has 527 yards receiving in his last three games. He had probably the most casual 200 yard receiving game you’ll ever see against the Steelers. And his 231 total was the highest for any receiver this season. The combination of Burrow having time, the offense finding its identity, and Tee Higgins emerging as the most physically dominant receiver in the league have led to Chase being able to break out his entire bag on a regular basis.

title: Ja’Marr Chase has spectacular showing in Bengals’ big win vs. Steelers
summary: Ja’Marr Chase said he loves primetime games. On Sunday night, he showed everyone why. Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals‘ 38-18 win over Pittsburgh at Paycor. It was the fourth 200-yard game of his career and the third-best yardage total he’s ever had, and it came against a Steelers team […]
full_text: Ja’Marr Chase said he loves primetime games. On Sunday night, he showed everyone why. Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals ‘ 38-18 win over Pittsburgh at Paycor. It was the fourth 200-yard game of his career and the third-best yardage total he’s ever had, and it came against a Steelers team that walked in tied for first in the AFC North and walked out a game behind. Chase didn’t find the end zone, and it didn’t matter. He was the engine of the drives that buried Pittsburgh early. His two deep shots, a 53-yarder and a 43-yarder, each set up Bengals touchdowns. The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions and took a 24-3 lead into the locker room, while the Steelers managed just 40 total yards and four first downs before halftime. The only thing that stopped Chase was the scoreboard. With the game in hand, the Bengals eased off in the fourth quarter and brought in Joe Flacco for mop-up duty. Sunday was Chase’s fourth regular-season game with at least 200 receiving yards. The headline record of the night belonged to his quarterback. Burrow threw four touchdown passes, giving him five straight games with at least four total touchdowns, which ties Peyton Manning’s 2004 run for the longest such streak in NFL history. The Bengals also completed 21 passes before Aaron Rodgers completed his first, tying the most by one team before its opponent’s first completion since 1978. None of that happens without No. 1 stretching the defense. When Chase is getting behind safeties like he did Sunday night, everything underneath opens up for Chase Brown, Drew Sample, and Dohnte Meyers, which is exactly how all four touchdown passes were scored. The Bengals are 7-2 and alone in first place in the AFC North. And their best player just reminded everyone that the bigger the stage, the better he gets.

title: Bengals News: Statement win vs. Steelers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals absolutely whooped the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. It ended up 38-18 thanks to some late scores for Pittsburgh. After the Bengals made it 31-3 early in the third quarter, the game was essentially done. It has to be one of the best performances the Bengals have had when both teams […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals absolutely whooped the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. It ended up 38-18 thanks to some late scores for Pittsburgh. After the Bengals made it 31-3 early in the third quarter, the game was essentially done. It has to be one of the best performances the Bengals have had when both teams still have something to play for in the season. Being 7-2 now, the Bengals are tied with three other teams also at 7-2 (Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Jacksonville Jaguars), trailing only behind the Buffalo Bills. These past few weeks, people have pointed out Cincinnati’s closer games with struggling teams and that all of their wins had come against teams below .500. That ended tonight as they dominated offensively and defensively against Pittsburgh. The rest of the Bengals schedule is fairly easy as well. The only teams with a winning record, currently, are the Chiefs and Browns twice. So they do not have many more chances to show what their ceiling is, but the Steelers sure got a taste tonight. Bengals news Bengals Beat Steelers 38-18 | POSTGAME RECAP, NOTES & QUOTES Burrow sets the tone by talking about how they aren’t satisfied at 7-2. This team should have more on their minds after this win, but you could end up finding yourself growing complacent looking past the opponents on your schedule. Joe Burrow throws 4 TDs as Bengals rout Steelers to top AFC North Over the past five games, Burrow has thrown for over 1,600 passing yards, 22 total touchdowns, and only three interceptions. People will have to come to terms with the fact that, even though he has Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, he is absolutely the leader for the MVP award. Back from Madrid, Bengals face Steelers team that is back from a bye The Bengals also had this performance with arguably one of the biggest disadvantages a team can have in the NFL. Teams are now 1-5 coming back to the States after playing internationally against a team coming off a bye week. Even with the deck stacked against Cincinnati, they dominated from the first snap. NFL News Patriots QB Drake Maye suffers ankle injury early in loss to Lions This has a pretty big impact on the AFC playoff race. Not only does it seem to take a team out of the race, which may make it easier for the Cleveland Browns to sneak in, but it also makes the AFC East even more of a cakewalk as the Bills face them in a couple of weeks, and they also play the Chiefs and Broncos down the road. Kirk Cousins emotional after win over Packers in Vikings return: ‘There’s more to this story’ This has to be one of the best stories of the week. Cousins wins in his return while also exorcising some demons after it being on the field he suffered a terrible injury. It will be interesting to see how high the Minnesota Vikings can go. NFL Network: Lions’ Aidan Hutchinson feared to have suffered significant knee injury on sack celebration There are plenty of people with hindsight talking about how players shouldn’t jump when celebrating. Well, these guys jump just a ridiculous amount. It is ridiculous to look back on this and see it as anything more than unfortunate for one of the best pass rushers in the NFL. Now, whether you are upset with him about the hip tackle on Maye right before that injured him is your prerogative.

title: Scorigami! Bengals and Steelers final score has never happened before
summary: Earlier on Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys and San Fransisco 49ers played a game that ended with the 1099th unique score in NFL history. On Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers finished with the 1100th unique score in NFL history. It’s the second time this season we’ve had two Scorigamis in one weekend. It […]
full_text: (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier on Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys and San Fransisco 49ers played a game that ended with the 1099th unique score in NFL history. On Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers finished with the 1100th unique score in NFL history. It’s the second time this season we’ve had two Scorigamis in one weekend. It is the second Bengals Scorigami of the year following their 43-36 win two weeks ago. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami . Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. We got both on Sunday with the Bengals and Steelers. The Bengals just kept scoring, taking a 31-3 game early in the fourth quarter. It’s a pretty typical 28-point, four-touchdown lead. Nothing weird. Then the Pittsburgh Steelers scored a touchdown and went for two. If turned a three-touchdown deficit into a… three-touchdown deficit. Really not sure when the Steelers chose to do it. That 31-11 score would have been a Scorigami. The Bengals scored again very quickly and kicked an extra point to make it 38-11. That would not have been Scorigami but the Steelers scored one last time and kicked the extra point to make it 38-18 for the Scorigami. The only 38-point winners that haven’t hit now are 38-2 and 38-4. Our friends at Secret Base have done extensive work on Scorigami. If you want to see it, it is fascinating. 2026 NFL Scorigamis This is the fifth Scorigami of the 2026 NFL season. September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37 September 13: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22 November 1: Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 November 15: San Francisco 49ers 46, Dallas Cowboys 40 November 15: Cincinnati Bengals 38, Pittsburgh Steelers 18 During the 2025 season we saw four Scorigamis: Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 Bills beat Ravens 41-40 Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 Texans beat Jaguars 36-29

full_text: If you were to ask anyone to describe the 2026 Cleveland Browns, a lot of words will come to mind. Confusing. Frustrating. Resilient. Gritty. Heart. After falling into a 17-point deficit in the 2nd quarter against the Houston Texans, the Browns followed it up with 20 unanswered points in Week 10. It ended up being enough as Cleveland improved to 6-4 heading into their bye week with some momentum and bigger picture questions. Now, on to our 4-Downs review from the Browns’ Week 10 win over the Texans : 1st Down: Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face When the Houston Texans jumped out to a 10-point lead, it was looking pretty dark. Defensively, the Browns couldn’t get a stop as Texans QB CJ Stroud was doing whatever he wanted in the passing game. Offensively, Cleveland couldn’t sustain drives or get any form of rhythm going. It appeared that Houston was going to turn this game into a rout. It wasn’t until this play specifically that things started to change: a HUGE catch to set up the score 👏 #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/KUwh2NXJBx — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 Quarterback Deshaun Watson later scored on that drive, and then the Browns forced a turnover a couple of plays later: Tyson with the hands to take it back! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/rkBxeAhLME — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 After that, the entire complexity of the game changed. In the 2nd half, Cleveland outcoached and outplayed the Texans. After getting punched in the mouth early in the game, the Browns responded with a punch of their own. 2nd Down: QB Change talk is over and done with After Cleveland’s loss against the New Orleans Saints in Week 9, in which quarterback Shedeur Sanders started over quarterback Deshaun Watson, who missed the game while recovering from a concussion, there was a lot of quarterback conversation. Sanders played well, but the topic of discussion was whether Watson’s leash was short after how Sanders played. After Watson’s performance on Sunday, any talk of a QB change should be over. Watson’s 1st half was rough, but he responded with a solid 2nd half. It’s a night-and-day difference between how Watson looks now in 2026 and how he looked in 2024. He looks more confident, mentally tough, and has an unwavering belief in himself. Confidence is key when playing the quarterback position, and if you don’t have it, it will be a short stint for you in the NFL. It’s clear that the Browns offense runs more efficiently and effectively with Watson under center, and Monken trusts Watson more than Sanders. Watson hasn’t been perfect, but he has provided competent quarterback play. 3rd down: Cornerbacks have a huge day, defense shines Overall, the Browns defense had a solid day overall, but Cleveland’s secondary (mainly their cornerbacks) were the star of the show. Cornerback Denzel Ward is one of the most underrated corners in our league. The Texans’ wide receivers were finding success early and often with the route combinations, but Cleveland eventually found a way to slow them down. The Browns are going to live and die by playing man coverage on the back end, but the corners are sticky in coverage, so it doesn’t matter as much as it should. Cornerback Tyson Campbell also had a solid day and, overall, the secondary stood out once adjustments were made. Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg’s adjustments once again stood out. It feels as if Cleveland’s defense was trying to figure out what Houston’s offense was going to do, and it led to a ton of hesitation and overthinking early. At their best, this defense is best at attacking and causing chaos. It worked as Stroud looked uncomfortable in the 2nd half. Credit to the defense for a solid performance, especially the cornerbacks. 4th Down: Postseason seems like a possibility If the season ended today, the Cleveland Browns would have the last playoff spot in the AFC. Yes, you read that right. For a team that many people thought would be picking towards the top in next year’s draft, the Browns have completely changed that. Remember when owner Jimmy Haslam said this before the season started: #Browns owner Jimmy Haslam on what success looks like this season: “I think the odds are for us to win 5.5 games. I’ll take the over.” pic.twitter.com/7z98HSKaaS — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) July 31, 2026 Haslam knew something we didn’t. With 7 games remaining and the second-youngest team the NFL, the Browns have already exceeded their win total from last season. Cleveland is the AFC’s seventh seed and in control of its destiny when it returns from the bye. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 15, 2026 The Browns have exceeded expectations, and it should be commended. Yes, Cleveland is 6-4 with a negative point differential, but who cares? Honestly? Winning in the NFL is hard, and the Browns are finding ways to win every week. The scary part about this team is they haven’t played their best football yet. Granted, no one is saying this team is a Super Bowl contender, but if they continue to get better, this team can find a way to get into the postseason and maybe make a little noise. Extra Points Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans getting fired after this season is a strong possibility. The Texans have been a massive disappointment, and today might have been the nail in their coffin in terms of their playoff hopes. The Browns offensive line had one of their best outings of the season. Cleveland only had 2 penalties for 47 yards. Impressive. Don’t want to hear about the officiating on the late-game call when the Browns have been on the wrong end of it more times than not, including the DPI on Emmanuel McNeil-Warren wasn’t a DPI 6-4 heading into the bye week sounds pretty good to me. title: Browns winners, losers from Week 10 versus Texans: Defense steps up in big win
summary: The Cleveland Browns came into the contest against the Houston Texans with a two-game losing streak. The Texans, meanwhile, came into the game with winning three of their last four games, including defeating the impressive Jacksonville Jaguars. RELATED: BROWNS COMEBACK AT HOME The Browns’ five wins have come against some of the most mediocre teams […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns came into the contest against the Houston Texans with a two-game losing streak. The Texans, meanwhile, came into the game with winning three of their last four games, including defeating the impressive Jacksonville Jaguars. RELATED: BROWNS COMEBACK AT HOME The Browns’ five wins have come against some of the most mediocre teams in the league (except Pittsburgh) and haven’t really played any good teams on their schedule except the Steelers. The Texans began the year as being predicted as one of the four best teams in the AFC, but started off a horrible 0-4-0 and, like Cleveland, find themselves in need of a win. Deshaun Watson was earmarked to return to the starting quarterback position and will face his former team, the club that drafted him. This year, Cleveland is 3-0 at home, while Houston is 3-1 on the road. Neither team came into this game able to run the ball, while the Texans have a good passing attack. The first quarter was not kind to Cleveland, who could not generate any offense, but this group settled down. The offensive line played well for the majority of the game and left QB Deshaun Watson with many good pockets to work in. But they also allowed four sacks. At the final gun, the Browns came back and won 27-24. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? ______________________________________________________ BROWNIES – Browns winners TE Harold Fannin – Is this name just a default entry each week? Might as well be, as each game he does something extraordinary that assists in the final score. the YAC king strikes again!!! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/CKHdPRMIIN — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 Against Houston, his reception at the 15-yard line and then took the ball down to the four after the tackle by LB Jake Hansen. One play later, the Browns went up by three. Had several other good catches, but this one got Cleveland in scoring range when they were behind by four. Back-to-back weeks of Harold Fannin Jr. fighting for yards on game-winning drives. — Nick Pedone (@NickPedone12) November 15, 2026 Did you see Fannin’s block on S Calen Bullock on Deshaun Watson’s TD scamper in the second quarter? Bullock was the only defender who had a chance, but Fannin walled him off. Led all receivers with 9 targets, 7 catches for 91 yards. CB Tyson Campbell – On the second-to-last play, Campbell was able to get a fist into the nest of WR Nico Collins and break up the pass. Two plays earlier, he was in coverage with WR Kayshon Boutte, which became an incompletion as Houston was trying to drive downfield. The contest did not begin swimmingly for Campbell as his soft coverage on Collins resulted in their first touchdown and a 7-0 lead. But he rebounded all game long. His interception in the second quarter was a “look what I found” moment and gave the offense hope. concentration on lock 🔒 https://t.co/Olw9kkjrsZ pic.twitter.com/w0wpj0wvoo — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 QB Deshaun Watson – Was a roller coaster of a game for Watson with numerous throws behind the receiver or in the turf. The Blake Whiteheart interception was leading the tight end just a smidge too far in, which he couldn’t get all of his fingers on the ball and instead tipped it. The overthrow to WR Jerry Jeudy would have been six. And why didn’t he toss the ball out of bounds right before the half instead of running up the gut with zero timeouts? a listen in to our first TD of the day 🔊 pic.twitter.com/zLEzpkb82j — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 However, Watson marched his offense up and down the field for most of the final three quarters. Had a shaky first half, going 8 for 15 for 126 yards, but had nerves of steel in the second half. Key third-down throws to Corley ended up with 10 points. Finished going 25 of 40 for 312 yards, a 7.8 yards per completion ratio, zero TDs with one pick, sacked four times with a 76.2 QB rating. Defense – What a good game from this side of the ball. Had a few throws that had little coverage on, but Houston QB C.J. Stroud was making small-window throws when either CB Denzel Ward or CB Ty Campbell was all over the receiver. nowhere to go 🙅 #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/CgFkW8tYpv — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was active all game with eight tackles, while LB Quincy Williams had nine. Both DT Mason Graham and DT Maliek Collins plugged the middle, which gave Houston little running room up the gut. Texans’ second-half possessions: punt, punt, punt, punt, TD, punt, punt, downs. Superb second-half effort. DE Isaiah McGuire – Early in the third quarter, Stroud ran out to the right flats, and McGuire beat RT Trent Brown and got a hand on his foot but could not trip up the QB. a big… DDDUUUBBB pic.twitter.com/KYZhCsRuak — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 But it forced an incompletion and another punt. He caught Stroud on the third-and-10 in the third quarter for the sack. With 34 ticks left in the game, it was McGuire who just missed bringing Stroud down on the third-and-10 incompletion. Three tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one QB hit. LB Carson Schwesinger – Another default name added to the top. This kid will miss a tackle, and then get right back up and trail and take down the ball carrier. With five minutes remaining, Schwesinger nailed RB Emari Demercado for no gain on first down. ate. pic.twitter.com/dcgu7QzNQD — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 Two misprints??!! – The scorecard for the Browns-Texans displays Cleveland went 7 for 15 on third-down efficiency. That can’t be right. And what’s this? Two penalties for 47 yards? With one being a 31-yard PI call? And undefeated at home this year? Will let ya know when the corrected stats come out…… ______________________________________________ FROWNIES Offense first quarter – What a dead group this was in the beginning. Three-and-out twice with three punts. Yawn. Three incompletions, one pass for loss, one run for zero yards, and a single first down. Big yawn. Big man doin' big things 📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/w7QUD1FgzK — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 15, 2026 RG Austin Barber – Had a bad day trying to keep out DT Logan Hall, who sacked Watson twice. Half of Houston’s four sacks were past Barber. Drops/misthrows – How many passes were touched by a Browns receiver and then not cradled in? The long bomb to WR KC Concepcion that he caught and then the ground flipped the ball loose killed a good drive. Fannin dropped a key third down. The overthrow to Jeudy was six points, and the Texans interception was off of TE Blake Whiteheart’s fingertips. Too many passes thrown behind their intended targets for one game. No running game – Still can’t run the ball. Anytime an offense has to throw 40 times means only one thing. _______________________________________________ Milk Bones – Why is the alphabet in that order? Is it because of that song? WR Malachi Corley – Definitely a role player, but had some moments. In the third quarter, he caught an 18-yard pass on a third-and-one that kept the drive going. This drive ended up with a touchdown, but without Corley’s effort in getting open, it would not have happened. He also grabbed the scramble throw from Watson with 4:40 left in the game for 11 yards on a third-and-two. This drive ended up with three points. Three catches for 37 yards. this team doesn't blink 👊 @canadadry | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/kOrMqyM8XA — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 Punt coverage team – The Texans had no luck gaining any yardage both times they dropped back to return a punt. Two punts for a grand total of 29 yards. Excellent coverage by Corley, Donovan McMillan, and Adin Huntington. S Donovan McMillion – Another key role player. Three tackles, with one being on punt coverage. The final play of the game was McMillion batting the ball down without holding onto the WR Xavier Hutchinson and giving the Texans another shot. title: Browns hit numerous milestones in win over Texans
summary: The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 NFL season with several question marks surrounding the franchise. How would Todd Monken fare at age 60 in his first head-coaching gig at the NFL level? What would the defense do with defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz at home in the recliner and Mike Rutenberg running a defense for the […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 NFL season with several question marks surrounding the franchise. How would Todd Monken fare at age 60 in his first head-coaching gig at the NFL level? What would the defense do with defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz at home in the recliner and Mike Rutenberg running a defense for the first time? And, since these are still the Browns, just what the heck is going on with the quarterback position? Those questions all laddered up to the one that counts the most, which was just how many wins this team can get in 2026. The expectations for that last one were low on the national level, as the sportsbooks set the over/under on Cleveland’s win total at 5.5, a figure that owner Jimmy Haslam confidently said he would take the over on prior to the start of the season . Well, if you believed that Haslam knew more than the oddsmakers, then you are one happy person, as Sunday’s latest comeback victory, this one a 27-24 defeat of the Houston Texans, means the Browns hit the over as they are now 6-4 on the season. That was not the only milestone the Browns reached on Sunday, however, as the victory pushes their record to 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. The Browns are the first team in NFL history to have their first 6 wins of a season all come by 4 points or fewer. 📽️via ( @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/X4fGIrFMaD — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 15, 2026 Cleveland’s three-point win was their sixth of the season (it would have been seven if quarterback Deshaun Watson had played against the New Orleans Saints), which makes the Browns the first team in NFL history to have each of their first six wins in a season come by four points or fewer. So let’s go back to those questions from the preseason and check on the answers: Monken as a first-time head coach? He has the Browns playing meaningful games in November , so check! Rutenberg as a first-time defensive coordinator? The defense is a huge part of why the Browns are 6-4, and today they held Houston to seven points and quarterback CJ Stroud to just 21 passing yards in the second half, so check! And that question about the quarterback? No one saw it coming, and no one can explain how he is doing it, but Deshaun Watson is the unquestioned starting quarterback for the rest of the season, so check! Enjoy the bye week, everyone. title: AFC playoff standings: Browns move up in Week 10 after big Texans win
summary: The Cleveland Browns Week 10 game versus the Houston Texans has huge implications for the AFC playoff picture. Heading into this week, the Browns were tied with the New England Patriots for the final playoff seed in the conference, losing out on the spot due to a tiebreaker, despite losing two straight games. While we […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 8: Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns on the field during the before a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on November 8, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns Week 10 game versus the Houston Texans has huge implications for the AFC playoff picture . Heading into this week, the Browns were tied with the New England Patriots for the final playoff seed in the conference , losing out on the spot due to a tiebreaker, despite losing two straight games. While we await kickoff in Cleveland’s game versus Houston, the Patriots were playing the Detroit Lions over in Germany. Early in the game, both teams lost key players when DE Aidan Hutchinson injured QB Drake Maye during a sack, then injured himself while celebrating that sack. While the Hutchinson injury is a big deal long term, New England’s loss of Maye to an ankle injury all but finished off any hopes they had of securing a victory this week. The Lions ended up controlling the rest of the game, leading to the lopsided 35-10 final score. With the loss, the Patriots drop to 5-5 and were a half game behind the Browns, who move up to the seventh seed. Cleveland’s come-from-behind victory in Week 10 then solidified their seventh seed. As of the end of the early Week 10 games, the AFC playoff standings are as follows: Buffalo Bills: 8-1 Kansas City Chiefs: 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars: 7-2 Pittsburgh Steelers: 6-2 Denver Broncos: 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals: 6-2 Cleveland Browns: 6-4 New England Patriots: 5-5 Las Vegas Raiders: 4-5 Baltimore Ravens: 4-5 Houston Texans: 3-6 Indianapolis Colts: 3-7 New York Jets: 2-8 Miami Dolphins: 1-8 Tennessee Titans: 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers: 0-8 With a big game on Sunday Night Football (Bengals vs. Steelers) and Monday Night Football with the Baltimore Ravens playing, we will update the AFC playoff picture and AFC North standings early Tuesday morning. No matter what, the Browns head into their bye week in a playoff spot, with a winning record and three straight home games, where they are undefeated this season.
