title: Browns Week 10 takeaways from huge comeback win over Texans
summary: The Cleveland Browns got good news before their Week 10 matchup with the Houston Texans, but started the game poorly, once again, which led to a lot of discontent among fans. Then the Browns turned things around to pull off the huge 27-24 win, solidifying their playoff position. Takeaways for Week 10 were written as […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns got good news before their Week 10 matchup with the Houston Texans , but started the game poorly, once again, which led to a lot of discontent among fans . Then the Browns turned things around to pull off the huge 27-24 win , solidifying their playoff position . Takeaways for Week 10 were written as the game went on, with the top notes from early in the game and building as the contest went on: Tackling problems again on the first Texans drive Missed tackles on Houston’s first offensive play, then again on the long 29-yard catch-and-run by Xavier Hutchinson . In the last few games, Ronnie Hickman was a big part of the issue, but he’s out this week, and it’s still happening. Sometimes the issue is trying to do too much; other times it is bad angles, and sometimes it seems like a lack of effort. No matter what, it is a problem Run game problem: Chicken or egg? It seems that Browns HC Todd Monken is trying to open up run lanes by throwing early, but is the problem that the backs and line don’t get enough carries to get the feel for the game early, or is Monken doing it that way because he doesn’t think the run game is good? Too much man-to-man? Just like they did in the playoffs a couple of years ago, Houston’s route combinations took advantage of all the man-to-man defense played by Cleveland. Routes going away from defenders: crossers, rub routes, etc., are easy pickings against all-man defense. It also opened up scramble lanes early for CJ Stroud. No quick pressure continues to be a problem Along with concerns with so much man-to-man, “marrying pass rush with coverage” is important, and Cleveland struggles to get any (ANY) quick pressure. Every once in a while, a defensive tackle might get one; otherwise, QBs have nothing to worry about going through their first few progressions. Deshaun Watson inconsistent ball placement is a problem A lot of good plays, especially with his legs, but Watson missed rookie KC Concepcion twice in the first quarter; the second could have been a long gain, but he was well behind the rookie, who had a lot of space in front of him if the ball was placed well. “Clown show” to let Stroud go instead of sacking him early 2nd Q Not even sure how to describe it, except two Browns defenders had hands on Stroud who looked like he threw the ball, so they didn’t finish the play and both let go of the QB, who then scrambled and threw the ball away instead of taking a sack. Described by many as proof of a “clown show,” Stroud then threw for a first down on the next play. Here is said play, if the description wasn’t good enough: The Browns Defensive Line Thought They Had CJ Stroud Sacked. They Thought He Threw The Ball, Then Realized He Didn't, And CJ Just Ran Away. Yeah, The Browns Are Gonna Brown. pic.twitter.com/4BnbUXb7r3 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 15, 2026 Browns not good enough to have big drops Jerry Jeudy in the first quarter, Conecpion in the second, Cleveland’s offense and team as a whole are not good enough to have those big drops on plays that would have been first downs and maybe huge gains. Players will drop the ball at times, but the ones on those big third downs or deep plays are not something the Browns can afford. Don’t take Szmyt for granted While kickers are crushing field goals, it’s important not to take Andre Szmyt for granted. Assuming a 49-yard field goal will be made is a nice place to be, and the kicker took care of that in the second quarter. Unfortunately, a long 54-yarder was no good in the fourth quarter, when he just pulled it. Big play and “grit” help CLE stay in it After going down 17-0, Watson to Jeudy for 65 yards and a designed Watson run helped put the Browns within 17-10 with four minutes left in the first half. 65 yards for Jerry Jeudy! HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GOSJ7PsssP — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 CJ Stroud’s ball placement was elite On most of his throws, it didn’t matter what Cleveland’s defense was doing in coverage because Stroud was leading his receiver perfectly, hitting them in their hands while they were on the move. Something Browns fans are hoping to find long-term. His early stats back up what we were seeing on the field: #Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud 13 for 16 for 166 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, 149.5 passer rating — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) November 15, 2026 Shortly after writing this, Stroud was intercepted by Tyson Campbell, a great play by the Cleveland cornerback: Tyson with the hands to take it back! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/rkBxeAhLME — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 2-minute drill run well, then not at all With less than a minute left, Cleveland’s offense got the ball over midfield, but twice they were unable to get out of bounds, forced to use timeouts instead of having them available for later. Then Watson just missed a wide-open Jeudy for what would have been a touchdown if the receiver had caught it, but the ball was just way too far. Then a surprising QB run and fumble meant the Browns didn’t get a field goal attempt to end the first half. Another one of those things where Cleveland is not good enough to have that missed throw or poor late-half decision-making. Zero penalties in the 1st half For a team that has had a huge penalty issue , important to note that they did not have a single penalty in the first half. The Browns got called for their first penalty on the punt return to start their first offensive possession of the 2nd half. As they usually do, the penalty made things more difficult on the offense with poor field position. Huge change after 1st quarter It often seems like DC Mike Rutenburg spends the start to the game trying to figure out the other offense, then makes some kind of huge change. This happened again after the first quarter, with stop after stop, including early in the second half. “A game of adjustments.” Will Houston change things to adjust to Cleveland? Monken’s offense also seemed to make some key adjustments, even though the run game continues to struggle early in the second half. Creativity works! A callback to a creative inside run that Jarvis Landry scored on (and is used by other teams), Monken calls a creative, misdirection run for Concepcion: KC takes it in! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/jKfEppfyRi — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 Browns defense in 2nd, 3rd quarters After giving up 17 points, Cleveland’s defense forced a punt, intercepted Stroud, then forced three straight three-and-outs by Houston’s offense, and another to start the fourth quarter. “Houston does not have a first down in the second half,” as said by the announcers early in the fourth quarter. Watson does just enough, quite often While the Browns quarterback was behind receivers often, as well as the victim of some drops, Watson makes enough plays to keep Cleveland’s offense moving. Whether it is scrambling, running, or nice touch on a pass to Dylan Sampon late in the third quarter, Watson is often moving the offense forward. Far from perfect, but enough can be enough at times. Late 3rd-quarter drive gave defense rest; Browns take first lead After Houston’s punt, Cleveland’s offense was able to burn over six minutes off the clock, leading just six seconds on the clock going into the fourth quarter after the ensuing kickoff. The Browns defense had one play to defend, a run, over the span of 20-plus minutes of real time. Could be very helpful in the final stanza. Unfortunately… Redzone issues continue It happens to all teams, but Cleveland’s offense seems to bog down a lot in the redzone with plays having almost no chance of success. Late in the third quarter, the Browns couldn’t convert on 1st and 10 from the 10-yard line, settling for a field goal and taking a 20-17 lead. Cheap penalty takes away INT “He was actually in good position…” started the announcer, but most looking at the play would say it wasn’t a penalty, and it eliminated…

title: Houston Texans vs. Cleveland Browns recap: A big comeback at home leads to Browns win
summary: It was all Texans to begin this game, as their offense couldn’t be stopped and Cleveland was down 17-0 early. But then, the switch flipped, and the Browns scored 20 unanswered to lead 20-17. A little back-and-forth saw the Browns re-take the lead in the final minute, 27-24, with the Texans needing a field goal […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns scores a 6-yard rushing touchdown during the second quarter against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was all Texans to begin this game, as their offense couldn’t be stopped and Cleveland was down 17-0 early. But then, the switch flipped, and the Browns scored 20 unanswered to lead 20-17. A little back-and-forth saw the Browns re-take the lead in the final minute, 27-24, with the Texans needing a field goal to tie. The defense held on, and Cleveland won to improve to 6-4! That also includes being 4-0 at home, with the bye coming up and then three more homes games in a row. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Texans vs. Browns The Cleveland Browns got the opening kickoff, with QB Deshaun Watson at the helm. After a quick 7-yard pass to TE Harold Fannin , a swing pass to RB Quinshon Judkins was dropped for a loss of 2 yards, and then Watson’s third-down pass sailed over WR KC Concepcion , leading to a punt. Cleveland allowed a 22-yard return on their punt, allowing the Texans to start at the 39 yard line. Their offense went fast then: an 8-yard run by RB Woody Marks , a 29-yard pass to WR Xavier Hutchinson , and a 13-yard pass to WR Nico Collins to set up 1st-and-goal at the 8 yard line. An illegal formation penalty, followed by a run, put the Texans in 2nd-and-goal at the 12 yard line. It didn’t matter: QB C.J. Stroud tossed a perfect pass over the middle to Collins, just beyond the reach of CB Tyson Campbell , for the 12-yard touchdown, as the Browns gave up their league-leading sixth opening drive touchdown this season to put Houston up 7-0. Ball magnet Nico 📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/mwUTwIbjSs — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 15, 2026 The Browns also went three-and-out on their next drive, as WR Jerry Jeudy couldn’t haul in an intermediate pass on 2nd-and-7. Then, on third down, Concepcion caught a pass short of the marker, and the defender made a good tackle to prevent a first down. P Corey Bojorquez angled his second punt to the boundary, going out of bounds at the 12 yard line. Stroud hit Collins on a crossing pattern against CB Myles Harden for an immediate 22-yard gain. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-1, a simple playfake and quick toss to Marks gained 15 yards. Even on a broken play after that, Stroud just took off, wide open, over the middle for 7 yards. Two plays later, on 3rd-and-3, Stroud’s sideline pass for WR Tank Dell was incomplete, leading to a field goal try by K Ka’imi Fairbairn . He hit from 45 yards out to put the Texans up 10-0 with 4:25 to go in the first quarter. On the Browns’ third drive, an 8-yard run by Judkins was followed by a 1-yard run by RB Dylan Sampson , and then a quarterback sneak by Watson picked up the team’s first first down of the game. A few plays later, Watson threw it behind Concepcion, leading to the defender knocking the ball away. On third down, Watson had to scramble, but only got 8.5 yards, leading to another punt. This time, Bojorquez’ angled punt was only 30 yards, going out of bounds at the 25 yard line. In one play, the Texans got right back to where Cleveland just punted from. Stroud faced no pressure, then calmly rolled to the sideline, waited, and was able to hit Dell for 29 yards. Then, to close out the quarter, he again took off for 11 more yards to the Browns’ 35 yard line, with Cleveland being out-gained 159 to 34 yards. Mooooovin' the chains! 📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/INy8omIK4I — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 15, 2026 2nd Quarter – Texans vs. Browns The rather pathetic performance by the defense continued to start the second quarter, including a bizarre play when DT Maliek Collins had Stroud in his arms for a sack, then let him go to allow Stroud to throw the ball away. Several plays later, on a playaction rollout, Stroud threw the ball back to the inside for Hutchinson, who was wide open for an 8-yard touchdown to put the Texans up 17-0. Another one, thank you! 📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/0XVidGjWqw — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 15, 2026 On the Browns’ fourth drive, Watson launched one deep to Concepcion, and he got both hands on it as he dove to the ground, but then lost it for an incompletion. After that, Watson hit Fannin for 17 yards, and then Watson scrambled for 20 yards on the next play. The drive went no further after that, but K Andre Szmyt gave the Browns their first points of the day with a 49-yard field goal to make it 17-3. 20 yards down the line for Deshaun! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/F1O2NNvFKg — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 The Browns had CB Denzel Ward on Collins to start the next drive. Stroud targeted Collins all three plays, and it led to a pass breakup, a 5-yard gain, and then a tightly-contested 6-yard gain to move the chains. After that, the Browns finally forced a punt, in part thanks to LB Carson Schwesinger bringing down Dell for a loss of 4 yards on second down. WR Denzel Boston , in for the dinged up Concepcion, fielded the punt at the 13 yard line and returned it 16 yards to the Browns’ 29 yard line with 5:05 remaining in the half. For the second drive in a row, Watson launched another bomb that was beautifully placed for Jeudy, and he hauled it in for a 65-yard gain. a HUGE catch to set up the score 👏 #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/KUwh2NXJBx — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 One play later, Watson faked it to Judkins and then kept it himself, going around the right edge, for a 6-yard touchdown run to make it a 17-10 game with 4:12 left in the half. strollin' into the end zone! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/wwrB6r3qBi — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 On the Texans return, they were flagged 15 yards for a personal foul after the kickoff, pushing them back to the 19 yard line. Marks began with an 11-yard run to give them some more comfortable position. A 12-yard connection to Collins eventually set up 2nd-and-10 heading into the two-minute warning. The Texans kept marching on, but then Stroud tried to hit Collins on a slant that he got jammed up in, allowing CB Tyson Campbell to come up with an interception with 39 seconds to go at their own 21 yard line. Tyson with the hands to take it back! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/rkBxeAhLME — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 With all three timeouts, the Browns got to their own 38 yard line on two plays, burning two timeouts, with 22 seconds left. A 16-yard strike to Boston, and the use of their final timeout, got the ball to the Texans’ 46 yard line with 16 seconds left. Cleveland needed a completion and spike to have a field goal chance. Stunningly, the Texans had a weird defense, and Watson overthrew an open Jeudy that could have gone for a touchdown. Watson overthrows a wide open Jerry Jeudy. This would've been a TD. pic.twitter.com/oZfXsnGEFj — Roberto Shenanigans (@Rob_Shenanigans) November 15, 2026 Now, with 11 seconds left, the Texans were guarding the sideline. Cleveland ran a quarterback draw for some reason to take the game into the half. 3rd Quarter – Texans vs. Browns The Browns’ defensive pressure was present to start the second half, forcing Stroud into three incompletions and a quick punt. An illegal block in the back penalty on Boston’s punt return forced the Browns to begin at the 21 yard line. Unfortunately, they also went three-and-out after Watson was sacked for the first time on the day on third down. After the punt, and a hold on the Texans, Houston took over at their own 22 yard line. Houston began their next drive with two runs, setting up 3rd-and-5. After a false start by Houston, the Browns’ defense finally sacked Stroud as DE Isaiah McGuire got to him for a loss of 9 yards. Boston returned the punt 9 yards to the Texans’ 47 yard line. Watson hit a returning Concepcion for 8 yards to set up…

title: Cowboys vs. 49ers Stock Report: Caleb Downs has rough day
summary: The scoreboard can often lie. On Sunday, the final between the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers read 46-40 in favor of the visiting Niners, but anyone who watched the game knows that it was in no way that close. It is a stretch to call Dallas’ flurry late in the game “garbage time,” but […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The scoreboard can often lie. On Sunday, the final between the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers read 46-40 in favor of the visiting Niners, but anyone who watched the game knows that it was in no way that close. It is a stretch to call Dallas’ flurry late in the game “garbage time,” but it all came when San Francisco was clearly ready to get on a plane and head home. The point is that nothing felt seriously in doubt. You only lose games so soundly, regardless of what the scoreboard said as noted, because of a collective failure from people involved. It should come as no surprise that our stock report is filled with more downs than ups as a result of it all. Let’s begin. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer We say it every week. What more is there to say? The scoreboard is a liar as noted, so it is in no way like Brian Schottenheimer had his team ready to play. What’s more is that he saw them take another third quarter off so that the game got out of hand, and then everybody started caring as time was running out in the fourth quarter. Maybe if the Cowboys were better we’d give Schotty a pass for this being the big, bad San Francisco 49ers. But you know what? They are the big, bad 49ers. Someone has to stand up and make Dallas respectable to a team they were once proper and legitimate rivals with. Someone has to be the head coach that has a second winning streak before Thanksgiving of his second season. Those people were not Brian Schottenheimer this week. Stock Down: Christian Parker It is Kyle Shanahan. We know that. But goodness. The Dallas Cowboys defense appeared to be taking a few steps these last few weeks, but we were cautious because of the quality of opposing quarterbacks they played. It turns out that context mattered. I’ve long been against moving on from Parker because the defense needs consistency at some point. But what is there to hang your hat on? How can you justify what is happening? In what world? Stock Down: Caleb Downs This was far and away Caleb Downs’ worst game as a professional. It unfortunately came a week after his best. I guess that’s what happens when you are tasked with hanging on for dear life against George Kittle. Downs fell short of that challenge, but at least unlike the rest of his defensive teammates, he can still say he is learning all of this on the fly. Still though, we really hyped Downs up over the offseason. We believed he was ready for this. On Sunday he wasn’t. Stock Down: Cobie Durant Caleb was one of two Cowboys defenders to get completely run over by San Francisco’s Kaelon Black as Cobie Durant was the other. The Cowboys are never ready for the physical fight that is the 49ers. Never. It is a shame. Stock Down: All linebackers It was impossible to boil this down to just one. San Francisco is very talented, but notably they are exceptionally well-coached. Kyle Shanahan had every Cowboys linebacker criss-crossing themselves all day with all of his uses of motion and play action. On the second Deebo Samuel touchdown, literally 10 Cowboys players bought the fake and left Joey Porter Jr. on one side to take on what Tom Brady called a red wave. You can’t get got every time. Stock Down: KaVontae Turpin He had a drop of a pass that landed squarely in his hands. How does that even happen? Remember when Turpin was regarded to be a special teams ace, though? Remember when he was providing the team with an elite advantage? Where is that? What is he offering that anyone else can’t from a return game standpoint? I will take any answer. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey His only miss in this game was an extra point, but the point (no pun intended) is that he missed yet another kick. We are sort of running out of excuses for Aubrey at this point. It can’t always be this, that, or whatever is convenient. He is the top-paid kicker in the NFL and he is in no way among the most reliable kickers in the league right now. His miss was an extra point as noted in this game. An extra point! At home! Indoors! The Cowboys hardly lost because of that missed point, but these keep piling up. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams The Cowboys absolutely have a war daddy. Quinnen Williams might be the best player on the Cowboys period right now. He did his best to singlehandedly save the team at the end as he forced a fumble that almost made the attempted rally actually possible. It is legitimately impressive how Quinnen is not allowing the state of things to impact his effort. I suppose spending a ton of time with the New York Jets will harden you in that way. Stock Up: George Pickens Let’s state that the taunting penalty was silly. We all agree. But wow what a game from George Pickens. He essentially was the entire offense for much of the game, at least before it got away from Dallas and they were playing catch up. It is hard to wonder what could or would have happened if this performance came right before the trade deadline. It didn’t, though. And now he and Dallas are stuck with each other until contract negotiations that will surely be calm and easy. Stock Up: LT Overton In addition to Quinnen Williams the Cowboys also saw some force up front from one of their rookies in LT Overton, including an impressive batted pass. If the Cowboys are ever going to find true and proper form in the future it is going to be because they develop a bevy of options along the defensive line. Hopefully Overton is a part of that future alongside Quinnen Williams and whoever else the Cowboys fan find between now and that hypothetical day.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 6 plays that cost the Cowboys vs. 49ers
summary: 46 points. The Dallas Cowboys defense, that we know isn’t very good, allowed 46 points on 9.4 yards per play. How many times can you be disappointed before you’re no longer surprised? At least just once more as we saw the defense surrender multiple big plays to San Francisco. The offense made their mistakes as […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images 46 points. The Dallas Cowboys defense, that we know isn’t very good, allowed 46 points on 9.4 yards per play. How many times can you be disappointed before you’re no longer surprised? At least just once more as we saw the defense surrender multiple big plays to San Francisco. The offense made their mistakes as well, but it’s hard not to focus on giving up nearly a 50-burger at home. You can pick so many plays to choose from as to why the Cowboys lost but perhaps it’s easier to choose the ones that most irritated you in watching the Cowboys lose to the San Francisco 49ers yet again. Here are the plays that should get under your skin the most and why they matter in the grander scheme. 1. Christian McCaffrey’s 74-yard touchdown on third-and-long The Cowboys looked like they had wrestled the early momentum back from San Francisco after a George Pickens score. It’s not too many times the Cowboys have led by multiple scores this season and the defense has needed any possible large lead it could get. Facing 3rd-and-8 with the 49ers on their own 26-yard line, the Dallas defense proved why. The Cowboys did a great job of putting initial pressure on Brock Purdy but he managed to scramble out of the pocket and found Christian McCaffrey as got behind the defense for a short pass from Purdy. From there he went untouched for a 74-yard score. For a moment you felt that the Cowboys could put the pressure on the 49ers for a change but boy would that be an ominous sign of things to come. 2. Deebo Samuel’s 70-yard touchdown run The theme of today was one explosive play after another. If there’s one thing you expect from a Kyle Shanahan offense is misdirection and out-leveraging the defense for an advantage. Deebo Samuel historically has been a thorn in the side of the Cowboys, and once again he stuck the Cowboys right where it hurts. Samuel took a reverse pitch from Kaelon Black and raced 70 yards down the sideline for a touchdown. When you watch the replay, notice how long it takes for the defense to process what is happening. Samuel has a convoy of blockers out in front while the majority of the Cowboys defense is on the other side of the field. What are some of the basic principles of defense at at any level let alone the NFL? Defensive pursuit and perimeter containment. That’s where the Cowboys tend to struggle mightily an Samuel made them pay. One missed assignment or poor angle against a player like Samuel can turn an ordinary running play into an instant touchdown. 3. Kaelon Black’s 25-yard touchdown run The Cowboys avoided letting the 49ers score points at the end of the first half before they received the second half kickoff. Down by a one point, letting the 49ers score a touchdown would be detrimental. Unfortunately, Dallas could not prevent that from happening and rookie running back Kaelon Black ran all over the defense to make a point. The play puts another red-hot spotlight on Caleb Downs. The rookie safety was run over by Black on a touchdown that helped San Francisco seize control of the second half. Downs also had trouble finishing plays in space, including a missed opportunity to contain Purdy before the quarterback found McCaffrey for a long touchdown. For a player with his expectations, the Cowboys need more consistency, particularly against offenses that force defenders to make decisions in space. We need to see better from Downs down the stretch. 4. Brandon Aubrey’s missed extra point and Dallas’ failed two-point attempt This is where the wheels started to fall off. Sure Brandon Aubrey made two kicks beyond 50 yards. However, Aubrey hasn’t been as automatic anymore and now you sometimes have to hold you breath if he can make the routine kicks. With Cowboys looking to take seven-point lead, Aubrey missed the extra point. This left the Cowboys chasing points for the remainder of the game. With the game going the way that it did, any points at all were needed. Dallas had an unsuccessful two-point try in an effort to make up the difference after Aubrey’s miss. Aubrey has also had kickoff penalties this year and onside kick attempt at the end of the game wasn’t nearly good enough. There’s something off with Aubrey, and whatever it is, it is hurting the Cowboys. 5. Dallas’ comeback is undone by another McCaffrey touchdown For all intents and purposes, this was the last straw. The Cowboys fought tirelessly to get back in the game but fell short on defense. After Prescott connected with Ryan Flournoy for an 11-yard touchdown on fourth down, Dallas had reduced San Francisco’s lead to 38-32 with 3:42 remaining. The Cowboys needed one defensive stop to give Prescott a chance to win. Instead, just 10 seconds of game clock later, Purdy found McCaffrey for a 66-yard touchdown on second-and-10. San Francisco added a two-point conversion, extending its lead to 46-32. This was arguably the most decisive moment of the game. Dallas had finally pulled within one possession, only for the defense to surrender another enormous touchdown immediately. 6. Quinnen Williams almost forces the turn over the Cowboys need After the Cowboys drew the score to 40-46, it was longshot that the Cowboys could get the ball back with enough time to take the late lead. Quinnen Williams who has been one of the few bright spots for the Cowboys defense almost came up huge. Looking to drain the remaining time off the clock, the 49ers handed the ball of to Kaelon Black. Williams darted through the 49ers offensive line to meet Black in the hole. Williams was able to dislodge the ball from Black’s arms. The Cowboys had a chance to recover the ball before Black quickly regained possession for the 49ers. If the defense can’t be average, the least it can be is opportunistic and Williams almost gave that much when the team needed it badly. The Cowboys scored 40 points and still found a way to lose. That’s the frustrating reality of this team. Dak Prescott threw five touchdowns, George Pickens delivered three scores, and Quinnen Williams nearly gave Dallas one final opportunity to steal a victory. Yet none of it mattered because the defense couldn’t stop San Francisco from producing one explosive play after another. At some point, these breakdowns stop being isolated mistakes and become the identity of your football team. For Dallas, that point may have already arrived.
author: LP Cruz

title: Cowboys news: Dallas defense gets trampled in loss to the 49ers
summary: Dallas walked into Sunday afternoon’s game as an underdog with a lot to prove. With the Giants losing on Thursday night to the Commanders, and following a victory last week to the Colts, if the Cowboys defense showed some semblance of life, Dallas could turn the season around. Unfortunately, that is not what happened at […]
full_text: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dallas walked into Sunday afternoon’s game as an underdog with a lot to prove. With the Giants losing on Thursday night to the Commanders, and following a victory last week to the Colts, if the Cowboys defense showed some semblance of life, Dallas could turn the season around. Unfortunately, that is not what happened at all. Dallas allowed multiple explosive plays and the defense gave up 580 yards of offense and 46 points. The Cowboys’ defense was historically bad in 46 – 40 loss to 49ers- Shane Taylor, Inside The Star The Dallas Cowboys faced their biggest test of the season. And in a game where the Cowboys could have made a statement, they fell flat on their face. The Cowboys allowed 3 touchdowns of longer than 65 yards — all of which occurred without the player scoring the touchdown being touched. They gave up 46 points, 580 yards of offense — 370 passing and 210 rushing. If this was any other team, the defensive coordinator would be FIRE by tomorrow. Don’t Forget These 5: Effects of Aubrey’s missed extra point- Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com It is tough to pin the loss on a single play, given that the Cowboys defense had multiple opportunities to give the team a chance and continually fell short. However, these five plays definitely had a big impact. Onside kick decision? – The Cowboys were able to score and cut the lead to six with just 46 seconds left. While the onside kick made sense to try to get the ball back, the fact that the Cowboys had three timeouts could’ve made the case that they should have just kicked the ball deep. Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys’ Predictable Week 10 Loss to 49ers- Mike Moraitis, Sports Illustrated This is not a game that Dallas was expected to win. But given the defensive improvement over the last few weeks, one would have hoped to see a little more from that side of the ball. The Niners averaged an obscene 9.4 yards per play. The 584 total yards the Cowboys gave up amounts to the most Dallas has allowed in a home game in team history. We might very well be watching the worst defense in Cowboys history. 5 blunt reactions from Cowboys’ deflating loss to 49ers in Week 10- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat This game feels like another lowlight in a disappointing season. Although the final score may make it seem like Dallas was in it, they were thoroughly beaten by the 49ers. Brian Schottenheimer is his own worst enemy When looking back on why/how Dallas lost, Schottenheimer’s decision to punt on 4th-and-2 at the end of the first half looms very large. And in a game where the 49ers did whatever they so chose to do on offense, the jokes will follow. The 49ers poked fun at the Cowboys multiple times with Texas- and Dallas-specific posts, including cowboy boots outside of AT&T Stadium with a 49ers cowboy hat on top of them. In one post, lyrics from country star Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” were in the caption, while another caption read: “Brought the star power.” 4 losers and 2 winners from the Cowboys loss to the 49ers- David Halprin, Blogging The Boys Playoff hopes The Cowboys were given a chance to really tighten the chase in the NFC East. title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys from the 49ers game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost 46-40 to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Here’s what we learned. Sacks showed up during a holistically poor defensive outing Over the last three weeks coming into this game, the Cowboys pass rush has picked up the pace, racking up nine sacks over that time. The trend continued this week […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys lost 46-40 to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Here’s what we learned. Sacks showed up during a holistically poor defensive outing Over the last three weeks coming into this game, the Cowboys pass rush has picked up the pace, racking up nine sacks over that time. The trend continued this week with Cowboys exploding for five sacks against a stout 49ers offensive line that’s only allowed eight on the season. Four of those sacks came in the first half. The defense continued to apply pressure on Brock Purdy throughout the game, especially from the defensive interior. Unfortunately, at times Brock Purdy was able to clear the rush and make great plays downfield to Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and others. Still, the effort from the pass rush was a bright spot for the fourth straight week and should continue to improve as the season continues. Even with the sacks, however, Dallas was gashed on way too many big plays to be competitive for an entire game. The defense turned into a pumpkin (again) As well as the defense played in the first half (minus one big broken play), they fell apart in the second. Misdirection plays from an offense known for misdirection plays shocked absolutely nobody watching, yet Dallas bit hard time after time. A big end around touchdown from Deebo Samuel seemed to be the play that broke the Cowboys. After that point, the 49ers never looked back, scoring touchdowns on nearly every possession. The defense couldn’t muster much until halfway through the fourth quarter when they finally forced a 49ers punt before giving up the game sealing touchdown on the following 49ers drive. The defense continues to prove to be one of the most untrustworthy units in professional football. The offense disappeared for too long Dak Prescott and the offense put up 16 points in the first half behind an efficient rushing attack and a strong passing game. George Pickens grabbed two touchdowns in his return back to the field in the first half in a game that should have gone into the half tied if not for a missed Brandon Aubrey extra point. Pickens would go on to finish the day with three touchdowns in total. Despite the success, however, Dallas would put up just nine points through the second and third quarters until they broke through with 21 points in the fourth. At one point, the 49ers went on a 28-3 scoring stretch. If the defense is going to disappear, the offense needs to stop the bleeding and somewhat keep pace. Fair or not, it’s the position this team found themselves this week and oftentimes this season. At the end of the day, however, any team that scores 40 points should easily win the game. We can talk about the 49ers defense playing a bit soft with a big lead, but that point total should always result in a win. For the 2026 Cowboys, however, losing with massive offensive numbers is extremely unsurprising.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: 4 losers and 2 winners from the Cowboys loss to the 49ers
summary: We knew coming in it would be long odds for the Dallas Cowboys to beat the San Francisco 49ers. After staying competitive early, they eventually fell apart, only to make a mad dash to almost get back on top. In the end, they ran out of time in a 46-40 loss. Let’s take a look […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We knew coming in it would be long odds for the Dallas Cowboys to beat the San Francisco 49ers. After staying competitive early, they eventually fell apart, only to make a mad dash to almost get back on top. In the end, they ran out of time in a 46-40 loss. Let’s take a look at the winners and losers from the game. Losers Playoff hopes The Cowboys were given a chance to really tighten the chase in the NFC East. The New York Giants loss to the Washington Commanders gave Dallas a little opening to apply pressure on the Giants, and get their own momentum going. They needed an upset of the San Francisco 49ers, something that would have given the team some serious fuel going forward. Alas, none of that came true. They basically just handed that loss back to the Giants and time is running out. Christian Parker When you give up 584 yards on offense, you have to be on the losing end of things. We will stipulate that some of that yardage wasn’t directly on Parker, but the buck ultimately stops with the defensive coordinator. The Cowboys found themselves over-pursuing, missing tackles, and losing players in coverage – it was bad. The Cowboys did some good things on defense, but in a crucial moment they had Von Miller covering Christian McCaffrey. That can’t happen. Dak Prescott (with context) I understand that Dak Prescott threw for five touchdowns and had a rating over 100. I concede that fact. But honestly, a ton of that came in the frantic fourth-quarter comeback. He was excellent then. But earlier in the game, he wasn’t as sharp. He was off-target on some throws, and didn’t make good decisions when he left the pocket. His choice not to run the ball when flushed out hurt on several different occasions. It wasn’t like Dak was awful, but early in the game he wasn’t Superman, which is what Dallas needed. Once the Cowboys fell way behind, he donned the cape but it was too late. Big play/3rd down defense We already touched on defensive coordinator Parker, but we have to single out the defense for their extraordinarily bad play on third-downs, and their ability to give up the big play at all the wrong times. The Cowboys defense allowed the 49ers to convert six of eleven third-down attempts, and some of those were 3rd-and-longs. The Cowboys defense just can’t close the deal. Winners George Pickens Having George Pickens was what kept Dallas in the game early on. He caught 11 passes for 145 yards and three touchdowns. Yes, his taunting penalty late was another dumb Cowboys move. But he was keeping Dallas in the game. Pass rush (with context) For the most part, the Cowboys pass rush was the one thing the defense was doing well. They picked up five sacks and had Brock Purdy under pressure for much of the game. They also did okay in run defense, once you remove Deebo Samuels’ long run. One problem they had was letting Purdy escape the pocket. The Cowboys were undone by many heady plays from Purdy once he evaded the initial rush. They can’t be expected to do everything though, and getting five sacks was certainly good work. The best the pass rush has looked in a long time. And shoutout to Quinnen Williams who was dominant again, collecting 10 tackles and a sack, while helping to cause a couple of the other sacks.
author: David Halprin

title: The Cowboys and 49ers score literally never happened before
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost on Sunday… but we all won. Kind of. Except not. In case you have no idea what we are talking about… when the scoreboard read 46-40 at the conclusion of Sunday’s chaotic fourth quarter, it was literally the first time in NFL history that 46-40 was on one. If you are […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers and Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys meet after San Francisco defeated Dallas 46-40 at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Tsexas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys lost on Sunday… but we all won. Kind of. Except not. In case you have no idea what we are talking about… when the scoreboard read 46-40 at the conclusion of Sunday’s chaotic fourth quarter, it was literally the first time in NFL history that 46-40 was on one. If you are unaware this phenomenon is referred to as a “scorigami” as it is a score that has never occurred before in NFL history. Hey now, the Cowboys made history on Sunday! This was the 1,099th unique score to ever happen so it took quite a while before someone was able to say that they were a part of 46-40. History like this is the only kind that the Cowboys are going to be a part of these days as they are 4-6 and, despite how bad the NFC East is this season, very likely going to be missing out on the playoffs for a third year in a row. At least we have scorigami.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys late rally not enough, lose to 49ers as season slips away
summary: We knew it was going to happen, to be fair. The Dallas Cowboys were and have not been any sort of match for the San Francisco 49ers in quite some time. Sunday was just the latest example of it being put on display for all of the world to see. Honestly though, it was somewhat […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 15: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. breaks free for a touchdown during the NFL game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Dallas Cowboys on November 15, 2026 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We knew it was going to happen, to be fair. The Dallas Cowboys were and have not been any sort of match for the San Francisco 49ers in quite some time. Sunday was just the latest example of it being put on display for all of the world to see. Honestly though, it was somewhat of a game in the first half. The Cowboys trailed their big brothers by only a point at halftime, but the game is four quarters and Dallas has proven that they cannot go the distance with the elites of the NFL in recent memory. And the end was technically a rally, but San Francisco certainly took their foot off of the gas. With a 4-6 record the Cowboys are swirling in a way that is foreign to most, but natural and common for them. They failed yet again to establish Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak as the team’s next head coach and their next opportunity, should they beat the Tennessee Titans next week, will literally be an exact year after the last one concluded (Thanksgiving Day). This team is a shell of the ones that once upon a time took on physical and intimidating 49ers teams to claim victory. Will we ever see those days again? It is getting hard to even lie to ourselves and say yes. First Quarter San Francisco won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense on the field first. Everyone held their breath. It felt like such a grind for the Cowboys early on. Interestingly very early there was a roughing the passer called against Dak Prescott… by Osa Odighizuwa of all people. Weird times. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens each failed to come down a pass that they arguably should have, and as a result the Cowboys had to settle for a 52-yard field goal attempt that Brandon Aubrey converted. 3-0, Dallas. Field goals can often feel like failures and the 49ers made that one feel that way pretty quickly. The visitors were in the endzone in no time to make things 7-3 and put Dallas in an early position where they had to chase. Deebo is IN and the 49ers make a statement on the opening drive SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RJJg2M4KpS — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Early in the next drive the Cowboys faced a fork in the road. It was fourth and short right near midfield and they called a timeout to make sure they had the right play called. They did indeed. Dallas ran a quarterback sneak and moved the chains and everyone exhaled given the early deficit and a fear of growing. That bravery was rewarded. Soon Dak Prescott found George Pickens in the endzone and the Cowboys had taken the lead back. GP3 TD!!! pic.twitter.com/tbmdsoErIn — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 15, 2026 Amazingly, the Cowboys even forced a San Francisco punt right after and ran one play before the quarter officially ended. Second Quarter That newfound possession did not turn into much. The Cowboys punted it back just 21 seconds into the second quarter. San Francisco turned that possession into points by way of a field goal and the game was tied at 10. This is when things got particularly chaotic. After a conversion on another fourth and short, Dak Prescott found George Pickens once again for a big-time touchdown. GEORGE! CEEDEE! pic.twitter.com/pIWU3chGdk — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 15, 2026 Unfortunately Brandon Aubrey missed the extra point so Dallas only took a 16-10 lead. Still, it felt good. That did not hold for long. While the Cowboys got to Brock Purdy early in the next possession it was their inability to get to him on 3rd and 8 that proved costly. He found Christian McCaffrey with wide open space and CMC took it to the house for a touchdown that gave San Francisco a 17-16 lead. BROCK TO CMC OH MY SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JoKDvzWC3K — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Dallas was unable to do anything with the ball and punted it back away. What was particularly troubling about this was San Francisco had the ball with 1:10 left and it felt like they were going to set themselves up to double-dip as they were set to receive the second-half kickoff. Thankfully they were unable to do anything of note. Everyone went to break with the visitors leading 17-16. Third Quarter A penalty on the return and then a quick false start put San Francisco at a disadvantage early on. Never bad to see. That didn’t seem to bother Brock Purdy and his friends. After putting together a bit of a drive it was Kaelon Black who put the finishing touches on things… including Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant, unfortunately. KAELON BLACK RUNNING THROUGH THE DEFENSE SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/G9ZWuR4cLB — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Early on it looked like quick doom for Dallas. 49ers players were celebrating a fumble recovery, but the officials quickly said that Javonte Williams was down by contact. The FOX broadcast showed Fred Warner very clearly punching the ball loose before Javonte was down, but somehow Kyle Shanahan did not challenge it. Soon Dak Prescott found Ryan Flournoy for a big gain and Dallas was suddenly in striking distance. Things ultimately fizzled out though, but a 52-yard field goal attempt was salvaged and Brandon Aubrey was good on it just like he was from the same range early in the game. San Francisco retained the lead, 24-19. It was then that everything broke… again. The 49ers got Dallas to bite on defense and that was all Deebo Samuel needed to race to the endzone. San Francisco suddenly led 31-19 and it was getting dark both out and inside. DEEEEEEBOOOOOOO SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3RwQ4dNchJ — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Soon enough the Cowboys were facing a critical 4th and short from the San Francisco 40-yard line. Given the stakes and situation… this felt like a must-convert. The Cowboys rolled the dice. Dak Prescott threw an interception. At the very least it moved the 49ers back about 30 yards. You gotta take what you can. Malik Mustapha picks it off on 4th down! SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oIOxWW2PTG — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 The quarter ended with San Francisco moving once more. Fourth Quarter They wound up moving all the way to the endzone once more. It was Christian McCaffrey again. San Francisco held a 38-19 lead at this point and it was all the way over. Everything left was just logistical. Maybe you consider what happened next to be garbage time. Whatever the case, the Cowboys did narrow the lead a bit by way of the third Prescott-to-Pickens touchdown on the day. My fantasy opponent this week had them both… joy. George Pickens hat trick! SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OgMlJpLJQO — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 Technically the Cowboys held life at this moment. But they would have to stop the 49ers multiple times to see it through. They got a stop! And then a score! Ryan Flournoy found the endzone to make this feel legitimately possible. FLO pic.twitter.com/9i6M141wA6 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 16, 2026 The game was on the line. One stop. That’s all it would take. GOTI could finish it. Right? Right? Wrong. Don't leave CMC in the open field 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/hGnsBSY5V5 — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) November 16, 2026 Letting Von Miller, in the year 2026, be your last line of defense against Christian McCaffrey is a bold decision. Somehow, it is the one that the Dallas Cowboys made. San Francisco failed to get the two-point conversion if you are curious so Dallas “only” trailed by 14 with over three minutes left. The Cowboys were still doing what they could to make it a game. Prescott found CeeDee Lamb for a score and ran in the…

title: Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10
summary: The Dallas Cowboys return home at 4-5 after escaping the Indianapolis Colts with a nail-biting victory, but the difficulty level rises considerably this week. The San Francisco 49ers are at 7-1 and own the best record in the NFC. Dallas showed against the Colts that its offense can move the football against anybody, but beating […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys return home at 4-5 after escaping the Indianapolis Colts with a nail-biting victory, but the difficulty level rises considerably this week. The San Francisco 49ers are at 7-1 and own the best record in the NFC. Dallas showed against the Colts that its offense can move the football against anybody, but beating San Francisco will require a much cleaner performance, and scoring touchdowns rather than settling for field goals, or worse, falling victim to turnovers. When San Francisco has the ball Everything starts with Christian McCaffrey. San Francisco does not need him to simply line up and run between the tackles, Kyle Shanahan moves him around, gets him involved in the passing game and uses his presence to create space for everyone else. McCaffrey already has nine rushing touchdowns, while Brock Purdy has thrown 17 touchdowns against only five interceptions and ranks among the NFL’s most efficient quarterbacks. San Francisco also leads the league in red-zone touchdown rate at an incredible 84%, so Dallas cannot rely on tightening up once the 49ers get close to the goal line. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should take confidence from what it produced in Indianapolis. The Cowboys gained 508 total yards, with Dak Prescott throwing for 335, CeeDee Lamb producing 195 receiving yards and Javonte Williams topping 100 yards rushing. The problem was everything around those numbers. Dallas committed 14 penalties and lost two fumbles, turning what should have been a comfortable win into another game that required Prescott to rescue them in the final minutes. The good news is San Francisco’s defense can be attacked. Despite all the talent in its front seven, the 49ers have only 15 sacks, ranking 28th in the NFL. Nick Bosa and recently acquired DeForest Buckner make the defensive line much more dangerous than that number suggests, but Dallas should still give Prescott opportunities to attack downfield. Lamb is now up to 904 receiving yards and is coming off one of his best games of the season. San Francisco also began the week with injuries to their starting cornerbacks and their game status is questionable. If either is missing or limited, Lamb becomes the obvious place for Dallas to attack. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-5) I just don’t see the Cowboys being that competitive against one of the Super Bowl favorites. In a matchup of organizational dysfunction and well oiled machine, I’ll sadly pick the 49ers to win 31-16. Brandon Loree (6-3) At this point, it’s probably the Cowboys’ toughest challenge and, unfortunately, their biggest thorn in the side since 2021. The 49ers are way better in almost every category compared to Dallas despite having similar if not worse, injury luck. If the Cowboys can somehow pull a rabbit out of their hat and win this game, get ready to hear some outrageous playoff talk. Seeing is believing, so I’ll have to see it happen in order to believe—Dallas loses at home 33-23. Dyllan Rivers (5-4) Sometimes the NFL makes absolutely no sense. Teams that have no business winning will go out and upset the heavy favorite. But this is not one of those weeks. Christian McCaffrey goes crazy and Dallas falls to the 49ers 37-27. Matt Holleran (4-5) Until I see it happen I refuse to believe the Cowboys will beat a Kyle Shanahan-lead 49ers team. Dallas does not win back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer and I would be absolutely shocked if they did just that against a San Francisco team that just may be the best in the league. I hope I’m wrong, but I don’t see this one being close. Give me the 49ers in a rout, 37-17. Mike Poland (4-5) An entire panel going for the 49ers to win this one, and my head says the Cowboys lose this week to a strong San Francisco roster. But I’ll break the clean sweep here so any optimistic Cowboys fans here on BTB have something to align with on the staff predictions. A very tentative and nervous score prediction here where Dallas wins 28-21. And I’m willing to take the hit on this one. Put your prediction in the comments before the game begins.

The Denver Broncos won 28-24. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week our SBN Reacts question focused on a situation that 24 hours later completely dissolved — the Broncos’ trade with the Chargers for Daiyan Henley. Which was a shame for multiple reasons, mainly that 87% of us generally liked the trade. Of course, that was before anyone knew of the injury issues. And with the Chiefs’ win over the Falcons, they reclaimed the top spot in the AFC West (for now), putting the Broncos as the fifth seed Wild Card team for the playoffs — a very different position than the No. 2-knocking-on-the-door-to-No.1-seed that they were a week ago. Chiefs still play the Cardinals, Bills, Rams, Bengals, Patriots, Niners, Chargers, Raiders. Broncos’ remaining schedule is Raiders, Steelers, Dolphins, Jets, Raiders, Bills, Patriots, Chargers. On paper, the Broncos’ path seems much easier, but the Broncos don’t make anything easy and a healthy Patrick Mahomes always makes it difficult for opponents. The Broncos can still win the AFC West — and even regain the No. 1 seed in the AFC — but it could be a neck-and-neck race all the way to the finish line. title: Broncos quarterbacks past and present, how does Bo Nix measure up?
summary: As Broncos fans, in our lifetime, we’ve had the absolute privilege of watching some of the best quarterbacks in football play for the Denver Broncos… and the frustration of having to watch the not-so-great struggle. Needless to say, Broncos fans know how to measure quarterback play, both good and bad, when they see it. That’s […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts after winning in overtime against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Broncos fans, in our lifetime, we’ve had the absolute privilege of watching some of the best quarterbacks in football play for the Denver Broncos… and the frustration of having to watch the not-so-great struggle. Needless to say, Broncos fans know how to measure quarterback play, both good and bad, when they see it. That’s what’s so frustrating about the Bo Nix debate that has emerged this season. How could someone be ‘an insult to the quarterback position’ while simultaneously willing his team to victory every single week, breaking and setting records in the process? With the bye week nearly behind Broncos Country, it’s time to take an in-depth at just who Bo Nix is through the lens of Broncos quarterbacks past, the good, the bad, and the universally disliked. John Elway represents the gold standard for quarterback play in Denver. If you need explanation of how fundamentally important he was to the Denver Broncos, I question your Broncos Country citizenship (but welcome you anyway). The best part of Bo Nix just so happens to be the best of John Elway. They both share that ‘never-say-die’, ‘they ain’t licked us yet’, ‘we got them right where we want them’ mentality once the 4th quarter starts. It doesn’t matter what the score is. Call it Mile High Magic , persistence, dedication, or whatever you wish, but when the 4th quarter begins, fans know that the Broncos are never out of it so long as these special quarterbacks were/are under center. It’s hard to come up with a negative for the eternal face of the franchise, but there is one. At the time of his retirement, John Elway had thrown 226 interceptions – bringing him in all-time at 11th in NFL history (currently 17th all time). Bo Nix is different from Elway in that he does a better job of protecting the football. Throughout his young 43-game career, Nix has thrown just 27-interceptions compared to Elway’s 52 over the same number of games. Sure, Nix may throw passes 2 or 3-yards shorter than other quarterbacks, but he he just doesn’t throw the interceptions others do. No fan needs to be told how important limiting turnovers are, so no fan should need to be told how central Bo Nix’s ball control has been to the Broncos recent success. Jake Plummer was the first real spark of hope in the post-Elway era. Sure, Brian Griese had his moments, but not only did Griese never win a playoff game, he never played in one. Plummer was a fan favorite for his explosive plays, crazy beard, and unpredictability that stacked enough wins to go deep into the AFC playoff race during the 2005 season. Like Plummer, Bo Nix was the breath of fresh air after a long period of less-than-stellar Broncos football. Coming after the likes of Gus Ferrotte, Steve Beuerlein, Jarious Jackson, and Bradlee Van Pelt, Broncos Country embraced the confident (and successful!) quarterback that arrived as a free agent from Arizona. Here are two quarterbacks that had/have a deep understanding of what their arrival meant to the Broncos and the city of Denver as a whole. They have both risen to the occasion and grew into leaders that took their teams to AFC Championship games. Because Nix was drafted by the Broncos and not an unrestricted free agent acquisition like Plummer was, Nix benefits from a total franchise buy-in at least for another year (and likely longer). After losing the AFC Championship game in the 2005 season to the Pittsburgh Steelers, coach Mike Shanahan drafted Jay Cutler. Following a miraculous season, Denver suddenly had the supposed ‘quarterback of the future,’ on the bench and it was a fatal blow to Plummer’s security and confidence. Throughout the Bo Nix media saga this year, there has been nothing but unwavering support from inside the Broncos facility. No murmurs. No whispers. No attempts to find someone better. Why would there be? All he does is win. Who knows what the future holds, but it’s hard to not believe in a quarterback who consistently stacks wins like Bo Nix. Jay Cutler is a _________. You fill in the blank. It’s no secret that Broncos Country has intense feelings about him that are anything but positive. Like Jay Cutler, Bo Nix was one of the few Broncos quarterbacks actually drafted by the franchise. Although Cutler didn’t start until the inaugural Thursday Night Football game in 2006 (then on NFL Network), hopes for both quarterbacks’ careers were at the franchise’s highest when they debuted. They both could extend plays with their feet, generate highlight reel passes for touchdowns, and generally invigorated the franchise with the promise of youthful energy. Bo Nix is not like Jay Cutler in that he’s a likable, mature, quarterback who clearly has a desire to win above all else. Cutler, quite frankly, had none of those qualities. His body language would tell anyone all they needed to know about how things were going in Cutler’s head. In the face of adversity, Cutler would pout and mentally check-out when things got tough. When former coach and documented cheater Josh McDaniels took over in 2009, it was the threat of (checks notes) QB Matt Cassell that sent him into a full-blown tantrum, tailspinning him in a trade to the Chicago Bears. Bo Nix has thrown no tantrums. When things are tough, he locks in and, more often than not, finds a way to win. He has the maturity and drive that Jay Cutler never had and, sadly, never will. Peyton Manning is the only quarterback that could ever, or likely will ever, challenge Denver’s devotion to John Elway. In 2013, early in his Broncos career, Manning set records for single-season passing touchdowns (55), single-season passing yards (5,477), single-season passing yards per game (342.3), tied the single-game passing touchdowns record (7), total touchdowns in a season (56), and more. Like Manning, Bo Nix has had his fair share of records set, bested, or broken. Nix has the highest single-game completion percentage by a rookie (89.7%), most home passing touchdowns by a rookie (19), most games with 2+ passing TDs and 0 interceptions as a rookie (7), most games with 300+ passing yards, 4+ passing TDs, and a 140.0+ passer rating by a rookie (2). As for Denver Broncos franchise records, Nix stands alone with the longest rushing touchdown by a quarterback (62-yards), most passing yards by a rookie (3,775), most passing touchdowns by a rookie (29), most completions by a rookie (376), and most wins by a starting rookie QB (10). Before the bye, in the Broncos week 9 victory over the Carolina Panthers, Nix’s Broncos set the record for most consecutive 1-score games in NFL history (16). Unlike Peyton Manning’s time in Denver, Bo Nix has the benefit of youth on his side. The tragedy of the Peyton Manning era, that he didn’t get to Denver sooner. He toiled with the Colts for 14-season before landing in Denver and so, sadly, age and then injury caught up with Peyton after that record-shattering 2013 season. During his final year, the Super Bowl 50 2015 season, Manning missed 6-games to injury. As for Bo Nix, he’s never missed a regular season game due to injury and has only missed that one, crucial AFC Championship start to end last season. While it seems like everyone has been micro-analysing Bo Nix’s performances this season for reasons why he’s not ‘it,’ most people have overlooked the wealth of evidence that he is ‘it.’ Every quarterback that has strapped on the orange and blue has had their talents and their flaws. Never before has there been this level of scrutiny on a Broncos quarterback who has had so much success, especially coming off a decade of embarrassingly awful football in Denver. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again, don’t be so focused on identifying what Bo Nix isn’t that you miss all that he is . When you look at…

title: AFC playoff picture: Denver Broncos fall to the 5th seed during their bye week
summary: After last Sunday’s victory over the Carolina Panthers, the Denver Broncos moved into the #2 seed in the AFC and still controlled the AFC West. However, after their bye week, things have changed a bit. The Chiefs moved to the top of the AFC West after their victory over the Atlanta Falcons due to a […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills leaps over the line for a first down against the New York Jets in the first quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images After last Sunday’s victory over the Carolina Panthers, the Denver Broncos moved into the #2 seed in the AFC and still controlled the AFC West. However, after their bye week, things have changed a bit. The Chiefs moved to the top of the AFC West after their victory over the Atlanta Falcons due to a tiebreaker, and that dropped the Broncos to the 5th seed in the AFC. The Broncos will have a chance to reclaim their AFC West lead, but for now they trail the Chiefs and would be a wild-card team if the playoffs started today. Your AFC Playoff picture after Week 10. The Broncos fell to the 5th seed due to a Chiefs win, the Bengals took control of the AFC North and the Browns are in and the Patriots are out. pic.twitter.com/dpnKWzLBS3 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 16, 2026 As for the rest of the AFC, we saw some big changes. The Bengals moved into the top spot in the AFC North, and the New England Patriots dropped out of the playoffs after their loss to the Lions. The Bills, Chiefs, and Jaguars all won their matchups this Sunday. Buffalo Bills (8-1) Since we last talked, the Bills outlasted the Vikings on Monday Night and then dominated their AFC East rivals, the New York Jets, this past Sunday. Now, the Bills have an easy path to an AFC East title with the Patriots, Dolphins, and Jets all struggling, but can they win the one seed? Looking ahead, they host their division rivals, the Dolphins, before going on a tough stretch where they face the Patriots and Packers on the road, host the Bears, and then face the Broncos at Mile High on Christmas. If they want the one seed, they have to earn it by going against some of the better teams in the NFL this season. Looking ahead: vs. Dolphins, vs. Chiefs, @ Patriots, @ Packers, vs. Bears, @ Broncos, @ Dolphins, vs. Jets 2. Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) Even without Kenneth Walker, the Chiefs dominated the Atlanta Falcons. Patrick Mahomes had a vintage performance, while rookie running back Emmett Johnson filled in as the starter and had 171 yards from scrimmage and 2 touchdowns. With this win, they moved back into the top spot in the AFC West, but this will be a battle that will continue throughout the coming weeks. Next week, they host the struggling Arizona Cardinals before going through a tough stretch of games that will define their season. They will travel on the road to face the Bills, Rams, and Bengals before hosting the Patriots and 49ers. This is the stretch of games the Broncos need the Chiefs to struggle so they can hopefully extend their lead in the division and win the AFC West for a second straight season. Looking ahead: vs. Cardinals, @ Bills, @Rams, @ Bengals, vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, @ Chargers, vs. Raiders 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) The Jags remained one of the hottest teams in the NFL with a convincing victory over the Titans on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence continues to play well; their run game is explosive, and Parker Washington continues to be one of the best playmakers in the entire NFL. We can already crown them as the 2026 AFC South Champions. Looking ahead, they have an easy road ahead and appear to be strong contenders for the one seed in the AFC. They have a road game vs. the Giants next Sunday, followed by a home game vs. the Titans, a road game vs. the Bears, followed by games against the Steelers, Texans, Cowboys, Commanders, and Colts. Due to their victory earlier in the season, but the Broncos own a tie-breaker vs. the Jaguars. Looking ahead: @ Giants, vs. Titans, @ Bears, vs. Steelers, @ Texans, @ Cowboys, vs. Commanders, and @ Colts 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ explosive passing offense remained hot on Sunday Night with a big win against their division rivals, the Pittsburgh Steelers. This win put them at the top of the AFC North and likely the favorites to win that division moving forward. After their big win tonight, the Bengals will travel on the road to take on the Commanders before facing the Saints at home and then another divisional road game vs. the Browns. Then, they have a big game vs. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs before finishing out the season against the Panthers, Colts, Ravens, and Browns. Looking ahead: @ Commanders, vs. Saints, @ Browns, vs. Chiefs, @ Panthers, @ Colts, vs. Ravens, and vs. Browns Wild Card teams 5. Denver Broncos (7-2) The Broncos enjoyed a much-needed bye week and will hopefully emerge from this week healthier than they were coming into it. Both starting safeties, Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones, missed multiple games; Riley Moss and Jaylen Waddle left the Panthers game with concussions, and the rest of the roster needed some time off after a tough 9-game stretch to start the season. Coming out of the bye week, the Broncos host rookie QB Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders before traveling to the East Coast on a short week to face the Steelers on Black Friday. After that, they face the Dolphins, Jets, and Raiders before two important games vs. the current one seed, the Buffalo Bills on Christmas, followed by a road date in Foxboro to face the Patriots before ending the year against the currently winless Chargers. Looking ahead: vs. Raiders, @ Steelers, vs. Dolphins, @ Jets, @ Raiders, vs. Bills, @ Patriots, and vs. Chargers 6. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) The Steelers ran into Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ offensive buzzsaw on Sunday Night and suffered a tough loss to their division rivals. This loss knocked them to 6-3 and out of the AFC North lead and into the 6th seed in the AFC. They have a tough defense and a really good run game, so they are built to be productive as the days turn colder as we near closer to winter. Looking ahead, they take on a banged-up Eagles team before hosting the Broncos on Black Friday. They will follow that up with a game vs. the Texans, a tough road game vs. the Jags, a game vs. their division rivals, the Baltimore Ravens, before finishing out the year against the Panthers, Titans, and Ravens again. Looking ahead: @ Eagles, vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, @Jaguars, vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, @ Titans, and @ Ravens 7. Cleveland Browns (6-4) It hasn’t always been pretty, but the Cleveland Browns keep finding ways to win and had yet another comeback victory vs. the Houston Texans on Sunday. After the Patriots were blown out in Germany, the Browns moved from the “In the Hunt” category into the 7th seed in the AFC. Can they keep it? Time will tell, but they are in a good position moving forward. The Browns will enjoy a week off next week before starting their second half of the schedule with the hopes of continuing their playoff run. Coming out of the bye, they have three home games in a row vs. the Raiders, Bengals, and Falcons before having road games vs. the Giants and Ravens, a home game vs. the Colts before ending the season on the road vs. the Bengals.
