title: Ultimate Fans x 3: Just keep Bo-lieving in this clutch team
summary: Have I got the most amazing Broncos-less Sunday post for you today! Not only is this Bye Week UFG the usual fantastic read we always get with this weekly post, but this week it’s triple the fun as we have THREE ultimate fans bringing us the insight, humor, critique and rally cries. And if you […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a catch by Courtland Sutton #14 during the first quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Have I got the most amazing Broncos-less Sunday post for you today! Not only is this Bye Week UFG the usual fantastic read we always get with this weekly post, but this week it’s triple the fun as we have THREE ultimate fans bringing us the insight, humor, critique and rally cries. And if you didn’t know it, you would have thought that AusBroncosFan, jupistar, and since61 made this a group project because their answers work off each other so well and so often. Also, all three are Courtland Sutton fans and have the greatest “Broncos Mount Rushmores” so you know it’s going to be a great post. Sit back and enjoy this long but highly entertaining read. It’s so good, you’ll forget the Broncos aren’t even playing today! Week 10: BYE WEEK MHR – Before we talk mid-season stuff, let’s review last week’s win over the Panthers (where I was in attendance). Is it concerning when the Broncos barely beat a team that was missing half its starters? Even so, how awesome was that Devon Key INT and Bonitto strip sack? AusBroncosFan: Hmmm, I feel like this team tends to play up or down to their opponent. The continued absence of a reliable run game is the part I find the most worrying, but it was encouraging to see Nix pushing it down the field a little more. The defense seems to go through cold patches, but then gets it done when it matters most. I’d put my concern level as a 4/10, and the INT and strip sack as a 10/10 of awesome. jupistar: First game notwithstanding, where we got punched in the mouth and weren’t ready like we should have been, I think we have a wonderfully consistent offense. We had one outlier in 9 games: a 10 point low (that first game). Maybe you could consider the 14 to the 49ers, as well. Look, you have to realize, we played six games against top-8 defenses and three games against bottom-5 defenses. Four of those top-8 defenses were mercifully played at home. And we scored almost 24ppg against them. On the road, however, we don’t do so well, even against the bottom-5 defenses. All I’m saying is, we play up and we play down to the competition. I have a theory that Bo Nix is an entertainment mastermind. He’s intentionally keeping games close just so we have a thrilling conclusion in each and every one. And c’mon, Bryce Young put on a clinic. Dude was lights-out and had some breaks go against him (ex. in one play: Strnad does not get flagged for mugging the receiver when he’s already got hold of him as the ball hits him in the back, the ball falls to the ground but hits an arm to bounce up and get scooped up by Key, Payton throws the red flag at the last possible instant to roll back the play on the next snap [which didn’t matter so much because dude got stuffed], *and* we get an int off him). Young just did everything he could and our secondary wasn’t stopping their game plan. But yeah, three heads-up plays (int, strip-sack, and the red flag) and some good fortune, and we’re right there taking the game away in an east coast road contest. We’ve had good fortune, tough teams, incredible resilience, and playmakers making plays when it mattered. Compare this to last year when we had our defense playing like a top 10 defense, sack sack sack, no turnovers. This year? Giving yards away like Halloween candy and then playing tricks on the little kiddies who come to take it. since61: Nope. Winning ugly against a depleted team beats losing pretty to a good one. Denver was missing two safeties and a running back itself, so the shorthanded excuse cuts both ways. MHR – What was your favorite win this season? Which loss (or win, if you’re like Sean Payton, lol) irritated you the most? AusBroncosFan: Favourite? The last second win over the Chiefs of course! The worst? The week 1 loss to the Chiefs. jupistar : In no world does us dropping 28 points on KC, denying them a come-from-behind victory on a goal-line stand, and watching them whine and bitch because the game didn’t go their way not count as the sweetest of victories. And then we get to savor the tears of their fanbase because their lineman false-started and they don’t want to admit it. Finishing with a wiped-away TD and a sack on Mahomes… gravy. Neither loss irritated me. Okay, not true. I REALLY freaking hate it when we set records or near-records for historically bad play (still hurting from the Miami game). So, I’m still upset about how badly we performed against KC in Week 1. But I feel better because… see Favorite Win. So, KC wins both. At least we ended with the revenge win, and not them. *AND* we’re leading them in the AFC West. Go Broncos! since61 : Same answer as what’s the best drink – the next one. Most Irritating, the opener in KC. It had the same disgusting stench of the Hackett/Wilson heartbreaker in Seattle – a punch in the gut on what was supposed to be a promising season. I’m not over it and have made peace with never getting over it. The 2nd & Goal play by the Broncos isn't being talked about enough⬇️ This stop-motion play is a Chiefs / Andy Reid special They ran it in both Super Bowl 57 & 58 Short-yardage goal line, Broncos stone it. Very hard to defend IF you aren't prepared, CLEARLY the Broncos were. pic.twitter.com/riKDoisZPE — Ryan (@RyanKnowsBall) November 2, 2026 MHR – The Broncos are one of four teams with 7 wins so far, barely ahead of the Chiefs in the AFC West and just behind the Bills for lead in the AFC. Does their 7-2 record feel dominant or fragile…or somewhere in between? AusBroncosFan: Definitely somewhere in between. We’re 7-2 and I feel like we’re building towards something, but if we’d had just a few more untimely hiccups on offense or defense we could have lost a lot of the close ones and be 3-6 (though I admit it would be very unlucky for that to happen to such a well coached team). jupistar : Strangely enough… and I can’t believe I’m saying this, but nothing about the Broncos feels fragile this year. Last year, despite our high ranking as a defense, we played a lot of bad offenses and it felt fragile to me. What I see in our team this year *doesn’t* feel illusory at all. We’re playing complementary football and it’s a winning team. We are not a dominant team in the traditional sense of dropping 30s everywhere and holding opponents to single digits. But… I don’t know. I feel like when the team needs to do more, it can and does. And you do not get 16 wins in a row in one-score games and think of your team as fragile. This is a lunch-pail team. They go to work, get the job done, thrill the fans with terror all the way to the end, and go home to listen to the critics whine about them disrespecting their positions. since61: Somewhere in between. A team that won sixteen one-score games isn’t fragile – fragile teams lose those. But we aren’t dominant either because dominant teams aren’t routinely in those one-score games. Frankly, I don’t see any dominant teams this season. Most 1-score wins this season Win pct Broncos 6 1.000 Browns 5 .714 Bills 4 .800 Steelers 4 .800 Lions 4 .800 Vikings 4 .800… pic.twitter.com/Bc0z9qpBBK — PFF (@PFF) November 13, 2026 MHR – The remaining schedule should NOT be as tough as the first 9 games, but division games are never easy, and there are a few tough ones on the schedule. So how do you feel about the Broncos’ W-L record for the next 8 games…easy wins over the Raiders and Chargers? Do they take care of the JETS the way they should or continue with the low-scoring, messy wins? What do you expect against the Steelers? And how ‘bout those Bills? AusBroncosFan: I think we take care of business with dominant wins over the dolphins, jets and raiders (twice!), and we’ll make Aaron Rodgers feel like a grandpa (no offense to grandpas out there) but win messy in that…

title: Detroit Lions Week 10 snap counts: Derrick Moore steps up after Hutchinson injury
summary: In Week 10, the Detroit Lions moved to 7-2 after beating the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. The Lions dominated the game in every way, and while key injuries will certainly be prominent storylines, they shouldn’t overshadow the fact that Detroit is playing complementary football right now and looks like it can go head-to-head […]
full_text: Detroit Lions edge rusher Derrick Moore (8) celebrates a sack of Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (not in the photo) during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In Week 10, the Detroit Lions moved to 7-2 after beating the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. The Lions dominated the game in every way, and while key injuries will certainly be prominent storylines, they shouldn’t overshadow the fact that Detroit is playing complementary football right now and looks like it can go head-to-head with anyone. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. Quarterback Jared Goff: 61 (86%) Josh Dobbs: 10 (14%) With roughly seven minutes left in the fourth quarter and Detroit up 25 points, the Lions rested their starters, and Goff gave way to Dobbs for the final two possessions. Dobbs handed the ball off to the running backs six times, completed a first-down pass to Isaac TeSlaa, and the team went into victory formation for the final three plays. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs: 49 (69%) Sione Vaki: 18 (25%) — 20 special teams snaps (71%) Jacob Saylors: 6 (8%) — 20 (71%) Gibbs once again put on a show, totaling 252 all-purpose yards and finding the end zone twice—despite only playing three-and-a-half quarters. Before the Lions pulled their starters, Gibbs saw over 80% of offensive snaps, with Vaki taking the RB2 snaps. Vaki also got the first three touches with the reserves, before giving way to Saylors, who closed out the game. Wide receiver Jameson Williams: 56 (79%) Amon-Ra St. Brown: 47 (66%) Isaac TeSlaa: 46 (65%) Tay Martin: 11 (15%) — 20 (71%) DeAndre Carter: 5 (7%) — 11 (39%) The St. Brown storybook game will be talked about for years, and it played out even better than the NFL script writers could have hoped. His overall snaps were very similar to TeSlaa’s in this game, but context matters: St. Brown was pulled with the starters, and TeSlaa stepped into a WR1 role over the final 11 snaps, bringing things statistically closer than they were when the game was on the line. TeSlaa not only made a terrific acrobatic touchdown catch, again, but he also made the final catch of the game to seal the win. Tight end Sam LaPorta: 56 (79%) Brock Wright: 39 (55%) — 9 (32%) Tyler Conklin: 22 (31%) Like the other skill-position groups, the tight end reserves saw a slight uptick in usage after the starters (including LaPorta) were pulled. Not much box-score production from this group—a combined 4 catches for 30 yards—but they were all vital contributors in the run game. Offensive line LG Christian Mahogany: 71 (100%) — 5 (18%) RT Blake Miller: 71 (100%) — 5 (18%) LT Penei Sewell: 61 (86%) RG Tate Ratledge: 61 (86%) — 5 (18%) C Juice Scruggs: 61 (100%) — 5 (18%) LT/6th OL: Larry Borom: 10 (14%) — 5 (18%) LG Miles Frazier: 10 (14%) — 5 (18%) C Seth McLaughlin: 10 (14%) C Cade Mays: Inactive (injury) Absolute dominance up front throughout the day. PFF only faults the Lions for six (!) pressures allowed in this game, and the entire unit was mauling people in the run game. When the starters were pulled, Sewell was swapped out for Borum at LT, Frazier took over for Ratledge at RG, and McLaughlin got reps at center in place of Scruggs. Interior defensive lin e 3T Alim McNeill: 42 (71%) — 2 (7%) 3T Skyler Gill-Howard: 31 (53%) — 3 (11%) DT Tyleik Williams: 19 (32%) — 2 (7%) DL Levi Onwuzurike: 17 (29%) 3T Mekhi Wingo: DNP ( Inactive ) With the Patriots trailing by double digits most of the game, New England needed to pass a lot to stay competitive, and as a result, rookie Gill-Howard saw more snaps than Williams opposite McNeill. This situational rotation has worked all season, and the Lions shouldn’t feel the need to alter it. EDGE Rush End DJ Wonnum: 44 (75%) — 3 (11%) Rush End Derrick Moore: 40 (68%) — 3 (11%) Big End Tyler Lacy: 22 (37%) — 5 (18%) EDGE Aidan Hutchinson: 9 (15%) — INJURY Rush End Eric O’Neill: 7 (12%) — 11 (39%) Big End Ahmed Hassanein: DNP ( Inactive ) Following Hutchinson’s reported season-ending injury , the Lions turned to Wonnum and rookie Moore to step into larger roles. For Wonnum, it was a slight uptick from his typical starting reps, but Moore saw his opportunities increase sharply. Moore rewarded the Lions with four pressures and two sacks. Moore is expected to see his role increase following Hutchinson’s injury, but in the two games where his opportunities increased due to injury, he accounted for nine pressures and four sacks, giving Lions fans some hope he can soften the blow of losing their All-Pro defensive end. Linebacker SAM Derrick Barnes: 59 (100%) — 1 (4%) WILL/MIKE Malcolm Rodriguez: 34 (58%) — 2 (7%) WILL/SAM Trevor Nowaske: 33 (56%) — 22 (79%) MIKE K.J. Britt: 22 (37%) — 17 (61%) MIKE Joe Bachie: 1 (2%) — 20 (71%) WILL Owen Pappoe: 0 (0%) — 20 (71%) WILL Amen Ogbongbemiga: DNP ( Inactive ) Last week, their first without Jack Campbell in the lineup, the Lions leaned on Barnes and Rodriguez to play almost every snap, with Nowaske seeing about half the defensive snaps in a situational LB3 role. This week, Barnes and Nowaske’s roles stayed the same, but Rodriguez saw his snaps reduced in favor of Britt. Rodriguez still played a significant role, but Britt’s inclusion is an interesting wrinkle to keep an eye on. Was Britt’s familiarity with the Patriots the catalyst for this decision (the Lions signed him off New England’s practice squad) or is this a sign of things to come? We’ll have to wait and see. Cornerback CB/NB Roger McCreary: 59 (100%) — 3 (11%) CB Rock Ya-Sin: 55 (93%) — 1 (4%) CB Khalil Dorsey: 21 (36%) — 18 (64%) — INJURED CB Nick Whiteside: 7 (12%) — 3 (11%) CB Ennis Rakestraw: 5 (8%) — 7 (25%) CB D.J. Reed: Inactive (injury) McCreary and Ya-Sin have settled in as starters with Reed out, and both are noticeably more comfortable with the defense now that they’ve scaled up man coverage. When Reed returns, look for Ya-Sin to step back into a CB3 role but still play a significant role in nickel sets. Dorsey was injured in this game, and it’s unclear how that will affect him long-term, but it would be surprising to see the Lions turn to Whiteside or Rakestraw for more snaps, as both have struggled lately. Safet y S Brian Branch: 59 (100%) — 1 (4%) S Chuck Clark: 57 (97%) — 3 (11%) DB Andre Cisco: 5 (8%) — 5 (18%) DB Christian Izien: 1 (2%) — 16 (57%) DB Keith Abney: DNP ( Inactive ) Branch’s return has been felt in the secondary, and with him at a point where he doesn’t need to leave the field, the Lions have options at safety. Cisco played sparingly in his first game with the Lions, and it’s notable that he may have already passed Izien on the depth chart. Specialist s K Jake Bates: 11 (39%) P Jack Fox: 9 (32%) LS Hogan Hatten: 9 (32%) Bates had a kickoff out of bounds that he would like back, but otherwise it was a clean day for the group.

title: What’s next for the Detroit Lions’ defense after Aidan Hutchinson’s injury?
summary: The Detroit Lions are 7-2 and in the driver’s seat of the NFC North. They’re on a five-game winning streak; they’ve yet to lose a divisional game despite it being an extremely strong set of teams, and they are in the midst of playing their best football right now. That’s all the good news. The […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions are 7-2 and in the driver’s seat of the NFC North. They’re on a five-game winning streak; they’ve yet to lose a divisional game despite it being an extremely strong set of teams, and they are in the midst of playing their best football right now. That’s all the good news. The bad news is that Aidan Hutchinson likely suffered a season-ending injury on Sunday, and it comes two weeks after the Lions lost another star captain, Jack Campbell, to injury. On this week’s PODcast—where Erik Schlitt takes my place amongst the panel—we discuss everything that transpired during Sunday’s Detroit Lions vs. New England Patriots game in Munich, Germany. We talk about Amon-Ra St. Brown magical weekend, Jahmyr Gibbs’ continued path to MVP and Offensive Player of the Year consideration, and an inspired performance on the defense. But for the second half of the show, the fellas mostly talk about the Hutchinson injury fallout. Who will need to step up on the defensive line? Who will get more opportunities? What kind of formations and schematic changes will defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard consider moving forward? And can the health and improvement of the secondary help mitigate some of the damage? Check it all out on this week’s show. I’ll be back on Tuesday for the Midweek Mailbag podcast. As always, you can catch the video version of the PODcast over on our YouTube and Twitch pages. Those versions include some between-segments banter about the other Week 10 games, and some thoughts on the NFC North. Please follow and subscribe to those channels, as well. We are SO CLOSE to 20,000 subscribers on YouTube.

title: Detroit Lions grades vs. Patriots: Team win offers hope despite Hutchinson injury
summary: There was plenty to love about the Detroit Lions’ dominant win over the New England Patriots. And while Aidan Hutchinson’s injury may be the biggest headline from the Munich game, there was plenty from Allianz Arena that should keep Lions fans optimistic about the team moving forward. Here is my Lions Week 10 report card […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Jahmyr Gibbs of Detroit Lions runs with the ball during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was plenty to love about the Detroit Lions’ dominant win over the New England Patriots. And while Aidan Hutchinson’s injury may be the biggest headline from the Munich game, there was plenty from Allianz Arena that should keep Lions fans optimistic about the team moving forward. Here is my Lions Week 10 report card and positional grades for Detroit’s 35-10 victory. Quarterback: C+ Jared Goff threw two interceptions; both were his fault, and the second was an inexcusable decision that took points directly off the board. Because of those two plays alone, it feels like I can’t give him a grade above C+ in good faith. But the truth is the rest of his day was pretty dang good. I thought he navigated the pocket well, especially on his 50-yard pass to Jahmyr Gibbs. He didn’t make a ton of downfield throws or display any jaw-dropping plays, but he was very efficient, finishing with an electric 9.8 yards per attempt and a 101.9 passer rating. Running backs: A+ Jahmyr Gibbs was incredible all freakin’ day. He finished with 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The Patriots couldn’t handle his speed, his change-of-direction, or his strength. What was even better about his performance than normal is that the negative plays were almost completely non-existent. He had just one touch that went for negative yards, and only a couple more were stopped for zero yards. Sione Vaki was very efficient, too, earning 28 yards on just six carries (4.7 YPC). Overall, the Lions produced an impressive 55% success rate and +0.21 EPA/play on running plays vs. the Patriots. For comparison’s sake, the Patriots were allowing just a 36.9 success rate going into this game and had produced a negative EPA/run. Tight ends: B I was a little disappointed with Sam LaPorta’s play as a receiver. He didn’t create much separation against the Patriots’ defenders, and he had a touchdown grab knocked out of his hands. He finished with just a single catch for 16 yards on four targets. However, the Lions used a ton of tight ends against the Patriots in the running game, and that played a significant role in Detroit controlling the line of scrimmage. LaPorta (26), Brock Wright (29), and Tyler Conklin (17) all logged over 15 run-blocking snaps on the day. Wide receivers: A+ Amon-Ra St. Brown was seemingly unstoppable on Sunday. It was going to take the entire country of Germany to stop him on both of his long catch-and-run touchdowns, and they certainly weren’t going to do that against their most beloved NFL player. Jameson Williams’ day shouldn’t be overlooked, either. He caught four passes for 50 yards, including an impressive toe-tapping catch on the sidelines. Even Isaac TeSlaa got in on the fun with a highlight-reel touchdown grab. This unit lived up to its full potential for the first time in several weeks. Offensive line: A- Outside of some early pass protection issues, the Lions’ offensive line was nails in Munich. They were getting significant push in the run game, and after settling down, they helped Jared Goff breathe comfortably in the pocket. When the offensive line plays this well, the Lions’ entire offense is as close to unstoppable as we’ve seen. Defensive line: A- While the Lions’ pressure was inconsistent at times without Aidan Hutchinson in the lineup, they still gave the Patriots hell for most of the game. In the run game, the Patriots were unable to do anything. Their running backs combined for 17 carries, 31 yards, and just 1.8 yards per carry. The pass rush generated five total sacks, six quarterback hits, and over a 50 percent pressure rate: Pressure was a problem again for the Patriots today Lions pressured them on 51% of plays (up from 46% season rate, 2nd highest in the NFL). *This is the 5th time this season NE has allowed a pressure on 50% or more of dropbacks* Data: @SumerSports — Lindsay Rhodes (@lindsay_rhodes) November 15, 2026 It will be tough to maintain that without Hutchinson and against a better offensive line, but Derrick Moore, Alim McNeill, DJ Wonnum, and Skyler Gill-Howard have all played some pretty sound football, and all were disruptive on Sunday. Linebackers: B The linebackers deserve a lot of praise for Detroit’s stout run defense, but they were a bit of a liability in the pass game again. It didn’t end up costing the Lions too much in this game, because once Drake Maye went down, it looked like Tommy DeVito just didn’t see the field very well. But coverage against tight ends and running backs continues to be a bit of an issue. Still, this defense continues to play good football without its field general at MIKE linebacker, and that means something. Secondary: A- I thought the safety play was fantastic on Sunday. Brian Branch was all over the place in the run game and the pass game. Chuck Clark flipped a couple Patriots and made the receiving corps pay for every DeVito murderball. I can’t give them an A, though, because of a couple of stupid and costly pass interference flags. It wasn’t a great game for Ennis Rakestraw—who also missed a key tackle—nor Nick Whiteside. But the good news is the top corners in this game—Rock Ya-Sin and Roger McCreary were very, very good. Or, as Dan Campbell said: “I thought the back end played outstanding,” Campbell said. “We played some sticky coverage today, bought us a little bit of time.” Special teams: B Nothing too notable from this group on Sunday. The return team didn’t look particularly good, but coverage was good on both punt and kickoff. Jake Bates is still perfect when Jack Fox isn’t blocking his kicks. He did put a kickoff out of bounds and a touchback in the end zone. Coaching: A This was a tough week for both coaches. Flying across the globe, adjusting to a time zone six hours away, and dealing with all of the crazy logistics of getting ready for Sunday is not easy. It’s clear one team was way more prepared than the other. On top of that, Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing is really starting to come into his own, building plays off of previous plays, and seemingly having the right call in the right moment more often than not. As he hits his stride, the Lions offense can carry them a long way. But don’t sleep on the defensive coaching, either. Kelvin Sheppard has had to deal with two emotionally draining injuries to two of their best players. Yet through a heavy rotation at every level of the defense, things have never looked more steady and controlled. Say what you will, facing a beat-up Patriots offense with a backup quarterback leading most of Sunday afternoon, but Detroit used to get beat up by backups all the time. The defense finally feels like it’s coming together.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Discussion: Are you confident in the Detroit Lions defense without Aidan Hutchinson?
summary: The Pyrrhic victories are unfortunately mounting for the Detroit Lions. Despite winning five games in a row, they have lost two irreplaceable parts of their team. The Lions have now lost two cornerstone pieces of their defense over the last three weeks. Jack Campbell suffered a scary neck injury and will be sidelined for an […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions goes down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pyrrhic victories are unfortunately mounting for the Detroit Lions. Despite winning five games in a row, they have lost two irreplaceable parts of their team. The Lions have now lost two cornerstone pieces of their defense over the last three weeks. Jack Campbell suffered a scary neck injury and will be sidelined for an unknown period of time. Against the New England Patriots in Munich, the Lions lost yet another heartbeat of their defense. Aidan Hutchinson suffered a serious knee injury that will likely sideline him for the rest of the 2026 season —and perhaps into the 2027 season as well. The impact Hutchinson has on this team is difficult to quantify. For a team built on grit, Hutchinson exemplified that to a tee. Without Hutchinson, can the Lions defense continue to play at a high level? Today’s Question of the Day is: Are you confident in the Detroit Lions defense without Aidan Hutchinson? My answer: I am cautiously optimistic. Few teams boast a pass rusher like Hutchinson, and he was by far the most potent edge on the Lions’ roster. Hutchinson will finish the season with 52 pressures per PFF, while the next-closest defender is Alim McNeill (36) and the next-closest edge is DJ Wonnum (18)—that’s a significant gap. Without question, the Lions are in a far worse position than they were entering the week. The ceiling for the Lions to be a great defense is gone, in my opinion. However, I think the floor is still intact. When the Lions lost Hutchinson back in 2024, their defense was ill-equipped to handle it. The pass rushing depth was largely just Josh Paschal and Al-Quadin Muhammad and The Lions had to make a deadline deal to acquire Za’Darius Smith. They lost Alim McNeill to a torn ACL in Week 15. By the time they rolled into the postseason, their pass rush was limited. This limitation put a lot of pressure on the secondary, and the defense wound up allowing 45 points to the Commanders. This, in turn, forced the offense to be perfect, and on a day when Jared Goff threw three interceptions, it was not. I think the rest of 2026 will be tough sledding for the defense, but the Lions have some options. For one, Wonnum has been playing very well this season. He is not the game-wrecker that Hutchinson is, but he is a steady presence capable of sound run defense and pass rush. Secondly, rookie Derrick Moore is coming into his own of late, now having four sacks in two games. Refining his skillset is still a priority for him, but it’s not hard to see the potential with him. It might be earlier than expected, but he now has to step into a sizable role on defense. The Lions also have McNeill playing at an All-Pro level, while Tyleik Williams is quietly entrenching himself as a menace up the middle. Sprinkle in guys like Tyler Lacy (another underappreciated player) and Skyler Gill-Howard (the pass-rushing rookie tackle), and the Lions not only have more talent on the defensive line than in 2024, but also more flexibility. The loss of Hutchinson will put more pressure on the secondary to step up. The secondary has been balling as of late, but there will be questions about whether that is a mirage or not. Over the last five games, the defense has played the hapless Arizona Cardinals, the inconsistent Green Bay Packers, the formerly-hapless Minnesota Vikings, the hapless Miami Dolphins, and the Drake Maye-less New England Patriots. You can only play the opponent on the schedule, but concerns about the authenticity of this defensive turnaround are certainly justified—are they actually good now or just benefitting from weak and misfortunate opponents? If the Lions can put up a great defensive showing versus the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, then you can squash some of my doubts. What makes me encouraged about the secondary is that they look invigorated. They are intercepting passes. They are batting away balls. They are (mostly) limiting the explosive plays. Whereas the defense looked lost to start the season, they are playing with far more confidence at this point. Getting Brian Branch was certainly a catalyst, and if the Lions can add Kerby Joseph to the mix as well, then the defensive back group suddenly looks far more capable You cannot replace a player like Hutchinson. You will struggle to even recreate him in the aggregate. He is a rarity amongst NFL players, a player with a high level of talent and the motor to back it up. However, I think that the Lions have enough pieces on their defense to weather the storm. If they can be a good defense, that might be enough when paired with this potent offense. Do you have faith in this defense without Hutchinson? Let us know in the comments below.
author: John Whiticar

title: 14 winners, 3 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the New England Patriots
summary: Guten tag, Detroit Lions fans. The Munich road trip comes to a close with a victory, as the Lions beat the schnitzel out of the New England Patriots on Sunday. In perhaps their most complete game of the season, the offense was nigh unstoppable while the defense silenced the entire New England arsenal. The final […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Amon-Ra St. Brown of Detroit Lions celebrates scoring his team's fourth touchdown with teammates during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Guten tag, Detroit Lions fans. The Munich road trip comes to a close with a victory, as the Lions beat the schnitzel out of the New England Patriots on Sunday. In perhaps their most complete game of the season, the offense was nigh unstoppable while the defense silenced the entire New England arsenal. The final score ended as 35-10, but it could have been far worse for the Patriots. Two injuries were at the forefront of this game—both happening on the same play. Quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury after being tackled by Aidan Hutchinson on a sack. The Patriots offense was paltry under backup Tommy DeVito and would not score until late in the fourth quarter. Hutchinson, meanwhile, suffered an injury while celebrating that very sack . He too did not return and is likely done for the season. The season-ending Hutchinson injury looms large for Detroit, but we should at least appreciate the team-wide performance in this beatdown. Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Winner: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB I am running out of words to describe Jahmyr Gibbs, so instead, I will use only three: most valuable player . There is no other way to illustrate Gibbs’ impact on the Lions right now. He gets the most out of every play—give him an inch and he takes a mile. Gibbs finished with 22 carries for 153 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 99 yards. He was arguably more impressive than those numbers indicate, too. Gibbs looks untouchable. The offensive line, receivers, and tight ends were moving people ahead of him, but Gibbs’ ability to turn any play into a big gain was a game-changer. We are truly witnessing something special. Winner: Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR Can you tell that St. Brown wanted to make the most of his first game in Germany? The Lions star receiver of German ancestry put on a clinic in Munich, rattling off chunk play after chunk play. He ended the day with just four catches, but he turned those into 98 yards and two touchdowns. The first was a brilliant 56-yarder in which he juked most of the Patriots defense. The second was just 28 yards, but the final eight of those were a rugby scrum powered by will, determination, and a handful of Lions pushing behind him. For most teams, a performance like this would be the highlight of the game. For the Lions, it’s just another day at the office. They are so fortunate to have players like St. Brown and Gibbs playing at an All-Pro level on a weekly basis. Winners: Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin, CBs The absence of Drake Maye definitely benefitted the Lions defense, but that should not detract from the sticky coverage provided by Ya-Sin and McCreary. The Patriots only had 90 passing yards on the day as A.J. Brown and the other Patriot pass catchers were smothered by the Lions defensive backs. McCreary got his first interception of the season and was phenomenal in coverage, recording two passes defended and zero explosives allowed. Ya-Sin, after struggling to start the season, has found his footing of late. He also had a pass defended and, per PFF, did not allow a catch on three targets. Early on in year, losing D.J. Reed would have been a death sentence for the Lions defense, but Ya-Sin and McCreary have stepped up and the Lions have weathered the storm. Winner: Offensive line A week after the offensive line got bullied by the Miami Dolphins, they got their act together against the Patriots. Gibbs’ shined on Sunday, but he never reaches that level without capable blocking ahead of him. All five of the starters were blasting through the Patriots front seven, generating plenty of rushing lanes for Gibbs to showcase his speed and agility. The return of Christian Mahogany surely impacted this blocking turnaround—hopefully the disciplinary penalty he received last week sticks going forward. Jared Goff was sacked twice on the day, but both were arguably coverage sacks. Aside from a pair of penalties (one on Blake Miller, one on Tate Ratledge), there was very little to criticize from the blocking up front. Winner: Derrick Moore, DE Are we witnessing Moore’s rookie breakout? It was a slow start to his season, but he is coming into his own lately. Moore had a pair of sacks against the Patriots and now has four sacks across his last two games. He has flashed the full toolkit—speed, bend, power, finesse, and motor. Consistency is still the name of the game for Moore’s development, particularly in run defense, but his pass rush prowess over the last month has been encouraging. His rapid development becomes even more paramount with Aidan Hutchinson missing extensive time due to his injury. Winner: Derrick Barnes, LB I thought that this was arguably Barnes’ best game of the season. Barnes was a menace in run defense, racking up a team-leading seven tackles and three run stops per PFF. As a pass rusher, Barnes flashed some serious closing speed, pressuring the Patriots quarterbacks on multiple occasions. Most encouraging of all, Barnes looked capable in coverage—normally his weakness. The Patriots had little success with their tight ends and running backs and Barnes was a key reason why. He never looked lost in coverage and shadowed his man effectively. The Lions needed Barnes to step up after Jack Campbell’s injury, and performances like these do a lot to instill confidence in the linebacking corps going forward. Quick hits: Winner: Drew Petzing, OC Petzing was on fire on Sunday. The Lions got a lot of great performances on offense, but none of them happen without the right play call at the right time. Nearly everything Detroit threw at New England worked. Petzing deserves to be in the conversation for best offensive coordinator in the league. Winner: Sione Vaki, RB Vaki only had a limited number of touches before garbage time (six carries for 28 yards and one catch for 17 yards), but he continues to make impactful plays when called upon. He also had a brilliant pass block that enabled Goff to hit St. Brown for his 56-yard touchdown. Even if Isiah Pacheco returns this season, Vaki has cemented his spot as a dependable RB2. Loser: Sam LaPorta, TE He and Brock Wright are doing well as blockers, especially with the sidecar formation, but his lack of impact as a receiver (one catch for 16 yards) is concerning. Over the last four games, he has just nine catches for 99 yards. Winner: Alim McNeill, DT Another week with a sack for McNeill. Few defensive tackles in the league have his combination of run stopping and pass rush. Winner: DJ Wonnum, DE Moore finished with two sacks, but Wonnum was a solid contributor as well. He had a sack of his own along with multiple pressures. Given his ability as a pass rusher and run defender, he will be relied upon as an every-down player with Hutchinson missing time. Winner: Brian Branch, S Branch has unquestionably played a massive part in the Lions’ defensive turnaround. His ability in coverage and run defense are instrumental to the entire defense succeeding. He had two passes defended and three run stops on Sunday. Losers: Ennis Rakestraw and Nick Whiteside, CB Rakestraw only played a few snaps but made the least of them. He gave up a catch to Hunter Henry after a poor tackling attempt. On the ensuing drive, he committed a pass interference—a 30-yard penalty that nearly outpaced the Patriots offense. As for Whiteside, he got called for pass interference late in the game that helped facilitate a Patriots touchdown. With Ya-Sin and McCreary playing well, Rakestraw will likely stay limited to…

Jumping into the air in celebration, Hutchinson landed on his feet, only to immediately crumple to the ground with […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions celebrates sacking Drake Maye of New England Patriots before going down with an injury caused by celebrating during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. But what he did afterward may be the story of the game. Jumping into the air in celebration, Hutchinson landed on his feet, only to immediately crumple to the ground with an injury. After down on the field for a couple of minutes, Hutchinson was able to walk to the sideline on his own and into the blue tent. Hutchinson is obviously one of the most important players on the Lions, currently leading the entire NFL in pressures through nine weeks. He has 6.0 sacks on the season. Hutchinson is also just two years removed from a broken leg injury that shortened his 2024 season. UPDATE: The injury is feared to be significant and season-ending, per several reports: Lions star DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a significant knee injury, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Imaging in Munich confirmed the injury to Hutchinson, whose right knee buckled as he celebrated a sack against the Patriots. He’s out for the season. pic.twitter.com/HiQqKghQew — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 15, 2026 UPDATE: The Lions listed Hutchinson as QUESTIONABLE to return with a knee injury. #Lions Injury Update: EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, Knee, Questionable — Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) November 15, 2026 UPDATE 2: Hutchinson was officially downgraded to OUT in the second half. UPDATE 3 : Dan Campbell did not offer any sort of definitive update on Hutchinson after the game, only noting that he was happy with how the team responded to his injury, and they’ll need to step up if Hutchinson’s injury is long term. For a full transcript on what Campbell said, check out this post on what the Lions coach had to say about Hutchinson’s injury .
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Everything Dan Campbell said about Aidan Hutchinson’s injury
summary: We still don’t have a firm update on Aidan Hutchinson after he suffered an injury celebrating a first-down sack in the Detroit Lions’ Week 10 win over the New England Patriots. However, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked several questions about the situation, even though he didn’t provide an exactly diagnosis. UPDATE: There are now […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions receives medical attention after going down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images We still don’t have a firm update on Aidan Hutchinson after he suffered an injury celebrating a first-down sack in the Detroit Lions’ Week 10 win over the New England Patriots . However, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked several questions about the situation, even though he didn’t provide an exactly diagnosis. UPDATE: There are now reports that Hutchinson’s injury is feared to be season-ending. What’s the latest update on Aidan Huthcinson? Hutchinson was initially listed as questionable with a knee injury, then downgraded to out in the second half. Campbell would not offer up any additional information. “Nothing new. We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell said. “But anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate that he is, he’s a captain of ours, that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out.” Does Hutchinson’s injury put a damper on the win over the Patriots? Campbell: “Anytime you lose a player like that and you don’t know the entirety of it–but knowing Hutch for who he is. It’s like he doesn’t stay down long. It does, it hurts a little bit, but as far as this game was concerned our guys stepped up and finished. We stayed strong. This is the second time this has happened—our guys have responded in a tough situation and didn’t bat an eye. Just went back to work, and that’s not easy to do. But, no, certainly you don’t want to know that a player like that is down.” What kind of depth do the Lions have? Detroit managed to create four more sacks on the day after Hutchinson’s injury—two by rookie Derrick Moore, one from Alim McNeill, and one from DJ Wonnum. Campbell expressed confidence in the Lions’ group of pass rushers, regardless of what Hutchinson’s ultimate diagnosis is. “We like ‘em,” Campbell said. “That’s why we applied them where we did. And I know this, Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets, he gets better. It was good to get Wonnum back today. We know what Mac [McNeill] is, Sky(ler Gill-Howard). So can Tyleik (Williams). And all those guys, even Levi (Onwuzurike), (Tyler) Lacy, they play a different flavor, but they push the pocket, they got movement. But I think the important thing is, man, we knew we had to do to get out of this game with a win. We had to play really good defense. “And I really thought the back end played outstanding. We played some stick coverage today […] We’re improving. We gotta go. We gotta go. We’ll see where Hutch is at, but we’ve gotta step up now. We need some guys to really step up—and if that is the case (with a serious Hutchinson injury), fill that role.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: 5 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ dominant 35-10 win over New England Patriots
summary: Early-morning football today as the Detroit Lions faced the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Detroit hasn’t played overseas since 2015, and they did a lot better than back then. Instead of losing 45-10, Detroit came out on top, winning 35-10, improving to 7-2. They’re back up above .500 overseas, improving to 2-1 in that […]
full_text: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Amon-Ra St. Brown of Detroit Lions celebrates scoring his team's first touchdown with teammates Christian Mahogany and Isaac TeSlaa during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images Early-morning football today as the Detroit Lions faced the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Detroit hasn’t played overseas since 2015, and they did a lot better than back then. Instead of losing 45-10, Detroit came out on top, winning 35-10, improving to 7-2. They’re back up above .500 overseas, improving to 2-1 in that regard. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ 35-10 beatdown against the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson gives Lions fans PTSD Let’s get the biggest negative out of the way. EDGE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a knee injury early in the game while celebrating after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. It reminded multiple Lions fans of when former linebacker Stephon Tulluch got injured after celebrating as well. Hutchinson didn’t return after it was labeled a knee injury. After the game, Lions head coach Dan Campbell didn’t have an update on Hutchinson. No Hutch? No problem for the Lions’ pass rush Unlike 2024, the Lions defensive line can still generate pressure without its best player, Hutchinson. Even without him, the line came away with three sacks. Team sack leader EDGE DJ Wonnum got a sack in his return after missing a game due to a concussion. Defensive tackle Alim McNeill is continuing to have a solid season and also got a sack. With Hutchinson out, rookie EDGE Derrick Moore saw more playing time and stepped up, essentially replacing one Wolverine with another. Moore didn’t just get one sack, but he got two. Back-to-back games with multiple sacks is a good look for the rookie, who has needed time to adjust to the NFL. A third-down SACK for Derrick Moore!! pic.twitter.com/xfk49zju6f — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 15, 2026 The secondary helped out too, giving the defensive line time to get to either quarterback. This team has depth along that defensive line, which is why it can still be a problem even without Hutchinson. Hutchinson is certainly an important piece, but good teams can survive when their stars go down, and this unit didn’t fold without him this morning. Amon-Ra St. Brown made the most of his return to Germany All week, Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was talked about in his return to Germany. He has family ties and spent summers in the country, so he was excited to play football in front of their fans. Quickly, St. Brown balled out and made a huge play, scoring the first touchdown and giving Detroit the lead they would never give back. AMON-RA ST. BROWN 56-YARD TOUCHDOWN IN GERMANY NEvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/47fPY2mHzx — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 St. Brown wasn’t done; he got another touchdown on a great play call by Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. St. Brown was due to have a big game in front of the German fans, and the Lions made sure of it. St. Brown finished with four catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. Touchdown No. 2 for Germany's own Amon-Ra St. Brown ✅🇩🇪 pic.twitter.com/eAeQ2KijiL — St. Brown Podcast (@StBrownPodcast) November 15, 2026 Gibbs helping case for MVP While St. Brown dominated through the air, running back Jahmyr Gibbs dominated on the ground and through the air. New England has a strong run defense, allowing an average of 96.7 yards entering Sunday, ninth-lowest in the NFL. Detroit got left guard Christian Mahogany back after suffering an in-team suspension, and his return helped Gibbs too. All that said, Gibbs finished with 22 carries for 153 yards, two rushing touchdowns, and seven catches for 99 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs has 171 yards in the 1st half (93 rushing yards, 78 receiving yards) That is the most in a 1st half in a game this season and tied for 2nd in a game since 2022, @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) November 15, 2026 It’s great to see Gibbs play well against a respectable run defense. He’s the best player in the NFL trying to win the MVP trophy who isn’t a quarterback. He’s been dominant this season, with few poor performances, and when he has a solid game, he goes off. This offense was humming, and he was a big factor in it. He deserves the biggest push for the MVP trophy in December, when the focus starts to shift toward awards. Jared Goff had an up-and-down performance Despite Gibbs playing well and St. Brown scoring multiple times, quarterback Jared Goff had an up-and-down performance. While he threw for 303 yards and three touchdowns, he threw two interceptions, his first multi-interception game of the year. Goff was in his bag at times, throwing great passes to St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Gibbs. But Goff also made some head-scratching errant throws. The first interception came off a bad throw to a covered St. Brown, where Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez picked it off as St. Brown fell. Even if St. Brown didn’t fall, he was still covered, and it was the first interception this year solely on Goff. He wasn’t hit as he threw it, and the receiver falling wasn’t a factor. His second interception was even worse, as Detroit was inside the five on third down with less than 10 seconds left in the first half, a situation where you either score or throw the ball away. Goff instead threw a ball into coverage, where it was picked off, and instead of at least getting a field goal on the drive, the Lions came away empty-handed. Goff had some good throws and some bad ones, a roller coaster game that, luckily, the good outweighed the bad. If Gibbs and the defense didn’t play as well as they did, this game could’ve been closer.

title: The Aaron Banks situation gets worse and worse for the Packers
summary: Aaron Banks, the Packers’ $77 million left guard, played three snaps on Sunday. None were on offense. Exiled from the starting lineup, Banks only appeared on the field for two field goal attempts and the Packers’ lone extra point, lining up at left guard on all three plays. And that’s a fitting fate for Banks, […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - JANUARY 04: Green Bay Packers guard Aaron Banks (65) looks on before the NFL game between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings on January 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Aaron Banks, the Packers’ $77 million left guard, played three snaps on Sunday. None were on offense. Exiled from the starting lineup, Banks only appeared on the field for two field goal attempts and the Packers’ lone extra point, lining up at left guard on all three plays. And that’s a fitting fate for Banks, considering how the Packers seem to have evaluated their offensive line heading into this week’s game. Asked in his postgame press conference why Banks was out of the lineup, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur offered a brutal assessment. Simply put, LaFleur and the coaching staff view Laken Tomlinson as the better choice at left guard, and, given the chance to earn reps at right guard with Kevin Zeitler ailing, Banks failed, falling behind Travis Glover. “We were going to shuffle up the o-line a bit. Laken’s been doing a pretty good job and we put him back to his natural position [at left guard], and we were going to let Banks compete at the right guard,” LaFleur said. “He doesn’t have a ton of time on task at that position, so we went the way we did tonight.” To say nothing of the overall state of the Packers’ offensive line, what a catastrophe Banks has been. 20 months after signing a rich free agent deal, Banks finds himself behind a player the Packers plucked from the Dallas Cowboys practice squad in September and unable to outcompete a sixth round pick who, coming into this week, had appeared in 11 total NFL games, counting a disastrous playoff performance in 2024. And presumably he only got the chance to compete because Kevin Zeitler, the player the Packers signed to solidify right guard, was unavailable all week with an ankle injury. And that’s just this week! On the season, Banks has appeared in just four games. In one of those four (this week) he didn’t play on offense. In another, he couldn’t finish out the game. For the millions they’ve spent this year, Banks has given the Packers just 137 offensive snaps. Again, what a catastrophe. This is a player the Packers portrayed as ascending when they signed him. General manager Brian Gutekunst said he was excited to get a player “ in the prime of his career ” when he inked Banks in 2025, making him a centerpiece of an effort to get bigger up front. Instead, the only size-related discussion we’re having related to Banks is the enormity of his failure. Banks is due a $9.5 million roster bonus on March 15, 2027, but it’s hard to imagine he’s going to see a cent of that. Releasing Banks outright would actually cost the Packers a touch more than keeping him thanks to a contract restructuring last offseason, but there are still mechanisms in place to avoid that payout. Designating Banks as a post-June 1 cut would scuttle that roster bonus and spread Banks’ cap hit over the Packers’ 2027 and 2028 books. And given what the Packers are telling us about their internal assessment of Banks, you can probably go ahead and pencil in Banks for a change of address sometime before March 15 of next year. But that will only finalize what’s already happening. The Packers have functionally moved on from one of their priciest free agent signings in recent years. The only remaining question is why they thought it was a good idea to sign him in the first place.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Back to the drawing board on the Offensive Line
summary: No quarterback — even one who has been playing at an MVP level of late — can sustain an offense when he can’t get the ball out of his hands. Jordan Love is no exception, and Green Bay Packers fans saw the team’s fatal flaw get exploited over and over and over again on Sunday […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Levi Drake Rodriguez #50 of the Minnesota Vikings sacks Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images No quarterback — even one who has been playing at an MVP level of late — can sustain an offense when he can’t get the ball out of his hands. Jordan Love is no exception, and Green Bay Packers fans saw the team’s fatal flaw get exploited over and over and over again on Sunday afternoon. The Minnesota Vikings defense is a singularly bad matchup for the Packers, who continue to make inexplicable decisions with their personnel on the offensive line. Yes, the team has had a glut of injuries up front, and third-string center John Williams was one of the biggest problems on the line on Sunday, but every single player shared in the blame for the constant and, even more problematic, instant pressure that Love faced all game long. Love couldn’t even get the ball out quickly without players in his face, let alone try to dial up any deep balls, which have been a staple of the team’s recent success. So what is there to do? Is the answer just as simple as “don’t play the Vikings again”? Are there answers on this roster, perhaps on injured reserve (looking at you, Sean Rhyan), who could help get this unit back on track? Maybe this team needs to get back to the drawing board at a more fundamental level when it comes to the offensive line — starting with the position coach and working all the way up. The Packers have a long week to start working on some answers before their next game, which is a week from Wednesday in Los Angeles. They’ve got seven more chances to sort things out and find a way into the postseason. It’s time to get this under control Game recap: 5 takeaways from Packers’ loss to Vikings | Packers.com This was a major missed opportunity to get right back into the thick of the NFC North race. Instead, the Packers are two losses behind each of the other three teams in the division, who are all tied at 7-2. Jordan Love and a true outlier pressure performance from Vikings | Packers Wire Love averaged less than 2.5 seconds in his time to throw, but still was pressured on 21 of his 35 dropbacks. Packers can’t function against Vikings’ blitz barrage | Packersnews.com ($) There are only so many times that Matt LaFleur can say that the offensive line wasn’t coached well enough. Where’s the accountability for those failures? It’s not unlike tipping pitches in baseball – you have to make everything look the same until it isn’t. title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 10 vs. the Vikings
summary: Part II of the Green Bay Packers vs. Minnesota Vikings matchup kicked off at Lambeau Field on Sunday afternoon, and it was…something. When these two teams met to open the season back in September, the Vikings embarrassed the Packers, scoring 22 unanswered points in the 4th quarter to win by 17. This time, the Packers […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Part II of the Green Bay Packers vs. Minnesota Vikings matchup kicked off at Lambeau Field on Sunday afternoon, and it was…something. When these two teams met to open the season back in September, the Vikings embarrassed the Packers, scoring 22 unanswered points in the 4th quarter to win by 17. This time, the Packers embarrassed themselves and left with a 6-4 record after a 30-1o loss. There were no winners this week. Let’s look at the worst of the worst. Loser: Matthew Golden I don’t know how many drops WR Matthew Golden will be officially credited with, but my own eyeballs saw at least 3. On 2nd and 6, Golden had a bad drop which would’ve been a huge first down had he been able to hold on. On the very next play, they almost picked up the first down again, but he was unable to maintain possession before the ball hit the ground. Against a suffocating Vikings defense, the Packers have to take advantage of every moment QB Jordan Love is able to actually get the ball out, and today, they failed miserably. Golden is having a pretty stellar breakout year so far, and it’s frustrating to know it’d be even better if he could stop being his own worst enemy. He finished the game with a team-high 5 catches on 9 targets for 70 yards. Jordan Love is playing every down like he has two seconds to throw. And he’s still putting it on the money. Matthew Golden’s rough game gets rougher. pic.twitter.com/UUjMUt6g11 — Henry McKenna (@henrycmckenna) November 15, 2026 Loser: Tucker Kraft TE Tucker Kraft’s disappointing year got even worse on Sunday. He had no energy and looked like he didn’t want to be out on the field. The Packers tried to get him involved, with Love targeting him 4 times, but he only came down with 1 catch for 19 yards. I’m not sure if he’s in his own head, or just not feeling 100% after last year’s torn ACL, but he is not the same TE with the killer mentality we’re used to seeing. A small bright side: this fun play where he went under center and pitched the ball to Jordan Love. Tucker Kraft takes the snap and tosses it to Jordan Love, who completes it to Christian Watson 😮 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aPbjRkO4Pj — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Loser: Trey Smack The Packers drafted you to make 53-yard FGs. Try doing that sometime. Loser: Mark Redman Tucker Kraft is having a down year. I think he can get back to his normal self, but in the meantime, we must deal with TE Mark Redman. After fumbling the first Packers pass of the day, I think I’d like to stop dealing with Mark Redman. SNATCHED! @AndrewVanGinkel 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/A1bTh9RgWq — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 15, 2026 Loser: The Offensive Line OH MY GOODNESS I’M TIRED. Every time I saw a player creeping up on Jordan Love, I screamed. Collapse after collapse after collapse, and the offensive line gave up 8 sacks when it was all said and done. John Williams in particular had an atrocious game at center, botching multiple snaps. One of these botched snaps came on their opening drive of the second half, and the ball was recovered by the Vikings. The Packers knew this was coming. HC Matt LaFleur, OC Adam Stenavich, and OL coach Luke Butkus KNEW this was coming. They had 9 weeks to prepare, and then they put out an offensive line that marched onto the field and pooped everywhere. What is Jordan Love supposed to do when there’s poop everywhere? The Packers have finally reached their bye week, which isn’t really a bye week, because they play the Los Angeles Rams next Wednesday, November 25th. At 6-4, they are still very much in the race for the NFC North, as well as a Wild Card spot. Will we see the return of Micah Parsons in LA? Will the receivers’ hands start working? Will the offensive line…exist? Tune in on Netflix at 8pm ET/7pm CT on Thanksgiving Eve to find out.

title: Packers Snap Counts, Week 10: Green Bay’s offense played heavy
summary: For the second week in a row, the Green Bay Packers’ reserves got on the field. Last week, it was because they were beating down the New England Patriots so much. This week, it was because the Minnesota Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times while building a three-score lead. It wasn’t a pretty game, but […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second week in a row, the Green Bay Packers’ reserves got on the field. Last week, it was because they were beating down the New England Patriots so much. This week, it was because the Minnesota Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times while building a three-score lead. It wasn’t a pretty game, but that’s not going to stop us from breaking down the Packers’ depth chart coming out of the loss to the Vikings. Below are all of the offensive and defensive snaps their players took today. Quarterback Jordan Love: 51 snaps Tyrod Taylor: 3 Tyrod Taylor got one drive of garbage time, a three-and-out, at the end of the game, but he’s going to see more playing time soon if the team can’t protect Love. Running Back Chris Brooks: 26 Kaleb Johnson: 14 MarShawn Lloyd: 13 The Packers chose to make Pierre Strong Jr. a healthy scratch in this game in favor of the three backs they kept up. Together, those players ran 16 times for 56 yards on the day. Chris Brooks, who nearly played as many snaps as both Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd combined, only carried the ball twice for one yard. At some point, you have to wonder if Brooks’ blocking back role is a clear tell to opposing defenses that they’re free to fire off the ball and get penetration, because the team is obviously going to pass the ball. Receiver Christian Watson: 46 Matthew Golden: 45 Savion Williams: 20 J. Michael Sturdivant: 9 LaFleur on waiting til the second half to go with the quick-hitting passes: “Bad decision because our quarterback was getting abused just like he did in the first game.” — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 15, 2026 This might come as a surprise to many, but the Packers, who never had a lead in this game and were only tied for less than five minutes, played most of this game out of two-receiver sets. On a per-play basis, Green Bay averaged 2.2 receivers per play. For whatever reason, the Packers must have thought that the key to beating this Vikings defense was to add more bodies into the formation to help block blitzes, rather than spreading out pass-catchers to put more stress on blitz paths. Receivers Bo Melton and Skyy Moore both got hurt before they could even play offense. Melton went down with a thigh injury. Moore went down with an ankle injury after just being activated from the injured reserve this week. Matt LaFleur wasn’t asked about either injury in his post-game press conference on Sunday. Tight End Tucker Kraft: 51 Jonnu Smith: 20 Mark Redman: 20 Drake Dabney: 3 The Packers averaged 1.8 tight end snaps per play once you include their extra offensive line looks. For perspective, tight end Tucker Kraft played every single snap on offense that Jordan Love did in this game. Every snap that Jonnu Smith and Mark Redman played was as second or third tight ends (Drake Dabney played garbage time). Bringing an extra tight end in the formation only allowed Minnesota to bring another defender into the box, though. Eventually, you have to win one-on-ones. The Packers just weren’t able to do that, as their heavy formations weren’t able to punish the blitz-heavy Vikings on the ground. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan: 54 Laken Tomlinson: 54 John Williams: 54 Travis Glover: 54 Anthony Belton: 54 Mekhi Becton: 3 Green Bay didn’t sit any of their offensive linemen when Taylor went in at quarterback in this game. Mekhi Becton’s snaps came as an extra tight end. The full-time offensive line was Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, John Williams, Travis Glover and Anthony Belton (left to right). Neither Jager Burton nor Aaron Banks got any snaps. In the post-game presser, LaFleur said that the team wanted to move Tomlinson back to his “natural position” at left guard. That’s why Banks (who usually played left guard) was displaced in favor of Glover in this game. LaFleur stated that Glover had more “time on task” at right guard. It looks like we’re going into the bye without any answer at right guard, as we’re getting ready to ramp up another competition between Glover, Banks and Kevin Zeitler, who was inactive today after being listed as questionable with two injuries on Friday. Defensive Line 39: Devonte Wyatt 39: Karl Brooks 30: Chris McClellan 27: Jordon Riley 24: Anthony Campbell Edge Defender 36: Lukas Van Ness 33: Barryn Sorrell 32: Brenton Cox Jr. 31: Dani Dennis-Sutton Linebacker 64: Isaiah McDuffie 63: Ty’Ron Hopper 1: Nick Niemann With both starters already out, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper had to play the Mike and Will positions this week. McDuffie missed one snap with an injury, forcing Nick Niemann, a core special teamer, onto the field. That one play was a touchdown, where Niemann was given a lot of eye candy and let a tight end cross his face. They did it!! Double Screen + TE Delay! pic.twitter.com/xEmDOFTSjN — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) November 15, 2026 Cornerback 65: Keisean Nixon 52: Carrington Valentine 13: Brandon Cisse 2: Kamal Hadden Brandon Cisse left the game with a rib injury but was never officially ruled out by the team, only listed as questionable. Carrington Valentine took Cisse’s snaps at right cornerback for the remainder of the game. Usually, Valentine is the team’s second slot defender in their dime personnel looks, which they rarely use. Because he was forced to play on the outside, Kamal Hadden played two snaps in the slot today. One of those was a third-and-15 conversion, where he simply got beaten in man-to-man coverage. Packers were in dime for a rare time this season (enter 36 Kamal Hadden), and Cousins hit Tai Felton to set up an Aaron Jones TD. Vikings lead 17-0 with 6:17 left in the second quarter. pic.twitter.com/KSzxY14wnB — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 15, 2026 With enough injuries, special teamers being forced into defensive roles become a problem. Hadden had played 101 special teams snaps to just 13 defensive snaps (12 of which came in garbage time blowouts against the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots) in 2026. LaFleur was not asked about Cisse’s injury in his press conference. Safety 65: Xavier McKinney 65: Evan Williams 34: Javon Bullard Slot defender Javon Bullard was only on the field for about half of the game today, as the Vikings tried to play a heavy offense that kept Bullard sidelined in favor of an extra interior defensive lineman. The slot defender rate varies a lot game-to-game because of offensive personnel and game situation, but usually the Packers play Bullard around two-thirds of the time on defense.
author: Justis Mosqueda

title: Packers-Vikings Final Score: Green Bay’s comedy of errors continues
summary: The Green Bay Packers’ 30-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday had a little bit of everything: the offensive line getting their butt kicked, the rest of the offense having crucial errors, special teams woes and a small window of hope where it looked like the team was going to piece it together — […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers’ 30-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday had a little bit of everything: the offensive line getting their butt kicked, the rest of the offense having crucial errors, special teams woes and a small window of hope where it looked like the team was going to piece it together — just to let down the fans at Lambeau Field again. Pre-game, it was revealed that not only was guard Kevin Zeitler, who played pretty solid last week against the New England Patriots, not going to start, but he wasn’t going to play at all today. Zeitler, who came into the weekend listed as questionable with ankle and triceps injuries, was inactive. Instead, the offensive line was comprised of Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, John Williams, Travis Glover and Anthony Belton (left to right), while Aaron Banks, previously part of the three-man guard rotation last week, watched from the sideline. That offensive line didn’t give the Packers the shot in the arm that the Packers probably expected, as the team only ran for 56 yards on Sunday and surrendered an astonishing eight sacks. The Vikings are the first team with eight sacks and three takeaways over the first three quarters of a game since the 2015 Cardinals (also against Packers), per ESPN Research. The third quarter, by the way, still has 3:57 left in it. — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 15, 2026 From the jump, this game was off the rails for the offense. On the opening drive for head coach Matt LaFleur’s offense, tight end Mark Redman fumbled the ball. The defense held the Vikings to -2 yards over the first two drives, but Minnesota came away with three points on the board due to their starting field position. Then rookie kicker Trey Smack, who came into the week as the second most costly kicker in the league this year behind only Harrison Butker, missed a field goal when Green Bay was finally in scoring position. After that, the Packers declined a penalty to attempt to push the Vikings out of field goal range on their next drive, allowing Minnesota to not only to convert that third down but also score a touchdown to go up 10-0. Jordan Love later threw an interception in the red zone, where it was unclear whether or not tight end Tucker Kraft was expecting the football, which halted the offense’s momentum. The next score again came from Minnesota, which converted a long third down when the Packers played dime defense — a package the team rarely uses. The second slot in these looks is usually cornerback Carrington Valentine, who had to play right cornerback for the injured Brandon Cisse on this play — forcing Kamal Hadden into this role. That conversion set up a touchdown for former Packers running back Aaron Jones to punch in a score to go up 17-0, and in the stands at Lambeau Field for what might be his final leap in the stadium. Xavier McKinney intercepted Kirk Cousins late in the first half, but the Packers weren’t able to do anything with the possession because they took multiple sacks on the drive. Coming out of halftime, the offense posted just 57 yards and was averaging 2.2 yards per play. The first play of the second half was fitting: Yet another sack. A bad snap from third-string center John Williams led to the Vikings recovering the ball just outside of the red zone. The Packers’ defense held Minnesota to a field goal, making it 20-0. This is when momentum started to change for Green Bay. After playing multiple tight end sets for the majority of the game (they averaged 1.8 tight ends played in the first half), LaFleur began to spread out the offense with three-receiver looks regularly. Undrafted rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, who played just one snap in the first half, caught the first touchdown of his NFL career to put the Packers on the board 20-7. Shortly after, another field goal cut the lead to 20-10. From there on out, it was a game against the clock. Minnesota realized this, draining the clock starting in the mid-third quarter. The Vikings had a long sustained drive that took nearly seven minutes of time off the clock in just 11 plays. They were able to finish it off with a touchdown when linebacker Isaiah McDuffie dropped out with an injury. For one play, and one play only, Nick Niemann, a core special teamer, had to play the Mike position in place of McDuffie. On that one play, Kevin O’Connell’s offense cooked up all sorts of eye candy to isolate Niemann on a tight end, who ended up in the end zone to put Minnesota up 27-10. They did it!! Double Screen + TE Delay! pic.twitter.com/xEmDOFTSjN — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) November 15, 2026 Before the Packers’ offense got the ball again, Sturdivant, the spark that started Green Bay’s offense earlier in the game, fumbled on a kickoff and the ball was recovered by the Vikings. Sturdivant was put into the game on kickoff returns because two other receivers-returners, Bo Melton and Skyy Moore, left the game with injuries. You really can’t make this stuff up. Minnesota kicked another field goal in garbage time, but the game ended on the Sturdivant fumble. The whole game, outside of a two-drive stretch on offense, it looked like this team wanted to be put out of their misery. Four turnovers. Eight sacks. 56 yards rushing. Special teams still not being fixed. Reserves on defense getting picked on because they’re forced into the game due to injuries. Your 2026 Green Bay Packers!

full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Both the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings need a win today to avoid being the seventh seed in the NFC playoff race. After the Vikings’ big loss on Monday Night Football , they brought back an old friend — quarterback Kirk Cousins — to try to keep their title hopes alive. Meanwhile, the Packers are coming off maybe their best game of the season, blowing out the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots last week. In case you missed it, Green Bay’s roster has been very fluid lately, so let’s catch you up on who is in and who is out for Week 10. Tight end Josh Whyle was placed on injured reserve Saturday, and receiver/returner Coleman Owen was released. These moves were made so that running back Chris Brooks and receiver/returner Skyy Moore could be activated from the injured reserve . Tight end Drake Dabney was also elevated from the practice squad for this game. Running back Josh Jacobs, who just had surgery on his fractured finger, was not placed on the injured reserve, but he won’t play today. Center Sean Rhyan, guard Kevin Zeitler and linebacker Zaire Franklin will also miss Sunday’s game due to injury . The two healthy scratches against Minnesota were running back Pierre Strong Jr. and offensive lineman Donovan Jennings. The Packers picked Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson over Strong today. title: Packers Inactives, Week 10: Pierre Strong Jr., Kevin Zeitler won’t go
summary: The Green Bay Packers had to announce six scratches on Sunday after they made five roster moves on Saturday. Two of them were obvious, as running back Josh Jacobs (finger) and center Sean Rhyan (ankle) were already ruled out against the Minnesota Vikings on the Friday injury report. Here is the full list of inactives […]
