title: Value of Things: In the rearview mirror
summary: There are moments in our life that we know are coming before they happen. For me, this usually happens on the golf course. I come to a particular hole and I know it will at least be a double bogey. Often times it is even worse than that. It gets to the point where I […]
full_text: There are moments in our life that we know are coming before they happen. For me, this usually happens on the golf course. I come to a particular hole and I know it will at least be a double bogey. Often times it is even worse than that. It gets to the point where I would rather just write the six on the card and move on to the next hole. So, the actual end result is not the most maddening part. It is all of the lead up to it. You feel so helpless to prevent it. That’s when I am in charge of my own fate. Imagine watching that on television. That is what watching these Texans is like. It is like watching a car wreck in slow motion. You try to yell but nothing leaves your vocal cords. You just sit there in silence knowing what is going to happen. We have seen this movie before. We have seen it in past seasons and we have seen it several times this season. The Texans have a lead and find some way to fumble it at the end. The only real drama is in the figuring out exactly how it is going to happen. Obviously, we will be looking at the good, bad, and ugly from this game and this one will hit a little closer to home. This felt like the final nail in the Texans coffin. Sure, they have not been mathematically eliminated. They could win eight in a row and close out the season 11-6. However, that would defy any and all logic given what we have seen in the first nine games. If there is a clutch gene, this club does not have it. Key Statistics Total Yards: Texans 63/290, Browns 67/379 Rushing Yards: Texans 24/88, Browns 23/99 Passing Yards: Texans 39/202, Browns 44/280 Third Downs: Texans 3/12, Browns 7/15 Fourth Downs: Texans 0/1, Browns 0/0 Sacks. Texans 4, Browns 1 Turnovers: Texans 1, Browns 1 Penalties: Texans 13/112, Browns 2/47 Time of Possession: Texans 29:38, Browns 30:22 Before anyone goes on an on about how this team blew another game they should have won, they should take a good long look at these numbers. There is very little there that indicates that the Texans should have won the football game. Of course, games don’t happen in the box score and that is why we go through the good, bad, and ugly. The Good For the majority of the game this was actually a good defensive effort. Of course, we will hit more on that in a moment. They did register four sacks and got Watson moving on multiple other plays. In particular, it looked like Jalen Pitre, Kamari Lassiter, Derek Stingley, and Calen Bullock played a lot better than they had on previous afternoons. Of course, there is one more defensive back on the field, but we cannot mention him in this section of the proceedings. The unit was missing Danielle Hunter and Azeez Al-Shaair as well. If they had those two in the lineup I’m sure they get more pressure on Watson and they do a better job on the underneath stuff. The fact is that this team played good enough to win defensively. I will have some targeted negative comments, but as a whole this was a decent enough defensive effort. The Bad This game was a coaching failure top to bottom. The Texans got off to a good start offensively and defensively. They were up 17-0 in the second quarter. They had shut down the Browns on three straight possessions (two of them three and outs) and had scored on three straight possessions. Then, the Browns pivoted. I really am struggling to understand this. Of course they pivoted. That’s what coaches are supposed to do when they are getting their rear ends kicked. This seemed to flummox the Texans and we are looking squarely at the defense in this section. M.J. Stewart might have had his worst game as a Texan. He allowed a couple of big plays and another couple that could have happened if the Browns had been more competent. Commentators as far as the eye can see have talked about how simple this defense is. They expect the front four to get there and if they don’t get there we just shrug and move on our way. They had four sacks on the day, so they did get home on occasion and hurried him a handful of other times. When they didn’t get home they got picked apart. This is nine games now. This is who the Texans are. The coaches can say it’s early, that the field was slick, the other side has a great quarterback, or Uranus is not aligned with Venus and Haley’s comet. It’s been nine games for crying out loud. This is who you are. Make some damn adjustments. This is who you are and you wind up in these holes because it takes you longer than anyone to figure out who you are. The Ugly I’m done with Nick Caley. I’m just done. I’ve massaged the numbers. I’ve squinted from every conceivable angle. I can see where if you don’t watch the games and just look at the numbers then you see a good offense. I get that and have said it in the past. The fact is that when another team stops his first plan or when they adjust he has no second plan. He has no counter. He just sits there like a Judge Judy defendant with his mouth slightly open saying “hummuna hummuna hummuna.” Predictably, the Browns were going to amp up the pressure and clamp down on Nico Collins. See, other teams don’t allow a wide receiver to get 17 catches. They make adjustments before that happens. You see how that works? So, the Browns weren’t going to allow Nico to dominate them all day. They weren’t going to sit back and watch you pick them apart. Most teams have a plan for when the other team makes adjustments. The Texans apparently aren’t most teams. There are things you can do when the other team amps up pressure. You can use motion to confuse them. You can use misdirection like some of the wide receiver runs we have seen at different points of the season. Heck, I have heard a rumor that there is something called a screen play that some teams use to good effect. I certainly haven’t seen it in Houston, so I don’t know if this is really a thing. Obviously, this commentary is dripping with sarcasm because you either laugh or throw your laptop through the window. On two separate occasions the defense gave you the ball back with a 24-20 lead and you sent your fourth string running back straight into the line in a jumbo set where everyone on the planet knew what was coming. It is a set where you came into the game averaging two yards a carry in that formation. It is a formation that you ran out of 90 percent of the time. It needs to go the way of the dodo bird. Not only did you go three and out both times, but you didn’t even gain a yard. If you get even one first down the game likely ends. Plays seemed to be drawn from “Coaching Offense for Dummies” and it is time for Caley to be sent on his way. Focus on Stroud This is one of those games where Caley and his apologists will point to Stroud only being sacked once and say, “see we are doing a good job protecting him.” It’s all complete horse manure. He escaped sure sacks on at least three occasions and it was a minor miracle he escaped. He was under constant pressure in the second half, so I’m not putting this one on Stroud. Even his interception was probably a blown pass interference call from the officials. Yet, that is a different story for a different day. Officially, he was 20 for 38 for 211 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception. He had an 84.4 rating, but this one is on Nick Caley. It is not even a question of whether Stroud deserves an extension at this point. It is whether he wants to commit to Houston. I would demand the coordinator fired and I’d also demand a seat at the table when hiring a new one. He will be on his third offensive coordinator in his fifth year in the league. In spite of that instability, he now has 19 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Shoot that straight into my veins every year. I did feel like the interception was forced, but this is a guy that has been fitting throws into tight windows all season. He did say that he wanted a more diverse route tree and maybe they should run some more motion. He knows this offense is dog excrement. He is the whipped cream on the cow patty. He is the…

title: RECAP: Texans Lose Heartbreaker to Browns, 27-24
summary: Can the Texans just have a normal game? Will the Texans ever be capable of giving us pure, unfettered joy on a Sunday, without the stress and the heartbreakers? Well, if that ever happens, it’s not happening this season, as the Texans have now lost another heartbreaker, losing to the Cleveland Browns 27-24 in a […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Wide receiver Nico Collins #12 of the Houston Texans catches a touchdown pass during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Can the Texans just have a normal game? Will the Texans ever be capable of giving us pure, unfettered joy on a Sunday, without the stress and the heartbreakers? Well, if that ever happens, it’s not happening this season, as the Texans have now lost another heartbreaker, losing to the Cleveland Browns 27-24 in a game they absolutely had to win in order to stay in the AFC playoff race. believe the Texans playoff odds dropped from 29% down to 12% with that loss per the Athletic's playoff predictor https://t.co/6BUCWQ5kgr — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) November 15, 2026 Why? Why must they torment us? After getting everyone’s hopes up after a dominant victory over the Chargers last week, why bring our dreams and ambitions of a comeback season crashing down in such dramatic fashion? Maybe this is just who the Texans are in 2026: flashy, unpredictable, exciting, but ultimately too sloppy and injured to get out of their own way. Houston opened up the game on a heater, the offense appearing to pick up right where they left off last week by repeatedly targeting wide recievers. Following a Browns three-and-out to open the game, CJ Stroud and the Texans offense marched downfield, with multiple impressive passes to WRs Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson, capping off the drive with a wonderful touchdown pass to Nico Collins, who beat Browns DBs Tyson Campbell and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren for the score. CJ Stroud into a tight window to Nico Collins for 6! HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gZg6uDeOlt — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Following the Texans touchdown drive, the Browns would go three-and-out again thanks to pressure from Sheldon Rankins, Will Anderson, and a good tackle by CB Kamari Lassiter on third down. The Texans would march downfield yet again on the ensuing drive, with Stroud successfully targeting Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson to keep moving the chains. However, Browns LB Quincy Williams puts an end to this Texans drive on the Browns side of the field, and holding the Texans to a field goal. Now leading 10-0 with 4:25 left in the first quarter, the Texans seemed to be in control of the game right away. Was it fool’s gold? The Browns follow that drive up with another punt! Now, if you’re a Texans fan, you’re starting to get the same feeling you had at the beginning of the Chargers game. Are the Texans going to stamp out the Browns in the first half of the game and make the entire second half a laugher? Well, after the Texans went on a nine-play, 75-yard touchdown drive to make the score 17-0 in the second quarter, I know I was sure feeling like that! I was jumping around, high-fiving my sister, getting on with life like the Texans were about to put this game away. Just another successful drive or two in the second half, and this game should be over! Oh how wrong, how very, very wrong I was. Immediately following that Texans touchdown drive, the Browns responded by making two explosive plays: a 17-yard pass to TE Harold Fannin, and then a 20-yard run by QB Deshaun Watson himself. These were the only “good” plays Cleveland made on this offensive drive, but they would be a harbinger of future big plays to come. Backup LB Jake Hansen, filling in for an injured Azeez Al-Shaair, just wasn’t big enough to bring down Fannin on his own, nor fast enough to seal the edge on Watson on the ensuing rush, and those two plays led to Cleveland’s first score, a field goal to make it 17-3. Still a nice lead for the Texans. All they need to do is continue targeting Collins and put a few positive plays together and they should score again! Well, targeting Collins worked on the first set of downs, but Houston’s first of many penalties pushed them back five yards, and a negative play on WR Tank Dell made by Browns LB Carson Schwesinger forced Houston into their first punt of the game with a little more than five minutes left in the first half. The Browns wouldn’t need five minutes to remind the country of how bad the Texans defense can be at times. They only needed 53 seconds. Watson dialed up a 65-yard deep ball to a wide open Jerry Jeudy, who cooked Texans S M.J. Stewart for a big gain. One play later, and Deshaun Watson was streaking into the endzone for the Browns first touchdown, cutting the Texans lead to to just seven points. Six plays later, and the Browns were getting the ball back, courtesy of a CJ Stroud interception. Panic time!!! A wild juggling INT from Tyson Campbell 😳 HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o05D4nQ0We — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Granted, I don’t blame Stroud for targeting Collins in this circumstance, and I’m not entirely sure how this isn’t considered defensive pass interference, but regardless, this went down as an interception for Browns CB Tyson Campbell, giving the Browns the ball back with under a minute left in the second half. Watson would immediately start successfully targeting his receivers covered by Texans LB Jake Hansen again, who struggled to cover Cleveland’s RBs all game, and then Kamari Lassiter gave up a big pass to Browns’ rookie WR Denzel Boston. At this point, with 16 seconds left in the half and at midfield, Watson targeted Jerry Jeudy, who was left wide open once again by M.J. Stewart, but fortunately dropped the pass before he could walk it in for the game-tying touchdown. Deshaun Watson would run forward, fumble, and then have his lineman recover his fumble to end the half, and Houston was left counting its lucky stars to still have the lead entering halftime. At this point, my wish for a game like last week was gone, and it was replaced by the nightmares of the big plays the Texans’ defense gave up in the Bills game, the Cowboys game, and the dreaded Giants game. M.J. Stewart and Jake Hansen couldn’t cover anyone in that second half, how were the Texans going to escape this game? It would take CJ Stroud donning his Superman cape once again to deliver the Texans from defeat in the second half, and even if he was intercepted targeting Nico Collins, I thought their connection was going to save Houston in the end. How wrong I was, again! Coming out of halftime, the Browns had adjusted their defense to put more bodies in Nico Collins’ general vicinity, and were able to get far more pressure on Stroud coming out of the first half. The Texans offense completely cratered in the second half, going three-and-out four times in a row, only completing a single pass for that entire stretch of time, and the biggest play – a three-yard run by RB Woody Marks on second down with 12:21 left in the third quarter – resulted in Woody Marks potentially suffering a concussion and needing to leave the game after an injury timeout. This was immediately followed up with a false start penalty on LT Aireontae Ersery, who then gave up a sack on the very next play. The Browns followed that nightmare drive up with their game-tying touchdown drive, which featured M.J. Stewart giving up an eight-yard catch to Browns WR KC Concepcion, then giving up a seven-yard catch to Harold Fannin, which he then followed up by incurring a seven-yard penalty by trying to tackle Fannin by his FACEMASK. Now, the moon is crashing down on us. KC Concepcion runs it in for a touchdown to tie the game up with 8:35 left in the third quarter, and it feeling of impending doom is here. Following this Browns touchdown drive would be Houston’s third of four consecutive three-and-out to start the second half (of course), because who needs momentum when you’ve got NICK CALEY? The Texans chuck the ball back to the Browns like it’s a hot potato, and then Cleveland – who just seem delighted at their opponent’s conniption – start marching with the ball…

title: The Colts playing Daniel Jones is indefensible
summary: Why? Just why? Why is Daniel Jones out there for the Indianapolis Colts? It literally doesn’t get any worse, so maybe that’s the reason. Maybe it’s the $50 million Chris Ballard gave him this year. Maybe he has something on Shane Steichen? I don’t know what it is. All I know is Jones shouldn’t see […]
full_text: Why? Just why? Why is Daniel Jones out there for the Indianapolis Colts? It literally doesn’t get any worse, so maybe that’s the reason. Maybe it’s the $50 million Chris Ballard gave him this year. Maybe he has something on Shane Steichen? I don’t know what it is. All I know is Jones shouldn’t see the field again this year. Jones started his career with the Colts in the most incredible fashion. It is ending that way too. Incredibly. It is incredible how he is playing right now. A 1.7 QBR is the worst of any starting quarterback this year. That’s worse than Baker Mayfield completing zero passes. That’s worse than Carson Wentz on Monday Night Football against the Bills. Both of those performances were dreadful statistically. Jones beat them both. This wasn’t against the Vikings’ defense. This wasn’t him trying to keep pace with the best offense in the league. This was against the 1-7 Dolphins who ran a quarterback out there for his first start. Jones threw two picks and had 108 yards. Not all picks are fully on the quarterback, but the one returned for a touchdown could have been thrown better. Everything this year for Jones could be better. Not that the options to replace him are glowing, but Shane Steichen sticking with him at this point is insanity. Nothing tells you he is the guy. Wanting a change at quarterback isn’t just whiny fandom. It is a legitimate concern. Daniel Jones was horrid against one of the worst teams in the league. Things don’t get any easier than a home game against the Dolphins. Yes, talent has been depleted due to trades, but Jones has to be better. If he can’t be, then he needs to be done. The Colts have to make the change.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 8: Houston Texans helmet during an NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Los Angeles Chargers on November 8, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts won. Let me repeat. The Indianapolis Colts won. FanDuel Sportsbook isn’t predicting a repeat as the Colts are 9.5-point underdogs. With that line, Thursday Night Football could be rough. The over/under comes in at 43.5, and the money line is +440. It doesn’t look like things are going to change, however. Let’s hope the winning doesn’t either.

title: Colts survive late Dolphins rally to snap 5-game drought
summary: The Indianapolis Colts found a way to scrape through a 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins inside Lucas Oil Stadium, dodging a pair of missed field goals to snap a five-game drought. Behind a punishing backfield tandem and a timely defensive touchdown, the Colts outlasted the Dolphins to secure their third victory of the 2026 […]
full_text: The Indianapolis Colts found a way to scrape through a 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins inside Lucas Oil Stadium, dodging a pair of missed field goals to snap a five-game drought. Behind a punishing backfield tandem and a timely defensive touchdown, the Colts outlasted the Dolphins to secure their third victory of the 2026 season. It was not pretty, nearly surrendering a late lead as Indianapolis spent much of the fourth quarter barely clinging onto a two-point edge instead of a two-possession advantage. Both teams stumbled through early three-and-outs before Miami leaned heavily on running back Ollie Gordon. The Dolphins drove into Indianapolis territory before the Colts tightened up their screws near the red zone. A pair of pass break ups from rookie C.J. Allen and veteran cornerback Charvarius Ward forced a field goal try from a distance. Dolphins kicker Zane Gonzalez missed wide left on a 47-yard attempt from the right hash. Indianapolis capitalized with an 11-play march, saved as Jonathan Taylor’s early fumble was recovered by Dalton Tucker. Quarterback Daniel Jones hit Laquon Treadwell on a drag route, then rookie running back Seth McGowan bullied his way for enough yards to convert a first down. Faced with third-and-short, the Colts established their rushing attack as Tyler Warren picked up the first down on a fullback dive. Taylor danced in the backfield, patiently waiting for a hole to open to dive ahead for another first down. On the first play of the second quarter, McGowan lowered his shoulders and punched in a two-yard touchdown to take a 7-0 lead. It took a second effort from right guard Matt Goncalves and right tackle Luke Tenuta to sled push the rookie sledgehammer into the end zone. 2nd push from Indy gets Seth McGowan in for a TD MIAvsIND on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YtxqrK6PMZ — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Miami answered with a little trickery to level the score. After moving into Colts territory, the Dolphins motioned Malik Washington to the right side of the field for what appeared to be a routine bubble swing pass. Once Washington caught the initial lateral, he reared back and launched a deep pass downfield to receiver Jalen Tolbert, who slipped behind safety Cam Bynum for an explosive 34-yard touchdown to tie the game. The Colts handed the Dolphins another instant opportunity when Jones tossed a fourth-down throw into traffic. Rookie safety Michael Taaffe intercepted the lofted pass to terminate a promising drive in Dolphins territory. Miami threatened to take control by driving inside the 10-yard line before the stampede delivered another critical stand. On fourth-and-2, Dolphins coach Jeff Haley chose to burn a timeout and remove his kicking unit from the field. Miami decided to go for it instead, but McCord’s pass toward tight end Greg Dulcich was broken up on an excellent play in the end zone by rookie safety A.J. Haulcy. Indianapolis responded with its best offensive drive, a 97-yard drive in nine plays. Receiver Ashton Dulin ignited the drive, taking a slant for a 30-yard catch-and-run on third-and-5. Taylor followed up with consecutive strong runs for a combined 29 yards, ripping through the Miami defense. Shane Steichen switched it up with some misdirection as McGowan hit his strongest run, cutting back to break through the missed tackle of former-Colt JuJu Brents for a 23-yard burst that set up the offense near the goal line. There Seth goes. 😤 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/wSxaG7Y713 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 15, 2026 Two plays later, Jones threw a dart to Treadwell on a slant for a 7-yard touchdown to reclaim a 14-7 lead in the final minute of the first half. It was Treadwell’s first TD since 2021 and just the sixth of his 10-year career. Jones was held to 11 of 22 passing for 108 yards and a touchdown, but also fumbled and threw two interceptions. The Colts wasted no time adding to their lead out of the halftime break. On Miami’s first snap of the second half, Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo sent a nickelback blitz. Second-year cornerback Justin Walley blitzed untouched, hunted down McCord and knocked the football loose, allowing defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore to recover the fumble in the end zone for a defensive touchdown. Justin Walley and Adetomiwa Adebawore!!!! 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/6vRWIgioSk — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 15, 2026 Just 12 seconds into the second half, Indianapolis doubled its lead to 21-7. That two possession advantage evaporated when Gonzalez momentarily redeemed himself with a 51-yard FG. Jones tried to extend a broken play once he stumbled, then forced a throw while falling to the turf, which ultimately bounced off the hands of Drew Ogletree and landed in the hands of cornerback Chris Johnson, who took it 59 yards to the house for a pick-six. Taylor and McGowan steadied the offense with another physical possession, matching each other with tough gains to move Indianapolis into scoring range. Spencer Shrader drilled a 51-yard FG to restore a 24-22 cushion. The Colts struggled to find oxygen in the second half, generating just 39 total net yards in six true drives. Three consecutive possessions ended in punts, giving Miami opportunities to steal the lead. The Dolphins refused to disappear into oblivion as McCord guided a 71-yard drive to start the fourth quarter, punctuating it himself with his first NFL touchdown run from three-yards out. Miami attempted a two-point conversion to tie the game, but Haulcy broke up McCord’s pass intended for Dulcich again. Gonzalez later missed another field goal wide left from 51 yards, allowing the Colts to preserve a lead they never relinquished. Miami had one final chance to seize the lead once Washington returned a punt to the 42-yard-line, starting with excellent field position and three minutes to play. Gordon moved the Dolphins across midfield with consecutive runs before the front line stood strong. CJ Allen blitzed unblocked and sacked McCord for a 10-yard loss, then Tuimoloau batted away the fourth-down attempt at the line of scrimmage. CJ ALLEN 💪 Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/VW6S3uFsXs pic.twitter.com/UYinZqzmgi — Georgia Football (@GeorgiaFootball) November 15, 2026 The rookie class stamped their impact on both sides of the ball. Indy’s tailback tandem combined for 172 rushing yards, led by Taylor with 83 yards on 16 carries. McGowan added a career-best 77 rushing yards and a touchdown on 12 attempts. Allen and fellow rookie Bryce Boettcher combined for 15 tackles. Allen added a sack, two tackles for loss and a pass breakup. Haulcy delivered one of the most critical breakups to preserve the lead. It was far from a masterpiece, but Indianapolis emerged victorious through the finish line. The Colts will head South with a short week to prepare to face the Houston Texans in a rivalry Thursday Night Football game.

title: Indianapolis Colts discussion: Week 10 live chat during the Dolphins game
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are at home to take on the Miami Dolphins for week 10 of the 2026 season, kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST. With the trade deadline behind us, the Colts coaches and front office have to be hoping the distractions caused by a midseason mass exodus, are behind them as well. Now the problem […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts mascot Blue lies on the turf following a touchdown by the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, during a game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Indianapolis Colts are at home to take on the Miami Dolphins for week 10 of the 2026 season, kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST. With the trade deadline behind us, the Colts coaches and front office have to be hoping the distractions caused by a midseason mass exodus, are behind them as well. Now the problem is, what’s left for them to try to win with? The Indianapolis Colts will start Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin and Anthony Gould today at wide receiver. A former first round bust, a career core special teamer and a guy who didn’t make the initial 53 man roster. At this point in this lost season I am fully on board with benching Daniel Jones, but it has less to do with Jones’ play, which hasn’t been as awful as the TV copy has made it look (the playcalling and his supporting cast have been just as questionable as his level of play). Anthony Richardson should start at quarterback, not because it will provide better outcomes, but for literally every other reason. He’s exciting, even if he’s bad. He’s been sitting behind a guy who “does all of the right things” behind the scenes, let’s see if that time sitting has done any good. And finally, if the team is going to lose either way, what’s the point in not trying something, anything different? Now, having said all of that, I don’t think it matters if prime Andrew Luck were on this roster. No one is capable of getting open. Shane Steichen has forgotten how to scheme anyone open and teams are keying so hard on the run game when Jonathan Taylor is in (because they know the receivers can’t get open against even bad NFL cornerbacks), moving the ball down the field has been dependent upon luck and defensive pass interference calls. During Chris Ballard’s tenure there were always holes in the roster (there are holes in all 32 NFL rosters every season) but for most of those years it felt like they were just a quarterback away from contending. That’s no longer true. When the season started this was a bad team and this bad team has traded away most of it’s best players. The rest of this season could be very ugly. Side Note: I told you about this last week but I’m probably going to keep reminding you each week because I think it’s important for everyone who enjoys these gameday threads. The SB Nation app makes commenting, especially in these game feeds, so much easier. At this point I roll my eyes every time someone asks me to download another app, but this one really does improve the experience so much that even I am telling you that if you like to hang out here, chat, celebrate, commiserate, and argue in the comments, this app is actually worth your time. Links are directly below. Join Stampede Blue on game day! Stay on top of every Colts update and debate every snap with other diehard fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app. Fewer ads Jump easily between conversations Faster commenting and posting Download on iOS or Android . The Dolphins are sitting at 1-7. But since week four, they’ve only lost one game by more than one score. In that time they’ve played the Vikings, Bengals, Jets (their lone win), the Patriots and Lions (a 10 point loss). The Dolphins are also a bad football team but they haven’t really been “blown out” since week two, losing to the San Francisco 49ers 13-35. The Dolphins will be without starting quarterback Malik Willis. Kyle McCord will make his first career start. McCord was the 181st pick (6th round) in the 2025 NFL Draft. He was selected by the Philadelphia Eagles and frankly I’m not going to look up McCord’s transaction history to figure out how he ended up as the QB2 in Miami a year later, but I think the safe bet is on him not making the Eagles roster. So for as bad as things are in Indy, they might just be worse in Miami. The difference is, everyone expected Miami to be bad. Their owner didn’t tell fans she expected to win and the urgency to win had “never been higher”. Ultimately this is a game between two very bad NFL football teams. It should be terrible to watch. Frankly, every Colts game for the rest of the season will probably be pretty awful. But I’ll be watching players, not outcomes. I’m interested to watch CJ Allen’s development. I’ll be watching Bryce Boettcher, hoping he’ll start to figure out how to play linebacker in the NFL, because if he does that ability combined with his athleticism could make for a very exciting player. Right now, he’s fun to watch in the same way 2024 Anthony Richardson was, it wasn’t good but there were a lot of interesting plays and it all happened fast. I’ll be watching Jaylahn Tuimoloau continue his ascent as a player and I’ll be rooting hard for Caden Curry who has made plays each and every week. Offensively I’ll be watching Jalen Farmer and hoping the young man continues to grow. He’s had some good and some bad moments but each week is an invaluable opportunity to improve. I’ll also be watching receiver Deion Burks. For Burks as an individual, it’s difficult to imagine a better scenario. Sixth round receivers rarely get the kind of opportunity Burks is about to have for the rest of the season. I’m interested to see what he does with it. And if it happens, I’ll be very interested to see Anthony Richardson on the field for the Colts again. And as bad as he was the last time the team tried it, it is time to try it again. Prediction: Dolphins: 13 Colts: 12 As always, go Colts. title: 4 Players to Watch For the Rest of the Colts season
summary: Now that the trade deadline is finally over, we can finally start talking about the guys who are certainly not going to be here and focus on the guys who might be next year. Obviously the Colts won’t be competing for something meaningful this season, but there is always something to play for in the […]
full_text: Now that the trade deadline is finally over, we can finally start talking about the guys who are certainly not going to be here and focus on the guys who might be next year. Obviously the Colts won’t be competing for something meaningful this season, but there is always something to play for in the NFL. The Colts roster has some older vets, but they also have some younger developmental player that are going to get opportunities to play the rest of the way. Here are the 5 I’m watching 1. LG Jalen Farmer It goes without saying that Jalen Farmer was never going to replace Quenton Nelson. That is all but impossible. He is one the best LG’s to ever play the position. The one thing we took for granted in the Chris Ballard era was that the OL was rarely in flux. 2022 comes to mind, but other than that, the line was taken care of. Is Jalen Farmer the long-term answer? I don’t know that. It’s hard to project who the new OL coach is, who the new GM likes, and what resources the Colts want to invest in that position. And unlike Tanor Bortolini, Matt Goncalves, and especially Bernhard Raimann, there’s less of a proof of concept that he can play at a high level. But Farmer does have a chance. At the moment he’s struggled with stunts and twists in pass pro, but also some of the Run ID’s This is a consistent issue that keeps popping up. I'm not going to pretend that blocking Quinnen Williams is easy, but Farmer has to come off this and get to the linebacker We just can't have playside LBs untouched for a 2nd week in a row. First play of the game too. pic.twitter.com/Uu62cZieCn — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) November 9, 2026 He’s definitely a powerful presence on the OL, he can get movement in the run game, but he is lacking a bit of athleticism to climb to the 2nd level. I’m excited to see his development. Ultimately I think the Colts current run game has been predicated on having some of the most athletic interior offensive lineman in the sport, and Farmer has struggled to live up to that billing. However, that doesn’t mean he can’t develop into a great guard for them. 2. Seth McGowan I’m unsure as to what the future holds for Jonathan Taylor. He has not denied that he asked for a trade request, and where there’s smoke there’s fire. I think the Colts would be wise to keep him at this point, but if JT would like a change of scenery, we’ve seen these things drag out in the offseason. That being said, I think this is a great opportunity for Seth McGowan. I really like Seth McGowan. Not a flashy run, but you can see the vision and the ability to get some of the dirty yards. pic.twitter.com/QsjtqkII0C — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) October 6, 2026 Elite third down operation. Converting 3rd & long vs. a Flores defense shouldn't have been as easy as the Colts made it at times. Love Seth McGowan. pic.twitter.com/kxmAZ1ILLH — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) October 26, 2026 I think Seth McGowan can develop into a lead back. Like Farmer, those are massive shoes to replace and he will almost certainly not be able to live up to that kind of production. But I imagine something similar to what we’re seeing in Los Angelas with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. I don’t think McGowan has shown the twitchiness or home run speed that the elite backs have, but he is a tough hard nose runner that almost always falls forward. He has burst in gap scheme to hit the hole, and he’s already the best pass protecting running back on the team. He reminds me of Zack Moss, who I always thought played a pivotal role for the Colts in 2023. 3. Jaylahn Tuimoloau Defensive players are always the hardest to project. I have no clue what the defensive scheme will be and there’s a chance that, despite his growth as a run defender and pass rusher, Tuimoloau just won’t be a fit. But nonetheless, I think he’s a player that is intriguing. To be quite honest, I had no clue if Tuimoloau would even play on defense after the preseason he had. 91 driving me insane all preseason pic.twitter.com/YE8MiMledr — Zach Hicks (@ZachHicks2) August 26, 2026 But he’s responded in a way I’m not sure we could have predicted. Each week he’s played better and better and that’s exactly what a new GM wants to see as he looks to shape this roster for the future. A fantastic rep from Tuimoloau vs. Ronnie Stanley. Maybe just took him a bit longer to ramp up and get in better physical shape? Idk, but it's night and day from what we saw in the preseason https://t.co/Sd5v8DwRTg pic.twitter.com/LdBdn4AAoO — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 15, 2026 Jaylahn Tuimoloau is starting to flash a bit for the Colts. Still not putting it all together yet, but the run defense has been better and there's been some positives as a pass rusher pic.twitter.com/rRsgbzxAfp — Zach Hicks (@ZachHicks2) November 2, 2026 ‼️ Tuimoloau take down ‼️ 📺 Fox pic.twitter.com/EYkxoqlfoe — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 8, 2026 He’s shown he can kick inside and rush on guards, he’s setting better edges in the run game, and has done a nice job in his role as a contain rusher. I don’t know that is ceiling is high enough to be a perennial double digit sack guy, but when he was drafted, that’s never what was advertised. Right now I think he’s developed right where the Colts thought he would be. I am interested to see where he ends up. I’m not sure where he’ll factor in the 2027 scheme, but definitely a guy who has been a net positive for the team this year. 4. CJ Allen The expectations for CJ Allen always felt higher than they probably should have. I think that was partly because the Colts did very little to address the position, and then did very little to quell those expectations by touting his ability to be a potential green dot from Day 1. In today’s NFL with so much motion, condensed sets, under center play action, and unique body types at TE, I feel like playing LB as a rookie is as tough as it’s ever been. Despite some of the early hype for CJ Allen, he didn’t really get a full offseason and it always felt like it was an uphill battle for him to be a contributor early in his rookie tenure. I think he’s still getting into football shape, mentally and physically. It’s hard for a player, let alone a rookie, to get up to speed, when you don’t get that full training camp— and then definitely difficult when you aren’t getting reps in the beginning of the season either Weird linebacker rotations aside, I have a close eye on CJ Allen. Early on there’s not a ton of reps to gleam from, so take these early observations with the smallest grain of salt. In the run game, I think he’d benefit from a fast flowing defense that allows you to shoot gaps. Right now it feels like offensive lineman are moving him off the ball more than you would like. In pass coverage I think he’s shown he has relatively good instincts in vision zone. The change of direction appears a bit stiff, but that’s ok for a MLB. The play-style stands out, maybe in part because it’s been lacking from other guys on the defense, but maybe that’s just CJ. He’s a high energy linebacker that will fly to the football. I am excited to see where the ceiling for CJ Allen is when he gets more reps at the NFL level, but at a bare minimum, I think he’s earned the right to compete at the MLB spot next year.

title: Three reasons why the Jaguars beat the Titans
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are beginning to look like a serious problem for the rest of the AFC. Liam Coen’s side traveled to Nashville on Sunday and came away with a convincing 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans, extending their winning streak to three games and improving their record to 7-2. With the Houston Texans slipping […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 and Parker Washington #11 of the Jacksonville Jaguars react to a play during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars are beginning to look like a serious problem for the rest of the AFC. Liam Coen’s side traveled to Nashville on Sunday and came away with a convincing 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans , extending their winning streak to three games and improving their record to 7-2. With the Houston Texans slipping up against Cleveland, Jacksonville now holds a commanding four-game advantage at the top of the AFC South. There were plenty of positives for the visitors, but this wasn’t simply a case of taking advantage of a struggling divisional rival. The Jaguars demonstrated why they are becoming one of the most dangerous teams in the conference. Here are three reasons why Jacksonville came away with the victory. Trevor Lawrence is playing at an elite level Trevor Lawrence another ELITE performance 307 Pass Yards 3 Pass TD INT 126.7 Pass Rating pic.twitter.com/I76K6bFOfs — PFF (@PFF) November 15, 2026 There have been plenty of questions about Trevor Lawrence throughout his NFL career. Is he capable of being the franchise quarterback Jacksonville hoped they were getting when they selected him first overall in 2021? Can he consistently deliver the performances expected of a quarterback of his considerable talent? Right now, those questions are looking increasingly redundant. Lawrence was outstanding against Tennessee, completing 23 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns. He connected with nine different receivers, demonstrating the sort of command and confidence that makes this Jacksonville offense so difficult to defend. Perhaps most encouragingly, this wasn’t an isolated performance. Lawrence has now surpassed 300 passing yards in three of his last five games, while the Jaguars have scored at least 30 points in four consecutive outings. The connection between Lawrence and head coach Liam Coen is becoming increasingly apparent. The quarterback looks comfortable in the offensive system, understands where his opportunities are coming from, and is playing with the sort of conviction that can elevate an entire offense. Lawrence also reached 20,000 career passing yards against Tennessee, becoming the eighth-youngest player in NFL history to achieve the milestone. Jacksonville has a quarterback playing with genuine confidence, and that could make the Jaguars a very difficult proposition come January. Parker Washington is becoming a serious weapon Parker Washington said gimme that pic.twitter.com/OgvAaEPHxe — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 15, 2026 Trevor Lawrence deserves plenty of the credit, but he also needs players capable of turning opportunities into big plays. Against Tennessee, Parker Washington provided exactly that. The young receiver enjoyed a spectacular afternoon, finishing with 152 receiving yards and a touchdown. Remarkably, he had already accumulated 148 yards by halftime, giving the Titans’ defense all sorts of problems before the interval. Washington’s ability to create separation and generate yards after the catch gives Jacksonville another dimension in the passing game. He isn’t simply a possession receiver waiting for the ball to come to him; he is capable of turning relatively routine completions into substantial gains. His performance also highlights an important development in Jacksonville’s offense. Lawrence isn’t reliant on one individual to produce. Washington, Brenton Strange, and Josh Cameron all found the end zone, while nine different receivers caught passes. That variety makes life considerably harder for opposing defensive coordinators. Concentrate too heavily on one threat and another player is likely to make you pay. With Washington producing performances like this, Jacksonville has another weapon capable of making a significant difference down the stretch. Tennessee’s defense simply couldn’t get off the field Robert Saleh vs Liam Coen in a big spot… WIDE OPEN TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/JwKHTETyQQ — John Frascella (Football) (@NFLFrascella) November 15, 2026 There is no getting away from the fact that Tennessee’s defense had a miserable afternoon. Jacksonville finished with 459 total yards, averaged 6.4 yards per play, and converted seven of its 14 third-down opportunities. The Jaguars also controlled possession for more than 38 minutes, leaving the Titans with precious little opportunity to build any sustained momentum. It wasn’t just Lawrence’s passing that caused problems, either. Jacksonville accumulated 123 rushing yards, with Bhayshul Tuten adding a late six-yard touchdown to put the finishing touches on the victory. The inability to get off the field was particularly damaging. Jacksonville repeatedly extended drives, controlled the tempo, and forced Tennessee’s defense to spend long periods chasing the game. There were mitigating circumstances for Robert Saleh. Tennessee has undergone significant personnel changes, with injuries and trades leaving the defensive unit considerably depleted. But the numbers make for uncomfortable reading regardless. Giving up 40 points and 459 yards is not a recipe for success against an offense with the talent Jacksonville possesses. The Titans managed to stay within touching distance for much of the contest, but their inability to consistently disrupt Lawrence and get the ball back to their own offense ultimately proved costly. Jacksonville is a serious contender There is still plenty of football to be played, but Jacksonville is putting together an impressive body of work. Lawrence is playing with confidence, the receiving corps is developing into a dangerous group, and Coen’s offense is producing points consistently. The Jaguars weren’t perfect against Tennessee, and there are defensive areas they will want to address, but winning on the road by 17 points against a divisional opponent is exactly the sort of business a playoff contender should be taking care of. At 7-2, with a four-game lead in the AFC South, Jacksonville has given itself an excellent platform for the second half of the season. The question is no longer whether the Jaguars can win their division. It’s how far this team can go once the playoffs arrive. DUUUVAL! Join the game-day conversation on the SB Nation app! title: Jaguars Winners & Losers From Week 10: Parker Washington Explodes In Rivalry Win
summary: It certainly wasn’t a blowout, but good teams win and better teams cover. The Jacksonville Jaguars did just that in a 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Despite their record and their roster, the Titans aren’t a completely awful team and showed that a bit on Sunday. The Jags had their hands full […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Parker Washington #11 of the Jacksonville Jaguars carries the ball against Tony Adams #29 of the Tennessee Titans during the first half at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images It certainly wasn’t a blowout, but good teams win and better teams cover. The Jacksonville Jaguars did just that in a 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Despite their record and their roster, the Titans aren’t a completely awful team and showed that a bit on Sunday. The Jags had their hands full at times but made the plays when it mattered most to improve to 7-2 for the first time since 1998. Jacksonville is rattling off wins towards a potential play at the AFC’s top overall seed and with one of the league’s easiest schedules for the rest of the year, things are looking good in Duval County. There is only one place to start when talking about Jacksonville’s third straight win. It’s with Parker Washington. WINNERS Parker “Parker Washington” Washington Jacksonville chopped plenty of wood and carried buckets of water on the way to victory. It was the Washington show in Nashville as the former Nittany Lion rattled off a career-high 152 receiving yards. Washington was quiet in the second half but it didn’t matter because he did more than enough work in the first half, plucking ball after ball off the heads of hapless Titans defenders. Parker Washington just set a new career high with 152 receiving yards. 7 REC, 152 REC YDS, 1 TD vs Titans. Jacksonville is now 7-2 and looking like a serious Super Bowl contender. https://t.co/kp439ArwK8 pic.twitter.com/JTI8VCBdAm — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 15, 2026 Washington’s big day was part of an even bigger day by quarterback Trevor Lawrence who finished with 352 yards and three touchdowns and eclipsed 20,000 yards passing in Jacksonville. One of those touchdowns came on the first drive of the game where the QB found Washington at the back of the end zone. The only downside of Washington continuing to play so well is that Jacksonville still needs to pay him. As it has after almost every game this season, the price for the third-year receiver has gone up again. A career day for Parker Washington 👏 🏈 1st Jaguars WR with 145+ Rec yds in a half in the last 11 seasons 🏈 First Jaguars WR with 150+ receiving yards since Week 5 of 2019 🏈 Career-high 6th Rec TD of the season pic.twitter.com/4kifL9RKzK — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 15, 2026 Josh Cameron Back in 2023, Washington was selected in the sixth round, making his way up to wide receiver one status in Jacksonville. If Josh Cameron keeps it up, a sixth-rounder himself, he could be well on his way to Washington levels of status. The rookie Cameron was second on the Jags in receiving with three catches for 67 yards while catching his third touchdown of the year. Cameron also did decently in the return game once more, collecting 142 total return yards with a long of 32. He did get crushed by Tennessee kicker Joey Slye which resulted in a fumble, but those types of plays are few and far between anyway. There’s no question Jacksonville has a loaded wide receiver room. However, Cameron keeps proving he deserves to be on the field. If Brian Thomas Jr. continues to be up and down, Cameron will continue to reap the benefits. Josh Cameron (good player) with two big catches today. A 3rd down dunk and then a TD to make it a two score game in the 4th. pic.twitter.com/wJTsh3KSMi — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 15, 2026 Bhayshul Tuten For another Washington comparison: It should really come as no surprise that Bhayshul Tuten had another solid day. The running back had 113 total yards with 88 yards rushing and his fifth score of the year on the ground. Tuten now has touchdowns on the ground in three straight games and has gone over 100 total yards in two of his last three outings. Jacksonville made a great call when it turned over the keys to Tuten. His hard-nosed presence unlocks a nastiness in this offense that gives the Jags an edge anytime the ball is in his hands. In the same mold as Washington, Tuten is trusted to make the plays needed to propel the team to victory. He did so on Broadway. Bhayshul Tuten has reached 600 rushing yards ✅ Season Stats: 122 Car | 609 Rush Yds | 5 Rush TD Season Pace: 230 Car | 1,150 Rush Yds | 9 Rush TD #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/othk2X2rNP — PaceBall (@paceball__) November 15, 2026 Cam Little Here is your obligatory Cam Little Rocks section. Little went 4-for-4 on field goals and 4-for-4 on extra points. It’s almost indescribable how important it is to have someone as automatic as Little is. The Jags got points on all but two drives (8-10 overall), largely because once the team crosses the 50, they know they can rely on Little to convert. Liam Coen Much was said about last year’s dustup between then 49ers defensive coordinator Rob Salah and Liam Coen. How sweet must it be for Coen to beat Salah last year, only to turn around and drop 40 in Salah’s home stadium, now the head coach with the Titans? Running Tuten into the end zone with under two minutes to play had to feel damn good. Coen has done a tremendous job with the Jags since taking over. It doesn’t take this column to tell you that. Jacksonville has cut down on penalties (just two Sunday) and overall boneheaded mistakes. That game was one Lawrence batted-ball interception away from being about as good as you could get, at least offensively. Coen has won 20 of his first 26 games, and is just the third coach to do so in the last 15 years. He is tops in terms of winning percentage over those games in the history of the sport. Jacksonville is rolling and the head coach is a huge reason why. Keeping his coordinators in place after last year’s hiring cycle cannot go unnoticed too. This is the year to make a run. There’s no reason to believe right now that Coen isn’t the guy to lead it. “Division win on the road. Doesn’t get better than that.” #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/VU3ROQh66p — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 15, 2026 Jessie Bates Yeah, so that trade for Jessie Bates was a huge one because the safety play in Nashville was subpar. More will be said on the defense below, but Bates proved his worth before ever even taking a snap defensively for Jacksonville. This team needs help on the back end. Luckily, help is ready to play and maybe even sleeping in the facility. Do I have news for you https://t.co/2v4AlmrNWU — Daniel Griffis (@DanDGriffis) November 15, 2026 LOSERS The Defense At Times Does anyone want to talk about that Tony Pollard touchdown ? No? Yes, the Titans aren’t a great offense. Yes, the Jags have a smothering defense typically. But also yes that the Titans are playing well offensively as of late. The Jags got exposed at times by that offense and especially on Pollard’s 32-yard receiving touchdown where he broke through just about the entire Jacksonville defense. Cam Ward and company didn’t light Jacksonville up, but that game wasn’t the pure defensive domination many might have thought was coming. There were some solid individual performances though on defense. Travis Hunter had an incredible leaping interception . Ventrell Miller was crushing guys like usual . Dennis Gardeck even looked pretty solid . But this defense needs the help it acquired at the deadline. Overall, no worries probably. But that was not this unit’s best performance of the year at all. Cam Ward ranks among QBs to play Jaguars defense this season Rank Passing yards: 231 4th Passing tds: 2 2nd Rushing yards: 39 1st Completion %: 71.8%… — Titans Era (@titanserashow) November 15, 2026 Injuries There were no DaVon Hamilton-level injuries following Sunday’s game, but that doesn’t mean the Jags got out of Nashville unscathed. title: Liam Coen: Parker Washington was ‘the best player on the field’ on Sunday
summary: Look. Don’t shoot the messenger. I know you already know this. But as somebody who covers the Jacksonville Jaguars, I wouldn’t be doing my job if I didn’t tell you what I saw when I watched them play. In Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season, like the rest of the football-viewing world, I saw […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TN - NOVEMBER 15: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) and Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) bow to each other in celebration after connecting for a touchdown during a game between the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars, November 15, 2026, at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Matthew Maxey/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Look. Don’t shoot the messenger. I know you already know this. But as somebody who covers the Jacksonville Jaguars, I wouldn’t be doing my job if I didn’t tell you what I saw when I watched them play. In Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season, like the rest of the football-viewing world, I saw Randy Moss. The greatest deep threat in football history returned to the gridiron after a 5,000-day absence. Moss’ last official NFL action was on December 30, 2012 — but there was no doubt that the all-time receiver was playing for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Tennessee Titans. Moss’ first catch of the day capped Jacksonville’s opening drive for a touchdown. Some receivers climb the ladder; this cat broke the stratosphere. Parker Washington has a Jacksonville touchdown! JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pUVFGg72PT — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 His 33-yard gain on the ensuing drive was a classic “Moss.” Parker Washington is filthy 🙆‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/U3wh9EzdeA — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) November 15, 2026 Not to mention his 20-yarder the drive after that! Parker Washington is going ballistic today pic.twitter.com/cfK4HQ31w7 — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 15, 2026 Obviously, the guy I’m talking about is Parker Washington. After flaunting his above-the-rim abilities in the first half, Washington exhibited his route-running savvy with this flifthy 50-yard pickup. Parker Washington turning DBs 360 degrees pic.twitter.com/WOCBpP7b5j — Billy M (@BillyM_91) November 15, 2026 Washington finished with a career-high 152 receiving yards — the most by a Jaguars wide receiver since DJ Chark had 164 yards in Week 5 of 2019 — to help Jacksonville score 40 points on the road over the arch-rival Titans. “He was a man possessed in a lot of ways,” said head coach Liam Coen. “Parker was definitely the best player on the field today.” “Parker’s a baller,” said running back Bhayshul Tuten. “He had some crazy catches today, some contested catches, but he just keeps showing up. And I think that’s Parker’s MO, and he just goes out there, chop wood, carry water. He just goes out there and does him.” “Man, I don’t even get surprised no more,” said wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. Jacksonville’s offense has been a juggernaut for about a full season now. If you combine the first half of 2026 with the second half of 2025, the Jaguars have the NFL’s best record at 15-2. Trevor Lawrence ranks first in passer rating (105.9) and touchdown-to-interception ratio (40:10) in that span. Lawrence deserves all the credit he’s getting, and then some, yet the same should be said of Washington. He ranks 10th among all NFL wide receivers with 1,195 yards over his last 17 games. For context, the only Jaguars with more receiving yards in a sewason are Thomas (2024), Allen Robinson (2015), Keenan McCardell (2000), and Jimmy Smith (1996-97, 1999-01). So far this season, Jacksonville is 5-0 when Washington scores a touchdown and 2-2 otherwise. He may not be Randy Moss, but the kid can play. You already knew that, though. “Got some good opportunities to make some plays and most importantly we came out with this win, and that’s the plan out there,” said Washington. “Let’s keep it going.” Chop Wood, Carry Water. #DUUUVAL — Parker Washington (@CPW11_) November 15, 2026

summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars keep winning but they can’t move up in the AFC standings. Kansas City’s record in the AFC is 6-1, slightly better than the Jaguars at 6-2, so the Chiefs are the […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars carries the ball during the second half against Cor'dale Flott #18 of the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars keep winning but they can’t move up in the AFC standings. The Kansas City Chiefs won on Sunday to leap from fifth into second, bypassing the Denver Broncos in the AFC West. Kansas City’s record in the AFC is 6-1, slightly better than the Jaguars at 6-2, so the Chiefs are the two seed right now. In the AFC South, the Jaguars got help from a Houston Texans loss to the Cleveland Browns. The Jags have a stranglehold on the division now up four games. Explaining the 7-2 tiebreakers in the AFC The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker at 7-2, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beat all the others, so it heads to AFC record. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed. Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card. title: Jaguars Keep Rolling With Dominant Win Over Titans
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars made another statement on Sunday, traveling to Nashville and taking care of business against the Tennessee Titans with a convincing 40-23 victory. Jacksonville’s offense put up 40 points on the road, while the Jaguars continued to show why they’re clearly one of the teams to beat in the AFC. With Sunday’s victory, […]
full_text: Nov 15, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) makes a catch as Tennessee Titans cornerback Alontae Taylor (24) defends during the first quarter at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jacksonville Jaguars made another statement on Sunday, traveling to Nashville and taking care of business against the Tennessee Titans with a convincing 40-23 victory. Jacksonville’s offense put up 40 points on the road, while the Jaguars continued to show why they’re clearly one of the teams to beat in the AFC. With Sunday’s victory, Jacksonville extended its AFC South divisional lead over the Houston Texans with just eight regular-season games remaining. AFC South live #Jaguars 7-2 Houston 3-6 Indianapolis 3-7 Tennessee 1-8 — Ryan O'Halloran (@ryanohalloran) November 15, 2026 Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 10 40-23 victory over the Titans in Nashville, as they eye the AFC’s No. 1 seed . Favorite Highlight: Travis Hunter’s diving first-quarter interception to get the ball back for the Jacksonville offense, following their turnover, was a thing of beauty and my favorite highlight, as Anthony Campanile’s group continues to force turnovers inside their own 30-yard line. Travis Hunter is that guy. JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Xsbym92VSs — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 The first-half pick was Hunter’s third of the season. Post-game notables: Bend, But Don’t Break Defense, Broke? The stats sheet clearly shows that the Jacksonville defense had a great day on a down-by-down basis, holding the Tennessee offense to 4/14 (28.6%) on third- and fourth-down combined conversions. Yet, explosive plays via blown coverages and missed tackles still resulted in the Jacksonville defense surrendering two touchdowns to the Tennessee offense, in a way that is normally foreign to this Jacksonville defense. Outside of the blown drives, Jacksonville’s plan of forcing teams to put together extended drives, then clamping down in the red zone, worked, for the most part. Tennessee had just one red zone attempt, a successful one, and Campanile’s defense forced three long field goals (50, 53, and 54 yards) for the other scores. Jaguars Offense Struggles in Redzone The Jacksonville Jaguars offense has historically been dominant in the red zone of matchups. However, in this one, Jacksonville was nearly 1/4 (25%) in red zone attempts at the end of the third quarter, needing two questionable calls by the officials in their seventh drive with a touchdown. Following a third-down drop by Jakobi Meyers, Tennessee was called for roughing the passer to extend the series. Following that penalty, Jacksonville decided to attempt a fourth and two from the three-yard line, where Meyers could have been called for offensive pass interference on what looked to be a pick play. In addition to the red zone problems, the team settled for field goals from the 21, 27, and 30-yard line – just outside of the red zone area. The Jacksonville offense ended the day going 3/5 (60%) in the red zone, with the notable above drive impacting the numbers. Run Game Issues Continue Running back Bhayshul Tuten had a dominant game against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. However, since that time, the second-year running back has averaged less than 3.4 yards per carry in four of five games (Philly, Houston, Baltimore, ****and Tennessee*****). Similar to last season, when the Jaguars’ run game fell off in the second half of the season, this issue seems to be presenting itself again in consecutive weeks. Tuten ended Sunday’s matchup with 26 carries for 88 yards (3.4 YPC). Parker’s Down There Somewhere Parker Washington passed his full-game career-high in yardage in the opening half against the Titans, while opening the day’s scoring. Parker Washington has a Jacksonville touchdown! JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pUVFGg72PT — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Washington climbed the ladder on multiple first-half catches, resulting in a dominant first half where the contract-year receiver ended the half with more receiving yards (148) than the Titans had passing yards (99). Parker Washington or Peter Parker? JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/l02kcfOngG — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 The highlight show continued, as Parker put Titans slot cornerback Alontae Taylor on skates for another explosive second-quarter gain. Parker Washington turning DBs 360 degrees pic.twitter.com/WOCBpP7b5j — Billy M (@BillyM_91) November 15, 2026 Parker’s day cooled somewhat after the half, finishing with just one additional catch for four yards after halftime. His 152-yard day on seven catches led the team. In Case You Missed It Sunday’s matchup against Tennessee didn’t start off as the cleanest affair for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Following an opening drive featuring a 28-yard explosive Josh Cameron gain, Jacksonville took the early lead. However a Trevor Lawrence tipped pass interception set Jacksonville’s defense up for a huge seesaw emotions, shifting from the down after the interception, to a high following Travis Hunter’s subsequent diving interception of Cam Ward. Lawrence has his pass batted in the air and the Titans take it away JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7Um2mBJkcg — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Following the back-and-forth early turnovers, Jacksonville’s mistakes allowed this one to stay closer than it felt. title: NFL predictions: Expect a Strange day against the Hooker-less Titans
summary: Here are some predictions for what we’ll see today when the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 1-7 Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the good guys are favored by 10.5 points. Prediction #1 The NFL is a week-to-week league. A limited number of plays leads to extreme unpredictability. One or two […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 04: Brenton Strange #85 of the Jacksonville Jaguars reacts after a touchdown in the second quarter against the Tennessee Titans at EverBank Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here are some predictions for what we’ll see today when the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 1-7 Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the good guys are favored by 10.5 points. Prediction #1 The NFL is a week-to-week league. A limited number of plays leads to extreme unpredictability. One or two specific matchups can determine a win or a loss. And because of the sport’s physical nature, injuries cause constant attrition. In today’s game between Jacksonville and Tennessee, both teams will be without their top safety. The Jaguars lost Eric Murray for the season to an elbow injury. They secured not just a replacement, but an upgrade by trading for Jessie Bates III — although the team is resting him today to give him an unofficial bye week. That means another start for Rayuan Lane III. The Titans lost their leader in the secondary, Amani Hooker, by trading him to the Buffalo Bills after Brandon Beane whiffed on Bates. It sounds like Hooker will be missed. Titans head coach Robert Saleh on Amani Hooker: “I love that dude, man. I’ve been blessed, knock on wood, I’ve had some really really really good Safeties in my career…when you look at Hook, his instinct and where he ends up on the field, I’ve told him several times on certain… — Anthony Cover 1 (@Pro__Ant) November 11, 2026 When the Jaguars played in Nashville last season, Trevor Lawrence threw 2 touchdown passes against rookie safety Kevin Winston Jr. Today, while Winston won’t be safe himself, expect Lawrence to mostly go after Tony Adams. He was signed to a one-year flier this offseason after spending his first three NFL seasons with Robert Saleh’s New York Jets. With his experience under Saleh, the Titans shouldn’t be immediately busting coverages now that Hooker is gone. That said, Winston and Adams aren’t exactly a fearsome safety tandem. The prediction: Brenton Strange records his first 100-yard game Strange’s receiving prop is set at 35.5 yards on FanDuel. Prediction #2 Like Bates, new Jaguars defensive tackle Jordan Davis will be inactive today. The entire locker room will appreciate Liam Coen’s decision to put the players first. While we’ll have to wait a week for our first glimpse of Bates and Davis in black and teal, today will be Davon Godchaux’s first game as a Jaguar. The former New Orleans Saint is an immediate substitute for DaVon Hamilton as an early-down run-stuffer who can man two gaps at once. Don’t get me wrong — nobody will ever replace Ham — but even without him or Davis, Jacksonville should be well-equipped to slow Tennessee. Tony Pollard has been balling out for the Titans lately. He has 5 rushing touchdowns in the past two weeks! With that said, in the six weeks prior, he scored once while ranking sixth-worst in success rate (34.5%) and 12th-worst in explosive run rate (8.0%) among qualified running backs, per NFL Pro. Is the 29-year-old really going to keep up this recent spike in performance? The prediction: Jacksonville’s rushing defense gets back on track Pollard’s rushing prop is set at 58.5 yards on FanDuel. Prediction #3 I like Strange to have a good game today, partly because of the matchup, and partly because he’s due. The guy has 2 catches in consecutive games. Another Jaguar who’s been quiet is rookie receiver Josh Cameron. He notched a career-best game in Week 5 with 3 catches for 43 yards (and a negated kick return touchdown), but since then, the Baylor product has logged 1 catch for 6 yards. Despite the lack of receiving production, Cameron’s top three games this season by offensive snap rate have come in each of the past three weeks — because the dude is a killer in the run game. Cameron's not a high-end volume wide receiver yet but still a valuable player for the Jaguars. Their 13P basically becomes 13.5P because of his utility as a blocker. Underrated cog in JAX's rushing attack. https://t.co/BN3rvAQva1 pic.twitter.com/ujuQrOjURx — AJ Schulte (@AJSchulteFB) November 6, 2026 Even with Brian Thomas Jr. still in the fold, Cameron will continue seeing critical snaps thanks to his unique role in Coen’s offense. full_text: Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ snap counts in the 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Joshua Ezeudu, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Kenneth Walker, TE Noah Gray and TE Travis Kelce Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, NT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Nohl Williams, CB Mansoor Delane, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: N/A Inactive: QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), RB Kenneth Walker (groin), FB Ben VanSumeren, RB Jaydn Ott (hamstring), DT Peter Woods (neck), CB Melvin Smith Jr. and RT Jaylon Moore (ankle) The big takeaway: Ashton Gillotte is the front seven’s Swiss-Army knife As the season has worn on, defensive end Ashton Gillotte has become an increasingly important part of the defense. He started the season recovering from a plantar fascia injury, and now he’s one of the most versatile players in the defense’s front seven. He has played two-thirds of the defense’s snaps in each of the last three weeks; in Atlanta, he was on the field for 75% of the time the defense was. He didn’t start against the Falcons, but he racked up five tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss and a pass broken up. Pro Football Focus credited Gillotte with six pressures total and led all Chiefs defenders in “Stops” (4), tackles that constitute a failure for the offense. DE Ashton Gillotte is the Swiss-army knife of the Chiefs' front seven Inside pass rusher, off-ball linebacker, edge defender, always playing with his hair on fire pic.twitter.com/Tsj7Ro4Awm — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 16, 2026 He made a big impact while lining up in the B-gap 31 of the 52 times he was on the field; most of that time, he rushed the passer from the inside. He also lined up as an off-ball linebacker on two snaps, giving the Chiefs a unique run-defense look in their base 4-3 formation alongside linebackers Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill. The Offensive takeaway: Josh Downs plays just 10 snaps In his Chiefs debut, new receiver Josh Downs lined up for just 10 snaps and ran eight routes, totaling 51 yards and a touchdown over four catches. It was clear that Downs will be a key part of the passing game moving forward, so whose snaps are going to be reduced to make room for Downs in future weeks? Xavier Worthy (56 snaps) Rashee Rice (30 snaps) Cyrus Allen (22 snaps) Jalen Royals (19 snaps) Andrew Armstrong (17 snaps) Worthy is the easy answer here, because it’s incredible how little production comes out of leading the receiver room in snaps each week. In Atlanta, he was targeted three times, and none were completed. The Defensive takeaway: R Mason Thomas has empty box score Rookie edge rusher R Mason Thomas played 48 snaps in Atlanta, the second-most snaps in his career. However, Thomas did not register a quarterback pressure over the 39 pass-rush snaps; it’s the first time he was held without a pressure this season. Despite the Chiefs playing with a lead and giving Thomas plenty of opportunity to rush the passer, his impact was not felt. Kansas City generated plenty of pressure, but none came from Thomas, a recent trend: the rookie has only two pressures over the last three games. In the three games between Weeks 4-7, Thomas racked up 14 pressures — but hasn’t reached the same level of impact since. Offensive Snaps Defensive Snaps Special teams snaps
