title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs feasting on Dirty Bird
summary: For most of the first half, it looked like the Kansas City Chiefs were the better team, even if the offense on the field didn’t reflect that. Then, just before halftime, the Chiefs trotted Harrison Butker out to attempt a field goal — and he made it! Harrison Butker actually made a field goal. But […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) For most of the first half, it looked like the Kansas City Chiefs were the better team, even if the offense on the field didn’t reflect that. Then, just before halftime, the Chiefs trotted Harrison Butker out to attempt a field goal — and he made it! Harrison Butker actually made a field goal. But a flag was thrown on the play. An Atlanta Falcons player jumped offside. The extra five yards gave the Chiefs a first down. The very next play, quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw a dime to his brand-new target, Josh Downs, who brought in the pass for a touchdown. That was it; the rout was on. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs’ 35-13 victory over the Falcons. 1. The Chiefs are officially better than they were last season I say this a little tongue-in-cheek. We’ve known this team was better than their 2025 iteration pretty much from the jump. But it’s like they say, you are only as good as your record. And up until now, the Chiefs had not surpassed their disappointing 6-11 record from a year ago. But that was then, and this is now. With this week’s drubbing of the hapless Falcons, the Chiefs have amassed their seventh win of the season, ensuring that no matter what happens the rest of the way out, they’ve locked up a better record than last year. Now, the only question that remains is: how much better are they? A few games better? 11-6 better? 15-2? Only time will tell. 2. The Chiefs’ lack of a deep ball isn’t a Mahomes issue A lot has been said about the decline in the Chiefs’ air yards per attempt in recent years, including their modest 4.15 air yards per attempt over the last four games heading into Atlanta. Over the years, we’ve heard every speculated reason for why the Chiefs couldn’t seem to find success throwing the deep ball. Some said it was because we traded away Tyreek Hill. Some said it was because Mahomes had lost his ability to throw the ball 20+ yards accurately. Some blamed it on coaching and playcalling. Some said it was a deficit of talent at the receiving position. Some said teams adapted to take away the deep ball. Most said it was a combination of all four — but we now have definitive empirical evidence that rules Mahomes out of the equation. On Sunday, Mahomes completed six out of seven passes downfield. Mahomes never lost the ability to throw the ball deep — he just needed the pieces to fall back into place for it to make sense to air it out. Patrick Mahomes threw 2 deep TDs (20+ air yards) against the Falcons, his first game with multiple deep TDs since 2021. Mahomes had thrown just 1 deep TD since the start of 2025 entering Week 10. @KCvsATL | #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/WwjbciRIF6 — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) November 15, 2026 3. Josh Downs looks like everything we hoped he’d be We knew the Chiefs needed help at wide receiver. We knew that the Chiefs had their eyes set on trading for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . And when they pulled off the trade just before the deadline, we all crossed our fingers and prayed he was the missing piece to this passing attack. And while the jury is still out on whether the issues around this passing attack are fully solved, I think it’s fair to say Downs looks like everything we were hoping for. Sure, it’s a small sample size, and he’s not a superstar. But he’s a good route runner, with great hands, and a smart head on his shoulders. In short, he’s a pro. Something the Chiefs have been missing at wide receiver for the last couple of seasons. The only question now is, just how good is Josh Downs? It’s hard to say, especially when he’s had the likes of Anthony Richardson, Gardner Minshew, and Daniel Jones throwing him the football over the last four seasons. I think the jury is still out. Another thing that the jury is still out on is how much better this team is with Downs on it? Mahomes steps up and drops a dime to Josh Downs for a TD! KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dwTMy1qZYC — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 4. Emmett Johnson is the real deal Maybe we already knew this one before this game. But there is a difference between being the change-of-pace back and being the workhorse expected to put the offense on your shoulders and carry it downfield to the promised land. With starting running back Kenneth Walker sidelined with injury, the Chiefs rookie running back got his first chance to be the first man up in the backfield, and boy howdy, he did not disappoint. Fifth round rookie Emmett Johnson just had a breakout performance in his FIRST NFL start. 19 CAR, 93 RUSH YDS, 6 REC, 70 REC YDS, 2 REC TD vs Falcons. The OROY race is wide open. Could Johnson become a serious contender down the stretch? https://t.co/AVdhMhzgcq pic.twitter.com/SRJ2JRdjop — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 15, 2026 This Twitter post sells Johnson short. According to ESPN , Johnson finished the game with 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards, and two touchdowns. This kid is a star in the making. I don’t think there is any question that Johnson has been the best rookie running back in the NFL this season. It’s not surprising, considering he was fourth in the nation in rushing last season while playing at Nebraska. A lot will be made this week about the Chiefs rediscovering their deep ball. But none of the above happens without Johnson keeping the defense honest. We obviously want Kenneth Walker III back as soon as possible, but until then, we’ve got E-Money. 5. The Chiefs cannot afford to lose Trey Smith for an extended period of time With the turmoil at the Chiefs’ offensive tackle position this season, Kansas City has at least been able to rest on the fact that when left guard Kingsley Suamataia is not in head coach Andy Reid’s doghouse, the Chiefs have one of the better interior offensive lines in the NFL. So when right guard Trey Smith left the game with a concussion, the Chiefs had no choice but to put Mike Caliendo back in. Look at Caliendo on this play pic.twitter.com/GzpFCGFY5I — NlCKBOLTON (@NICKB0LTON) November 16, 2026 The results were less than inspiring.
author: Rocky Magaña

This was his seventh career game with at least five passing touchdowns, breaking a tie for the fourth-most such games in NFL history. Only Drew Brees (11), Tom Brady (nine) and Peyton Manning (nine) have more than Mahomes. George Karlaftis before the bye week: 0 sacks, 2 passes defended Since the bye week: 5.5 sacks, 8 passes defended — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 16, 2026 Through Week 5, four games and the bye, Karlaftis had no sacks, two tackles for loss and two passes defended (including an interception against the Miami Dolphins). Since then, Karlaftis has 5.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and eight passes defended. According to Chiefs Communications , prior to “Sunday Night Football” and “Monday Night Football,” Karlaftis has the second-most sacks and tackles for loss in the NFL since Week 6. George Karlaftis this year and J.J. Watt (2012) are the only DL with 10+ passes defended in the first nine games of a season since 2000 (Per @ChiefsPR ) — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 16, 2026 Karlaftis’ season has been defined by his ability to make a play in the pass game without sacking the quarterback. He leads the team in passes defended this year (10), joining former Houston Texans great J.J. Watt in his 2012 Defensive Player of the Year campaign as the only two defensive linemen to reach double digits in passes defended through nine games in a season since the turn of the century. However, since the team’s week off, Karlaftis has been as productive as any pass rusher in the NFL, on top of constantly getting in the way of quarterbacks’ throws. He has defended a pass in seven consecutive games and has tallied a sack in four of the last five weeks. With Kansas City’s secondary looking sound, Karlaftis and the rest of the Chiefs’ pass rush should keep getting chances to bring the quarterback to the ground, especially if the offense can keep playing with a lead.

title: 9 Winners and 3 Losers from the Chiefs’ win over the Falcons
summary: Your Kansas City Chiefs kept pace in the AFC race by outclassing the Atlanta Falcons from kickoff to the final play. Somehow, the game wasn’t even as close as the 35-13 score would indicate. The new-look, next-man-up Chiefs offense had its way with the Falcons defense on the ground and in the air. Meanwhile, the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Kansas City Chiefs kept pace in the AFC race by outclassing the Atlanta Falcons from kickoff to the final play. Somehow, the game wasn’t even as close as the 35-13 score would indicate. The new-look, next-man-up Chiefs offense had its way with the Falcons defense on the ground and in the air. Meanwhile, the Chiefs defense stifled a talented Atlanta offense, keeping them from sniffing the end zone until the fourth quarter. Here are a few who stood out on Sunday — more good than bad this time. 9 Winners Wide receiver Josh Downs: Any questions about why the Chiefs went out and traded for Josh Downs? Anyone? In limited snaps, No. 12 quickly became a favorite target for Patrick Mahomes. Downs caught 4 of 5 targets for 51 yards and a spectacular touchdown. Earning Mahomes’ trust for a back-shoulder throw in the end zone is a big deal. The way Downs helped open up the entire offense is even bigger. He also handled (and mishandled) punt returns in a really solid Chiefs debut. Running back Emmett Johnson: The Chiefs went out this offseason and brought in two #1 running backs. In his first career start, the rookie went off — 22 carries, 6 catches for 171 total yards and two receiving touchdowns. The unfortunate injury to Ken Walker should be healing well while he watches the kid dominate for another week if needed. Defensive ends George Karlaftis and Ashton Gillotte: These two picked up right where they left off last week. Both were too much for the Atlanta offensive line and made Michael Penix Jr.’s afternoon miserable. Karlaftis had 1.5 sacks and another batted pass, while Gillotte notched two tackles-for-loss a sack and a batted pass of his own. Steve Spagnuolo and Joe Cullen seem to be building a rotation of diverse skill sets on defense, getting production from these guys and solid play from Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Khyiris Tonga. Linebackers Drue Tranquill and Nick Bolton: Remarkably, the pass-rush success came while they held the NFL’s best running back to 71 yards on the afternoon. Substantial credit goes to the duo of Bolton and Tranquill, who combined for 18 total tackles (one for a loss). Their aggressive tackling helped contain Bijan Robinson and kept the Falcons offense from sustaining drives. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: It wasn’t just the numbers, although they were spectacular— 348/5/0. It was the confident downfield throws to a number of different targets. It was the stepping up in the pocket, the scrambles and the tight spirals. It was a vintage Patrick Mahomes game, the likes of which we haven’t seen in a while. He threw a touchdown after a penalty erased a Chiefs field goal. He threw a deep touchdown when the Falcons took away the short option he wanted. He gave his receivers a chance to make a play—and they delivered this week. Wide receivers Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong: Both young receivers hauled in their first NFL touchdown this week—39 yards for Allen, 43 for Armstrong. Cyrus Allen showed off his route running— using a double move to blow by the cornerback for a wide-open score. Andrew Armstrong made a great adjustment to a ridiculous throw by an improvising Patrick Mahomes. When the quarterback shows this much trust in his receivers, especially ones he hasn’t played with as much— the league is in trouble. Honorable mention : Rashee Rice, who caught a 50-yard bomb this week and led the team, bringing in 5/6 targets for a team-high 82 yards. 3 Losers Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: Not every receiver was able to feast on Sunday. Worthy caught exactly none of his three targets and seemed to get out-hustled on a successful Falcons onside kick. The offense worked well without a contribution from Worthy, which doesn’t bode well for his value going forward. The Chiefs’ depth chart: Injuries seem to be piling up— Kelce was in and out with an ankle, Trey Smith had a concussion, Jared Wiley hurt an ankle, and Creed Humphrey went out for a while after being poked in the eye. The Chiefs were already thin on offense with Ken Walker and Jaylon Moore out. When Mike Calliendo, Hunter Norzad, and Nate Carter are in the game, things don’t usually go this well. Special teams coach Dave Toub: On one hand, Harrison Butker didn’t miss a kick for once. On the other hand, the Chiefs’ special teams units still made the kinds of mistakes that led us to question their leadership. After cutting Nikko Remigio (likely the right move), Toub tried a few returners, including newly signed Josh Downs, who fumbled and recovered his first punt return. The coverage units missed more tackles than usual, and there were still costly penalties on special teams. This group feels like a bit of a mess. Note: Applying the labels “winners” or “losers” is not meant to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s just a simple way to grade their job performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.
author: Matt Stagner

title: Emmett Johnson proves a lot to Chiefs in 100-rushing yard game
summary: When news broke on Friday that the Kansas City Chiefs’ starting running back Kenneth Walker (groin) would be questionable for Sunday, there was some concern about the sudden injury and its affect on this game, a potentially tricky road spot. However, many in Chiefs Kingdom — including a passionate faction in Lincoln, Nebraska — turned […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) When news broke on Friday that the Kansas City Chiefs ’ starting running back Kenneth Walker (groin) would be questionable for Sunday, there was some concern about the sudden injury and its affect on this game, a potentially tricky road spot. However, many in Chiefs Kingdom — including a passionate faction in Lincoln, Nebraska — turned their attention to rookie running back Emmett Johnson. In Week 10, against the Atlanta Falcons , he made his first career start after Walker was ruled out, and he delivered on the anticipation for a heavy workload. Johnson started strong with 48 total yards on the opening drive and finished with 171 yards from scrimmage, looking every bit the part of a starting running back. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Johnson forced 10 missed tackles on the way to 100 rushing yards. He has the highest rate of missed tackles forced (46%) among running backs with at least 50 touches this year; his teammate, Walker, sits at third on that list. It speaks to the lack of drop-off from the Chiefs’ offense overall, especially the run game. Johnson had a special performance, and head coach Andy Reid made sure it was as memorable as possible by ensuring he passed the century mark. “Emmett, getting himself over 100 yards there with the help of the offensive line, I thought that was great,” Reid told reporters at the podium after the win. “We left him in there so we could get that, and he took care of business there.” Johnson’s big game happened despite multiple injuries up front. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was ruled out before the game, then right guard Trey Smith entered concussion protocol in the first quarter. Still, the offense found a rhythm by riding Johnson. The playmaking was evident to everyone involved. “I look at the players; the players have confidence in him, and the players are going to tell you the whole story,” Reid pointed out. “He’s doing the right things, as far as protections go, the cerebral part of the game, he’s taking care of that part. Knowing the plays, the direction of the plays, how to set the plays, all those things, he’s got — and then he has that skill that goes with it. He wants to be in there; he’s a great kid that way.” Johnson helped the Chiefs continue to build on the early lead he earned with a third-down catch and run into the end zone. By the fourth quarter, his attention had turned to ball security, helping Kansas City ice the game away. It’s a veteran detail for the rookie back, something Reid made sure to point out about Johnson. He talked about the Falcons forcing four turnovers in an upset of the San Francisco 49ers earlier this season, and how the rookie noted the performance. “Emmett, more so than any of us, was aware of that,” Reid said about the Falcons’ takeaway potential. “He saw it on tape. Keeping the ball high and tight becomes important; covering it in traffic, he did all of those little things. If you’re going to spin, keep it close to your body. All of the little fundamental things, I think he did a nice job with. We all have trust in him, he does that, he’s very coachable and a smart kid.” The trust that Johnson has built, from his teammates to the coaching staff, will only become more important as the season wears on. Walker won’t be 100% all the time, so even when he isn’t, the Chiefs still have a high-quality back to keep the offense on track.

(Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs turned in a dominant performance against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, but the 60 minutes of winning football saw multiple injury scares early and often. On Kansas City’s first offensive possession, tight end Travis Kelce — who has been playing through an ankle injury — came up limping after making a 23-yard catch. While fans are used to seeing Kelce rest a moment on the sideline before reentering the game, this time the future Hall of Fame member was seen returning to the locker room with training staff. After Kansas City’s drive ended with a touchdown, the CBS broadcast showed fellow tight end Jared Wiley being carted back to the locker room. Kelce was ruled questionable and later returned. Wiley was almost immediately ruled out . Later in the first half, right guard Trey Smith went into concussion protocol. Smith too was later ruled out . Speaking after the game, head coach Andy Reid confirmed the worst news for Wiley. “As far as the injuries go, Wiley,” said Reid, “it looks like he fractured his ankle. That’s not a good one. Trey is in the concussion protocol. So, we’ll see where that goes. Kelce left for a bit with a calf. He’s been battling this ankle. It’s all kind of part of it there. He got landed on it on that first catch and twisted it up a little bit.” Smith’s return to action will require clearance from the team’s independent neuroglial consultant per the league’s concussion rules. Center Creed Humphrey had played every snap in 2026 until Week 9’s blowout win over the New York Jets firmly entered garbage time. Humphey briefly left the field in pain against Atlanta after a hand to the face. “Creed got poked in the eye,” Reid confirmed. Humphrey returned to play on the Chiefs’ next drive, and Reid showed no concern about his availability going forward. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has battled a shoulder fracture the entire season. After breaking up a pass in the end zone, Delane was reported to be in pain and receiving aid from trainers. Delane missed Kansas City’s previous two games. Mansoor Delane is in pain on the Chiefs' bench. The trainers are heading his way. — Sam McDowell (@SamMcDowell11) November 15, 2026 Reid appeared confident that Delane avoided the worst case scenarios. “He landed on his back and kind of up in that shoulder area,” Reid remarked. “I think it sacred him more than anything. He’s going to be alright.” The Chiefs will welcome the Arizona Cardinals — now starting rookie quarterback Carson Beck — to Arrowhead Stadium in Week 11. With consecutive Thursday games against tough competition looming, we will see if the Chiefs are more conservative with injuries ahead of a short week. We will monitor the status of these players — and running back Kenneth Walker, who was sidelined late in the week with a groin injury — when Kansas City returns to the practice field on Thursday.

title: The Chiefs’ offense rediscovers the deep ball in Atlanta
summary: Leading into the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 10 bout with the Atlanta Falcons, quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ last deep-ball completion — a pass thrown 20 or more yards in the air — came in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders. The recipient of the throw was wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who dislocated his ankle on […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Leading into the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 10 bout with the Atlanta Falcons , quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ last deep-ball completion — a pass thrown 20 or more yards in the air — came in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders . The recipient of the throw was wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who dislocated his ankle on the play and was placed on the Reserve/Injured list. Between that play and Week 10, Mahomes completed none of his five downfield attempts. Poetically, the midseason trade for wide receiver Josh Downs was followed by Mahomes’ most prolific game of the year, with plenty of throws down the field. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Mahomes completed three of six passes 20 or more yards downfield — each to a familiar face in the receiving corps. Rookie Cyrus Allen got open on a double-move down the left sideline for a 39-yard touchdown Veteran Rashee Rice came down with a 50-yard catch on a post route in traffic Training-camp standout Andrew Armstrong hauled in a long bomb in the end zone from a scrambling Mahomes It was Mahomes’ first game with multiple deep-pass touchdowns since 2021. It felt like his confidence throwing the long ball started with intermediate passes — including an 18-yard strike to Downs at the front pylon of the end zone. The back-shoulder touchdown is a rare sight in the Chiefs’ offense, but clearly, Downs has already earned enough respect from Mahomes to step up in the pocket and rifle the attempt there. After that pass put the Chiefs up 14-6, Mahomes kept challenging Atlanta’s coverage downfield and didn’t stop until the team was coasting to a late-fourth-quarter victory; he even threw a bomb to tight end Jake Briningstool into the end zone at one point. Downs may not be the target on these deep targets all the time, but it feels as if Mahomes needed a player like Downs to help establish a rhythm — and the rest of the receivers needed a player like Downs to relieve the pressure snap to snap.

title: Chargers-Ravens Game Preview: Harbaugh, Minter reunite under the primetime lights
summary: The Chargers and Ravens face off this week on Monday Night Football after eight weeks of failed expectations. Jim Harbaugh was supposed to have the Chargers gearing up for a Super Bowl run this season. It’s year three of his tenure and back-to-back 11-win seasons were seemingly going to be the stepping stones to finally […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (83) fends off Arizona Cardinals linebacker Jack Gibbens (50) during the NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 13, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers and Ravens face off this week on Monday Night Football after eight weeks of failed expectations. Jim Harbaugh was supposed to have the Chargers gearing up for a Super Bowl run this season. It’s year three of his tenure and back-to-back 11-win seasons were seemingly going to be the stepping stones to finally getting Justin Herbert passed the wild card round. Now, they’re 0-8 and the season is already far past being “lost.” The 2027 season, and maybe even 2028, is now currently viewed as their next opportunity to be competitive. That’s one heck of a wrench thrown into the plans for the team that entered 2026 with the sixth-best Super Bowl odds. As for Minter and the Ravens, the young defensive genius was supposed to come in and fix the other side of the ball so Lamar Jackson did not have to be Superman each week and outscore the opposing offense all by himself. Well, Jackson has only been healthy for about two-thirds of the season and now they’re down to a brand new quarterback who they just traded on top of being the 25th-ranked scoring defense. That’s a bit of a far-cry from his two top-10 units with the Bolts. Even with all the negatives surrounding these teams, Monday night should still be entertaining (in the good OR bad way). The connections and storylines hold well here, even if the final viewership numbers don’t. With all that said, let’s go ahead and dive in to the three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Monday night. 1.) Is this the best chance for the Chargers to get their first win? The Chargers have come close on several occasions this year in getting their first win of the season, but ultimately couldn’t capitalize on anything that may have went their way through the first three quarters. This week MAY be different as they are on the road to face a 4-5 Ravens team that is now starting their fourth different quarterback of the year in Jacoby Brissett. Injuries have sidelined both Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano started in Week Nine, but it went about as bad as you’d expect. Brissett is a career backup who got some starting time with the Cardinals last year and to begin this year, but his momentum from 2025 did not carry over into this season. That led to him ultimately being dealt. Baltimore’s defense under Minter has not been great, either. They’re middle of the pack in total defense (15th), but rank 23rd in defending the pass (229.8) and 25th in points allowed (26.2). All of this combines to become the Chargers’ best chance at winning a game before they face the Jets in Week 11. After that, the best remaining matchups on the schedule are the Bucs (3-6), Raiders (4-5), and Dolphins (1-7). Do the Chargers even get to four wins this year if they lose to the Ravens? Even three? Yikes! 2.) Will Minter get the best of Mike McDaniel again? The Chargers narrowly beat the Dolphins in 2025 by a score for 29-27. Minter’s defense was gashed by running back De’Von Achane for a pair of touchdowns, but they did intercept Tua Tagovailoa three times and held him to just 205 yards through the air. With that experience under his belt, will he execute a similar strategy to put Justin Herbert in the same kind of hell? Herbert has been throwing plenty of interceptions already this year so you’ve got to think Minter is expecting at least one takeaway, but could he have key to unlocking an even bigger turnover party for his current defense? The Ravens pass rush is fine enough this year with 17 sacks in nine games. They’re led by Tavious Robinson and Mike Green, both of whom have 3.5 QB takedowns. Trey Hendrickson, the team’s big offseason addition, only has two in seven games played. As much as this may tell us Herbert could have a better day in the pocket, the Chargers offensive line is coming off a Texans loss that saw them allow a career-high eight sacks on their quarterback. Chances are it’s not going to be an easy time given the intimidating atmosphere in a loud venue fill of black and purple. 3.) Will offensive reinforcements make a difference? I basically used this storyline in last week’s game preview, but of course the players I highlighted were once again ruled out after I had published. Well, we’re going back to that well as the likes of Kayode Awosika and David Njoku were listed as questionable this week as opposed to being ruled out in the final injury report. It’s been a long time since either played and both are going to be welcomed additions around Justin Herbert. Awosika will replace rookie Logan Taylor at left guard and immediately raise the floor of the whole unit. Taylor has played admirably, but Awosika was playing legitimately good football before his injury. Njoku, on the other hand, was one of Herbert’s top targets through the first two games of the year against the Cardinals and Raiders. Prior to his injury, he was top two on the team in both receptions and yards (bad drop-into-interception, aside). If both are active and back to 100 percent Monday night, then I’ll have hopes for one of the best offensive outputs of the year. If they don’t, well it’s likely to be another go-round on this awful carousel ride called the 2026 season.

title: Raiders-Seahawks: 17 Things we learned
summary: Fernando Mendoza is going to be a good NFL Player. But there are going to lumps and predictably those lumps came Sunday in his starting debut. After scoring on their first two drives, Mendoza and the Raiders stalled as the stout Seattle Seahawks defense adjusted. The defending Super Bowl champions took over in the second […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza is going to be a good NFL Player. But there are going to lumps and predictably those lumps came Sunday in his starting debut. After scoring on their first two drives, Mendoza and the Raiders stalled as the stout Seattle Seahawks defense adjusted. The defending Super Bowl champions took over in the second half turning a 10-7 halftime deficit into a 21-13 victory, in a game that wasn’t as close as the score indicated. Now, the Raiders are 4-6 and are in a big hole in the AFC as they have lost six of their past seven games after starting the season 3-0. The Raiders have not beaten a team with a winning record and they play at the Denver Broncos and the Cleveland Browns, both who have winning record, in the next two weeks. The Raiders are 1-4 at home. Here are some key aspects of the game: Mendoza’s day: It started well as Mendoza scored on the Raiders’ first drive and then led them to a field goal on the second drive. Then the Raiders stalled. The Seahawks had the Raiders in a blender in the second half as went three and out on five straight drives. Mendoza ended up going 17 of 29 for 143 yards. He was poised and showed accuracy early. He was sacked six times and hit a lot. But he hung in there. Of course, the mature Mendoza said all the right things after the game and he put the failures on himself. He will be fine. Ugly streak over, but defense still lacking: The Raiders’ defense ended their six-game streak of allowing, at least, 30 points. But it still wasn’t a good outing. Seattle backup quarterback Drew Lock made some big plays and Seattle ran for 150 yards. Seattle was sloppy on offense, but still dominated when it had to. Brutal second half: The Raiders led 10-7 at the half and got the ball to start the second half. They were in good shape. Well, they should have been. The Seahawks dominated on both sides of the ball in the second half. The Raiders had 27 yards of offense in the second half and that included a 38-yard pass play from Mendoza to running back Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders didn’t get their first first down of the second half until there was less than four minutes left in the game. Missing Bowers: Raiders’ star tight end Brock Bowers hurt his ankle early. He tried to play through it, but in the second quarter he left the game for good. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak had no update on Bowers’ injury after the game. it will clearly be a focal point of this week as the Raiders prepare to play Denver. Time of possession: The Raiders went into the game with the fourth worst time-of-possession percentage in the league. They lost that battle again in Week 10, but it wasn’t awful. Seattle had the ball for 31:41 and the Raiders had it for 28:19. Season slipping away: The Raiders’ 3-0 start seems like ages ago. They have lost six of their past seven games and are now two games under .500, erasing that great start to the Kubiak era. Run game brutal again: Another week, another meager showing by the Raiders’ running game. Las Vegas had 65 yards rushing and Mendoza had 22 of those yards. Jeanty struggled again with just 18 yards on nine carries. Rookie Mike Washington had 23 yards Washington had 23 yards on eight carries. It’s just not there. Crosby has a big day: Raiders’ star defensive end Maxx Crosby continued his hot play. He had four tackles for loss and has had, at least, one for five straight games. He’s had a sack in three straight games and has 5.5 on the season. No penalties: The officials let them play Sunday. There weretwo penalties called all game, both on Seattle. No penalties and still Las Vegas wasn’t lose to winning this game. Two turnvoers: The Raiders had two turnovers for the second week in a row. Bad third quarter: The Raiders had -minus two offensive yards on their first three series of the second half. They punted on all three drives. Seattle thin in trenches: The Seahawks entered the game with left guard Quenton Nelson and left tackle Charles Cross on offense and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams on defense. During the game, they lost right tackle Abe Lucas and defensive tackle Jarran Reed. What a start: The Raiders forced Drew Lock into a lost fumble on the second play of the game. Mendoza took his first snap as a starter in Seattle territory and the Mendoza ran it for a 10-yard touchdown run on third and goal to take a 7-0 lead. Las Vegas couldn’t have asked for a better start. Stokes hurt: Cornerback Eric Stokes appeared to hurt his hand in the third quarter, He was replaced by rookie Jermod McCoy. Stokes returned in the third quarter. Masses starts: The revolving door at an outside cornerback spot continued as fifth-round pick Zeke Masses started over Darien Porter and Jermod McCoy. It was Masses’ first start since Week 5 and his fifth start of the season. Masses struggled in the third quarter and was replaced by previous starter, Darien Porter. Four tight ends: The Raiders elevated tight end Carter Runyon from the practice squad for the game and he joined Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas on the game-day roster. Fan takeover: This is nothing new, but their were many, many Seahawks fans at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday. Seattle fans travel week and they showed up in Las Vegas. This was the Seahawks’ first regular-season game in Las Vegas.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 10 loss to the Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Miami Dolphins were extremely shorthanded heading into their Week 10 road-trip against the Indianapolis Colts. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a lingering groin issue. Stud center Aaron Brewer missed Sunday’s tilt due a concussion he suffered in last week’s loss to the Detroit Lions. Defensive […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs with the ball against the Miami Dolphins during an NFL football game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins were extremely shorthanded heading into their Week 10 road-trip against the Indianapolis Colts. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a lingering groin issue. Stud center Aaron Brewer missed Sunday’s tilt due a concussion he suffered in last week’s loss to the Detroit Lions. Defensive leader Zach Sieler tore his biceps in that same loss — forcing him to not only miss Miami’s game against Indianapolis, but the rest of the 2026 season as well. Well, as we all know, adversity is opportunity . The Dolphins — while starting rookie quarterback Kyle McCord — nearly overcame all of that adversity to upset their foes on Sunday. Instead, despite a spirited effort from Jeff Hafley’s squad, Miami lost by two-points against Indianapolis, dropping their record to 1-8 on the year after falling by a score of 24-22. GOOD Miami’s rookie defensive backs shine In a season where finding bright spots has sometimes felt like searching for a needle in a haystack, seeing two young players make game-changing defensive plays for Miami on Sunday was encouraging. Rookie safety Michael Taaffe and rookie cornerback Chris Johnson each came away with an interception of Colts’ quarterback Daniel Jones. Taaffe got things started with an interception with 10:30 left in the second quarter — giving Miami’s defense a much-needed takeaway while the Colts were driving for points. It was Taaffe’s third interception on the season. Not bad for a 5th round pick! But it was Johnson who provided the highlight of the afternoon. Miami’s 1st round rookie cornerback intercepted Jones with 8:52 left in the 3rd-quarter and returned the ball 59 yards for a dazzling touchdown — giving Miami a big lift and injecting some life into a game that was quickly getting away from the South Florida squad. Obviously, one game doesn’t make a career, but Taaffe and Johnson have been playing solid football for the Dolphins all season long. There hasn’t been a whole lot to celebrate in Miami this year, but seeing two rookies stepping up when their team needs them is part of the fuel that keeps the fires of hope burning as Dolphins fans look towards a brighter future. Now, if only the rest of the defense could figure out how to stop somebody… BAD Dolphins gashed on the ground by Colts On Sunday, Indianapolis ran the football 34 times for 172 yards, averaging a whopping 5.1 yards per carry. The Colts didn’t need to get particularly creative. They didn’t need to rely on some elaborate offensive scheme or trick plays. They lined up, handed the football to their running backs Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan, and repeatedly found themselves moving the chains. The Indianapolis rushing attack consistently found room to operate, putting Miami’s defense on their heels and making life difficult for the Dolphins throughout the afternoon, despite the fact that Miami’s defense only gave up 104 yards passing. When an opposing offense can consistently pick up five yards every time it hands the ball off, you’re eventually going to run out of opportunities to get off the field. The Dolphins have plenty of things to figure out defensively, but stopping the run needs to be near the top of that list — especially when a date with Josh Allen, James Cook and the Buffalo Bills is circled on the calendar for next Sunday. UGLY Zane Gonzalez misses two field goals and an extra-point try in a two-point loss When the Dolphins gave kicker Riley Patterson his walking papers on October 20th so they could sign Zane Gonzalez to take over kicking duties for the team, fans were encouraged by the move. Fast forward four games and that warm and fuzzy feeling has vanished in a hurry. On Sunday, Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point try. That’s 7 points Gonzalez was unable to put on the board for a Dolphins team desperate for them. Reminder: Miami lost Sunday’s game by two points. Gonzalez’s first missed opportunity came on a 47-yard attempt in the first quarter. Later, after Miami had clawed their way back into the game, he missed the extra point try following Chris Johnson’s spectacular interception return for a touchdown. However, Miami’s kicker saved his most heart-breaking moment for the fourth quarter when he missed a long try that would have given the Dolphins the lead in a tight, back-and-forth contest. As I gaze into my crystal ball, I predict the Dolphins to look elsewhere for a place kicker in very short order. ___ The Dolphins, with their backs against the wall, played a close game against the Colts on Sunday. Alas, they fell short — dropping the team’s record to 1-8 on the year. Were you impressed with quarterback Kyle McCord’s first start? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up .

title: Miami Dolphins news: Recapping Dolphins Week 10 loss to Colts
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, falling 24-22 and dropping to 1-8 in 2026. The game featured Miami starting a quarterback in his NFL debut, a shuffle among the defensive tackles due to injuries, an All-Pro center dealing with a conucssion, and a starting wide receiver missing the game due to […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, falling 24-22 and dropping to 1-8 in 2026. The game featured Miami starting a quarterback in his NFL debut, a shuffle among the defensive tackles due to injuries, an All-Pro center dealing with a conucssion, and a starting wide receiver missing the game due to injury. Yet, none of those were the reason behind Miami’s two-point loss. Football is a team sport, and there are always moments on offense and defense that could have been executed better. The Dolphins’ offense gave up a defensive touchdown on a sack fumble – not ideal. The defense could have been tougher against the run, stopping Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan from leading the team to over 170 yards on the ground. But, even with those issues, Miami was within two points of pulling off the upset win. Miami did enough to win on offense and defense. They fell apart on special teams, specifically with placekicking. Kicker Zane Gonzalez missed a 47-yard field goal in the first quarter. After connecting on a 53-yard kick, he missed an extra point in the third quarter. He also missed a 51-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Miami lost seven points on three kicks from Gonzalez. Even the extra point would have changed things; a converted extra point in the third quarter could have let Miami kick a tying extra point in the fourth quarter instead of attempting a failed two-point conversion. Maybe it is too harsh to blame the loss on a single player, but Gonzalez missed kicks Miami had to have, and this is not the first misses he has had recently. Gonzalez has struggled since joining the Dolphins, first on the practice squad, then being promoted to the active roster for Sunday. In four games, he is 6-for-10 on field goal attempts and 6-for-7 on extra points. Gonzalez has also struggled on kickoffs, leading Miami to move to punter Bradley Pinion to handle those responsibilities. Miami should have come out of Indianapolis with a win. It was there for the taking. They just could not connect on the kicks that would have changed the result. The kicking woes were among the top talking points around the web following the game. title: Dolphins vs. Colts final score, immediate reactions: Kyle McCord plays well as special teams fail Miami
summary: The Miami Dolphins faced the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, with starting quarterback Kyle McCord in his NFL debut after an injury to Malik Willis. A game featuring two teams in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, it felt like that at times. Neither team executed a complete game, but in […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Indianapolis Colts during an NFL football game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins faced the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, with starting quarterback Kyle McCord in his NFL debut after an injury to Malik Willis. A game featuring two teams in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, it felt like that at times. Neither team executed a complete game, but in the end, the Colts held on to squeak out the win. The Dolphins fell to 1-8 with the loss to the Colts. They had chances to win this game, but they lost after three kicks failed to put points on the board. The game was put on the shoulders of a young quarterback, and he responded. The offense moved the ball well enough to win the game. The defense shut down the Colts’ offense, especially in the second half. The Dolphins should be walking out of Indianapolis with a win. In the end, the special teams failed Miami. In the long run, this game could prove important to the Dolphins as they look toward the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami falling to 1-8 keeps them in contention for the first-overall pick and pushes the Colts further away from claiming it. Even better, the Colts’ pick is owned by the New York Jets after a trade last year. Not allowing an AFC East division rival to jump them in the draft order could be a way to find a silver lining on an ugly black cloud of a day. I’m trying to find the positive in what should have been a Miami win but now goes down as yet another loss. Final Score Dolphins 22 – 24 Colts Immediate Reactions Snap Winners and Losers Winners Malik Washington, wide receiver Washington had himself a day. The highlight will be his 34-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Tolbert on a double-pass play, but he was all over the offense on Sunday. He had three catches for 50 yards, plus returned four punts for 36 yards. Jordyn Brooks, linebacker Brooks was a wrecking ball throughout the game. He was just everywhere – in the backfield, shutting down runs at the line of scrimmage, breaking up passes in coverage. He was a force throughout the game. He led the game with nine tackles, had a pass defensed, and a forced fumble. It was a great day for Miami’s All-Pro linebacker. Ollie Gordon II, running back Miami’s offense is built to run the ball, and Gordon was not afraid to take carry after carry, despite the Colts stacking the box and daring Miami to find a way to run. Gordon had to grind out some of his runs, but in the end he tallied 20 carries for 76 yards along with four receptions for 39 yards. Kyle McCord, quarterback McCord spent his entire rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad, then joined the Green Bay Packers for training camp this year. Miami traded for him at the end of the preseason, and he made his NFL debut in this game as the starting quarterback. The game never felt too big for McCord. Some plays looked like a young player trying to force something, but overall, McCord was solid all game and kept the Dolphins in the game. He finished the game 17-for-32 for 209 yards and a 73.6 passer rating. He also ran twice for four yards and a touchdown. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred Zane Gonzalez, kicker I think there is a rule that someone from the special teams unit has to appear in the losers list this year. Gonzalez lands here after missing a 47-yard field goal attempt in the first quarter. Miami’s defense is playing hard to take some of the stress off a quarterback making his first career start. The offense did enough to move the ball down into Colts territory. Gonzalez just booted the ball left. He responded in the second half with a 53-yard field goal, but then missed an extra point and another field goal later in the game. Miami has to have better from their kicking game. Miami lost this game by two points. Gonzalez missed seven points’ worth of kicks. Other thoughts Why does Jaylen Wright have no space on any handoff? It seems like every time Wright is in the backfield and takes a handoff, he gets hit almost immediately. The same isn’t true of Gordon’s rushing attempts. It might be confirmation bias, and there is space on some of his runs, but it really does seem that Wright just cannot buy the space he needs to even try to make a move or get up to speed. Disaster strikes to open second half Miami opened the second half with the ball. On the kickoff return, safety Julius Wood was called for an illegal block, backing Miami up to their own 15-yard line. On Miami’s first play, cornerback Justin Walley’s blitz got to McCord’s blindside, stripped him as he tried to throw, and the Colts fell on the ball in the end zone. Miami had a chance to answer the Colts and tied up the game to open the half, but everything went wrong, and suddenly the Dolphins were down two touchdowns. Miami has to do something about special teams The Dolphins are a team still working through their growth and development as a rebuilding team. That is true in every aspect of the game, but that is no excuse for some of the issues on special teams. Even if some tackling issues or lane assignments are due to younger players, the miscues in the kicking game are inexcusable. I know I already listed Gonzalez above, but this is more about the unit as a whole. The Dolphins cannot afford to give up big gains, get flagged for holding or illegal blocks on returns, or miss kicks that take points off the board. Miami has to fix special teams, now.

summary: The Miami Dolphins are back on the field today, heading north to Indiana to face the Indianapolis Colts. Both teams are in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and both have made major roster changes over the past week. The Colts made several trades ahead of the deadline this past Tuesday, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins takes the field to face the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are back on the field today, heading north to Indiana to face the Indianapolis Colts. Both teams are in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and both have made major roster changes over the past week. The Colts made several trades ahead of the deadline this past Tuesday, sending veteran players around the league and receiving draft picks in exchange. The Dolphins stood pat at the deadline, but saw quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler, both starters and captains, land on injured reserve. Willis has a groin injury that is expected to keep him out for a few weeks, though season-ending surgery has not been completely ruled out. Sieler ruptured his biceps muscle during the team’s Week 9 game against the Detroit Lions, played through the injury for the rest of the contest, but will now require several months of rehab following surgery. Miami enters today with a 1-7 record and is in position to claim the third-overall spot in the 2027 Draft. The Colts are2-7 and in the fourth position, though they do not hold their pick after trading it to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 and in the top spot for the spring’s college prospect selection process while the 1-7 Tennessee Titans are in the second spot. How will Sunday’s game play out? Both teams have to adjust to the recent roster changes. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook seem to think the Colts are in a better position to pull off those adjustments and come away with the victory this afternoon. Phins up! Dive into game day on the SB Nation app! Celebrate every score and talk through every twist and turn with fellow Dolphins fans in real time. Join the live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly explore communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Dolphins at Colts (-3.5) This game feels like a matchup between a team that embraced a complete roster rebuild heading into 2026 and a team surprised to have been forced into a rebuild during 2026. Miami knew who they were entering the season as: stripping their roster down, filling it with younger players, and accepting that this season might be tough, but positioning themselves for future success. The Colts came into 2026 looking to compete in the AFC South; after back-to-back 8-9 seasons, Indianapolis was expecting to take a step forward. Instead, everything seems to have gone wrong for the Colts. That all said, Indianapolis now welcomes a Dolphins team with a first-year quarterback making his NFL debut after being a sixth-round pick in 2025 by the Philadelphia Eagles but spending the entire season on the practice squad. There are a lot of obstacles for the Dolphins in this game, and it feels like the Colts will be able to cover the 3.5 points – though it may end up closer than people think if Miami can get their running game established early. Prop Bets Ollie Gordon II rushing yards: 72.5 Over: -113 Under: -113 Miami’s offensive system this year was built around the run – first with De’Von Achane and now with Ollie Gordon II serving as the feature back. Gordon is only averaging 57.9 yards per game, but that includes Week 1 with no carries and Week 2 with three attempts for seven yards. Since becoming the starter in Week 4, Gordon is averaging 83 yards per game, which would be seventh in the league. Miami, with a first-time starting quarterback under center today, will rely on Gordon and the running game. The Colts will throw everything they can to stop the rushing attack, but Miami will have to commit to it and find ways to create space for Gordon. He should be able to top 72.5 yards. Kyle McCord passing touchdowns: 0.5 Over : -188 Under: +142 I like the +142 you could get with the under, but one passing touchdown seems plausible, especially if the Colts stack the box to try to stop Gordon. Then again, the Dolphins didn’t score a single touchdown last week against the Lions, so Miami could be held without a passing touchdown this week. I still lean toward the Dolphins finding a way to get McCord his first touchdown pass and build his confidence as the starter. Caleb Douglas receiving yards: 42.5 Over: -113 Under: -113 Douglas is averaging 15.6 yards per reception in his rookie season. If he sticks to that average, the question is whether he will get three receptions. If the Colts are stacking the box to stop Gordon and the running game, McCord should be able to find some space to get the ball to Douglas. I will take the over here, thinking it is a solid but not spectacular day for Douglas. Chop Robinson to record a sack Yes: +164 Daniel Jones is tied for the fifth-most sacks taken this year (we will ignore that he is tied with Malik Willis). He has been pulled down 24 times. The Dolphins defense seemed to break out last week against Detroit, and they know they will have to carry the game again this week, with a backup quarterback making not just his first NFL start, but his first regular-season appearance. Robinson should set the tone and get after Jones early and often. He cannot sell out and give up on trying to contain the Colts rushing attack, but he has to make an impression and there is no better way than getting an early sack. I will take the Yes here. title: Vikes Views: Sunday King: Week 10 – Vikings at Packers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings strolled into Green Bay and destroyed the Packers, 30-10. It was another dominant performance by the Viking defense, so much so it’s hard not to pick nearly every player in the front 7. The Vikings offense looked much better under Kirk Cousins despite missing T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison. A win is […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jalen Redmond #61 of the Minnesota Vikings sacks Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings strolled into Green Bay and destroyed the Packers, 30-10. It was another dominant performance by the Viking defense, so much so it’s hard not to pick nearly every player in the front 7. The Vikings offense looked much better under Kirk Cousins despite missing T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison. A win is always fun, a dismantling of Green Bay in Wisconsin is electrifying. Let’s take a look at Sunday’s best Vikings. Levi Drake Rodriguez The defensive front was overwhelming on Sunday. Levi led the team with 2 sacks and 4 hits on Jordan Love. Dallas Turner Turner showed off his versatile skill set on Sunday. He was in the backfield all day wreaking havoc. He recorded a sack on a bull rush straight through to Jordan Love and recovered the errant snap Love launched in the third quarter. Turner nearly added an interception as well, diving in coverage to break up a pass. Turner has become exactly the player the Vikings hoped they were getting when they drafted him in 2024. Eric Wilson Wilson was the signal caller (green dot) Sunday, filling the shoes of Blake Cashman. He also led the team with 7 tackles, including a sack of his own. Andrew Van Ginkel Van Ginkel made an immediate impact on the Packers’ 2nd offensive play of the game. He just stole the ball from TE Mark Redman. After the Vikings started with a three and out, he stepped up and gave them the ball back on the Green Bay 10. The Vikings were unable to punch it in, but it started them off on the right foot. Kirk Cousins Cousins wasn’t perfect on Sunday, but it was the best quarterbacked game by the Vikings this season. He made the throws neither of the previous quarterbacks could. The touchdown pass to Myles Price was a reprieve from the QB incompetence we’ve endured as fans. There’s no guarantee it will continue, but it was fun to enjoy yesterday. Honorable Mentions: Nolan Teasley – I originally had Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on my list, but the system only allows me six voting options. Trading for a starting QB mid-year is a bold move and it paid immediate dividends on Sunday. Jakobe Thomas – Thomas played his first game on Sunday. He took advantage of his window on special teams with a beautiful hit on the Packers kick returner to force a fumble. Harrison Smith, Elijah Williams, Kyle Van Noy, Jalen Redmond – they all had impact plays and were part of an elite defensive performance. There were too many to list. The Vikings have now beaten Green Bay twice this season by a combined score of 69-32.

(Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The stage has been set for a huge matchup on Sunday Night Football this week, and it will happen at about 7,000 feet above sea level in Mexico City, as the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers will be meeting south of the border at Estadio Banorte as the NFL’s International Series concludes for 2026. As the betting lines open for this heavyweight clash, the Vikings are starting the week as a slight underdog for what is, at least nominally, a San Francisco home game. Skol! Chat live throughout the game Enjoy fewer ads Jump easily between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings have started as a three-point underdog to the Niners. The over/under for this one has started at 46.5 points. The Vikings snapped their two-game losing streak this past Sunday at Lambeau Field, pasting the Green Bay Packers by a score of 30-10 to complete a sweep of the Border Battle for the 2026 season. The defense was dominant, sacking Jordan Love eight times and forcing three of the four turnovers committed by the Packers (the fourth came on special teams). But the big story was the Vikings’ offense and the return of Kirk Cousins, whom the Vikings acquired at the trade deadline on Tuesday, arrived in Minnesota on Wednesday, and started on Sunday, making him the first player since at least 1950 to start games at quarterback for different teams in consecutive weeks. Cousins’ last start for his former team, the Las Vegas Raiders, came against these same 49ers, who come into this game tied for the league’s best record at 8-1. Like the Vikings, the Niners got their season off to a 6-0 start before seeing their first loss, a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. After the bye, they came back to beat Cousins and the Raiders by a score of 38-17, and this past Sunday they had a back-and-forth battle with the Dallas Cowboys that saw them eventually emerge with a 46-40 victory at Jerryworld. Brock Purdy is on the short list of potential MVP candidates for this season, and he showed why against the Cowboys, completing 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, two of which came on long passes to Christian McCaffrey, who had 161 receiving yards on the day. This matchup looks to be another matchup of a very strong offense facing off against Brian Flores’ #1 defensive squad. Unlike what we saw when the Vikings faced the Bills on Monday Night, however, now it appears that the Vikings have the offense to actually allow their defense to have a bit of a rest and not allow them to get worn down late in the game. For the fourth consecutive week, the Vikings will go into a game as an underdog, ladies and gentlemen. What do you think about that? Let us know in the comments!

The Vikings have the tie-breaker over the Bears and the Lions have the tie-breaker over the Vikings. Kirk Cousins provided some key throws and generally provided competent quarterback play, allowing the Vikings to score 30 points. Meanwhile, the defense terrorized Jordan Love most of the game, generating 8 sacks and three turnovers. Special teams produced a fourth turnover. Overall, it was a bit of a statement game for the Vikings with Cousins now at the helm and the defense continuing to play absolutely lights out. Stock Up Kirk Cousins. It wasn’t an outstanding stat line from Cousins in his first start since the Vikings traded for him, but it was more than competent with some key passes that turned into touchdowns while allowing the Vikings to win the time of possession battle with intelligent play despite just two full practices since arriving in Minnesota. He finished 21/31 for 207 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, a 94.4 passer rating and a 74.1 QBR. His game highlights below. Myles Price. He had 4 receptions on 4 targets for 49 yards and the Vikings first touchdown on 3rd and 23. Great play to keep his balance and get into the end zone. Best performance by a WR3 this season and worthy of a more permanent role. The Entire Defensive Front Seven Including Backups. You wouldn’t know that Blake Cashman missed this game- which hasn’t been the case in the past- or Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins. They produced 8 sacks on 27 quarterback pressures and 2 turnovers while allowing just 3.3 yards per rush attempt. Levi Drake-Rodriquez, Dallas Turner, Jalen Redmond, Andrew Van Ginkel, Caleb Banks (yes Caleb Banks), Elijah Williams, Domonique Orange, Kyle Van Noy, Ivan Pace Jr., Eric Wilson, and Jake Golday. It’s great to see the backups getting worked in and doing well, which is encouraging should there be injuries and for future seasons. Tai Felton. He had 3 receptions on 5 targets for 33 yards including an impressive back shoulder grab on 3rd and 15 that setup the Vikings’ second touchdown. Justin Jefferson. The return of Kirk Cousins was music to the ears of Jefferson, who had 9 receptions on 13 targets for 74 yards. Still below his career game average, but his most productive game in the last four. Bret Thorson. He’s had a couple nice games punting the ball lately. He had three against the Packers, two of which were inside the 20 including a 64-yarder. He’s also done a great job as holder. Will Reichard. He is back to his perfect self, making all three field goal attempts and all three extra points. Joe Huber. He had a clean sheet in pass protection and a good preliminary PFF run blocking grade. Making a strong case to be a starter next year as well. Blake Brandel. He’s allowed just one hurry with a near elite preliminary grade as a run blocker. He’s proving to be very solid at center. Gavin Bartholomew. He did well in relief of T.J. Hockenson with 3 receptions on 4 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown (his first). Gavin Bartholomew's first NFL TD makes it a three-score game! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LlozbGAGyJ — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Solid IPO Jakobe Thomas. He got his first reps of the season on special teams against the Packers and forced a fumble which Jake Golday recovered and put the game out of reach. He gave up his #8 free of charge for Kirk Cousins, and he was rewarded with this awesome play today!! Jakobe Thomas well done young man #SKOL pic.twitter.com/L3hXk8bgaW — Vince Wright (@thebigsmooth1) November 15, 2026 Stock Down Jay Ward. He had a personal foul early in the game on special teams after some extracurricular activity that wasn’t smart. Can’t give away cheap yards like that, especially on the road. Buy The Minnesota Vikings as legitimate Super Bowl contenders with Cousins at quarterback and perhaps the most dominant defense in recent years. Sell It being automatic that the Vikings will have a deep playoff run. There’s still a lot of football left to play and key games against the 49ers next week in Mexico, the Lions, and Bears. The Vikings will need to stay healthy and keep their foot on the gas from now until February. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Classic Cousins, Dominant Defense Lead Way as Vikings Thrash Packers
summary: For the first eight games of their 2026 season, the Minnesota Vikings’ offense struggled to put points on the board while their defense made life miserable for offenses around the NFL. On Sunday afternoon at Lambeau Field, it appears that the tide might be turning for the Minnesota offense, thanks to the addition of one […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first eight games of their 2026 season, the Minnesota Vikings’ offense struggled to put points on the board while their defense made life miserable for offenses around the NFL. On Sunday afternoon at Lambeau Field, it appears that the tide might be turning for the Minnesota offense, thanks to the addition of one man. Kirk Cousins threw a pair of touchdown passes and, more importantly, allowed the Minnesota defense to actually get some rest after two straight weeks of getting overworked. The defense responded by sacking Jordan Love eight times and shutting down an offense that had scored 45 points the previous week in a thoroughly dominant 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 10 action at Lambeau Field. The Packers won the opening coin toss and deferred to the second half, putting Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota offense on the field first. The Vikings went three-and-out, as Cousins’ first pass was too high for Justin Jefferson and his second, a screen to Myles Price, was dropped for a loss of yards. Brett Thorson blasted a 64-yard punt, and the Packers started their first possession inside their own 10-yard line. On the Packers’ second play from scrimmage, Andrew Van Ginkel made his presence felt, as Jordan Love completed a pass to tight end Mark Redman, and Van Ginkel stripped it away, recovering the fumble at the Green Bay 10 for a turnover. SNATCHED! @AndrewVanGinkel 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/A1bTh9RgWq — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 15, 2026 The Vikings’ offense capitalized on the turnover with. . .a false start and a sack of Cousins that moved them back 14 yards in two plays. After an Aaron Jones run on third down, the Vikings called on Will Reichard, who connected on a 34-yard field goal to give the Vikings a 3-0 lead just under five minutes into the contest. Green Bay got some help on the ensuing kickoff, as Jay Ward committed a 15-yard penalty to put the Packers near midfield to start their next possession. The Packers moved the ball into Minnesota territory inside the 30-yard line, but the drive came to a screeching halt when Dallas Turner dropped Love for a sack. The Packers brought on Trey Smack to attempt a 53-yard field goal, but his attempt sailed wide to the right to give Minnesota the ball back near midfield, still leading 3-0. Minnesota started their next drive with a first down into Green Bay territory, as Cousins found Gavin Bartholomew to move the chains. The Vikings then got a look at a familiar connection, as Cousins found Justin Jefferson for a 13-yard gain to convert on third down and keep the drive moving. The Vikings were then called for a face mask penalty to push themselves back to the edge of field goal range. . .but Cousins decided that the Vikings didn’t need a field goal, as he hit Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown that saw Price bounce off of a Green Bay defender and make his way into the end zone. COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 The first receiving touchdown of Price’s NFL career increased the Minnesota lead to 10-0 with just over two minutes left in the first quarter. And in the ninth game of the season, that was the Vikings’ first offensive touchdown in the first quarter of any game this season. Green Bay got off to a quick start on their next drive, as Love found Marshawn Lloyd on a quick pass for a big gain to near midfield, and Lloyd then took a handoff into Minnesota territory for another first down. The Vikings then got called for a couple of 15-yard penalties, one on Eric Wilson for roughing the passer and another on Dallas Turner for. . .something. . .to help move the Packers into the red zone. But when it looked like the Packers might get on the scoreboard, Harrison Smith decided to put an end to all that. Harrison Smith picks it off in the end zone! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4FyAQkSdGU — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 The Hitman picked off Jordan Love in the end zone to end the drive and bring the ball out to the 20-yard line for the Vikings’ next possession. Unfortunately, the Vikings’ offense couldn’t do anything with it, as a loss on first down stalled the drive early as they went three-and-out again. Thorson’s punt put the Green Bay offense at its own 25 to start their next possession. The Vikings’ defense went to work again, as they registered back-to-back sacks of Love to force a three-and-out, one from Levi Drake Rodriguez and one from Eric Wilson. Green Bay’s punt gave the Vikings good field position at their own 45-yard line to start their next possession. The Vikings marched the ball down the field with a nice mix of passes before a run by Jordan Mason put the ball into the red zone. The Vikings then dodged a bullet when it looked like Cousins had thrown an interception, but it was ruled by replay that his knee was down before he threw the ball, allowing the Vikings to keep possession. Cousins then hit Tai Felton on a big third-down throw to make it first-and-goal. On the next play, the former Packer, Aaron Jones, took a pitch and went around the left side for a 2-yard score to extend the Minnesota lead to 17-0 with just over six minutes left in the first half. Aaron Jones finds the end zone at his old home MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qmWo3qMWoO — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Green Bay’s offense went three-and-out on its next possession after a third-down catch by Matthew Golden that had been ruled a first-down completion was ruled incomplete after Kevin O’Connell challenged the call, as replay showed that the ball hit the ground before Golden controlled it. Minnesota took over again and pushed into Green Bay territory before the two-minute warning, but on the first snap after the two-minute timeout, Cousins’ pass for Tai Felton was overthrown and intercepted by Xavier McKinney for a turnover. The Packers took the ball after the interception and got the ball close to midfield, but then the Vikings’ defense turned things up again and collected two more sacks of Love: one that was split between Van Ginkel and Kyle Van Noy, and one that Van Noy got all by himself. That concluded a five-sack first half for the Vikings, and they went into the locker room with a 17-0 lead. Green Bay got the ball to start the second half, and pushed their first possession to near midfield. However, they turned the ball over again when a shotgun snap flew right past Jordan Love for a fumble that Dallas Turner recovered at the Green Bay 27-yard line for the third turnover of the game for Green Bay, setting the Vikings up nicely. Jordan Love fails to recover the bad snap and the Vikings take the ball back early in the 2nd half 👀 pic.twitter.com/dc4U6ruSvY — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 15, 2026 The Vikings got the ball into a goal-to-go situation, but the offense stalled, and they had to settle for another field goal from Reichard, this one a 32-yarder to make it 20-0 with ten minutes left in the third quarter. The Packers got the ball back and once again moved into Minnesota territory, but the sack parade continued again, with Jalen Redmond and Elijah Williams taking Love down to add to the total. The Packers faced a 4th-and-11 from the Minnesota 44-yard line, and they converted on a pass from Love to Matthew Golden to stay on the field. On the next play, Green Bay finally got on the scoreboard, as Love found J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard score to make it 20-7 with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter of play. Minnesota went three-and-out on its next possession, putting Green Bay at their 14-yard line to start their next…

If Minnesota makes the playoffs, Cousins can become the first QB ever to start a playoff game for a team after starting… pic.twitter.com/8w82PNdidu — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 15, 2026 According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Cousins is now set to become the first quarterback to start for two different teams in back-to-back weeks since quarterback starts became an official stat in 1950. That’s 76 years ago, if you’re scoring at home. Last week, of course, Cousins started for the Las Vegas Raiders against the team the Vikings will play next week in Mexico City: the San Francisco 49ers. Today, he starts for the Vikings in the place where he played his last game with Minnesota. Not only that, but should the Vikings make the playoffs this season, Cousins would become the first quarterback to start a playoff game for a team after starting games for another team during the same season. So, yes, even though the Vikings are returning a familiar face at quarterback today against their most-hated rival, we really are in uncharted waters in terms of what they’re trying to do at the quarterback position. Hopefully, this all works out the way that the Vikings. . .and the rest of us fans. . .would like it to.

title: Did Drake Maye get injured on an illegal play?
summary: Penalties played a decisive role in the New England Patriots’ opening drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, but it was a flag that wasn’t flown that generated the most discussion after the game: should Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson been penalized for taking down Drake Maye and, along the way, injuring his ankle? Before […]
full_text: Penalties played a decisive role in the New England Patriots’ opening drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, but it was a flag that wasn’t flown that generated the most discussion after the game: should Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson been penalized for taking down Drake Maye and, along the way, injuring his ankle ? Before trying to figure out whether or not referee Clay Martin and his crew should have flown penalty flags, a look at the play in question. This was Drake Maye's final play before leaving the game questionable with an ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/Yi1rQYpMeW — Doug Kyed (@DougKyed) November 15, 2026 Hutchinson quickly worked his way into the backfield on an apparent communication breakdown involving left tackle Will Campbell, and wrapped up Maye from behind as he was climbing the pocket. In doing so, he lifted his entire body off the ground and subsequently came down on Maye’s now-injured ankle. Was Hutchinson’s form illegal, though, and should have been penalized as a hip-drop tackle? Not according to NFL rules Section 2, Article 18: Article 18. Hip-Drop Tackle It is a foul if a player uses the following technique to bring a runner to the ground: – grabs the runner with one or both hands or wraps the runner with both arms; and – unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips and/or lower body, landing on and/or trapping the runner’s leg(s) at or below the knee. FOX rules analyst Mike Pereira gave a similar explanation on the air. “Three things have to happen,” he explained. “You have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee. This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse collar penalty.” The NFL agreed, as reported by ESPN’s Mike Reiss: Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, confirmed Pereira’s explanation through a league spokesman, noting it was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting. It was also not a foul for a horse collar tackle, as Pereira noted, because neither the collar nor the nameplate were grabbed. No penalty was called on the play by referee Clay Martin’s crew. Mike Vrabel, who has been at odds with the officials multiple times so far this season, also saw nothing nefarious on the play. “I don’t think it was [a hip-drop tackle],” he said on Monday. This comment follows up similar remarks made by Vrabel after the game on Sunday. “I’m not going to assume there was something there,” he said. “However it happened, I don’t think it was anything intentional. I’m sure that it wasn’t. That’s part of the game.” Neither Maye nor Hutchinson have since commented on the play, because both got injured. Whereas Maye suffered the aforementioned ankle injury, Hutchinson is believed to have suffered a torn ACL while celebrating the sack.
