title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
summary: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due […]
full_text: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would “almost certainly” be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport. What does it mean for the Patriots? “Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions,” safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game. The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future. What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period. DeVito described his and the offense’s performance after he took over for Maye as “not good enough.” The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots’ upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Mike Vrabel gives update on Drake Maye after injury
summary: The New England Patriots flew back from Germany to the United States shortly after their loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. One player wasn’t with them: quarterback Drake Maye, who was unable to finish the game after suffering an ankle injury in the first quarter. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, Maye initially stayed […]
full_text: The New England Patriots flew back from Germany to the United States shortly after their loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. One player wasn’t with them: quarterback Drake Maye, who was unable to finish the game after suffering an ankle injury in the first quarter. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, Maye initially stayed behind to best prepare him for the trip across the Atlantic. “The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,” Vrabel said during an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday morning. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” Maye hurt his ankle on a third-down sack on the game’s first series. He limped off the field and shortly thereafter made his way into the blue medical tent on the sidelines. The 24-year-old headed straight to the locker room when he emerged, and was ruled out for the rest of the game shortly thereafter. The Patriots reportedly fear that Maye suffered a fractured ankle . He will be out “indefinitely” and is set to undergo further testing once back in the U.S. “We’ll have to see what comes back and what he looks like when he’s back here,” said Vrabel, “and make sure we’re doing what’s best for him and his health.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Drake Maye injury: Patriots QB might miss rest of the season
summary: Update 11/16/2026: Drake Maye out indefinitely with potential ankle fracture The New England Patriots fear that Drake Maye suffered an ankle fracture during Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions. According to a report by ESPN’s Adam Schefter, he underwent further testing in Germany to determine whether or not surgery would be necessary. Regardless of that […]
full_text: Update 11/16/2026: Drake Maye out indefinitely with potential ankle fracture The New England Patriots fear that Drake Maye suffered an ankle fracture during Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions. According to a report by ESPN’s Adam Schefter, he underwent further testing in Germany to determine whether or not surgery would be necessary. Regardless of that decision, Maye will be out ‘indefinitely’ and potentially for the remainder of the season. Original story 11/16/2026: Drake Maye might miss rest of the season with ‘significant lower leg injury’ The New England Patriots appear to have suffered a major blow on Sunday. Quarterback Drake Maye, who exited the game against the Detroit Lions in the first quarter, is expected to be “out an extended period of time” and might even miss the remainder of the season altogether. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” in the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Lions . Maye, 24, exited the game after the opening drive. He had completed three of his first four pass attempts for 48 total yards and also gained 11 yards on a scramble, but was taken down for a third-down sack to end the series. After the play, which also saw Lions edge Aidan Hutchinson suffer a potentially season-ending injury while celebrating, the Patriots’ third-year QB limped of the field. He later entered the blue medical tent on the sidelines and after emerging made his way to the locker room. Maye was initially announced as questionable to return with an ankle injury, but was ruled out for the remainder of the game shortly thereafter. In his absence, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito entered the contest. DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception. New England scored once with him under center. The Patriots flew back to the United States on Sunday, after their game against the Lions in Munich. Maye is expected to undergo further testing to determine the exact severity of the injury and establish a recovery timeline. The Patriots are on their bye this week before a Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Lions
summary: For a second week in a row, the New England Patriots got blown out by an NFC North team on Sunday. Once again, they looked listless and disengaged for the majority of the game. Let’s get into our lessons learned from the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. If Drake Maye is […]
full_text: For a second week in a row, the New England Patriots got blown out by an NFC North team on Sunday. Once again, they looked listless and disengaged for the majority of the game. Let’s get into our lessons learned from the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. If Drake Maye is out for any extended period, the Patriots are going to borderline unwatchable The Patriots haven’t had many playmakers on offense this year, but Drake Maye has still put together a (mostly) solid year. Without him, however, it looks like one of the worst offenses in football. Sunday’s game was concrete proof of that. Tommy DeVito couldn’t get the ball to open receivers, separation was on and off, and they couldn’t run the ball. If Maye misses time after the bye, and it’s looking increasingly likely that that is going to be the case , it’s going to be tough to watch. Tommy DeVito isn’t good Speaking of Tommy DeVito, after Drake Maye went out with an injury, the Patriots were forced to turn to him. The media likes DeVito and the Patriots clearly like him too, since they gave him a contract extension this offseason. Unfortunately, he just isn’t that good of a quarterback. On Sunday, he missed open receivers left and right and on more than one occasion threw guys directly into contact. I understand that he’s the backup inserted on short notice, and that the Patriots aren’t asking him to be a great player because they really don’t want him playing at all, but it would be nice if he was at least able to competently run the offense. Against Detroit, he wasn’t. The A.J. Brown trade keeps looking worse by the day A.J. Brown’s inability to do anything positive this year has been almost laughable. He got hurt in the first game, missed a good chunk of time on injured reserve, came back, was a non-factor, and then got hurt again. He returned on Sunday, was unable to get open and had a drop as well. He finally made a nice catch-and-run to move the stick on a third down, and then promptly went to the locker room with a hamstring injury . It’s been a rough year for Brown, and the Patriots front office: they effectively bid against themselves to trade for him and still gave up a first-round pick in 2028 to do so. Unless he somehow manages a complete 180, the trade is going to go down as a massive failure, and potentially hamstring the Patriots for years to come. The defense continues to play without any fire Their defense was the reason the Patriots made the Super Bowl last year, and the hope was that it would take another step forward in 2026. Unfortunately, that has not happen and the unit has instead taken a step back. It did register a couple of turnovers on Sunday, but the unit was unable to stop its opponent more or less all day long. They came out without any fire, missed tackles all over field, and put the Patriots in a hole right away. We all were impressed with the job that Zak Kuhr had done last year, but the league has seemed to figure him out, and whatever he’s doing isn’t working. Yes, they have dealt with some injuries, but, for the most part, the defense has been fairly healthy. They have been out-coached, out-played, and, to be frank, it oftentimes looks like the other team simply wants it more than they do. With this defense, the Patriots aren’t going anywhere, especially if Drake Maye ends up missing time. Christian Gonzalez gets burned again, but recovers with a pick Christian Gonzalez is one of the best corners in the NFL, and surely one of the best players on the Patriots. The last two weeks, however, saw him have back-to-back rough games for the first time in his career. On the game’s first third down against the Lions, his struggles continued, when Amon-Ra St. Brown caught a pass in the flat, shook Gonzalez into oblivion, and then took the ball 56 yards for a touchdown. It was a bad start for Gonzalez, who later also fell victim to a pick play on another St. Brown score. it wasn’t all bad, however. He also registered an interception on a play where he ran the route for St. Brown and undercut him for the pick. It was a play that showed the player he has been, and will try to be again. The Patriots finally win the turnover battle While we are on the topic of interceptions, the Patriots have finally won the turnover battle for the first time this season. They picked off Jared Goff twice, and only turned it over once. In a game where they got embarrassed again, and with everything looking absolutely terrible in New England now, I’ll take any positive notes I can get. Now, if they only were able to go a game without turning the ball over… Jahmyr Gibbs might be the best player in the NFL The NFL is filled with players who are really fast, really strong, and really elusive. None of those players, however, measure up to Gibbs. His ability to stop and start is ridiculous, and his speed is nothing short of blazing. He leads the NFL in touches, and there is no sign of him slowing down. People had thought that TreVeyon Henderson would be the Patriots’ version of Gibbs, but there is no one in this league like him, and, just like most teams that have played the Lions this year, New England had no chance of stopping him on Sunday. In fact, he ended up out-gaining them by himself: Gibbs had 153 rushing yards and 99 receiving yards for a total of 252 yards. The Patriots offense finished the day with a grand total of 151. Reggie Gilliam has a tough first game back The Patriots activated Gilliam off of injured reserve before the game, and they were hoping he would be a factor in the running game and on special teams. Instead, the Patriots couldn’t run the ball to save their lives, Gilliam twice ran into his return man when he was trying to block, and he also committed two penalties on special teams. Personally, I didn’t love activating him off the IR, and, for Sunday at least, the Patriots didn’t get any better with him on the field. With Drake Maye set to miss time, however, they might have to start relying on him and the running game. We might have to start questioning Mike Vrabel Mike Vrabel did a fantastic job last year, there is no denying it. The culture he was trying to build was obvious, and the result was a mentally and physically tough team that reveled in the opportunity to go on the road and prove itself. This year, however, the team has been a disaster. There have definitely been a lot of injuries, but the mental toughness has almost completely disappeared. The amount of pre-snap penalties is alarming, and the unforced errors in judgement and physical play have been bad. To go along with that, the way that he and some of the players have been speaking to the media is confusing as well. If you’re going to be a culture guy, then the culture has to matter, and it doesn’t look good right now. I’m not saying that they should fire Vrabel or anything, but it bears watching. If the team doesn’t start playing better, and they don’t fix the fundamentals (turnovers, penalties, tackling), then there might be a reason to move on sooner rather than later. Obviously, not every team is going to be great every year, but he has hand-picked a lot of these guys for the culture here because he coached them before. If this team has any sort of culture issue, it’s squarely on Vrabel’s shoulders. (I also think that it’s notable that they seemingly rushed A.J. Brown back twice instead of giving him a long rest, and he’s been hurt both times. Maybe that’s the medical staff, but it’s ultimately the coaching staff who makes the decision to play the guys, even if they are physically cleared.) Thank god for the bye Perhaps no team in the NFL has needed a bye week as much as the Patriots do. They played two bad games in a row, have a ton of injuries, including at quarterback, and desperately need to get their minds right and get healthy. The Patriots are going to have to come up with something significantly better than what they’ve brought lately, because they are getting crushed and look…
author: Pat Lane

title: What the reported Drake Maye injury means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots did not just lose their Week 10 game to the Detroit Lions, they also saw their starting quarterback depart early in the 35-10 contest. And not just that: Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that is reportedly expected to keep him out an extended period […]
full_text: The New England Patriots did not just lose their Week 10 game to the Detroit Lions, they also saw their starting quarterback depart early in the 35-10 contest . And not just that: Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that is reportedly expected to keep him out an extended period of time and might even end his season. While further tests will be conducted to determine a return timeline, Maye’s immediate future is, at the very least, in question. What does this mean for the Patriots? Let’s find out. On to 2027? The Patriots are 5-5 and despite dropping out of the playoff picture on Sunday remain in the race for a postseason spot in the AFC. However, if Maye is indeed forced to miss extended time or even the rest of the season, the outlook changes drastically: given all of the issues, this does not look like a playoff-caliber team without its Pro Bowl-caliber quarterback. At least publicly, the Patriots and head coach Mike Vrabel won’t care. We will hear the classic “next man up” and “everybody is preparing like a starter” lines, while there will be no outward readjustment of the goals. Make no mistake, however. This is the worst-case scenario for the Patriots and their 2026 season. It might not mean they will go 0-7 down the stretch, especially if Maye does come back, but the sights might have to be set on 2027 sooner rather than later. It’s the Tommy DeVito show Sunday’s game against the Lions might not have been an accurate reflection of their capabilities, but that doesn’t mean the Patriots’ offensive outlook is not bleak. Fact is, after all, that Tommy DeVito is a serious downgrade from Drake Maye. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . That said, the Patriots are still expected to rely on their backup for however long Maye will ultimately be out. Rookie Behren Morton, who served as the emergency third option throughout the season thus far, will be elevated to the No. 2 spot with a third passer potentially being added to the roster or practice squad if need be. DeVito, 28, entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie with the New York Giants in 2023. He started eight total games over two year but was waived in 2025. He subsequently joined the Patriots in a backup role, serving as the third passer behind Maye and Joshua Dobbs. When Dobbs was let go earlier in the year, DeVito officially took over the backup spot. As such, he saw minimal action over the first nine weeks of the season. Against the Lions, however, he played most of the game and finished with 12 completions on 24 attempts for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception. The Patriots scored once with him at the helm and punted eight times, including seven three-and-outs. Cultural stress test However long the Patriots’ medical staff determines Maye will be out might also have an impact on other injury situations. Frankly, if the starter is sidelined and the losses keep piling up, there would be no need for any players to be rushed back from injury. There shouldn’t be any way, to be honest, but the threshold of “pushing through” an injury might be reconfigured should Maye indeed be out an extended period of time. That “pushing through” process, however, appears to be an integral part of New England’s culture this season. Multiple players are currently banged up or still dealing with the effects of injuries they suffered earlier; the bye week will come handy in that regard. If the overall goals begin to shift, however, so might the culture — for better or worse. It will be on Mike Vrabel, who was hired in 2025 in large part due to his abilities as a leader and team-builder, to make sure the locker room sees through this latest challenge in a season full of them. The schedule might change As of Monday morning, three of the Patriots’ final seven games of the season are scheduled as prime time games. One of those is a realistic candidate to be flexed out of its spot, and would have been so even before Maye got hurt: the Sunday night game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. That being said, with Thanksgiving that weekend and games taking place on Thursday and Friday as well, the alternatives are actually minimal. Unless the league wants to flip it to the 1 p.m. ET spot currently occupied by Raiders-Browns, only the 4:25 p.m. ET contest between the Seahawks and 49ers makes sense. Whether or not FOX will give that one up, however, will be seen. As for the other prime time games on the schedule, they likely will stay in their slots due to their nature as Thursday (Week 14 vs. Vikings) and Monday (Week 15 vs. Chiefs) games. Still, the two undetermined slots in Weeks 17 (vs. Broncos) and 18 (vs. Dolphins) could now very well end up as 1 p.m. games. Grain of salt It could very well be tied to the “pushing through” culture at One Patriot Place, but on multiple occasions this season players have come back sooner than their initially-reported injuries made it sound. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is the latest example: he was expected to miss multiple weeks due to the knee injury he suffered in Week 9 against Green Bay, but was back at practice four days later and ended up playing 26 snaps against the Lions. With that in mind, Monday’s reports might have to be taken with a grain of salt. With the bye week coming up, the Patriots do have some extra time at their hands for recovery. At the end of the day, of course, they would be wise to play the long game with Maye. Yes, the playoffs are still a distinct possibility even at 5-5, but they need to be careful with their franchise quarterback.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: 2 winners and losers from Patriots loss to the Lions
summary: The New England Patriots were uncompetitive again in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-5 on the season, and currently find themselves out of the playoff picture. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 10 contest. Winners Nobody: […]
full_text: The New England Patriots were uncompetitive again in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-5 on the season, and currently find themselves out of the playoff picture . Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 10 contest. Winners Nobody: There could be an argument for Drake Maye, who generated four positive plays on the Patriots’ opening possession before leaving with an ankle injury . Anyone who still had doubts (for some reason) about Maye’s impact on the offense got their answer once he left the game. Still, nobody earns a spot here after an embarrassing 35-10 loss. Losers Everybody: The No. 1 pillar of Mike Vrabel’s team identity is effort and finish. Yet it was another week without seeing enough of either across the roster. Kevin Byard called it a “slap in the face” game. Tommy DeVito said the team got bullied. It was an alarming performance for Vrabel himself and the program he is trying to build. As for more specific performances: Honorable mentions Injuries continued to be one of the storylines of the season as the Patriots lost the one player they couldn’t: Drake Maye. The QB left after the first drive with an ankle injury and the offense was uncompetitive from that point forward. The Patriots also lost A.J. Brown (hamstring), Robert Spillane (illness), Charles Woods (unknown) and Dre’Mont Jones (cramps). DeVito struggled mightily in relief competing 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards and one touchdown and interception. It’s a tough spot for any backup being thrusted into the fire, but DeVito generated -0.32 EPA per play (10th percentile) against the worst pass defense in football. He struggled to see the field missing several open receivers downfield and led his pass catchers into multiple big hits due to poor ball placement. A.J. Brown caught just two-of-six targets for 27 yards before leaving with a hamstring injury. He had another drop. In his return, fullback Reggie Gilliam was called for two special teams penalties and lost a fumble that Brown recovered. Will Campbell struggled in pass protection allowing six pressures on 33 pass blocking snaps, per Next Gen Stats. Campbell allowed 2.0 sacks, including one to Aidan Hutchinson that led to Maye leaving the game. The Patriots defense does not have the injury excuse like the offense. Outside of Carlton Davis (knee), this is their unit and it has been ugly. They generated two turnovers, but missed 12 tackles while the explosive plays against piled up again. Detroit nearly totaled 500 (!) yards of offense. Christian Gonzalez matched up with Amon-Ra St. Brown 15 times on Sunday. While he hauled in his first interception of the season he allowed two receptions for 84 yards and two touchdowns across three targets. Vrabel noted Gonzalez got no help elsewhere on the first touchdown after he missed the initial tackle attempt. Safety Kevin Byard had perhaps his best sequence of the season with a pass breakup then interception in the end zone to end the first half. Byard was among the group, though, that did not help Gonzalez which appeared to be an issue on multiple occasions. Shoutout Mitch Wishnowsky for continuing to punt well. 8 punts and zero touchbacks as he has been one of the few bright spots this season.
author: Brian Hines

title: Tommy DeVito, Patriots offense ‘not good enough’ after Drake Maye injury
summary: The New England Patriots were never able to find an offensive rhythm without starting quarterback Drake Maye on Sunday. After Maye led the Patriots on an 11-play, 60-yard opening drive that ended in a field goal, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game with an ankle injury. With Tommy DeVito taking over […]
full_text: The New England Patriots were never able to find an offensive rhythm without starting quarterback Drake Maye on Sunday. After Maye led the Patriots on an 11-play, 60-yard opening drive that ended in a field goal, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game with an ankle injury . With Tommy DeVito taking over under center, the Patriots managed just one more scoring drive the rest of the way while going three-and-out on seven possessions. “Not good enough are the words I would say,” DeVito said post game. “Offensively, just never really got going; never really was able to get into a rhythm, really get drives going. Too many three and outs and just hurting ourselves. Even the one drive that we had that resulted in a touchdown took 16 plays and there were still errors on that that happened. “We just need to be better at that and just sustaining drives.” DeVito finished the game 12-of-24 for 81 yards, one touchdown and an interception. He appeared to have multiple receivers open before forcing the pick over the middle of the field to Mack Hollins. There were other instances in which DeVito appeared to miss open receivers, while he also led his pass catchers into big collisions on multiple occasions. The offense as a whole finished with just 151 yards on 55 plays, averaging 2.7 yards per play while converting just four of 13 third downs. Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about his level of concern with the unit’s performance. “I mean, again, we have a lot of — it’s not. I don’t think Drake’s being in there or not would have really — I mean it may have. I would highly doubt it,” Vrabel began. “Until we start doing the little things better in all three phases, the fundamentals, being able to run the football, being able to get open and catch and protect our quarterback, tackle, get off the field on third down, create turnovers, obviously we have to start turning it over offensively and then special teams, got to be able to create a spark for us and create some momentum plays.” Vrabel did not have an update on Maye’s status following the game. The quarterback is expected to undergo additional testing on his ankle when the team returns to Foxborough. A much-needed bye week will give the Patriots an opportunity to reset and refocus before preparing for a challenging final seven games of the season. Whether they will have Maye available for that stretch remains to be seen. In the meantime, DeVito will continue preparing as he has throughout the season. “I’m going to continue the process I have been doing up to this point. Something that as a two, as cliche as it sounds, you have to be prepared to be a starter,” DeVito said. “So just keep doing what I’m doing, keep my head down, and then if something like that were to happen, you would have the reps and practice and the walkthroughs and everything going forward, so just keep on preparing and on to the next.”
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots’ defensive woes continue against the Lions in Munich
summary: After a historically poor defensive performance against the Green Bay Packers seven days ago, the hope across New England as the Patriots traveled to Munich, Germany, centered around the potential of an improved and more cohesive unit on that side of the ball against the Detroit Lions. But while defensive backs Christian Gonzalez and Kevin […]
full_text: After a historically poor defensive performance against the Green Bay Packers seven days ago, the hope across New England as the Patriots traveled to Munich, Germany, centered around the potential of an improved and more cohesive unit on that side of the ball against the Detroit Lions . But while defensive backs Christian Gonzalez and Kevin Byard each intercepted Jared Goff on Sunday, those turnovers masked the defensive woes that still plague New England as it has now dropped three of its last four games, capped by a 35-10 defeat. Head coach Mike Vrabel and Byard identified “execution” as an area in need of improvement last week. And those issues have led to assignment breakdowns and poor tackling efforts across the unit. The Patriots’ pass rush sacked Goff twice in the first half, but the group behind the defensive line struggled from the beginning of the Lions’ opening drive. Despite Jacas taking down Goff and backing Detroit into a second-and-16 snap, Amon-Ra St. Brown caught a pass off a quick-out and juked Gonzalez to the ground. The receiver then sliced through New England’s defense and raced 56 yards into the end zone as defenders appeared hesitant to commit to a tackle. Following the Lions’ subsequent scoring drive, Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose on a couple of solid drives, again allowed by lackluster tackling, extending Detroit’s lead 21-3. Gibbs leaked out of the backfield and trailed down the right sideline 50 yards with the ball in his right arm. Byard hurried to the sideline to stop the running back short of the red zone, yet hesitated considerably, giving Gibbs an extra 15 yards of grass to cover. Near the goal line, Gibbs faked Cory Durden out behind the line of scrimmage before cutting back inside for an easy lane into the end zone. The Lions operate one of the NFL’s most dynamic offenses. By halftime, the group totaled 312 yards and punted just once. “There’s a lot we have to fix,” Vrabel said. “[If] you play good teams in this league and you don’t play well, you have no chance. And again, we know that, and there are glimpses of good defense. [We] gave up too many [explosive] plays, too many missed tackles and too many clean pockets for [Goff].” Even during Byard’s end-of-half interception, they drove 39 yards in 30 seconds, threatening to score. Gibbs concluded the contest with 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. Still, a team looking to compete for a title nine months after a Super Bowl appearance needs to show more resistance against high-scoring offenses. That’s what championship teams do and what the Patriots did last season. Overall, Detroit’s offensive production dipped in the second half; however, New England’s defensive mishaps remained. Early in the third frame, St. Brown lined up out wide, appearing to block for a screen before cutting inside and following his lineman downfield. He then slipped between the seams, where Byard failed to wrap him up, as two Lions pushed St. Brown into the end zone against two Patriots defenders. Gibb’s fourth-quarter touchdown along the right sideline didn’t look too different either. It’s difficult for a defense to stay motivated when the offense isn’t producing. We saw that noticeable shift in body language against the Jacksonville Jaguars during Week Three after the offense continuously failed to find the end zone. And that certainly was the case when backup Tommy DeVito replaced an injured Drake Maye in the first quarter on Sunday. Yet for a team built around one of Vrabel’s four pillars, effort and finish, the lack of execution directly contradicts the identity established in 2025. “They played harder than us today,” Byard said. “They played more physically than us. As a defense, that feels like a slap in the face that we let them play that hard.” Heading into the bye week, New England is 5-5 in desperate desire of a victory to get back on track. Vrabel views the situation as a 0-0 start. “I don’t know what else [the message] could be,” Vrabel said. “… If we don’t get things corrected, improved or fixed, that’s going to go the other way.” Gonzalez reiterated the defense’s lack of execution after the game. Whether or not Maye takes the helm against the Los Angeles Chargers in two weeks with a playoff spot in serious question, the Patriots will need to return to that philosophy to prevent frequent early deficits and a downward spiral during the most important stretch of the season.

title: 4 things the NY Giants have to do better to win the NFC East
summary: The New York Giants’ loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday tightened the NFC East race and made their weekend off less enjoyable than it could have been. Thanks to the San Francisco 49ers outscoring the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, though, the Giants’ division lead entering Week 11 is not as tenuous as it could […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Getty Images The New York Giants’ loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday tightened the NFC East race and made their weekend off less enjoyable than it could have been. Thanks to the San Francisco 49ers outscoring the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, though, the Giants’ division lead entering Week 11 is not as tenuous as it could have been. The 5-3-1 Giants have a 2½-game lead over the 4-6 Cowboys and a two-game lead over the 3-5-1 Commanders. The Athletic’s playoff simulator gives the Giants a 56% chance of winning the NFC East and making the playoffs. The Cowboys are at 28%, and the Commanders 16%. Much has been made of the fact that the Giants’ schedule, beginning this weekend with the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars, is about to get tougher. Over the Giants’ first nine games, their opponents were a combined 25-49-1, a .340 winning percentage. Their upcoming opponents are a combined 43-33, a .566 winning percentage. Head coach John Harbaugh said recently that the Giants “don’t live in that scared world” of worrying about schedule difficulty. The Giants are a resilient team. Harbaugh has made them that way. They have, to this point, overcome the losses of quarterback Jaxson Dart and star edge defender Brian Burns. In each of their five wins, they have made plays late in the game to secure the victory. Fight and resilience alone, though, won’t win the NFC East title for the Giants. The Giants are an imperfect team that has things to fix in order to win the division. Below are some of the things the Giants are going to have to do better over the final eight games. Four-minute offense The Giants, holding a 21-17 lead, intercepted Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels twice in the last 5:31 of Thursday’s game. That should be enough for the Giants to have won that game. But it wasn’t. The Giants went three-and-out after both interceptions, failing to run significant time off the clock or force the Commanders to use up their timeouts on either occasion. The first possession included three runs, with the last being a Jameis Winston third-and-1 sneak on which running back Cam Skattebo never really got out of his stance to participate in the play. Harbaugh explained that this was a straight sneak, not a tush push. The second possession, which started at the Washington 46-yard line with 2:15 to play, also featured three runs. The last was a designed quarterback run for J.J. McCarthy on which the Giants didn’t even have a running back on the field. Sonny Styles said absolutely not on 3rd down. WASvsNYG on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d9S7zwsT3 — NFL (@NFL) November 13, 2026 You can see from the jump he got that Washington linebacker Sonny Styles knew this play before the ball was snapped. Center Bryan Hudson had no chance to block him. “We had thought we had good runs. We thought we could get it with the runs. Also keep the clock running and make them burn the timeouts. We thought we could do both,” Harbaugh said. “But looking back on it, I think a good pass there might’ve been good too. I think if you throw the ball and you throw three incompletions or whatever, the question is flipped, you know, “why didn’t you run the ball, make them burn the timeouts?” Being successful really is the bottom line. It’s not like we’re trying to play it safe or anything like that. We’re not afraid to throw the ball there. The run that we had, the last run that got the two-yard loss, that’s got a chance to crack them. It’s a quarterback-driven run with an extra blocker. They had everybody up on the line. Honestly, on that one play, we can block that play better. And so that’s the way the game went in that situation.” The problem is, four-minute offense failure has been a theme for the Giants. In Week 3 against the Tennessee Titans, the Giants got the ball with 5:31 to play, protecting a 12-7 lead. They got a quick first down on a 12-yard Jameis Winston to Malik Nabers pass, but then punted with 3:12 to go after two runs and an incomplete pass. Jevon Holland bailed the Giants out, intercepting Cam Ward in the end zone with :24 to play. In Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, the Giants got the ball at midfield with a 3-point lead and 4:47 to play. They could muster only 16 yards in five plays, with a Dominic Zvada 52-yard field goal giving them a 20-24 lead with 2:16 to play. It took a Deonte Banks 98-yard interception return on the final play to seal that victory. In Week 5 against Washington, Skattebo’s fumble at the two-minute mark in overtime cost the Giants a chance to win. In Week 8 against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Giants got the ball with 1:56 to play after a Jake Elliott field goal pulled the Eagles within one score. After three handoffs to Devin Singletary netted just 2 yards, the Giants punted and once again relied on their defense to bail them out. “That’s something that I’ve always prided myself [on], playing on an offense that’s able to ice the game,” fullback Patrick Ricard said after Thursday’s loss. “I feel like this year we haven’t been able to do that as an offense. Only probably Week 1 that we actually ran the ball or got first downs, and were able to kneel the game out. “We’ve always had to rely on our defense, and our defense is very clutch, and they’ve been winning a lot of games for us. It’s something that we as an offense have to really harp on to finish games out like that because we can’t keep relying on our defense to keep going out there and just keep getting stops after stops. We need to be able to convert first downs in those moments.” I don’t have the answer. A head coach in his 19th season and a veteran offensive staff, though, need to do everything they can to figure it out. The Giants can’t ask their defense to close every game in the final seconds. We saw that on Thursday night. Placekicking consistency We went in-depth on Zvada’s issues from the right hashmark on Saturday. It simply isn’t possible to design an offense to get every field goal attempt from the left hashmark. This is something that Zvada and veteran special teams coordinator Chris Horton are going to have to figure out. Harbaugh’s refusal to move on from Zvada, an undrafted rookie who won the job with a fantastic summer, after his struggles since Week 9 has driven the fan base to distraction. I understand Harbaugh’s desire to ride things out with Zvada and hope he becomes the kicker the Giants believe he can be sooner rather than later. Look around the league. For every team that has a Brandon Aubrey, Cam Little, or a solid veteran like Chris Boswell, there are teams riding what former special teams coordinator Thomas McGaughey called the “kicker train”, and finding it an unpleasant experience. Just like there aren’t 32 top-10 caliber quarterbacks in the NFL, there aren’t 32 kickers teams feel good about every time they need three points. Or even one point. Zvada, 23, has the leg strength and talent to be one of those long-range placekicking weapons every team is seeking. Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri kicked for 24 years, but made 80% of his field goal attempts just once in his first four seasons. Former Giants kicker Lawrence Tynes certainly believes in Zvada: Right footed kickers can struggle on the right hash when they try to "steer" the ball to the left vs having a bullet proof alignment process and just kicking the ball normally. You want to just "kick" the ball and swing away when kicking, let your alignment take care of the… https://t.co/GC2wOm1Zem — Lawrence Tynes (@lt4kicks) November 15, 2026 Over the years, the Giants have seen many good young placekickers like Chris Boswell, Brandon McManus, and Joey Slye get away from them and go on to have excellent careers. They don’t want Zvada to be the next one. Still, with a playoff berth at stake, how patient can they be? Don’t be so conservative Everything good about the Giants’ season comes from Harbaugh. The credibility he brought when the Giants hired him and the way he has led this team…

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the headlines you need to start your week. ‘The Coach Hated Him’ — Ex-NFL Scout Raises Eyebrows With Claim About Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell’s Feelings Towards J.J. McCarthy | Pro Football Network “And if I wanted to speak for you in regard to J.J. McCarthy, you hated his guts as a player. You couldn’t (expletive) stand him,” Middlekauff insisted. “Because you were clearly the driving force for making him the third quarterback and helping the GM: ‘We gotta get this guy out of here. Fifth-round pick, I’ll drive him to the airport.’ Which is fine. You’re not the first or the last coach to feel that way toward a QB.” “It’s happened before and it will happen again. Then a couple of weeks later, when you’re starting Carson Wentz, who couldn’t hit water from the middle of the ocean and then J.J.’s making plays like that for (Matt) Nagy and Greg Roman you’re like, ‘Uh, no one is acting like this guy is Joe Montana, but this is way better than what we had.’” What I’m hearing about Chargers-Broncos trade bitterness, why Jonathan Taylor stayed | The Athletic But the Colts weren’t high on dealing Daniel Jones, who played well before his torn Achilles last year. Anecdotally, it appears players are better two years out from Achilles tears, and Jones tore his 11 months ago. Though he hasn’t played well lately, the hope is he will improve. And Jones needs a quality running back in Jonathan Taylor, whom the Colts might have overvalued these past few weeks. League sources aren’t sure a deal of a second and fifth will be on the table for Taylor in March, so it could be easy to say Indy should have dealt him this past week. But by trading players on expiring deals and keeping a quality running back like Taylor and a quarterback who could improve (but could also be released before the team pays him $38 million more), Dodds has created optionality for the next GM. That GM could be Dodds himself, who has been on short lists across the league the last few years, or it could be an outsider. Giants’ Sneak Over Tush Push Call Remains a Head-Scratcher | Giants on SI The numbers supported a tush push on 3rd-and-1, so why didn’t the Giants run it? We have some a theory. Continued Giants growth requires John Harbaugh fourth down adjustments | Daily News The Washington Commanders didn’t win Thursday’s game. The Giants lost it . John Harbaugh and his staff have given this franchise a coaching advantage this season, but their decision-making fell short in their biggest game to date. Teams lose in the NFL. The Giants still look like they’re going in the right direction. But Harbaugh needs to learn from his mistakes if the first-place Giants (5-3-1) intend to win the NFC East. The coach’s conservative calls on fourth downs on offense in the fourth quarter stood out in particular: Former Pro Bowler Donte Whitner says Jameis Winston should be cut for ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’ stunt | New York Post “I’d cut Jameis Winston this morning,” Whitner said on ESPN’s “Get Up” on Friday. “It was so unrealistic. You have 10 other guys out there and guys on defense that are busting their butt every week, and it’s very hard and difficult to win a game in the National Football League. So, when you get up there – first and foremost, whoever says hut 1, hut 2, hut 3? That’s 1950s football! “And then when you go into ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’? Are you serious? He’s clearly just trying to go viral on social media while they’re trying to win a football game. He’d get his pink slip this morning.” There are plenty of reasons to believe these Giants have what it takes | New York Post The weekend off for the Giants could have been a glorious respite if they had been able to hang on and beat the Commanders on Thursday night. That did not happen and the 24-21 loss was their most agonizing and wasteful of the season. From Big Blue View Tougher schedule ahead? full_text: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants will open Week 11 as 6.5-point underdogs at home against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per FanDuel . This game has been penciled in as a loss for the Giants for weeks now, and it shouldn’t be much of a surprise to anyone paying attention that the 5-3-1 Giants are (nearly) touchdown underdogs to the 7-2 Jaguars. The Giants are coming off of a disappointing, and frustrating, loss to the Washington Commanders, squandering a golden opportunity to put the NFC East in a strangle hold and cement their position as a playoff contender. The Giants had multiple opportunities to put the game away, and instead played to not-lose on offense and defense — only to lose anyway. The Jaguars, meanwhile, are coming off of a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans, though that game was closer than the final score until the final 5 minutes or so. One of the biggest questions in the upcoming game is how the Jaguars will incorporate their newly acquired defensive players. The Jags elected to rest NT Jordan Davis and S Jesse Bates, both of whom were acquired in trades last week. DT Devon Godcheaux (acquired from the New Orleans Saints) did play, and ended the game with a tackle. The Giants can find comfort in the fact that they were 10.5-point underdogs on the road to the Houston Texans and came away with a win. However, the Jaguars have been far better than the Texans were when the Giants played them in Week 7. The Giants can win this game, but they’ll certainly have their work cut out for them. title: Film review: Pressure and coverage looks vs. Washington
summary: The New York Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL—a 40%+ rate reminiscent of the Wink Martindale days. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has found success generating pressure and free rushers with an aggressive style that features a loaded line of scrimmage and deceptive tactics the offense can’t easily diagnose. I respect Wilson’s approach […]
full_text: The New York Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL—a 40%+ rate reminiscent of the Wink Martindale days. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has found success generating pressure and free rushers with an aggressive style that features a loaded line of scrimmage and deceptive tactics the offense can’t easily diagnose. I respect Wilson’s approach and game plans, but they don’t always yield sacks. New York blitzed Jayden Daniels often in high-leverage situations on Thursday night, but David Blough and Washington had a plan for the pressure. Daniels finished 23 of 33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions that New York’s offense failed to capitalize on. Wilson stuck to his aggressive style and tried to dictate to Washington’s offense, as he did in Week 5, but the Giants’ defense managed only one sack by Shelby Harris. Nevertheless, the Giants designed several pressure looks to try to attack Washington’s subpar offensive line. Plus, the back-end coverage on these blitzes were impressive for much of the game. Here are those pressure looks: Q1, 7:45, third-and-8 via GIPHY via GIPHY Wilson has run a fire zone all season, and the Giants provide various looks to bring five rushers with zone on the back end. Dawuane Smoot (96) drops off as the end man on the line of scrimmage ( EMOLOS ) to assume the middle hook away from the strength ( the three-receiver side ). Both Micah McFadden (41) and Arvell Reese (52) sugar the A-gap before the snap and blitz, with Greg Newsome II (20) locked up in MEG ( man everywhere he goes ) on the back side No.1: The Commanders design this play to Rachaad White (1), who drops the pass by Jayden Daniels(5). McFadden slides off his blitz — after forcing a blocker to engage him — to account for White in the flat. Wilson often devises blitz packages with contingencies; sure, there are five rushers, but one of them is rushing to force blocker engagement, and they’re keeping their distance to either contain the quarterback or worry about a potential receiving threat — McFadden was that defender on this play. In doing this, New York frees up two rushers who are unblocked, and Daniels is forced to release the football a tad early, resulting in an incomplete pass and a punt. Abdul Carter (3) was unblocked because Kayvon Thibodeaux (5) aligned as a 4i-shade to engage the tackle. The center mistakenly didn’t block anyone, and the Giants’ defense got off the field. Dennard Wilson wastes blockers and creates confusion up front, and the back end of the defense is communicative, with good coverage rapport. Q2, 10:40 third-and-5 via GIPHY via GIPHY This Cover-0 look by the Giants is common. New York initially rushed seven but dropped both Darius Alexander (91) and Smoot off the line of scrimmage into underneath zone looks, but their initial commitment dictates protection. The left guard is blocking no one by the time Daniels takes his second step backward in his drop. White does well to locate Jevon Holland (8) as the free rusher, but Daniels fails to complete the far-hash throw to Stefon Diggs (3). This look also allows Carter to get a free one-on-one matchup to the outside of both dropping defensive linemen. He does seem tasked, though, to be wary of Daniels’ legs on the rush, for his pass-rush is controlled. New York aligned the same way and dropped two defenders off the line of scrimmage on Diggs’ fourth-quarter touchdown. Washington had the last laugh after seeing this Cover-0 look multiple times on Thursday night. Q2, 2:00, second-and-2 via GIPHY via GIPHY The Giants ran a simulated pressure where Kayvon Thibodeaux dropped off the line of scrimmage to the strength on the play-action sprint-out by Daniels. New York has three deep, and they’re communicating on the back end, with Holland staying between the hashes. Jason Pinnock (25) assumed the deep dig route by Treylon Burks (13) and Holland stayed deep in the middle of the field. Tae Banks (2) jammed Diggs at the line of scrimmage and then followed the flow of the play to the inside, which prompted Pinnock to make a push call that wasn’t heard: The sprintout was designed to Austin Ekeler (30), but the Giants had Thibodeaux and Dru Phillips (22) outside the hash in underneath zones. Daniels did an excellent job seeing Diggs and throwing across his body to create an explosive play to the backside. The threat of his rushing ability forced McFadden out of his zone. I presume Banks was told to run playside on sprintouts after passing Diggs off, but Diggs also ran inside and Pinnock’s push went unheard. Q3, 3:22, third-and-10 via GIPHY via GIPHY I’m impressed with the Giants ‘ communication on the back end when they send five or more rushers. This is another fire zone blitz where Thibodeaux and Reese both drop off the line of scrimmage, and Phillips is the extra blitzer to the outside of Carter. Kayvon Thibodeaux — an EDGE rusher not known for dropping into coverage — is incredibly heady and aware on these fire zone blitzes. The Giants handle this very well, even down to Smoot’s rush, which goes wide to contain the possibility of a Daniels’ rush while also being in the area code of Chig Okonkwo (85), who helped block him initially. Reese and Thibodeaux communicate well and pass routes off to one another. Q4, 9:09, fourth-and-2 via GIPHY via GIPHY Above is a Giants’ Cover-0 look without defenders sliding off the line of scrimmage a second post-snap; this is a six-man rush with Holland and Reese as extra rushers, with man coverage on the back end. Ar’Darious Washington (24) makes an elite play on the football to force the first of three turnovers for in the fourth quarter. The Giants stacked Reese behind D.J. Reader (98) to try and give him leverage against the center on the delayed rush, which would have worked excellently against Washington’s empty look, but the center did well to stop Reese. Still, the Giants came away with the big play. Final thoughts The loss was tough for the Giants. New York could have, and possibly should have, won the football game, but that’s not how the NFL works. Although the lack of statistical success in the sack department is frustrating, the aggressive style did significantly alter and influence Washington’s game plan. Credit to the Commanders for executing well to mitigate the strategy. Dennard Wilson and his defense forced three fourth-quarter turnovers and consistently forced Daniels to get the ball out quickly. I was very impressed, again, with Wilson’s strategy, and New York is doing well with their communication on the back end of their blitz packages when they’re in man-zone, but Washington executed fantastically on all three of their third-down touchdown passes. Overall, the Giants are in good hands defensively, and I look forward to how they’ll bounce back against much tougher opponents that are coming up on the schedule.
author: Nick Falato

title: Tougher schedule ahead? NY Giants ‘don’t live in that scared world’
summary: During our post-mortem podcast discussing the New York Giants’ 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders, Tony Del Genio and I raised the likelihood that the Giants are now likely to have win at least one game they are not expected to in order to win the NFC East. The 5-3-1 Giants have played just one […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | Getty Images During our post-mortem podcast discussing the New York Giants’ 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders, Tony Del Genio and I raised the likelihood that the Giants are now likely to have win at least one game they are not expected to in order to win the NFC East. The 5-3-1 Giants have played just one team with a .500 or better winning percentage so far, this season, losing to the Los Angeles Rams 28-6. That changes beginning in Week 11 with the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars. Over their final eight games, the Giants face the Jaguars, the San Francisco 49ers (7-1), the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (5-4), the Cleveland Browns (5-4), and the Detroit Lions (6-2). There are division games with the Dallas Cowboys and Phiiladelphia Eagles, and a must-win game against the 2-7 Indianapolis Colts. Thursday’s loss meant the Giants missed a chance to build a cushion with their schedule about to become more daunting. That, though, is a discussion Giants head coach John Harbaugh did not want to entertain on Friday. “We don’t live in that scared world,” Harbaugh said. “I said it was an important game before the game for that very reason. But now you don’t sit back and go, oh no, we’ve got to beat a heavyweight or whatever you want to call it. It’s the National Football League. We’re planning on going out there and playing and win the game. So we don’t look at it from that perspective.” Harbaugh and the Giants have had a “go 1-0 every week” mentality, and you often see players, coaches, and staf members around the team’s facility wearing ‘1-0’ t-shirts. “It’s okay if you’re not part of the team or you’re covering the team or you’re a fan, you look at that and say, well, which games can we win in these and what chances are we going to have to win? But these guys are going to go play the game,” Harbaugh said. “They’re not going to go into the game saying, “Oh man, this is going to be a tough one for us to win.” They’re all tough to win. Every single one of these games is going to be a big challenge. Every single one of these games is going to be really hard to win. It’s hard winning. It’s tough to win football games in this league. “I’ve said it from the beginning, we’re going to expect to win every single game. We’re planning on winning. Every game that we go into play, we’re taking the field planning to win. We’ll be preparing that way and that’s what we’ll be doing. We’re going to win as many of them as we can. If we win them all, we win them all, but we’ll win as many as we can.” Harbaugh knows his team will fight, no matter who the opponent is. “We’re going to do everything we can do to try to win the game. Our guys are going to fight like crazy. They’re going to compete and we’re capable of making plays. It’s pretty obvious that we can make plays on both sides of the ball. We’re chasing consistency, just like every single team in this league is chasing consistency. “The so-called heavyweights, I’ve seen them play bad games, too. I’ve seen them have plenty of bad plays. There’s no perfect team in this league. Is that pretty obvious to everybody? This is a tough league. It’s pretty even. We’re in it just like everybody else. We’ll be fighting in there just like everybody else. And I know our guys, nobody’s going to out fight us. That’s for sure. Nobody is going to out compete us without question.”
author: Ed Valentine

title: After the loss to the Bills, it feels like Aaron Glenn’s fate is sealed
summary: “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the […]
full_text: Nov 15, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn looks on during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the television series, The Office . Michael Scott didn’t end up losing his job as branch manager of Dunder-Mifflin in the end. Nevertheless, the review remains relatable. Sometimes people can improve their job performance, but other times you reach a realization that they just aren’t capable of doing it. We are past that stage with Aaron Glenn. We can point to any number of dubious marks of his resume as Jets head coach. He is now 5-22, sporting a worse winning percentage as an NFL head coach than Hue Jackson. Glenn now has more than twice as many double digit point losses than he has wins. The latest defeat was the ugly 31-12 blowout at the hands of the Buffalo Bills in Week 10. There isn’t much drama left surrounding Glenn. Barring an unexpected late season surge, he will not retain his job as Jets head coach for a third year. Even if there is a late season winning streak, it still might not be enough. NFL teams don’t reassign their coach to a different department. Coaching contracts aren’t written that way, and practical considerations make the sort of demotion recommended for Scott unviable. Glenn will be let go. He will make enough money to leave football if he so chooses. If he decides to continue his coaching career, he will be an in demand candidates for teams seeking a new defensive coordinator. In the meantime, we will have to endure seven more games. That will be no easy task. I am sure the Jets will invent new ways to lose along the way. In some ways, the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills was familiar. Like a week earlier against the Chiefs, the Jets stayed competitive through one half of football. Their offense settled for field goals instead of scoring touchdowns. Then things fell apart in the second half. This loss still was in many ways different from what we have seen before. Leave it to the Aaron Glenn Jets to lose by three scores in a game where they had an equal number of first downs to their opponent and only 13 fewer total yards. The Jets showed many of the coaching flaws that have plagued the team throughout the season. On offense this team shows no understanding of how to use its talent to the greatest effect. At this point, it feels like salary is the main consideration driving the decision to lean on Breece Hall as the lead back over Braelon Allen. It certainly isn’t performance. The Jets can lean on saying, “A starter can’t lose his job to injury,” all they want. Whether or not Hall missed time from injury, Allen has outplayed him. The Jets struggle just as much to play to their strengths in the passing game. It’s easy to dismiss Kenyon Sadiq’s lack of a role as a developing rookie showing inconsistency. But when backup wide receiver Isaiah Williams gets 7 targets, and a mismatch like Sadiq only gets 2, it speaks to mistaken priorities in the game plan. The Jets can’t put the ball in the end zone. There are no simple explanations for that. I’m sure it didn’t help that they had a fourth round rookie quarterback with zero first team reps through the week playing half the game, but the inability to score touchdowns has been a season-long problem. Anyone watching the team would likely conclude that play calling has been a factor. On the defensive side of the ball, the Jets are simply playing bad football. Aaron Glenn referred to play calling as his superpower, but Glenn’s inability to orchestrate this defense has him looking like a mere mortal. I think there’s a danger for the Jets in blaming all of their problems on coaching. The roster isn’t good enough just yet. Part of this is that the team had a long way to rebuild after their attempts to win a Super Bowl around Aaron Rodgers failed. Part of it is the team has made too many personnel misfires. The Jets need to ask themselves hard questions about the way they do business on many levels as they chart out their future. For now, though, the coaching is the obvious and glaring problem at the center of everyone’s attention. Seven games remain, and unlike binging a television show, we can’t just skip ahead to the next season when we don’t like what we are seeing.

title: Jets vs. Chargers odds: Opening lines for Week 11 matchup
summary: The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Austin Ekeler #30 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs in a touchdown against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it’s possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels’ system appears to be a poor match for Herbert’s skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It’s tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It’s come to this: the Jets aren’t even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! title: Jets vs Bills: Bills Blast Execrable Jets
summary: In the New York Jets’ 10th game of the 2026 season, on a breezy, chilly November day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Buffalo Bills blew out the Jets, 31 – 12. The game opened with the Jets on defense. The Bills advanced past midfield before they were forced to punt. The Jets then went […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills leaps over the line for a first down against the New York Jets in the first quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ 10th game of the 2026 season, on a breezy, chilly November day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Buffalo Bills blew out the Jets, 31 – 12. The game opened with the Jets on defense. The Bills advanced past midfield before they were forced to punt. The Jets then went nowhere and were forced to punt out of their own end zone. The Bills then went on a long, grinding drive ending in a Josh Allen quarterback sneak for a touchdown and a 7 – 0 Bills lead late in the first quarter. The first quarter ended with the score still Bills 7, Jets 0. The Jets had the ball in Bills territory. On third down and 14 the Jets did a Jets thing, throwing well short of the sticks to Mason Taylor. They settled for a short field goal to make the score 7 – 3 in favor of the Bills. Shades of last week against the Chiefs when the Jets constantly settled for field goals against a team they knew would score often against them. Trying to make the score respectable rather than trying to win. The Bills came right back with a scoring drive of their own. They narrowly missed a touchdown when James Cook dropped a perfect pass that likely would have ended in Cook scoring. Instead the Bills settled for a field goal and a 10 – 3 lead midway through the second quarter. Neither team got anything going again on offense until the Jets put together a drive featuring some nice Geno Smith to Garrett Wilson connections late in the quarter. The drive stalled inside the Bills 20 yard line and the Jets settled for another field goal with less than 20 seconds left in the half. The Jets went into the locker room trailing the Bills 10 – 6. The Jets opened the third quarter on offense. Geno Smith was on the sideline with an injury he incurred at he end of the first half. Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut at quarterback for the Jets. Klubnik put together a nice drive to open the second half, using his legs to run for a couple of first downs and finding Garrett Wilson for a long completion. Unfortunately, the drive stalled deep in Bills territory. The Jets had to again settle for a field goal, making the score Bills 10, Jets 9. The Jets momentum was fleeting. The Bills answered with a quick touchdown drive highlighted by a long catch and run by Dalton Kincaid. Josh Allen finished the drive by running it into the end zone and the Bills led 17 – 9. On the ensuing Jets drive Cade Klubnik exited and Geno Smith returned. Smith led the Jets on another drive that stalled deep in Bills territory. Jason Sanders hit his fourth field goal of the game, making the score 17 – 12 in favor of the Bills late in the third quarter. Again, the Jets momentum was fleeting. The Bills quickly struck back. James Cook ripped a 22 yard run, then Josh Allen hit D.J. Moore on a 45 yard bomb for a touchdown. Two plays, less than a minute and the Bills were in the end zone. The Bills were pulling away at 24 – 12 late in the third quarter. Cade Klubnik re-entered the game at this point, replacing an injured Geno Smith. Klubnik quickly threw his first NFL interception, but on a wild play the Jets got the ball back as Jeremy Ruckert forced a fumble and the Jets recovered the ball. The drive then went nowhere and the Jets were forced to punt. The fourth quarter opened with the Bills on offense deep in their own territory. Josh Allen threw a long pass that was intercepted by Azareye’h Thomas and the Jets had some life with 13 minutes remaining in the game. Unfortunately, Thomas was injured on the play. It would take a big comeback by the rookie Cade Klubnik and company, but the Jets had a little life. It didn’t last. The two teams exchanged drives going nowhere. Then the Jets put together a nice drive, getting deep in Bills territory before a hook and ladder play went awry. Garrett Wilson fumbled the lateral as he was getting tackled and the Bills recovered. On the next play James Cook broke a run for a 74 yard touchdown as the Bills put the final nail in the Jets coffin. The Bills led 31 – 12 with just under five minutes left in the game. The game ended a few minutes later without another score. Final score: Bills 31, Jets 12. The loss brought the Jets’ record to 2-8. One more loss and the Jets will have their 11th straight losing season to go along with their 16th straight season without the playoffs. Aaron Glenn is now 0-9 in the AFC East and 5-22 overall. The Jets are on the road the next two weeks against the Los Angeles Chargers and the Miami Dolphins. The weaker opponents give the Jets a shot at a victory or two before they get their bye week in Week 13. However, the Jets are in no position to take anything for granted against any opponent. We’ll see what kind of fight the team still has in them over the next couple of weeks.

title: Jets vs Bills Pre-Blame Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 8: Head Coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets speaks to Minkah Fitzpatrick #29 prior to an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. Today, for the second straight game, we’re handing out a pre-blame ball. It’s difficult to see a plausible Jets path to victory against the 7-1 Buffalo Bills, so pre-blame ball it is. The pre-blame ball for the Jets game against the Bills goes to (drum roll please) – Minkah Fitzpatrick! The Bills have a balanced and formidable offense. Josh Allen is as good a passer as any quarterback in the NFL. He also is one of the best running quarterbacks in the NFL. James Cook is one of the best running backs in the NFL. Through the air or on the ground, it doesn’t matter, the Bills can crush it. They field the best offense in the NFL in terms of yards gained and points scored. The defensive guys who have major responsibilities against the running game and the passing game tend to be the safeties more than anyone else. Minkah Fitzpatrick has responsibilities in the box and on the deep end of the Jets defense. Lately he has seemed to be mailing it in, making “business decisions” to not hustle. He is the latest in a long line of Jets mercenaries who grasp at one last paycheck with both hands, then choose not to earn it. That approach is great for the mercenary’s portfolio, not so great for the Jets. With Minkah being counted on in so many ways for this Jets defense, his failures have major consequences on game day. This seems like a nightmare matchup for a Jets defense that has struggled this season. Try to take away the pass and James Cook and Josh Allen will take it to you on the ground. Try to stop the run and Allen will light it up through the air. Don’t try at all, ala Minkah, and it will be a very long day indeed. Minkah, you stinkah, come on down! You’ve been singled out for blame before the first snap is taken. Let’s see you prove me wrong. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game or pre-blame ball to? Let us know in the comments.

title: Jets fans aren’t ready for Cade Klubnik yet
