full_text: Nov 1, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets quarterback Cade Klubnik (10) practices before the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jets have watched their season fall apart over the last three weeks. The team now sits at 2-7 with a daunting game against Buffalo in front of it. At this point in a lost season, fans frequently are ready to see a younger quarterback go into the lineup and get some reps. Most Jets fans haven’t reached that point, though, at least according to our most recent SB Nation Reacts poll. We asked whether it was Cade Klubnik time. A majority of fans who voted said they didn’t think putting in the fourth round rookie was the right move. While this might sound somewhat surprising on the surface, I think fans are making one simple consideration. Geno Smith hasn’t played badly enough to deserve a benching. Frequently when a season falls apart, the quarterback has done enough to lose his job. That has not yet been the case in New York. In other news, Jets fan confidence stayed stable despite a blowout loss in Kansas City. A week ago that number was 30 percent. I can only assume fan optimism is about the future. This should be an exciting offseason as the Jets are set to be flush with cap space and Draft picks. Unfortunately we must get through the second half of a pretty dismal season first before the fun. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! A.J. Brown looked really good for the Patriots against the Eagles in training camp. But he’s been pretty bad since getting banged up in Week 1. He hasn’t been able to get healthy and Pats fans seem to be wondering if he might be cooked at this point. Brown’s 26 targets this season have resulted in just 11 receptions for 128 yards (11.6 average). As a reminder, the Eagles will receive the Patriots’ 2027 fifth-round pick (which will become increasingly favorable for Philly as New England continues to lose) and their 2028 first-round pick from the Brown trade. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Lions – Pats Pulpit The A.J. Brown trade keeps looking worse by the day. A.J. Brown’s inability to do anything positive this year has been almost laughable. He got hurt in the first game, missed a good chunk of time on injured reserve, came back, was a non-factor, and then got hurt again. He returned on Sunday, was unable to get open and had a drop as well. He finally made a nice catch-and-run to move the stick on a third down, and then promptly went to the locker room with a hamstring injury. It’s been a rough year for Brown, and the Patriots front office: they effectively bid against themselves to trade for him and still gave up a first-round pick in 2028 to do so. Unless he somehow manages a complete 180, the trade is going to go down as a massive failure, and potentially hamstring the Patriots for years to come. Howie Roseman seen chatting up one of the top quarterback draft prospects – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles are on their bye this weekend and Howie Roseman is spending part of the team’s time off by attending Saturday’s college football game between Duke and the University of Miami. This isn’t necessarily a formal scouting trip for Roseman; his son, Jake, attends Duke and contributes to the Blue Devils’ football program. The Eagles’ general manager could be there to primarily spend time with family. That being said, it is interesting to see that Roseman was chatting it up with one of the top prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft. Here’s a video of him meeting with Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah during pregame warmups. Eagles rookie progress reports, midway through the season – PhillyVoice There have been a lot of excuses made for Makai Lemon’s low impact rookie season, some of which are valid, in my opinion, but some of which are not. Certainly, he is playing in a non-functional offense getting targets from Tanner McKee and Joe Milton. That’s valid. However, I’ve seen a number of Eagles fans cite a stat from PFF that says that Lemon has a high “separation percentage.” If you’ve seen this stat and have been encouraged by it, I hate to yuck your yum but there may not be a more useless metric in the NFL statistical zeitgeist. Here were PFF’s “separation percentage” leaders in 2025. It’s a “who’s who” of low impact receivers. I mean, JAHAN DOTSON (!) was in the top 10, lol. […] Lemon is not Jalen Reagor. But he is also not Amon-Ra St. Brown. If his drop issues are just a short-term rookie issue, then he can grow into a useful, gritty chain mover / frisky blocker from the slot in an efficient offense. However, I just don’t see a lot of explosiveness, and I do think his ceiling is capped by the combination of that and his lack of size. Examining Howie Roseman’s Eagles bye week: From trading Jordan Davis to watching Miami-Duke – The Athletic Moro Ojomo hasn’t shown it with sacks this season — and the sacks need to come — but the advanced pass-rushing data is encouraging. He leads the Eagles with 16 hurries and is tied for a team-high with 21 pressures. His pressure rate of 9.6 percent is down from 11.6 percent last season and 12.2 percent in 2024, but it’s still a strong rate for an interior rusher. His pressure rate and quarterback hit rate of 2.3 percent are both better than Carter and Davis. He also has the type of football character and work ethic worthy of an investment, and would fit on even fronts if the Eagles changed defensive schemes. The Eagles lost a respected locker-room figure with Davis’ departure, but I’d feel comfortable entrusting Ojomo with a bigger presence. He’s already called “Coach Mo” among the defensive linemen. The Eagles will have to pay a high price to keep him. It’s the type of move Roseman should feel comfortable making. It might even take off some of the sting of losing Milton Williams two years ago. NFL playoff chance tiers: Where all 32 teams fit in 2026 postseason picture – ESPN Tier 8: Just rest up for 2027. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Chances to make the playoffs: 0.3%. Fret not, Eagles fans, because if there’s one thing Philadelphia does better than any other team in the league, it’s taking advantage of the opportunity a losing season provides. Recognizing that they had virtually no shot at the playoffs with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles made some amazing pre-deadline trades, somehow getting a second-round pick (plus a Day 3 pick swap!) for center Cam Jurgens and first- and second-round picks for Jordan Davis. Admittedly, it wasn’t all his fault, which is why we will talk about the entire offense here. The Steelers’ passing game is incredibly limited, and not really built to play against teams like Cincinnati that can light up the scoreboard. Their receivers struggle to separate, and that won’t get better over the course of their last eight games. The Bengals were more than prepared for the Steelers’ run game, which they didn’t even try to establish until they were already down multiple scores. From the quarterback to the playmakers to the coaching, something is going to need to change drastically to take this team seriously against any quality competition. Giants vs. Jaguars odds: Opening lines for Week 11 matchup – Big Blue View The New York Giants will open Week 11 as 6.5-point underdogs at home against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per FanDuel. This game has been penciled in as a loss for the Giants for weeks now, and it shouldn’t be much of a surprise to anyone paying attention that the 5-3-1 Giants are (nearly) touchdown underdogs to the 7-2 Jaguars. The Giants are coming off of a disappointing, and frustrating, loss to the Washington Commanders, squandering a golden opportunity to put the NFC East in a strangle hold and cement their position as a playoff contender. The Giants had multiple opportunities to put the game away, and instead played to not-lose on offense and defense — only to lose anyway. 4 losers and 2 winners from the Cowboys loss to the 49ers – Blogging The Boys Christian Parker. When you give up 584 yards on offense, you have to be on the losing end of things. We will stipulate that some of that yardage wasn’t directly on Parker, but the buck ultimately stops with the defensive coordinator. The Cowboys found themselves over-pursuing, missing tackles, and losing players in coverage – it was bad. The Cowboys did some good things on defense, but in a crucial moment they had Von Miller covering Christian McCaffrey. That can’t happen. […] Dak Prescott (with context). He was excellent then. But earlier in the game, he wasn’t as sharp. Where Washington…

title: Eagles News: Is Philadelphia going to lose out?
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles’ remaining games following the bye: vs. Steelers, at Cowboys, at Cardinals, vs. Colts, vs. Seahawks, vs. Texans, at 49ers, at Giants. They might be able to win one during the two-game stretch against Arizona and Indy. It’s also possible […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni looks on during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles’ remaining games following the bye: vs. Steelers, at Cowboys, at Cardinals, vs. Colts, vs. Seahawks, vs. Texans, at 49ers, at Giants. They might be able to win one during the two-game stretch against Arizona and Indy. It’s also possible that the G-Men are resting their starters in Week 18. If the Eagles don’t win again, they’d finish the season on a 15-game losing streak, four longer than the current franchise record for in-season consecutive losses. 15 straight losses would also be one game longer than the biggest losing streak in franchise history (accounting for across multiple seasons). History is on the line. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Kracz: Examining Eagles’ Chances of Avoiding a 15-Game Losing Streak to End the Season – SI It’s a question I’ve been asked a lot during the bye week: Will the Eagles win another game this year? My guess is they will, but not many. Losing out wouldn’t be so terrible, though, because it would ensure a top-five draft pick this spring and heighten a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman secure a top-five draft choice this spring and accelerate a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman put in place with savvy moves to acquire plenty of draft capital over the next three drafts. There’s time to debate the course of action the general manager and his staff will take in the 2027 draft, and there will be plenty of discussion. Right now, it’s about finding a way to stem what could be a soul-sucking 15-game losing streak to close out the season. The losing streak wouldn’t break an NFL record because two teams—the Lions and Browns—had 0-16 seasons. Roob’s Eagles Observations: Time to turn to a Stout disciple who’s already here? – NBCSP CAN THE EAGLES LOSE OUT? How rare would it be for the Eagles to lose out after opening the season 2-0? Incredibly rare. Only one team in the last 84 years has won its first two games and not won another. That was the 2013 Texans – a team covered by Dave Zangaro for CSN Houston – who beat the Chargers and Titans to open the season, then lost 14 straight by an average of 11 ½ points to finish 2-14. The only other teams to lose out after a 2-0 start were the 1924 Dayton Triangles, who beat the Frankford Yellow Jackets and Buffalo Bisons before losing their last eight games to finish 2-8, and the 1941 Cleveland Rams, who opened with wins over the Steelers and Cardinals before losing their last 10 and finishing 2-10. Since 1942, 471 teams have opened a season 2-0, and 470 of them have won at least one more game the rest of the season. Can the Eagles really lose their last 15 games? Have you watched them lately? 3 Eagles tidbits coming out of the NFL trade deadline – BGN NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport shared an NFL trade deadline notebook on ESPN that featured several mentions of the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s take a look at those here. Young Guns – Iggles Blitz LB – Jihaad Campbell was up and down before a knee injury cost him to miss a few games. He’s got 49 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PD, 1 TFL, and 1 QB hit. Campbell has had issues on run defense. He gets tuck on blocks way too much. Campbell has been up and down in coverage. The Eagles put him in some tough situations to try and take advantage of his athleticism. Some of his coverage numbers are misleading because of that. Jeremiah Trotter Jr has started three games and is playing the best football of his career. He’s got 51 tackles, 2 QB hits, 1 PD, 3 TFLs, and half a sack. I thought teams might test him in coverage since that isn’t Trot’s strength. That hasn’t been an issue so far. The Eagles have blitzed him a decent amount, which is a way to limit exposing him in coverage. Trot is a good run defender. He is at his best attacking downhill and getting into the backfield. He is physical and tackles well. I love the emotion and intensity he plays with. I think he can be a starting LB. Smael Mondon got to play when Zack Baun got hurt last week. Mondon did well for a guy thrust into duty. He tackled well and showed good potential in coverage. Mondon is a good backup and STer. He could develop into a starter in time. The things to watch if he does play some more are run fits and shedding blocks. If he can be a solid run defender, Mondon could be an effective starter. NFL tells Senator that Jalen Hurts review will include “mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts” – PFT It’s still unclear how the investigation will proceed or what it will entail. The NFLPA has not yet invoked its absolute right to launch an investigation under Article 39 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement as the communications with the league continue. The ensuing delay is approaching the status of “head scratching.” With games being played every Thursday, Sunday, and Monday, there’s a constant risk of a similar situation arising. The sooner the Hurts situation is properly explored and any lessons learned from it are put into action, the sooner all players will benefit from any enhanced protections. The Eagles and the league created widespread skepticism regarding whether a coverup is happening. (The NFL may not appreciate that being said, but that doesn’t make the perception inaccurate.) The NFLPA can’t afford to be viewed as being complicit in an effort to sweep the incident under the rug. Dr. Gary Dorshimer, longtime doctor who worked for Penn, several Philadelphia sports teams, dies – CBS News Dr. Gary Dorshimer, who worked at Penn Medicine and multiple Philadelphia sports teams, died Saturday. Dorshimer was the medical director for the Flyers, the assistant primary care sports medicine physician with the Sixers and the team sports medicine physician with the Union. “Dr. Dorshimer took exceptional care of our players and their families, coaches and entire staff over the span of several decades and was always on call whenever the team needed him,” Dan Hilferty, the CEO of Comcast Spectacor and Flyers governor, said in a statement in part. “His combination of wit and humor always brought a smile to the countless number of athletes in the city that he treated and helped perform at their best.” The Sixers said Dorshimer was a “beloved member of our athlete care team and the Penn Medicine family.” Dorshimer also served as the Eagles’ head internist for nearly two decades. The team said it “extends its condolences to his friends and family.” Patriots inactives for NFL Week 10 vs. Lions – Pats Pulpit The New England Patriots offense received some good news ahead of its game against the Detroit Lions on Sunday. Wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson have both been given the green light for the game, despite originally being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report. 49ers checked in on veteran Eagles tight end; Mac Jones asking price was too rich for the Vikings – Niners Nation Goedert has lined up as an inline tight end 48.7% of the time this year, compared to 38.1% in the slot. I think these moves tell us the 49ers were looking to get another big body to pair with George Kittle, who they can throw the ball to. He’s been a serviceable blocker, but Luke Farrell only has six targets this season. Goedert had six targets in Week 9. Bengals could end up with more egg on their face from Arnold Ebiketie trade debacle – Cincy Jungle And now it gets worse (maybe). The Seattle Seahawks signed former Bengals guard Cordell Volson to their practice squad. If he were to make the active roster and play enough snaps as a starter for the Seahawks, he could, potentially, count as a compensatory free…

Therefore, the Eagles want the Jags to lose as much as possible. The Eagles also want to move ahead of the Titans in the draft order, so, Tennessee winning would be very preferable. Root for the Titans. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at DETROIT LIONS: Thanks to the A.J. Brown trade, the Eagles own the more favorable of either New England’s or Chicago’s 2027 fifth-round pick. However, the Pats are currently the No. 7 seed in the AFC playoff picture. And the Eagles should want to see the Jags fall out of playoff position. That becomes more possible with New England winning here. Root for the Patriots. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS at BALTIMORE RAVENS: Two reasons to root for the Bolts: 1) the Eagles want to move ahead of LAC in the draft order and 2) thanks to the Cam Jurgens trade, the Eagles own Baltimore’s fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Root for the Chargers. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS at ATLANTA FALCONS: The Eagles want to stay ahead of the Falcons in the draft order. Root for the Falcons. HOUSTON TEXANS at CLEVELAND BROWNS: Based on current draft position, the Texans are the bigger threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order. Also, Houston has the best chance of any non-Jags team to win the AFC South. And the Eagles want the Jags to not win their division. Root for the Texans. MINNESOTA VIKINGS at GREEN BAY PACKERS: The Vikings probably have a higher chance of bottoming out and going on a losing streak due to their questionable offensive outlook, even after the Kirk Cousins trade. So, could be good to see them win here, though it doesn’t look like it currently matters much. Root for the Vikings. MIAMI DOLPHINS at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS: The Dolphins have the fifth-toughest remaining strength of schedule while the Colts have the fourth-easiest schedule. Comparatively speaking, this is a rarer opportunity for Miami to get a win that can help move the Eagles above the Dolphins in the draft order. Root for the Dolphins. CAROLINA PANTHERS at NEW ORLEANS SAINTS: Whichever team you think has the lower floor, you want them to win, because they’re the bigger threat to moving ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. I think that’s the Saints, who are worse by point differential/DVOA/weighted EPA per play. Root for the Saints. BUFFALO BILLS at NEW YORK JETS: The Eagles want to stay ahead of the Jets’ own selection (currently No. 6, one spot behind the Birds) in the draft order. Root for the Jets. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS at LAS VEGAS RAIDERS: The Raiders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Raiders. LOS ANGELES RAMS at ARIZONA CARDINALS: The Cardinals are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Cardinals. SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS at DALLAS COWBOYS: I know it’s not fun to see the Cowboys win. But Dallas, which owes the more favorable of two first-round picks (either their own, most likely … or Green Bay’s) to the Jets, is the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Also, I think Eagles fans can agree it would be nice to see the Niners not get the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoff picture. And, once again, it’s preferable for the Giants to not just run away with the NFC East since they might be able to rest starters against the Eagles in Week 18. Root for the Cowboys. Then take a shower. PITTSBURGH STEELERS at CINCINNATI BENGALS: The Jags are currently No. 3 in the AFC playoff picture with a conference games win percentage tiebreaker over the No. 4 Steelers. Pittsburgh plays the Jags later this season, however, so there’s still a chance for the Steelers to earn a head-to-head tiebreaker over Jacksonville. The Bengals, meanwhile, already lost to the Jags. Since it could be easier for the Steelers to move ahead of the Jags in the playoff picture, it’s best to see them win in this spot. Root for the Steelers. title: Steelers stock report after 38-18 loss to the Bengals
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers were absolutely dominated by the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football by a score of 38-18. The final score doesn’t do it justice, as Pittsburgh scored most of their points after the game was already out of reach. The Bengals outgained the Steelers by 241 yards and picked up 30 first downs […]
full_text: (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers were absolutely dominated by the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football by a score of 38-18. The final score doesn’t do it justice, as Pittsburgh scored most of their points after the game was already out of reach. The Bengals outgained the Steelers by 241 yards and picked up 30 first downs compared to Pittsburgh’s 17. As always, here is my weekly stock report from the Steelers’ third loss of the season. Stock Up The Doubters Well, this game does not bode well for the Steelers’ chances at winning the AFC North. The Steelers were outplayed and outcoached for three straight hours on Sunday Night. The Steelers’ lack of weapons and overall passing game showed up big in this one. It certainly didn’t help that their defense did not show up in this one either. LB’s Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen On a night where not much went right at any phase, I came away feeling fairly positively about the linebackers. Queen posted the Steelers’ lone sack of the contest. Wilson was all over the field and once again led the team in tackles. Both Queen and Wilson continue to put together their best season in black and gold under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. Stock Down CB Asante Samuel Jr. Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense threw the ball all around the yard. Rookie third-round pick Daylen Everette eventually replaced Samuel Jr. in the third quarter. Samuel Jr. returned to the field in the fourth quarter, where he promptly let up a 42-yard catch to Ja’Marr Chase. The Steelers traded their best corner early in the season and did nothing to address it at the deadline, tonight was a cold reminder of that. Pass Rush The Steelers’ blitz had been dominant over the course of their four-game winning streak, but that was far from the case tonight. Joe Burrow was able to quickly diagnose the blitz and pick apart the Steelers’ secondary. What was a reliable formula so far this season was not the answer tonight, as Burrow finished the game with 409 yards and four passing touchdowns. Offensive Firepower Aaron Rodgers started this game 0/7 passing. Admittedly, it wasn’t all his fault, which is why we will talk about the entire offense here. The Steelers’ passing game is incredibly limited, and not really built to play against teams like Cincinnati that can light up the scoreboard. Their receivers struggle to separate, and that won’t get better over the course of their last eight games. The Bengals were more than prepared for the Steelers’ run game, which they didn’t even try to establish until they were already down multiple scores. From the quarterback to the playmakers to the coaching, something is going to need to change drastically to take this team seriously against any quality competition. title: Mike McCarthy: Loss to Bengals ‘not to the standard of the Pittsburgh Steelers’
summary: An unsurprisingly brief Steelers postgame press conference following a 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday Night Football yielded similar answers from Pittsburgh’s head coach and players: One team executed. The other did not. One team got out to a fast start. The other did not. And the final result, no matter how ugly, wouldn’t […]
full_text: Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images | Getty Images An unsurprisingly brief Steelers postgame press conference following a 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday Night Football yielded similar answers from Pittsburgh’s head coach and players: One team executed. The other did not. One team got out to a fast start. The other did not. And the final result, no matter how ugly, wouldn’t define the rest of the season. “That’s very dramatic,” quarterback Aaron Rodgers quipped postgame when asked how to keep the 20-point loss from damaging the Steelers’ trajectory. Still, no football platitudes could mask what was an undeniably disappointing end result for the once high-flying Steelers, who entered Sunday’s game with the same record as the 6-2 Bengals. Pittsburgh was coming off a bye week with a chance to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North on the momentum of a four-game winning streak. Instead, the Steelers fell flat in the biggest game of their season thus far. “Handling success is the biggest challenge in this league, and you come off the bye week, you worry about a letdown — I’ve seen it happen before, been a part of it,” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. “But give credit to the Bengals, they played extremely well — they played the game they wanted to play, and we didn’t get the game headed in the direction we wanted to play.” While the Steelers had already lost two games in 2026 entering the Bengals matchup, including a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots in Week 2, the result in Cincinnati was by far the most lopsided defeat the black and gold have endured all year. By halftime, the Bengals had already pulled ahead, up 24-7. “This is the first time we’ve been through one of these (losses) as a football team,” McCarthy said. “So, it’s gonna be an experience to go through it, correct it, and (see) how fast we move through that process and get on to (Week 11’s matchup versus) Philadelphia, a game where we have to get on a winning track.” Pittsburgh has rebounded from both of its prior losses this season with wins, but each time, a tough road loss was followed by a matchup at home. Next week, Pittsburgh will face a team with a 2-7 record in the Eagles, but it will be on the road in Philadelphia, a city the Steelers haven’t won in since the 1960s. But will there be any carryover, good or bad, from the Steelers’ Week 10 to Week 11? “No … It starts over every single week,” Rodgers said. However, McCarthy emphasized that Sunday’s result wasn’t what he wanted his team looking like at midseason with playoff seeding looming. “That’s clearly not to the standard of the Pittsburgh Steelers; it’s not to any of our expectations,” he said following the loss. “You had two teams that were playing good football over the month of October that came in here tonight. And being on the road, there were some things mechanically and operational that we were not on top of — we’re too far in the season for that.”

title: Steelers suffer blowout loss to Bengals, fall to 6-3
summary: In what was a game that displayed a severe gap between playoff hopefuls and true Super Bowl contenders, the Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18. At 7-2, the Bengals now have possession of first place in the AFC North, while Pittsburgh falls to 6-3. The Bengals started the game with the ball, marching 80 […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what was a game that displayed a severe gap between playoff hopefuls and true Super Bowl contenders, the Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18. At 7-2, the Bengals now have possession of first place in the AFC North, while Pittsburgh falls to 6-3. The Bengals started the game with the ball, marching 80 yards in nine plays before three straight incompletions forced them to settle for a field goal. The Steelers answered with a three-and-out, and the Bengals then put together a second consecutive 13-play drive that resulted in a Joe Burrow touchdown pass to Drew Sample, one of four on the night for Burrow. The Steelers then went three-and-out again, and were given a gift in the form of an Evan McPherson missed field goal to keep the game at 10-0, but the offense did nothing with the chance to remain in the game, going 11 yards in five plays before punting. The Bengals then stepped on the throat of Pittsburgh, as Burrow found Chase Brown for a two-yard score to put Cincinnati up 17-0. The Steelers then put together their first real drive of the game, driving 42 yards in 10 plays to set up a Chris Boswell field goal to cut the lead to 17-3. However, the 1:25 left on the clock was more than enough for the Bengals. Burrow led a 57-yard drive that saw Dohnte Meyers catch Burrow’s third touchdown pass of the night to go up 24-3 at the half. In the third quarter, the Steelers lost four yards on seven plays to open the second half before punting. The Bengals answered with a Joe Burrow touchdown pass to Chase Brown, his second on the night, to go up 31-3. Pittsburgh would finally put a touchdown on the board with Aaron Rodgers finding DK Metcalf for a 22-yard score. Metcalf also caught the two-point conversion to make it a 31-11 game. The Bengals erased that score in just over two minutes, driving 49 yards in four plays before Samaje Perine scored to make it 38-11. A Pat Freiermuth touchdown ended the scoring, giving Cincinnati a 38-18 win. There were plenty of noteworthy numbers that best describe just how outmatched the Steelers were. At one point in the game, the Bengals had 356 net passing yards to the Steelers’ 4. Of the game’s first 28 plays, 25 of them were run by the Bengals’ offense. Ja’Marr Chase had more receiving yards (231) than the Steelers had total yards (221). The Steelers averaged just 3.8 yards per play, a number that saw a bump in garbage time, compared to the Bengals’ 7.4. Pittsburgh will now take their 6-3 record to Philadelphia in Week 11, a place they haven’t won in 61 years. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers and Bengals final score has never happened before
summary: On Sunday, we saw two scores that have never happened in the history of the NFL. On Sunday afternoon, the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers were the 1099th and on Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers played to the 1100th. It’s the second time this season we’ve had two Scorigamis in one […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Ja'marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs the ball after a catch against Asante Samuel Jr. #22 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the fourth quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, we saw two scores that have never happened in the history of the NFL. On Sunday afternoon, the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers were the 1099th and on Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers played to the 1100th. It’s the second time this season we’ve had two Scorigamis in one weekend. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami . Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. We got both on Sunday with the Bengals and Steelers. The Bengals took a big lead on Pittsburgh in the fourth quarter, but it was a pretty typical 28-point, four-touchdown lead. Nothing weird. Then the Pittsburgh Steelers scored a touchdown and went for two. If turned a three-touchdown deficit into a… three-touchdown deficit. Really not sure when the Steelers chose to do it. That 31-11 score would have been a Scorigami, too. After the Bengals scored to make it 38-11, that would not have been a Scorigami but the Steelers scored one more time to make it 38-18. That threaded the needle. The only 38-point winners that haven’t hit now are 38-2 and 38-4. Our friends at Secret Base have done extensive work on Scorigami. If you want to see it, it is fascinating. 2026 NFL Scorigamis This is the fifth Scorigami of the 2026 NFL season. September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37 September 13: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22 November 1: Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 November 15: San Francisco 49ers 46, Dallas Cowboys 40 November 15: Cincinnati Bengals 38, Pittsburgh Steelers 18 During the 2025 season we saw four Scorigamis: Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 Bills beat Ravens 41-40 Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 Texans beat Jaguars 36-29

Oh man that ankle does not look good with McCormick. #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/2eV3v410wU — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) November 16, 2026 His leg was placed in an air cast according to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Ray Fittipaldo , and McCormick was carted off the field. title: Steelers vs. Bengals: Week 10 game picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will close the Week 10 Sunday slate on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the day at 6-2, with the Steelers holding the division lead by way of a tiebreaker due to winning the first matchup between these teams in Week 3. Will they be able to complete the […]
full_text: (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will close the Week 10 Sunday slate on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the day at 6-2, with the Steelers holding the division lead by way of a tiebreaker due to winning the first matchup between these teams in Week 3. Will they be able to complete the season sweep, or will the Bengals take over as the leaders in the AFC North? Our staff weighs in. Austin Bechtold: This game could very likely be for the AFC North, despite it only being Week 10. Joe Burrow is the NFL MVP to this point and out for revenge against the Steelers defense. Even when the Bengals are one-dimensional, they still find ways to attack opposing defenses with ease. This is going to be a close game and a good game, but I won’t punish the Steelers for losing unless they turn it over multiple times. I expect a good game from Aaron Rodgers, Jaylen Warren, and Germie Bernard to score a touchdown, but can Rodgers win a shootout against Burrow once again? I would not be stunned if the Steelers win, but very impressed and proves the team is for real. This is a key game and indicator of what the Steelers are going to be to end the season. Bengals 31, Steelers 28. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers enter this matchup well-rested following their bye week, while the Bengals are coming off an international game in Madrid. Pittsburgh should have a freshness advantage, but it will face a difficult challenge against a Cincinnati offense that has the firepower to put up points in a hurry. If this game is anything like their first meeting, fans can expect plenty of offensive fireworks. However, Pittsburgh’s best approach should be to establish the running game early and lean heavily on Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle. Controlling the clock and keeping Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ explosive offense on the sideline will be critical to the Steelers’ chances of pulling off a road victory. In their first meeting, Cincinnati made several costly mistakes that ultimately helped Pittsburgh secure the win. A special teams fumble and a late-game fumble by Burrow proved particularly damaging. The latter was forced by defensive lineman Derrick Harmon, who could potentially make his return to the lineup for this matchup. His presence would provide a boost to a Pittsburgh defense looking to disrupt Burrow and limit Cincinnati’s offensive production. Ultimately, I don’t believe the Steelers have enough offensive firepower to keep pace with the Bengals in their home stadium. Even with the benefit of extra rest, Pittsburgh will have its hands full trying to contain Cincinnati’s offense for four quarters. Bengals 27, Steelers 24 . Jason Aponte: It will be close, but the Steelers’ defense is able to stop a final attempt at a comeback on the game’s final drive to steal a close win and sweep the Bengals. Steelers 27, Bengals 24. Ryland Bickley: This game is a tough one to call. Obviously, the Steelers have what it takes to defeat the Bengals, as evidenced by the last time these two teams met, but with both teams playing good football at this point in the season, it feels like a series that should split. Cincinnati’s offense has scored 30-plus in its last four games, with a high-flying passing attack that’s more than capable of exposing the Steelers’ secondary. However, although the Bengals defense has been more competent this year with the addition of Dexter Lawrence, Pittsburgh scored 30 points off 411 yards of offense the last time it faced the Cincinnati defense. While the score is hard to predict, offensive fireworks from both sides feel like a safe bet. Ultimately, I’ll take the Bengals in a close game as I have more trust in the offense with Burrow/Higgins/Chase to win in a shootout. Either way, this looks like a fun divisional game on paper. Bengals 31, Steelers 30 . Ryan Parish : The Steelers-Bengals first matchup marked a turning point for Pittsburgh. They changed the right side of their offensive line, they changed the run schemes they are leaning into, and have only lost once in the time since. Cincy has also been winning, though in the same ways we’re used to: airing it out with Burrow, Chase and Higgins, with a little Mike Gesicki sprinkled in. The winner of this game walks away the division leader and in the drivers seat. With a win the Steelers would have the season sweep and hold the tiebreaker over Cincy. That said, my running bit of picking against them is still working, so we shan’t be changing now. Bengals 31, Steelers 28 . Joey Bray : oey Bray: This is easily the most consequential AFC North game of the season, the Steelers and Bengals have established themselves as the healthiest and best overall teams in the division. That being said, all of the pressure is on the Bengals to avenge their Week 3 loss to the Steelers. The Steelers are 6-3 against Cincy in their last nine meetings. Both teams come into the contest riding four game win streaks. A stat that sticks out to me is that the Bengals have yet to defeat a team with a winning record this season. However, their offense has been humming, as they continue to rely on Joe Burrow who is on pace for nearly 5,000 passing yards and over 40 touchdowns. The Steelers have proven that their defense can come up in big moments to stop even the best offenses in the league like Cincy. However, with the home crowd backing them and the team playing better football than they were in Week 3, I’ll take the Bengals to get their revenge on the Steelers and take control of the AFC North. Bengals 28, Steelers 24 . Jarrett Bailey: It’s hard to see the Steelers sweeping the Bengals. Their offense is clicking at an all-time rate right now. The last time they didn’t score 30 points was Week 4, while Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins have dominated over the course of the Bengals’ last three games. If the Steelers win, it will be because they were able to put together long drives by running the ball and playing the time of possession game. Pittsburgh’s defense is good enough to keep the scoring somewhat at bay, but the Bengals win. Bengals 26, Steelers 23. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Seahawks Droppings: Raiders first-round treasure sunk by Seahawks defense
summary: Everybody take a deep breath. Now exhale. Let that relaxation set in for the next two weeks as the Seattle Seahawks head into their bye on a two-game winning streak after coming alive in the second half in a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. It was one of those “get it done any […]
full_text: Everybody take a deep breath. Now exhale. Let that relaxation set in for the next two weeks as the Seattle Seahawks head into their bye on a two-game winning streak after coming alive in the second half in a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. It was one of those “get it done any way you can” games, with injuries piling up for Seattle. On the other side of the field was the No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza making his first start at quarterback, leading to a suddenly hot ticket in Sin City. Despite more injuries, turnovers, and a missed FG, Seattle found a way to get the win and now get a few weeks to regroup for the stretch run of the season. Seahawks Droppings Seattle’s defense started slow, then exploded. One would think that Mike Macdonald’s defense facing a rookie QB in his first start would mean a very rough day for Mendoza. It didn’t start out that way with two straight scoring drives given up by the Seahawks. Mendoza got the ball out quickly and accurately, and used his legs when needed to extend plays and get into the endzone. After those early drives, the Seahawks defense CLAMPED DOWN. At one point in the fourth quarter, the Raiders had -17 yards of offense in the second half. A stupid 38-yard pass play from Mendoza to Jeanty near the end of the fourth quarter bumped the numbers up for Mendoza, but he still finished with just 143 passing yards. The Seahawks sacked him six times for a staggering 45 yards lost! They also held the Raiders to 65 yards rushing for the game. That equates to 163 total yards for the suffocating Seattle defense. They didn’t force any turnovers, but the Raiders had nowhere to go after those first two drives. Seattle’s offense started slow, then exploded…mostly in the third quarter. Drew Lock was back in at QB, and Seattle had its one-two punch of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price at their disposal once again. Lock “fumbled” on the first offensive drive after it seemed like he was clearly trying to execute a basketball chest pass near a receiver’s feet to avoid a sack. The refs saw it differently, and it was still a poor decision on his part. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had a TD called back on a questionable offensive PI call and had a drop on a later third down. Everything just looked disjointed. Then, on a third and long, Lock rolled out, avoided a sack, stopped just short of the line of scrimmage and threw a long TD pass to Cooper Kupp. There wasn’t much after that until the third quarter where the Seahawks went wild mostly on the back of JSN. Lock found him in another scramble drill for a 71-yard TD, and the Seahawks also scored on Jadarian Price’s first NFL TD showing his burst to the outside. The offense went cold again in the fourth quarter when they had the chance to salt the game away, but Brian Fleury had maybe his best call of the game with the naked bootleg to essentially end the game. Seattle overcame a lot. Lock turned the ball over on the first drive. Abe Lucas got hurt early on leading to Bobby Hart playing RT after Josh Jones was already playing LT for the injured Charles Cross. That’s in addition to Quenton Nelson, Sam Darnold, Leo Williams also on the sidelines. The rest of the games where Seattle played like crap this season, they lost. To find a way to come away with a win when giving the other team extra chances and facing a litany of injuries – on the road no less – shows grit. The Turf Monster was busy. How many times did a Seahawks player eat dirt today after slipping on that terrible field? Charbonnet and Price both went down early multiple times. JSN actually fell down before he got loose for the 71-yard TD. Those are the worst field conditions I can remember seeing in the last number of years. I get it that the players want natural grass, but if that’s going to be the result, count me out. Spoon went blitz-crazy. Devon Witherspoon is a demon blitzing from his CB position. We saw him give Drake Maye fits in the Super Bowl, but he hasn’t been utilized that way as much as I anticipated this season. Until today. Spoon blitzed three times, and came away with 2.0 sacks and a QB hit on the third one. Each time, he hammered Mendoza and I can’t believe that he didn’t cough the ball up. Spoon is such a weapon and brings the juice for the whole defense. Stacking sacks. Spoon had 2.0 sacks, and the Seahawks defensive line added 4 more, one each from Derick Hall, DeMarcus Lawrence, Dante Fowler Jr, and Byron Murphy. They were a key to the second half surge against Mendoza and will look to keep the momentum going after the bye week, hopefully with Leo Williams added back into the mix. JSN. That’s it, I’m honestly running out of adjectives for his tremendous play. What can you say when a guy puts up 144 receiving yards in one quarter?? He finished with 8 catches for 178 yards and a TD. The rest of the team managed 6 catches for 69 yards. Can Seattle find someone else after the bye week to step up and take some pressure off of JSN? The running game is coming around. I shouldn’t have made it this far without mentioning the run game, but here we are. Am I crazy, or does Charbonnet actually look better now than he did before his injury? He runs ANGRY and is displaying great vision. Charbs finished with 20 carries for 94 yards and sent a bunch of dudes to the turf. Price only had 36 yards on 9 carries, yet got loose to the outside for his first TD. I’m still waiting on Price’s breakout game which I do think is coming. Still, with Charbs playing as well as he is, maybe it isn’t needed. Tory Horton made one of the coolest plays ever . Seriously, Horton skying to keep the ball in bounds on the kickoff, which was then returned by Rashid Shaheed to get the ball to the two-minute warning was awesome. It might not seem like a huge deal, but the Raiders weren’t dead at that point and still had 2 timeouts. With the two-minute warning, they could’ve stopped the clock three times and who knows what would’ve happened. Horton’s heady play put more pressure on the Raiders, and the Seahawks ended up icing the game away. Great stuff. With the way the Seahawks season has gone, getting to the bye week at 6-4 with a chance to heal up is just what they needed. We can all sit back and enjoy a stress-free few weeks until Seattle suits up again. Get healthy, continue to run the ball with authority, and play great defense. Everything is still there for Seattle, but it will take hard work and Seahawks Football.

title: Was Tory Horton’s heads-up play really a penalty? Here’s what the NFL rulebook says
summary: When the Las Vegas Raiders kicked the ball off to the Seattle Seahawks with a tick over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, the idea was to kick the ball through the back of the end zone so that they could preserve the two-minute warning and effectively have three timeouts remaining. Tory Horton had […]
full_text: When the Las Vegas Raiders kicked the ball off to the Seattle Seahawks with a tick over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, the idea was to kick the ball through the back of the end zone so that they could preserve the two-minute warning and effectively have three timeouts remaining. Tory Horton had other plans . One Of The Smartest Football Plays I Think I've Ever Seen. The Kick Was Headed To The Back Of The End Zone, But Tory Horton Tipped It So The Seahawks Could Return It. That Kept The Clock Running And Burned Past The Two-Minute Warning. This Effectively Almost Ends The Game. pic.twitter.com/JjsWymkt64 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 15, 2026 absolutely incredible. the Raiders boom the kickoff out of the end zone to keep the 2-minute warning in play. instead, Tory Horton gets up, swats it back into the field of play, and Las Vegas is down 8 with only two timeouts and under 2 minutes to play. AWESOME. pic.twitter.com/kHqgWOr5K7 — Christian D'Andrea (@TrainIsland) November 15, 2026 After a long conversation with Klint Kubiak and head referee Bill Vinovich, an announcement was made after the two-minute warning that the Raiders had declined the penalty. What penalty, you may ask? Illegal bat, which the Seahawks know a thing or two about from way back in the day… View Link Rules analyst Gene Steratore said on the CBS broadcast that “I don’t think it’s a foul. It’s a kick that never hits the ground. I believe you can bat a kick in the air provided that it has never hit the ground yet […] it’s a first for me though, fellas.” Well if the veteran official can’t commit to a ruling, maybe the rulebook provides some clarity. What constitutes an illegal bat? Based on Rule 12, Section 5, Article 1 of the current NFL rulebook , Horton illegally batted the ball. What I’ve highlighted is the most important part of the rule: No doubt that Horton “batted” the ball to keep it in play and it was in the direction of the Raiders end zone. And for those wondering about the “loose ball” rule… a kickoff in the air is still considered a loose ball. So that’s an open-and-shut case to me. Horton batted the ball forward and it didn’t matter that the ball hadn’t hit the ground yet. However, I want to shout out this comment we received from Leonson1 that made me think a little bit more. The “field of play” distinction Notice that the rule that Horton (presumably) violated was “loose ball in the field of play.” By the NFL’s definition, the “field of play” is only from goal line to goal line. The end zone is NOT part of the field of play , which is why certain plays are governed differently in the end zone than anywhere else on the field. Horton batted the ball in his own end zone aka not the “field of play.” So does the bat occurring in the end zone therefore negate the illegality? Is a loose ball in flight technically in the “field of play” because it never hit the ground? It can easily be interpreted that Horton batting the ball is legal because it occurred outside the field of play. Perhaps a loose ball in flight is officiated differently in terms of “field of play,” in which case maybe it was a penalty. This is such a rare, perhaps never before seen play that it’s actually understandable that this is not something that can be so quickly and accurately adjudicated. I suspect the competition committee may look at some clarifying language next offseason. The penalty didn’t matter because the Seahawks achieved their goal The Raiders were never getting the time back on the clock because of the penalty, which is why it was declined. The Sahawks accomplished their mission of taking away the two-minute stoppage. Seattle was backed up by five yards but it didn’t matter one bit. If you can fault the Raiders for anything, it’s not booting the ball out of bounds along the sidelines, because it’s not like starting at the 40 vs. 35 is all that big a deal. Ultimately, what Horton did was fantastic and making sure that Rashid Shaheed picked the ball up and got out of the end zone (which is when the clock is supposed to start) was also great thinking. No one else on the field is allowed to move until the ball is touched, so I doubt the Raiders would’ve hauled ass from the Seattle 40 to somehow get to the loose ball before Shaheed did. It was not as a risky as it was made out to be, and the Seahawks were able to get to victory formation in part because of Horton’s heroic heads-up moment.

title: Winners and Losers from the Seahawks’ much-needed road win over the Raiders
summary: The Seattle Seahawks had 30 minutes to arguably save their season after falling behind 10-7 to the Las Vegas Raiders at halftime. Given the deep nature of the NFC playoff picture, Seattle had little margin for error to lose too many more games, and especially not versus inferior (on paper) opposition. Mike Macdonald’s team locked […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks had 30 minutes to arguably save their season after falling behind 10-7 to the Las Vegas Raiders at halftime. Given the deep nature of the NFC playoff picture, Seattle had little margin for error to lose too many more games, and especially not versus inferior (on paper) opposition. Mike Macdonald’s team locked in after halftime and got the win they needed to stay afloat in the playoff race heading into their bye week. Let’s get to Winners and Losers from Seahawks 21, Raiders 13 ! Seattle Seahawks Winners Jaxon Smith-Njigba is incomparable You can take a TD away from JSN through a Super Bowl XL-esque “pushoff” penalty, but you can’t hold him down forever. JSN caught 8 passes for 171 yards and a 71-yard TD, and that’s with two explosive plays wiped out due to penalty and a drop. He could’ve easily broken 200 without much effort, which is ridiculous regardless of opposition. JSN is on pace for a 2,000-yard season and he has the Triple Crown lead over the rest of the NFL in yards, receptions, and touchdowns. When you’re the best in the business in a deep field of elite receivers, you’re special. JSN is one of a kind. Cooper Kupp does something he’s never done before It’s fitting that Seattle’s two slot machines scored touchdowns in Las Vegas. Kupp’s lone catch was a sliding grab for 34 yards on a scramble drill, marking the first time he’s ever caught a touchdown from a backup quarterback in his NFL career. That sounds nerdy and is partially down to the durability of Matthew Stafford, Jared Goff, and (well, at least until this season) Sam Darnold, but even great WRs occasionally get a garbage time TD from the backup. Jadarian Price is off the mark For the first time in his career, Jadarian Price is an NFL touchdown scorer. He had nine carries for 36 yards, showcasing his speed on his 12-yard touchdown run. Price also had a big kick return to start the game, although it was wasted on an opening drive fumble. There are ways for Price to get his touches without being the lead back, and he adds another splash play to his reel in the form of a TD. Zach Charbonnet gets some hard-earned yards The blocking wasn’t always there, but Charbonnet was on the cusp of his first 100-yard game since returning from injury. He had 94 yards on 20 carries, with several Raiders defenders left in the dust after he chucked them off of him. What sets him apart from Jadarian Price is his ability to drive forward after first contact more effectively than the rookie, and that’s one of the reason he’ll be RB1 moving forward. Drew Lock continues to be unbeatable Four games played, four wins for Drew Lock. In fact, when you add in his two starts in 2023 he has a 4-1 record as a starter and an unofficial 5-1 record as Seahawks QB. Lock was 14/17 for 240 yards and 2 TDs, and his numbers would’ve been better if not for a couple of negated plays via penalty. The first fumble was sloppy and not a smart play when a sack is totally fine, but the second fumble was unlucky. His biggest moment was lowering the shoulder and calling game on a bootleg run in the final minutes. Whether Lock starts after the bye or not, the important thing is that he’s comfortable in the offense and taking advantage of defenses he should be taking advantage of. He’s going to get significant money this offseason, whether it’s Seattle believing he might be the new long-term answer or some other team that sees Drew as a high-end bridge or “the next Sam Darnold” of sorts. This is the best Lock has ever been arguably in his entire career, irrespective of opponent. Devon Witherspoon is invaluable So what if Spoon doesn’t get interceptions? When you have a cornerback who can play slot or outside, defend the run as well as defend the pass, and blitz quarterbacks better than most linebackers, you’ve got yourself one hell of a chess piece. Witherspoon sacked Fernando Mendoza twice and is a total menace when anything is near the line of scrimmage. Byron Murphy II is halfway to his goal Big Murph has five sacks on the season, which leads the Seahawks. He wanted to reach 10 in his third year and he’s halfway there. Murphy’s run defense hasn’t always been strong this season, but he continues leveling up as a pass rusher. The edge rushers get it done Dante Fowler picked up his second sack in as many weeks, coming in unblocked on a blitz when Nick Emmanwori attacked the inside. DeMarcus Lawrence and Derick Hall both had sacks and several pressures of Fernando Mendoza. Fowler having any sort of positive contribution is welcome given his underwhelming start to the season, and if he’s going to keep having a low snap count then he might as well maximize his opportunities. Seattle’s secondary blankets Raiders’ outmatched receivers The Raiders don’t have a quality wide receiver group, with all due respect to Cody White and his one catch for 22 yards. When targeting wide receivers, Mendoza was 5/14 for 40 yards. Josh Jobe in particular had a fantastic performance and chipped in with two TFLs. Tory Horton’s 5D chess is part genius, part athletic brilliance For reasons already stated in this article , Horton basically cost the Raiders their two-minute warning timeout by saving a touchback. He channeled his inner Richard Sherman with “The Tip” to Rashid Shaheed, albeit one that’s an illegal bat by rule, and there went the Raiders’ ideal outcome. That was impressive. Bobby Hart gets the job done with Abe Lucas out I was a little worried when Bobby Hart had to sub in for Abe Lucas after his ankle injury. Hart’s last season starting with the Los Angeles Chargers was… brutal. Hart didn’t give up any pressures that I saw. If you can sub in and have to deal with Maxx Crosby and not be a disaster, that’s a win. Seattle Seahawks Losers Jason Myers with another missed kick Myers has missed at least a field goal or an extra point in four of his last seven games, and it’s not like 44 yards in an indoor facility is a difficult kick. I’m a little bit antsy with Myers and how he’s performed recently and particularly a contract year. The Seahawks were so injured that even the team doctor got hurt Abe Lucas, George Holani, and Nick Kallerup all left and didn’t return due to their respective injuries. Nick Emmanwori re-aggravated a shoulder injury, although he says he’s all good. Jarran Reed left with a toe injury and later returned despite an initial doubtful designation. Even Seattle’s team doctor then got whacked on the head by a wayward Fernando Mendoza throw, although thankfully he’s alright. Looool someone on the Seahawks staff just took a ball straight to his head #SEAvsLV pic.twitter.com/PCXjo7DayK — Waqy (@waqyyy) November 15, 2026 Gaining Quenton Nelson, Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, and (hopefully) Leonard Williams after the bye may be offset by what happened on Sunday. Hopefully the bye week is an ideal one-week buffer for any players who only have short-term injuries. Final Notes Mike Macdonald ratcheted up the pressure once the first couple of Raiders drives finished . Nothing can get a rookie’s clock sped up faster than dealing with all sorts of rushers coming right at him. The playing surface was unacceptable. Rolling in a natural grass surface for an indoor environment (or quasi-indoor like the Arizona Cardinals stadium) is not new but that was no different than playing at a random city park. So much slipping and sliding and uneven footing made it such a nervy game to watch. Don’t overlook Rashid Shaheed’s 3rd down conversion . His only catch kept Seattle’s opening second half drive alive and resulted in an eventual touchdown. Shaheed was also wide open on JSN’s TD but Lock turned him down for a bigger play. Brian Fleury called a much better 2nd half than 1st half. And what I mean is he didn’t make literally all but one first down playcall a pass like he did in the first 30 minutes. That was wild to see Seattle get overly obsessed with establishing the run to the point where Drew Lock had five pass attempts by halftime.…

title: Tory Horton’s 1,000 IQ kick return play helps Seahawks secure win over Raiders
summary: Although the Seattle Seahawks took the lead on the first drive of the second half and didn’t look back, the Las Vegas Raiders had a chance to come back in the dying minutes — but Tory Horton had other plans. With Seattle leading 21-13 and 2:04 left to play in the game, Raiders kicker Matt […]
full_text: Although the Seattle Seahawks took the lead on the first drive of the second half and didn’t look back, the Las Vegas Raiders had a chance to come back in the dying minutes — but Tory Horton had other plans. With Seattle leading 21-13 and 2:04 left to play in the game, Raiders kicker Matt Gay attempted to sail the kickoff through the endzone, which subsequently would’ve stopped the clock and given Las Vegas an extra timeout at the two-minute warning. However, Seahawks returner Tory Horton positioned himself at the back of the endzone and batted the ball forward, where Rashid Shaheed pick it up and ran it to Seattle’s 19-yard line — a move that burned additional time and forced the two-minute warning to occur prior to their possession. One Of The Smartest Football Plays I Think I've Ever Seen. The Kick Was Headed To The Back Of The End Zone, But Tory Horton Tipped It So The Seahawks Could Return It. That Kept The Clock Running And Burned Past The Two-Minute Warning. This Effectively Almost Ends The Game. pic.twitter.com/JjsWymkt64 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 15, 2026 Ultimately, the second-year receiver was issued a penalty for illegal batting, but because the play lasted long enough to cross the two-minute warning, the Raiders declined it. The game was still far from over as Las Vegas still had two timeouts remaining — one of which they used after they held running back Zach Charbonnet to a loss of one on the opening play of the drive. However, quarterback Drew Lock faked the handoff and ran for a first down on the ensuing play, putting an end to the Raiders comeback hopes. Prior to the kickoff, Las Vegas had strung together a field-goal drive, headlined by a 38-yard catch by RB Ashton Jeanty and were within one score for the first time since the 7:10 mark of the third quarter. Nevertheless, Horton’s play allowed extra wiggle room for the Seahawks on their final drive and played a major factor in the team’s second consecutive victory.
author: Michael Hapanovich

title: Seahawks-Raiders score: Seahawks use 2nd half surge to spoil Fernando Mendoza’s first start
summary: The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) will go into the bye week feeling good. They overcame a slow first half to put away the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) and send rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza to defeat in his first career NFL start. Seattle trailed 10-7 at the break before unleashing hell on Earth in the second half, […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) will go into the bye week feeling good. They overcame a slow first half to put away the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) and send rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza to defeat in his first career NFL start. Seattle trailed 10-7 at the break before unleashing hell on Earth in the second half, racking up over 300 yards of offense after halftime, while the Raiders had negative yards until their last possession. The 21-13 scoreline didn’t accurately reflect the closeness of the game, as Seattle had its wasteful moments that took points off the board. Drew Lock was far more aggressive and inventive than he was last week against the Arizona Cardinals, an indicator that his right elbow is getting better. He threw two spectacular scramble drill touchdowns to Cooper Kupp and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, although he did lose a couple of fumbles on some unusual plays. Lock’s “dagger” was taking a naked bootleg for 15 yards to pick up a first down and deny Vegas any chance of a miracle comeback. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator turned Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak did what he could to get Mendoza comfortable in the first half by spamming easy, quick throws. Mendoza also impressed with how he used his legs to extend plays and even scored on a QB draw. Ultimately, however, with Brock Bowers injured mid-game, there wasn’t much of a chance for Mendoza to shock the world. The Raiders had just 183 yards of total offense while the Seahawks had 382. It was a happy day for the Seahawks-heavy fans at Allegiant Stadium. The downside? Injuries. Lots of them for both the Seahawks and Raiders. Seahawks vs. Raiders 1st half recap Seattle got the ball on offense and had a big kick return from Jadarian Price to his own 42. The drive lasted two plays because Drew Lock, in trying to avoid a sack on his first dropback, tried to shovel the ball away and instead fumbled it to the Raiders. FUMBLE 🚨 Raiders recover! SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qM1FO6EsWN — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Fernando Mendoza completed his first three passes in his first NFL start. He capped off the short field opportunity with a QB draw touchdown on 3rd and goal at the 10. title: We watched vintage Deebo Samuel in the 49ers’ win over the Cowboys
summary: If I told you the San Francisco 49ers offense rode Deebo Samuel and Christian McCaffrey en route to a win, you’d probably assume I was talking about the 2023 season. Unfortunately for the Dallas Cowboys, it happened on Sunday, and the 49ers needed every bit of McCaffrey and Samuel, helping the 49ers edge Dallas in […]
full_text: (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If I told you the San Francisco 49ers offense rode Deebo Samuel and Christian McCaffrey en route to a win, you’d probably assume I was talking about the 2023 season. Unfortunately for the Dallas Cowboys, it happened on Sunday, and the 49ers needed every bit of McCaffrey and Samuel, helping the 49ers edge Dallas in a 46-40 slobberknocker. It looked for a bit like the 49ers would run away with things on Sunday, but a 21-point fourth quarter allowed by the 49ers’ defense kept things closer than they needed. At the end of the day, the 49ers offense outpaced the defense. With the offense outplaying the defense, it makes sense all three stars are from that side of the ball: 3rd star: WR Deebo Samuel Sunday was as vintage of a game as you can get from Samuel. Samuel opened the scoring for the 49ers in typical Samuel fashion: a quick screen going untouched for a touchdown. With San Francisco chasing an early field goal, the offense went to work for the first time, putting together an eight-play, 78-yard drive ending with Purdy swinging a pass out to Samuel, who used some blocks from Colton McKivitz and Dominick Puni to walk into the endzone to put the 49ers up 7-3. His next score would be on the ground and might become one of the most memorable play calls of the Kyle Shanahan era. With the 49ers clinging to a five-point lead early in the third quarter, San Francisco took advantage of another massive play. On the third play of the drive, Shanahan reached into his bag of tricks and pulled out a reverse. Kaelon Black would take a toss to the right, but pitch it to Samuel going right-to-left. As Tom Brady pointed out on the broadcast, when Samuel had the ball going to the left, ten Cowboys defenders were still following Black in the opposite direction. With all the space in the world and a couple blockers in front of him, Samuel played the sideline perfectly, tight-roping his way for a 70-yard score. With the two scores on top of 109 total yards, Samuel is deserving of Sunday’s No. 3 star. 2nd star: RB Christian McCaffrey It took McCaffrey a while to get things going in the run game on Sunday. However, with just the performance he put together in the passing game, his rushing wasn’t really relevant. McCaffrey led all pass-catchers with 161 yards on four catches, with two game-breaking scores to swing momentum the 49ers’ way. The first one we will get into more detail with our No. 1 star, but McCaffrey was the beneficiary of the play. With the 49ers facing a third-and-8 late in the third quarter, Purdy hit McCaffrey, who had plenty of space to take the short pass 74 yards to put the 49ers up one. His second receiving touchdown wasn’t as long, but it won the 49ers the game. Dallas cut what was a 38-19 San Francisco lead to 38-32 in the span of eight minutes. With the 49ers clinging to the six-point lead, Purdy again would find McCaffrey with an entire field’s worth of space in front of him, and this time McCaffrey would go 66 yards to put the 49ers up 14 and put the game out of reach. McCaffrey sandwiched a rushing touchdown between his receiving scores, finishing with three total touchdowns 1st star: QB Brock Purdy Without Purdy, there is no Samuel or McCaffrey performance on Sunday. Purdy earned Sunday’s No. 1 star with the play that completely swung momentum the Niners way, but it was his whole performance that stole the show. The quarterback used both of McCaffrey’s big plays with a few others to throw for a career-high 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. And not only did Purdy have a career day, but he may have made the best play of his already impressive highlight reel. With Dallas taking a 16-10 lead in the second quarter, San Francisco’s following drive got off to a less than ideal start. Purdy was sacked to lose six yards but would cancel it out with an eight-yard pass to Kittle to set up a third-and-8. That’s when Purdy magic struck. Purdy started the play by avoiding a Caleb Downs sack and rolled right. The quarterback might have had the angle to scramble for the first down with Shemar James bearing down. Instead, Purdy pulled up and found a wide-open McCaffrey 10 yards in front of him, and McCaffrey did the rest to give the 49ers a 17-16 lead. Oh, you thought that was the highlight play I was referencing? Not at all. The highlight I was talking about was Samuel’s 70-yard end-around. One of those blockers ahead of Samuel was none other than Purdy. The 49ers quarterback kept with the play the whole way, joining Trent Williams and Jordan Watkins as part of the convoy. It was actually Purdy who made the last “block” (more like got in the way) 40 yards downfield to give Samuel the space to finish the run. After a few weeks of his play stabilizing after a hot start, Purdy put together an MVP-level performance when the 49ers needed it the most. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 10, the standings are: QB Brock Purdy – 10 points WR Mike Evans – 8 points RB Christian McCaffrey – 7 points
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers hang 46 on Dallas; Rams rout Cardinals, Seahawks win
summary: The San Francisco 49ers put up the most points and yards in franchise history for a road game, which is also the most yards the Dallas Cowboys have given up at home. I’m just getting started on stats. We’ll begin with the 49ers averaging 9.4 yards per play. That do anything for you? How about […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 25: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers in the locker room before the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. The Falcons defeated the 49ers 29-20. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers put up t he most points and yards in franchise history for a road game , which is also the most yards the Dallas Cowboys have given up at home. I’m just getting started on stats. We’ll begin with the 49ers averaging 9.4 yards per play. That do anything for you? How about Brock Purdy going 22-of-28 for 389 yards passing and three touchdowns, finishing with a passer rating of 154.5. Then there’s running back Christian McCaffrey, who had 223 yards from scrimmage and three scores. And yet, they still, STILL had to recover an onside kick to win the game. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, while cornerback Deommodore Lenoir spent most of the afternoon chasing Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens. Renardo Green left with the same back injury he dealt with all week. There hasn’t been much about Green’s status for next week as of this writing, but Kyle Shanahan said he was already playing hurt . It was 38-32 in the fourth quarter. All points were by the offense. No sacks (well, there was one, but I wouldn’t call it “legitimate” outside of the stat sheet), and the Cowboys were coming back. Then this happened: CMC FOR THREE 🔥 No one can stop Christian McCaffrey in Dallas 😤 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/V9bJjR6slr — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 16, 2026 And even then, this thing wasn’t over until the most entertaining fumbleroosky play in recent memory as the clock ticked to zero: Final Play: #Cowboys come up short. 90 yards to go passing it backward isn’t a great idea #49ers hold out pic.twitter.com/4u95SfL2GR — FirstDownMedia (@FirstDownMediaa) November 16, 2026 Regardless of whether we want to be optimistic or skeptical, the 49ers stay the NFC’s No. 1 seed, a game ahead of the 7-2 pack of the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears. The Seahawks and Rams both won, so the division lead stays at 2.5 games. The 49ers face a tough gauntlet, starting with the Vikings. Any questions you have about this team are about to be answered over the next four games. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) After trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings on Tuesday, the Las Vegas Raiders gave Fernando Mendoza his first NFL start. At first it looked like an upset, but then the Seahawks had to spoil the party. There were moments, however. On Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock’s first dropback, he tried to shovel the ball away to avoid a sack and fumbled. Mendoza scored on a quarterback draw a few plays later, and the Raiders led 10-7 at halftime. The second half belonged to the Seahawks, with highlights like rookie running back Jadarian Price scoring his first career touchdown to take the lead, and a 71-yard Jaxon Smith-Njigba score. Final: 21-13. Smith-Njigba had 144 of his 171 yards receiving in the third quarter alone. Just like against the 49ers last week, the Raiders had a terrible second half with negative yards until their final possession. Mendoza took six sacks as well. The score could have been worse. Lock lost a second fumble when Zach Charbonnet ran into him on a play-action fake, and Jason Myers missed a 44-yarder. Right tackle Abe Lucas left with an ankle injury, which is worth watching before Seattle comes to Levi’s Stadium in Week 12. It was a lot of Seattle things, and then a lot of Raider-ing. Unfortunately, Seattle things usually don’t end in losses the way Raider-ing does. Los Angeles Rams (6-4)/Arizona Cardinals (3-7) Minshew Magic is gone to IR. That led us to Carson Beck starting for Arizona. A rookie, Carson Beck. So what happens? The Cardinals tried doing what worked last time they played the Rams: field-goal-ing them to death. This time, it wasn’t as successful, as they managed only six points throughout the game. Besides Matthew Stafford’s early-game interception to linebacker Cody Simon, it was all Los Angeles. Beck threw an interception just before halftime, and the Rams turned it into a 17-6 lead at the break. Final: 34-6 in Glendale, the Rams’ fourth straight win. Arizona finished with 123 yards of total offense: 89 net passing and 34 rushing. Beck was sacked five times, 1.5 of them by Aaron Donald. Stafford threw three touchdown passes. The Cardinals need to get through 2026 and make a football team next year. Credit where it’s due: the Rams look like a team again. They’re 1-2 in the division, and their bye week comes before a Thanksgiving Eve game against the Packers. No credit is given to them for getting a team like the Cardinals, a team that beat them solely on field goals a few weeks back. Luckily, the Rams also have a tough stretch coming up: the Green Bay Packers and the Kansas City Chiefs. Good luck. Onto Week 11 The 49ers “host” the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football. The Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick for Cousins , and he went 21-of-31 for 207 yards passing and two touchdowns in a 30-10 win at Lambeau . So they got the offense figured out; what about the defense? Well, they sacked Jordan Love eight times. Just a reminder, that’s not the Cowboys defense: Dallas sacked Purdy five times, and the 49ers still scored 46. This time the 49ers’ defense has to carry its share. The No. 1 seed is on the line, and Minnesota won the last two meetings. Cousins also became the first quarterback since at least 1950 to start for two different teams in consecutive weeks , and last week’s start was against the 49ers, when Jaden Dugger returned his pass for a touchdown. At least the game isn’t in Minnesota. The Rams and Seahawks are on bye. So, bye. The Cardinals visit the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat Atlanta 35-13 behind five Patrick Mahomes touchdown passes. Gotta love it when the 49ers get Atlanta’s best, but then they go back to doing Falcons things. 1st: San Francisco 49ers ; Next: vs. Minnesota Vikings (NFL Mexico City Game) TIE-2nd: Seattle Seahawks ; Next: BYE TIE-2nd: Los Angeles Rams ; Next: BYE 4th: Arizona Cardinals ; Next: at Kansas City Chiefs
