title: 3 quick takeaways from 49ers thriller win over Cowboys: There’s no such thing as defense
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 on Sunday in a high-scoring shootout that went down to the final minutes of the fourth quarter. Defense was optional in this one, as the 49ers compiled 584 total yards, while the Cowboys had 439. There were 36 points in the fourth quarter alone, as San […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers reacts to a first quarter touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 on Sunday in a high-scoring shootout that went down to the final minutes of the fourth quarter. Defense was optional in this one, as the 49ers compiled 584 total yards, while the Cowboys had 439. There were 36 points in the fourth quarter alone, as San Francisco allowed George Pickens to go for 11 catches, 145 yards, and three touchdowns. Still, their elite offense paved the way to another victory, and the 49ers remain atop the NFC at 8-1 with a key win going into a crucial stretch to begin the second half of the season. Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers win over the Cowboys on Sunday. Elite efficiency The 49ers did not have the prettiest game by any means on Sunday, especially on defense. They had 11 total penalties as a team for 100 yards, while Brock Purdy was sacked five times, as protection was the leakiest it had been all season long, specifically on the interior. Heading into the game, it was expected that the 49ers would try to establish themselves on the ground against the No. 31 run defense, but they really struggled to run the ball early, as Christian McCaffrey had just 13 yards on his first six carries. The run game didn’t really get going, aside from two big runs. But did it matter? Not at all, because Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy, and the 49ers offense were in their bag with another incredibly efficient performance. The Cowboys have been a pass funnel all year long, and Brock Purdy enjoyed another MVP-like performance with 389 yards and three touchdowns, completing 22 of 28 passes. He was incredible, playing mistake-free football while extending a number of plays that resulted in huge explosives for the 49ers. San Francisco averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. They converted 26 first downs. They were 6 of 11 on third downs. And they had a number of timely calls, such as Deebo Samuel’s 70-yard house call on an end around that had Dallas completely fooled. Additionally, I thought the 49ers ran hard on the ground throughout the game, relying on both Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black, who combined for 115 yards on 24 carries. McCaffrey was unguardable as a receiver and George Kittle regularly beat safety Caleb Downs for another big day. The 49ers won the way they knew best: efficiency. That was able to overcome their penalties and negative plays en route to 46 points. Corners struggle Deommodore Lenoir had a really rough game going up against George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb. Pickens did whatever he wanted to Lenoir, catching eight balls for 126 yards and two touchdowns on San Francisco’s top corner. Lamb also had a late touchdown in the red zone on Lenoir. San Francisco couldn’t cover anyone. Ryan Flournoy caught six of seven passes for 71 yards. Pickens had his monster game. And Lamb came on late for seven catches, 72 yards, and a touchdown. And the damage could’ve been even worse if not for three Pickens drops. It was also an interesting day, game plan-wise. Teams have beaten the Cowboys offense by blitzing Dak Prescott. The 49ers blitzed on only 18.5 percent of dropbacks on Sunday, but Prescott was 8 of 10 for 144 yards on the 10 dropbacks he was blitzed. For reference, Prescott was blitzed 51.1 percent of the time in a Week 3 loss to Baltimore. In a Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay, it was 52.4 percent. In Week 6 against Green Bay, it was 39.3 percent. In Week 7 against Philadelphia, it was 42.9 percent. In Week 8 against Arizona, it was 39.5 percent. Yes, Prescott had success against the blitz in a limited sample, but the 49ers’ game plan on defense did not work on Sunday in their worst defensive game of the season. Lack of pressure The 49ers were able to effectively stop the run on Sunday, but they were not able to get enough pressure on the quarterback, tying into the last point. Prescott averaged a 2.82-second time to throw on Sunday and was sacked just once for zero yards. San Francisco got pressure on just 12 of 51 dropbacks. Not one player had over a 10 percent pass-rush win rate, according to PFF, even though Mykel Williams had four pressures and Nick Bosa had three. The secondary was a bigger part of the issue on Sunday, but the 49ers needed to generate more pressure against Prescott, who was quite comfortable in the pocket. Moreover, if he did get pressure, Prescott was able to scramble a couple of times late in the game to extend drives. Now, this is an elite offense with two very talented pass catchers, and San Francisco won’t regularly face an opponent with such a good offense, but the 49ers have some questions to answer as they try to figure out their pass rush with Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner in the fold now.

title: Scorigami! 49ers and Cowboys final score has never happened before
summary: The NFL has been playing games for a really long time, and Sunday in the game between the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys, a score that has never happened before was the final. It is the 1099th unique final in NFL history. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys scores a two point conversion during the fourth quarter of a game against the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has been playing games for a really long time, and Sunday in the game between the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys, a score that has never happened before was the final. It is the 1099th unique final in NFL history. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami . Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. We got both on Sunday with the 49ers and Cowboys. The 49ers scored to make it 44-32. Because there was time left, the 49ers went for 2 to make is 46-32, a 14-point lead. A 45-32 final has happened, and so has a 44-32. San Francisco hit the two-point to push it to 46 points, which isn’t a normal score. Scorigami was in play. With the 46 points by San Francisco, 32 points or 39 points by the Cowboys would both have been Scorigami. Instead, the Cowboys scored a touchdown and went for two for a different Scorigami at 46-40. What a time to be alive. Our friends at Secret Base have done extensive work on Scorigami. If you want to see it, it is fascinating 2026 NFL Scorigamis This is the fourth Scorigami of the 2026 NFL season. September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37 September 13: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22 November 1: Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 November 15: San Francisco 49ers 46, Dallas Cowboys 40 During the 2025 season we saw four Scorigamis: Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 Bills beat Ravens 41-40 Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 Texans beat Jaguars 36-29

title: 49ers come close to putting up 50 points in a wild win over the Cowboys
summary: The San Francisco 49ers defense took the field to begin the game. After a questionable roughing-the-passer penalty on Osa Odighizuwa and an offside call, the stop unit settled in. Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir were challenged, and they both responded with plays. Brandon Aubrey’s 52-yard field goal gave the Cowboys a 3-0 lead early. Brock […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers defense took the field to begin the game. After a questionable roughing-the-passer penalty on Osa Odighizuwa and an offside call, the stop unit settled in. Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir were challenged, and they both responded with plays. Brandon Aubrey’s 52-yard field goal gave the Cowboys a 3-0 lead early. Brock Purdy found Jordan Watkins for a 22-yard gain to get the offense going. Rookie Caleb Downs held George Kittle on the next play. And just like that, the Niners were in Cowboys territory. Keenan Allen had a reception on the first drive. George Kittle and Deebo Samuel caught screen passes. Kittle gained 20+ yards on his. Deebo scored on his. That made it 7-3. The 49ers scored their 23rd touchdown on their 27th red zone trip of the year. Dak Prescott snuck for a first down on 4th & 1. Javonte Williams converted a 3rd-and-1. Dallas found themselves in San Francisco’s territory in no time. The cornerbacks would not have the same success on the next drive. George Pickens turned Lenoir around. Marques Sigle elected to come up in coverage and leave Lenoir out to dry. That led to a touchdown and a 10-7 Cowboys lead. After the 49ers went three-and-out, Sigle somewhat atoned for the previous mistake with a hit on CeeDee Lamb on 3rd and 4, leading to a punt. On the third drive, Demarcus Robinson returned after a stint in the blue medical tent. A blitz led to former Niners linebacker Dee Winters forcing pressure and an eventual sack. The Cowboys were poised to force another punt, but Brock Purdy escaped the chaos and found Allen for a 23-yard gain on third down. Purdy connected with Allen for another first down, this time for 14 yards. But the drive stalled when Connor Colby allowed a sack by Quinnen Williams. Eddy Pineiro’s 28-yard field goal tied things at 10. Prescott gave the 49ers a gift on the next drive. Nick Bosa got pressure, and Dre Greenlaw cut off Lamb, but Dre dropped the pass. Prescott and the Cowboys got to 4th & 1, and the Cowboys converted. Lenoir almost gave up another big play, but Pickens dropped the ball. Lenoir was not as fortunate on the next target. Pickens left Lenoir in the dust, gave up a touchdown, and, to make matters worse, took a big hit from Lamb. That was the 10th time Lenoir was targeted. He gave up 97 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions. Aubrey missed the extra point, keeping it 16-10. Kaelon Black made a rookie mistake on first down to begin the next drive. He ran the wrong way, turning it into 2nd and 16 after a sack. The 49ers’ drive looked like it would stall. But, as he tends to do, Purdy made a play on third and forever. He made a blitzer miss, then did the same to a linebacker. Instead of running, Purdy found McCaffrey wide open. After Kittle paved the way, McCaffrey’s 74-yard touchdown gave the Niners a 17-16 lead. The road team had a chance to double up on Dallas before the half. DeForest Buckner’s quarterback hit on third down forced a punt. But the Niners could not put together a drive in the two-minute drill to get into field goal range. At the half, it was 17-16, 49ers. The 49ers outgained Dallas 244 to 165, despite one less drive. San Francisco averaged 2.2 more yards per play than the Cowboys. But four sacks kept Dallas in it early. The 49ers were getting pressure on Dak. Multiple players had at least one pressure. They had four quarterback hits. But they gave up too much ground in the run game, and the Cowboys’ big passing plays made the difference. Improv Purdy found Watkins for a 27-yard gain on 2nd and 12. Watkins lost his footing, but the play developed so long that he had time to get up and make himself available for Purdy. Black more than made up for an earlier blunder after trucking a pair of Cowboys en route to a touchdown: YOU JUST CAN'T TACKLE KAELON BLACK SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DUcmDggwEx — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 That gave the Niners an 8-point lead. Dallas answered with a field goal of their own after a deep target to Pickens was incomplete, trimming the Niners’ lead to 24-19. Tom Brady thought Lenoir may have interfered, but no flag was thrown. Deebo took a reverse 70 yards to the house after letting the blockers do the work for him, giving the Niners a commanding 31-19 lead. Trent Williams showed off Hall of Fame athleticism on the play: Watch the 38-year-old 320-pounder open up the gait then redirect to make a key block. Shoutout to Deebo for letting the blocks develop and everybody do the work for him, but Trent Williams on this play…. pic.twitter.com/Lspw0RC09J — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) November 15, 2026 But it was still the third quarter, and we know Dallas wasn’t going anywhere. On 4th and 2, Prescott sailed a throw to Lamb, and it landed in the lap of Malik Mustapha, who should have dropped it for field position, but it looks great on the stat sheet. It cost the Niners roughly 30 yards in field position. There was never any doubt the Niners would get back to the original line of scrimmage if Mustapha had dropped it. A Christian McCaffrey third-down reception put the Niners in Dallas’s territory. Then, a 16-yard run made it 38-19. The 49ers went on a 28-3 run after Dallas took a first-half lead. A Lenoir defensive hold wiped out a Mykel Williams sack. Mustapha was flagged for a big hit. It was unnecessary or dirty, but the refs didn’t pick up the flag. Renardo Green came out of the game after he appeared to grab his lower back, the same injury he had during the week. Rookie Ephesians Prysock came in, and Dallas went right at him. Prysock gave up a touchdown to Pickens to make it 38-25. Purdy had a rare miss, and it came at an inopportune time. Allen looked like he had a step on the defender, but Purdy’s pass one-hopped Allen and fell incomplete. Green remained out, so Prysock stayed in. The safety duo was Sigle and Ji’Ayir Brown. Dallas wasted little time moving the ball and were in the red zone within a blink. On 4th & 6, Upton Stout gave up a touchdown to Ryan Flournoy. That made it 38-32. The 49ers needed another score to put the game out of reach. Good thing they have Christian McCaffrey. Shanahan schemed up McCaffrey on Von Miller, and 66 yards later, McCaffrey reached his fastest speed in a game since the end of 2023: Christian McCaffrey reached 20.29 MPH on this play. That's his fourth-fastest speed since joining the 49ers and his top speed in a game since Week 14 of 2023. pic.twitter.com/TJnSOYzRw3 — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) November 16, 2026 That was the nail in the coffin, making it 46-32. Not so fast…. The Cowboys made their way into the red zone, then Prysock committed a penalty, giving Dallas the ball at the 1-yard line. A fade to Lamb over Lenoir made it 46-38. Prescott dove for the two-point conversion to make it 46-40. Deebo recovered the onside kick, but the Cowboys had all three timeouts with 42 seconds remaining. Black made things interesting after Quinnen Williams stood him up. Fortunately, the ball bounced right back to Black. Corliss Waitman did what he’s done all season by pinning the opponent inside the 10. It was the most yards Dallas has ever allowed at home. It was also the most points and yards in franchise history on the road. The 49ers averaged 9.4 yards per play against the Cowboys, the most by any team in a game over the last 2 seasons. The 49ers are the first team with 370+ pass yards and 200+ rush yards in the same game since the Dolphins scored 70 against the Broncos in Week 3, 2023.

title: Buccaneers’ playoff chances improve during their bye week
summary: At 3-6, the Buccaneers’ playoff prospects would be quite dim if they played in a normal division…but they play in the NFC South so we all know what that means. Despite not playing a snap due to their much-needed bye, Tampa Bay’s chances to make the playoffs actually improved in Week 10. After losses by […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during the fourth quarter of the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images At 3-6, the Buccaneers’ playoff prospects would be quite dim if they played in a normal division…but they play in the NFC South so we all know what that means. Despite not playing a snap due to their much-needed bye, Tampa Bay’s chances to make the playoffs actually improved in Week 10. After losses by the New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Falcons, the Bucs are now estimated at a 43% chance to win the division and therefore make the tournament, per The Athletic’s Playoff Simulator, which is a 2% improvement over where they stood after Week 9. The Bucs already hold critical victories over the Carolina Panthers, who currently lead at 4-5, and the Falcons, who have lost 3 in a row and are now 3-7. If the Buccaneers can manage an upset win over the Detroit Lions in their return to action during Week 11, they will improve their odds to 54%. Conversely, a loss would drop their chances to at least 36% at 3-7. So, even without math, it’s pretty obvious to call this Lions game a critical inflection point in the season. Coming off of a bye with one of the league’s best defenses against a Detroit team that just played overseas and lost their best defensive player in Aidan Hutchinson should make for a very winnable game, but we’ve seen that nothing is easy for Tampa this year — particularly for its bottom-5 pass offense. Overall, salvaging the season is still very much a real possibility, but a negative outcome in Week 11 would then require a lot of help from their fellow putrid division mates.

title: Bucs could be without Baker Mayfield for Week 11 matchup against Lions
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield when they return from their bye week to face the Detroit Lions. According to a report from ESPN, citing multiple sources who spoke with NFL Network, Mayfield is dealing with a foot and ankle injury suffered during Tampa Bay’s 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers scrambles against Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield when they return from their bye week to face the Detroit Lions. According to a report from ESPN , citing multiple sources who spoke with NFL Network, Mayfield is dealing with a foot and ankle injury suffered during Tampa Bay’s 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears last Sunday. The veteran quarterback has reportedly been in and out of a walking boot in recent days to rest and rehabilitate the injury. Fortunately for Tampa Bay, its bye week provided Mayfield with additional recovery time before the team’s upcoming trip to Detroit. The injury occurred during a difficult fourth quarter for Mayfield, who took several hits and was slow to get up on multiple occasions. On one play, Bears defensive lineman Austin Booker briefly grabbed Mayfield’s helmet before a sack, resulting in a face mask penalty. Two plays later, defensive linemen Grady Jarrett and Jeffery Simmons combined to bring Mayfield down awkwardly, leaving the quarterback on the ground for several moments. Despite the apparent discomfort, Mayfield remained in the game and even converted a two-point attempt with his legs to tie the score at 24 with 2:51 remaining. Chicago ultimately kicked the game-winning field goal on its ensuing possession, preventing Tampa Bay’s offense from getting another opportunity. The latest injury adds to an already challenging season for Mayfield, who missed three games earlier this year after dislocating his right thumb during a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels started in Mayfield’s absence and would be the likely replacement should the veteran be unable to play against Detroit. There is some encouraging news for the Buccaneers, however. According to the report, Mayfield’s foot and ankle injury is not believed to be a long-term concern, and any potential absence is expected to be brief. A stint on injured reserve is not being considered. Mayfield has also not been ruled out against the Lions. Sources familiar with the situation pointed to his history of playing through injuries, suggesting that if his availability comes down to managing pain rather than limited functionality, the quarterback will make every effort to suit up. For a Buccaneers team sitting at 3-6 and just half a game out of first place in the NFC South, having Mayfield available could be crucial as Tampa Bay looks to turn its season around. The team will monitor his recovery when practices resume this week, with his participation potentially offering a clearer indication of whether he’ll be ready for Detroit. The Buccaneers and Lions are scheduled to kick off Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. ET.

summary: The Daily Slop Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Mark Bullock (paywall) David Blough shows development […]
full_text: The Daily Slop Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Mark Bullock (paywall) David Blough shows development vs Giants Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough has had plenty of ups and downs so far this season. That should be expected with a first year offensive coordinator who only has two years as an assistant quarterbacks coach under his belt prior to this big leap. Against the Rams last Sunday, he had one of his worst games with an almost non-existent protection plan against two future hall of fame pass rushers in Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald. Given that performance and the fact the Commanders were on a short week, I wasn’t expecting much improvement from Blough against the Giants on Thursday night. However, Blough and the Commanders offense looked a lot better. The Giants defense has a lot of talent at all three levels of the field and in the first matchup back in Week 5, the Giants got the better of the Commanders by spamming Cover-0 blitzes. I wrote on Sunday how Blough and quarterback Jayden Daniels had a much better plan this time around to handle those blitzes and it was key in the game-winning touchdown to Stefon Diggs. But it wasn’t just against Cover-0 that they had a better protection plan. title: Washington Commanders free agency: Has Odafe Oweh been a bust?
summary: When Commanders general manager Adam Peters signed edge rusher Odafe Oweh to a four-year, $96 million deal in free agency this offseason, fans and analysts alike were excited about his potential in Washington’s new attacking defense. Although Oweh had only one season with double-digit sacks (10 in 2024) and went without a sack in the […]
full_text: When Commanders general manager Adam Peters signed edge rusher Odafe Oweh to a four-year, $96 million deal in free agency this offseason, fans and analysts alike were excited about his potential in Washington’s new attacking defense. Although Oweh had only one season with double-digit sacks (10 in 2024) and went without a sack in the first five games of 2025, a midseason trade to the Chargers saw him finish the last 12 games with 7.5 sacks, a pace that would have put Oweh on track for double digit sacks over a full 17 game schedule. Seemingly a strong fit for coordinator Daronte Jones’ defensive scheme, fans were excited about the prospect of high-level production from the EDGE position after the team suffered from a lack of talent at the position last season. Nine games into the season, the preseason optimism has cooled. According to Pro Football Reference , Odafe Oweh has five sacks, 13 pressures, six hurries, and 20 tackles. While the numbers are respectable — Oweh ranks 14th in total sacks — his impact hasn’t been exactly what fans had hoped for before the season began. In this article, we will look at Oweh’s impact so far, his free agent value and what to expect for the rest of the season. We start our evaluation with Odafe’s performance in the run game. Before the start of the season, there were conflicting reports regarding his performance in this aspect of the game, but so far he has lived up to his 2025 numbers and has set the edge well. Analytics site Pro Football Focus continues to give him a poor run defense grade (60.0), but Oweh has six tackles for a loss, and Next Gen Stats credits him with 15 run stops while he generally looking disciplined in contain. Hell of a play by Javon Kinlaw (#99) and Odafe Oweh (#98) creating a pileup on this counter call. Excluding all Hurts carries the Eagles only had a 38.9% rushing success rate, 27th in the NFL last week pic.twitter.com/ZXM6ncFRka — JP Acosta (@acosta32_jp) September 17, 2026 great play by Odafe Oweh (#98) to make a mess of the edge and get the stuff. also, Sonny Styles is really, really fast. pic.twitter.com/HRb52oIcWX — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 22, 2026 Oweh plays this about as good as an EDGE can pic.twitter.com/FlHkGQ413I — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 28, 2026 Odafe’s performance as a pass rusher has been more mixed. Highly athletic ( 9.92 RAS ), Oweh has demonstrated both power and speed rushing off the edge. His second sack of the season came against the Colts, when Odafe showed off his strength in London, driving the offensive tackle backwards into Daniel Jones, creating a fumble and recovering the ball for an early turnover while flashing his pure speed on a sack against the 49ers in Week 6. Odafe Oweh is a strong man pic.twitter.com/9fmY0jPYvG — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 4, 2026 Odafe Oweh stepping up to get the sack 💪 WASvsSF on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zVad5MpO89 — NFL (@NFL) October 20, 2026 Oweh also stays disciplined in his rushing attack which is a key in Jones’ scheme. He has also exhibited the ability to convert speed to power, as demonstrated during his fourth sack of the year in Week 7 versus the Philadelphia Eagles and former All-Pro left tackle Jordan Mailata. Odafe Oweh is up to 5 sacks on the season. This one was schemed up via the Nick Cross blitz. pic.twitter.com/GHcIU0b3l2 — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) November 13, 2026 Oweh absolutely DESTROYED Mailata for the sack!!! pic.twitter.com/ZkYTFdnpCd — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 The problem with Oweh’s play lies in his lack of consistency. Heady readers will have already noted that the edge defender’s sacks haven’t come on a consistent basis over the full course of the Commanders schedule. Oweh has disappeared from several games during the season. After a strong opener, Odafe went the next two games without a sack before bottoming out in Weeks 5 and Week 9, recording zero tackles, no sacks, with just 1 quarterback hit and 1 quarterback hurry, respectively. The issue is that Oweh has failed to take the next step in his development that many projected after the strong closing with the Chargers. While thought to have finally possessed the necessary pass-rush tools, Odafe has yet to demonstrate the ability to consistently win his one-on-ones on the outside even when the matchups have been favorable. Oweh gets a 1 on 1 with a TE and is easily handled pic.twitter.com/lIgEVYxJaX — RefTheDistrict (@RefTheDistrict) October 20, 2026 Per Next Gen Stats , through Week 8, when facing one or more blockers, Oweh had produced a career-low 10.0% pressure rate. Oweh’s pass rush win rate of 8.9% through Week 9 ranked him 51st out of all edge rushers and, with Oweh’s $96 million contract value fresh in their minds, some fans have begun calling the free agent signing a bust, based upon the idea he was a reach that was overpaid in March. However, is that really the case? As usual with NFL contracts, the devil is in the details. Per Spotrac , Oweh’s average contract value ranks 17th out of all edge defenders in the league. This summer, Hogs Haven cap guru Bill Horgan compared the key metrics for several players with similar contract values, including former Washington EDGE Montez Sweat, to project a benchmark for Odafe’s production this season. By stepping out from the shadow of playing behind other veteran rushers, Oweh is expected to see his snap share rise from 575 snaps per year to 670+ defensive snaps in Washington’s scheme. If he can maintain his per-snap efficiency with the increased snap count, he could generate roughly 28 pressures and 10.5 sacks in 2026. If he plays closer to 800 snaps this season, then his production could align closely with that of Andrew Van Ginkel, who averaged 796 defensive snaps per season over the past two years. After nine games, Oweh is still playing in somewhat of a rotational role in the Commanders’ defense with 392 total defensive snaps (62%) heading into Week 10, which would give him 740 total defensive snaps for the season on an overall projection. Slightly past the halfway mark, PFF credits general manager Adam Peters’ marquee signing with 21 total pressures and five sacks, so while Odafe may be slightly behind in sacks, he is at or ahead of where he should be for expected pressures on the season. Furthermore, as BiB noted in his initial review of the signing , that, given the structure of Oweh’s contract which has a flat cap hit of $27.2m per year for the next 3 seasons and a minimal dead cap at the end of the deal, the signing will seem more affordable as the contract ages and the league salary cap increases annually. In conclusion, so far the signing of Odafe Oweh represents a solid addition at a position of need at, or slightly above, a fair market rate for edge defenders. The big commitment from a contract perspective was the associated $68 million guaranteed at signing and the length of the contract. But, if Oweh continues to play at his current level or above, he should continue to warrant his cap hit going forward. The issue for fans and the team is that the signing does not provide the Commanders’ defense a consistent pass-rushing threat who can win in one-on-one situations. Daronte Jones must continue to scheme opportunities for both Oweh and Chaisson in targeted situations instead of relying on them being able to generate pressure in a four-man rush. In the meantime, GM Adam Peters should continue to search for a true game-changing talent at the edge position via either another free agent addition or the NFL draft, which will likely cost more — in either cap space or draft capital — than the deal that Oweh signed this year. What is your opinion on Odafe Oweh so far in Year 1? Let us know in the comments below:

title: Should Washington Commanders sign Brandon Aiyuk after 49ers release?
summary: Yeah, we know.   You’ve got Brandon Aiyuk fatigue.   It was understandably built over the summer, when the 49ers receiver posted one stupid Instagram Story after another, hating on everyone from 49ers GM John Lynch to San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan to his former agent and the NFL, generally while rocking Commanders gear. […]
full_text: Yeah, we know. You’ve got Brandon Aiyuk fatigue. It was understandably built over the summer, when the 49ers receiver posted one stupid Instagram Story after another, hating on everyone from 49ers GM John Lynch to San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan to his former agent and the NFL, generally while rocking Commanders gear. Then he said some stuff about former Arizona State teammate and current Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. That was a no-no. Aiyuk still bought property in the DMV anyway and has posted some things that indicated he might be off kilter. But there’s no doubt about his talent. Aiyuk can play, but his refusal to do the things required for reinstatement rendered that moot. He has done that now, hiring Drew Rosenhaus and then complied with the tasks to achieve reinstatement. That has happened now, with the 49ers expected to release him before his roster exemption ends next week. The 49ers aren’t keeping him long term, though there’s an issue of bonus repayment to be worked out. That brings this topic back to the forefront. We know you’re sick of Aiyuk talk. But it’s relevant again, only because he and Daniels have figured things out. ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler reported that’s the case on the Rich Eisen Show . Does that mean Washington would be in on Aiyuk if/when he hits the open market? “I don’t know where Washington stands on that, but I can say that Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk have reconciled,” Fowler said on the Rich Eisen Show . “I’m told their relationship is now good, whereas with some of the stuff on Instagram, it wasn’t right.” It sure seems like Aiyuk wants to be a Commander. Do the Commanders want Aiyuk? Well, they’re in a spot after Thursday’s win over the New York Giants where they’re competing for the division title and coaches are competing for their jobs. And they’ve got a need at receiver with Terry McLaurin out for the season and having possibly played his last snap as a Commander. Would you take a flyer on Aiyuk? If so, at what cost? And, since we’re asking a bunch of questions into the ether, how would he fit into the Commanders locker room? Washington would seem like an obvious destination for Aiyuk to establish some street cred. General manager Adam Peters took the easy and rational way out when asked about Aiyuk nearly a fortnight past, saying he can’t comment on a player under contract (with the 49ers). And that’s accurate. Ultimately, however, it’s not up to Peters. It’s up to Daniels. Have fences been mended, as Fowler suggests? “I’m imagining Aiyuk has a Commanders hat on right now,” Fowler said, on the The Rich Eisen Show. “Every Instagram video he puts out, he’s got Commanders gear on. He’s made no mistake that he wants to be there. I am told he and the quarterback are good.” “For whatever that means, I don’t know what it means for where he signs, but I thought that was interesting,” Fowler continued. “So maybe the Commanders will think a little differently about that situation if they do entertain it. I still think he could have a hard time getting a job.” Should the Commanders sign Brandon Aiyuk once he’s inevitably released? Let us know in the comments below :

Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Giants gained 399 yards but scored 21—and Joe Burrow is next Through Week 6, opponents had scored touchdowns on 18 of 22 red-zone trips against Washington, yet New York left crucial points behind when Frankie Luvu punched the ball loose from Malik Nabers at the 16-yard line and Jeremy Reaves recovered. Washington also held the Giants to 4-of-12 on third down, including two critical late stops when it couldn’t afford to give New York another first down—a defensive standard that will be tested immediately when Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit Landover. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Learn Lesson vs Cover-0 One of the biggest turnarounds from the Commanders tie back in Week 5 against the Giants and their win over the Giants on Thursday night was the plan of attack against Cover-0. In Week 5, the Giants spammed Cover-0 blitzes throughout the second half and overtime and the Commanders just couldn’t handle it. They continually attempted to take shots down the field to try and hit explosive plays rather than just finding a simple quick solution. Daniels was seeing those blitzes a lot better and it showed in the most critical moment. Back in Week 5, the Giants spammed the Commanders with Cover-0 blitzes and Washington just completely failed to handle it. On Thursday, OC David Blough and QB Jayden Daniels showed they had learned their lesson. I broke it down: https://t.co/U1yrDEyKUZ pic.twitter.com/kMh2rjFdSU — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 15, 2026 Having thrown two late interceptions, it looked like the Commanders season was over, but the defense bailed Daniels out and gave him another opportunity, which he wasn’t going to pass up. On third and four with under a minute remaining in the game, the Giants of course show Daniels another Cover-0 blitz. This time, Daniels doesn’t adjust the protection, but instead signals to Stefon Diggs in the slot to change his route. In the first game, when Daniels saw Cover-0, he often checked into a shot play to try and attack the blitz and throw a big touchdown over the top of it. But clearly this time they were looking to play smarter, and it worked out much better for them. Daniels adjusts Diggs route, having him run a slant against the slot corner. When he snaps the ball, the defense comes on the blitz, but the defensive tackle to the right side of the line pops up and drops out into coverage, trying to take away a hot throw over the middle. Daniels just checked into a hot throw over the middle with Diggs running a slant, so that could potentially be a problem. But Daniels does a great job adjusting his throw to beat that defensive lineman dropping into coverage. Diggs runs a great route, beating the corner with a nice stutter move before sharply cutting across his face to get inside. The throw from Daniels has to be slightly behind him because of that defensive lineman dropping into coverage, but Diggs does well to adjust to the pass and make the grab. Diggs breaks a diving tackle from the slot corner and gets some help from fellow receiver Van Jefferson, who helps block the other nearby defender. With both defenders out of the picture, Diggs runs uncontested into the end zone for a 32-yard game-winning touchdown. It goes to show that you can still score a big touchdown against Cover-0 without having to try and take a deep shot constantly. As I said back in Week 5, I don’t mind that their philosophy against Cover-0 is to go on the attack, in fact I quite like it. It offers you one-on-one matchups and I like that they feel like they can take shots with those matchups. But they clearly went too far in Week 5 in trying to throw bombs down the field. This game proved there’s more ways to go about it. Winning a one-on-one doesn’t have to be 20 yards down the field, it can be a quick slant like this when you have Stefon Diggs or Antonio Williams in the slot. With it being Cover-0, if you win that one-on-one quickly, there’s every chance the receiver can run freely after the catch and score as there’s no safety help over the top. So credit should go to David Blough and Jayden Daniels for making that adjustment. It’s a shame they couldn’t have made it back in Week 5 because they would have won that game too if they had, but it paid off for them this time around and it meant that the Commanders have just about kept their season alive. title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape. We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 10 update 

 While Garrett didn't record a sack Sunday, Donald got his first sack of the season -- finishing with 1.5 to move ahead of Chandler Jones and Justin Houston for 31st at 112.5. 

 Hunter missed his first game of the season, and the rest of the list failed to record a sack -- with Mack and Campbell playing on "Monday Night Football."  

 Week 9 update 

 In his first game since Week 1, Garrett made his presence felt. He had three sacks to move ahead of Dwight Freeney, Derrick Thomas and Rickey Jackson for 18th on the list. He was the only one of the active leaders to record a sack this week. 

 Week 8 update 

 With two players on bye and Garrett out, only two of the five active players that played this week recorded sacks, but they were impactful. 

 Miller recorded his first sack as a Cowboy Sunday, moving him ahead of Terrell Suggs and into a tie with Jason Taylor for seventh.

 Watt added two sacks of his own, moving him ahead of Simeon Rice and Clyde Simmons for 23rd. He now has 7.5 sacks on the season. 

 

 Week 7 update 

 Hunter and Watt were the only ones to record sacks this week, with Hunter jumping back over Campbell in the rankings. 

 

 Week 6 update 

 With Garrett still out, it was another quiet week on the sack front. Of the active leaders, it was the oldest that recorded the lone sack of the week in Campbell. He moved back in front of Hunter. 

 

 Week 5 update 

 Hunter was the only player among the active leaders to record a sack this week, moving him ahead of Campbell to No. 26 all-time. Hunter now has three sacks through five games. 

 

 Week 4 update 

 Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR. 

 

 Week 3 update 

 There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

 

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more

full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

title: NFL Week 10: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 10.
full_text:
The Sunday slate for Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Munich between the Patriots and Lions. Detroit improved to 7-2 with a win after the Patriots lost Drake Maye early to an ankle injury.

 Back in the United States, the Vikings comfortably defeated the Packers in quarterback Kirk Cousins ' first game since being traded from the Raiders . Without running back  Kenneth Walker III (groin injury), the Chiefs started rookie  Emmett Johnson , who coasted to 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Falcons. And the Jets went their second straight game without scoring a touchdown, losing to the Bills.

 In the late window, rookie quarterbacks  Carson Beck  (Cardinals) and  Fernando Mendoza  (Raiders) made their debuts as NFL starters. Beck threw two interceptions and zero touchdowns in a loss to the Rams; Mendoza finished with a rushing score and zero turnovers in a loss to the Seahawks. Offense was not an issue in 49ers-Cowboys, as both teams combined for 86 points in a San Francisco win. Sunday night saw the Bengals put on a clinic in a blowout win over the Steelers and rise to first place in the AFC North.

 Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

 Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

 
 Jump to: 
 PIT-CIN |  SF-DAL |  SEA-LV 
 LAR-ARI  |  HOU-CLE | MIA-IND 
 CAR-NO | JAX-TEN |  BUF-NYJ 
 KC-ATL  |  MIN-GB |  NE-DET 

 Catch up on Thursday's game: 
 WSH-NYG 

 
 

 

 Cincinnati 38, Pittsburgh 18 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Bengals 
 Are the Bengals a true Super Bowl contender? With how the offense is playing, it definitely looks like it. For the first time in franchise history, Cincinnati has scored 30 or more points in five straight games. After a dazzling performance in Madrid, the Bengals carried that momentum into a big AFC North showdown at home. With quarterback Joe Burrow (35-for-44 for 409 passing yards and four TDs) playing at an MVP level and receivers Ja'Marr Chase (11 catches for 231 receiving yards) and Tee Higgins (five catches for 66 yards) also playing as well as they have in their respective careers, this offense is good enough to carry Cincinnati on a deep playoff run.

 What to make of the QB performance: At this rate, Burrow will be the unquestioned front-runner to win Most Valuable Player. There was nothing he couldn't do Sunday night -- including hitting Chase in stride on multiple deep balls. Burrow is the first player since 2013 with at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span. -- Ben Baby 

 Next game: at Commanders (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Steelers 
 Did the Bengals expose the Steelers' foundational weaknesses? Yes, in every way. The issues that lurked during the Steelers' 6-2 start were shoved into the spotlight in their primetime annihilation by a division foe. The defense, though stacked with some of the league's best and most highly paid defenders, has a talent deficiency in the secondary, significant tackling issues and coverage busts. With games against injured and flawed teams in the second half of the season, the Steelers might still finish with a winning record and even make the playoffs again. But Sunday night's loss showed that the Steelers aren't a serious contender as currently constructed.

 What to make of the QB performance: Aaron Rodgers had a career-high eight incompletions to open the game before he finally connected with tight end Darnell Washington for a 5-yard gain late in the second quarter. Unlike the last time the Steelers played in Cincinnati in primetime, Rodgers looked every bit his age Sunday night. In addition to being sacked three times, the 42-year-old finished the game completing just 15 of 29 passes for 143 passing yards, 54 of which came on two long completions to DK Metcalf with the game well out of reach in the fourth quarter.

 Best quote from the locker room:  "We're not going to drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy and we're going to pour our energy into ourselves looking in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control," Steelers HC Mike McCarthy when asked how to keep the Steelers' loss from impacting the rest of the season.  -- Brooke Pryor 

 Next game: at Eagles (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: Chase Brown posted a season-best 28.3 points in Sunday night's win. Brown had 10 carries for 44 rushing yards, but it was the receiving numbers that boosted his totals. He finished with eight receptions for 39 receiving yards, adding his first two receiving scores of the season. In the Bengals' pass-heavy system, Brown has the traits to produce on backfield releases, but managers shouldn't expect him to be a primary target inside the red zone at the rate he was Sunday. Brown fits as an RB2 for the Week 11 matchup versus Washington. -- Bowen 

 

 

 San Francisco 46, Dallas 40 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 49ers 
 As players get healthier, how good can the 49ers' offense be? The 8-1 Niners got WR Deebo Samuel Sr . back from a hamstring injury Sunday and the offense took off, averaging 9.8 yards per play and posting 584 total yards -- the most in any game under coach Kyle Shanahan (since 2017) -- against a bad Cowboys defense. Samuel had 109 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. But San Francisco is about to move up a few weight classes with showdowns against the Vikings and Seahawks defenses the next two weeks. That should offer a strong indication of where the offense is headed, especially if WR Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis for either or both of those games.

 What to make of the QB performance: On a day when he was under pressure frequently and sacked five times, quarterback Brock Purdy was unfazed, leading San Francisco's outburst. He made plays on the move, including a 74-yard touchdown toss to RB Christian McCaffrey . More of that will be needed in the coming weeks. -- Nick Wagoner 

 Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET in Mexico City)

 

 
 

 Cowboys 
 Is it time for the Cowboys to scoreboard watch? Anything is possible mathematically, but the only realistic way the 4-6 Cowboys will make the playoffs is by winning the NFC East. That means they will need help from the Giants (5-3-1). Five of New York's last eight games come against teams with a winning record (Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit). Whatever progress the Cowboys thought they were making defensively was exposed by the 49ers. The Cowboys have four games remaining against teams with a winning record (Seattle, Rams, Jacksonville, Giants). The Cowboys almost certainly have to win five of their last eight games to have a chance. And they have not won consecutive games this season.

 Trend to watch: In the past three games, the Cowboys have given up six plays of at least 50 yards (four touchdowns). On Sunday, they gave up three touchdowns of at least 66 yards, a first in AT&T Stadium history. On the season, the Cowboys have allowed a league-high eight plays of at least 50 yards. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: 49ers RB Kaelon Black scored a career-best 14.6 points after 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, plus two receptions for 13 yards. He has now seen 11 or more touches in three straight games, with at least 10 points and a touchdown in two. Given his recent usage -- and the 49ers' attempt to reduce the overall volume for Christian McCaffrey -- Black has value as a flex option in deeper leagues. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Seattle 21, Las Vegas 13 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Seahawks 
 Is the Seahawks' defense ready for Round 2 versus the 49ers? Seattle allowed the Raiders to net only 163 yards, and it sacked Fernando Mendoza six times.…

title: NFL playoff chance tiers: Where all 32 teams fit in 2026 postseason picture
summary: We placed all 32 NFL teams into tiers based on their likelihood of making the playoffs, from Super Bowl favorites to the top draft pick candidates.
full_text:
The back half of the  2026 NFL season  is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason , they don't tell us everything . Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.

 So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between, because for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index  (FPI), betting lines , metrics, health status and some instinct.

 Walder ranked the teams within each tier too. All percentages and statistical rankings are through Sunday unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 Tier 1: True Super Bowl contenders 
 

 San Francisco 49ers (8-1) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.7% 
 Chances to win the NFC West:  95.4% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  39.6%

 Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa   missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is   the   FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and the  Seahawks . Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR, and he is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far too.

 

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 Buffalo Bills (8-1) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  >99.9% 
 Chances to win the AFC East:  99.7% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  29.3%

 The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite, and nothing that has happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. Their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. Buffalo's defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen , running back  James Cook III  and the Bills' offensive line do more than enough damage on offense.

 

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.9% 
 Chances to win the AFC South:  98.7% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  22.6%

 The Jaguars were already playoff locks and clearly one of the top two teams in the AFC before the trade deadline, when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux . The Davis deal from the Jaguars' perspective is one of the worst trades in years , but there's also little doubt Jacksonville is better today than it was a week ago. And the Jaguars were great a week ago! The Jaguars rank in the top five in EPA per dropback on offense and EPA allowed per dropback as well as EPA allowed per designed rush on defense.

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 

 Tier 2: Playoff locks 

 

 Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.5% 
 Chances to win the AFC West:  45.1% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  16.1%

 The Chiefs faced three major questions entering the season:

 
 How would quarterback Patrick Mahomes fare after recovering from a torn ACL  suffered last December? 
 What kind of impact would free agent running back Kenneth Walker III have on the offense? 
 Could the defense survive the loss of starting cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson ? 
 
 

The answer to every question has been positive for Kansas City. In particular, Walker has helped transform the Chiefs' rushing attack into a strength. And coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has managed to keep the defense strong too: It ranks sixth in EPA per play.

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.8% 
 Chances to win the AFC North:  93.9% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  19.1%

 It's something we've wondered about for years: What would happen if the Bengals could manage to combine a peak Joe Burrow season with simply mediocre defense? Well, we're finding out. Burrow is in the MVP race, and Cincinnati's defense is ranked 11th in EPA per play. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been outstanding and provide a sky-high ceiling for the passing offense. Plus, the Bengals have a very easy schedule the rest of the way.

 

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 

 Denver Broncos (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.2% 
 Chances to win the AFC West:  54.9% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  9.0%

 Somehow, it's working . Despite Bo Nix falling well short of expectations -- he entered Week 10 ranked 24th out of 31 qualifiers in QBR -- the Broncos are a virtual lock to reach the playoffs and have a great shot at winning the AFC West. The defense hasn't quite lived up to its reputation (13th in EPA per play), but Denver also hasn't had All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II for every game, either. If the offense can keep its recent momentum (the Broncos have put up 26 points in each of their past three games), Denver can be a threat in the postseason. The Broncos have a soft schedule the rest of the way, too.

 

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 Tier 3: Likely in, barring a collapse 

 

 Minnesota Vikings (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  96.1% 
 Chances to win the NFC North:  45.0% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  14.4%

 Minnesota's trade-deadline deal for quarterback Kirk Cousins breathed new life into its season. That move instantly increased the Vikings' playoff chances from 65% to 83% at the time of the deal, according to the FPI. But that deal was about what comes next. With Brian Flores' incredible defense leading the way, the Vikings can and should have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The moment Flores leaves, a real possibility in this upcoming offseason, the team's contention window vanishes, so the Vikings need to take advantage of this opportunity. Minnesota's 30-10 dismantling of the Packers on Sunday only reinforced what a good trade it was.

 

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 Chicago Bears (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  85.4% 
 Chances to win the NFC North:  20.4% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  11.2%

 Chicago entered its bye week as a near lock to reach the playoffs and very much a team that could go all the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a significant step forward, and the fact that the Bears are 7-2 despite Williams missing three games is a testament to the coaching staff and how strong this team is. Coordinator Dennis Allen was already getting the most out of a lacking defensive roster when the Bears acquired the best defensive tackle in the league in Jeffery Simmons as they prepare for what they hope is a Super Bowl run.

 

 
 See remaining schedule 

 

 

 

 

 Detroit Lions (7-2) 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  89.4% 
 Chances to win the NFC North:  33.7% 
 Chances to make the Super Bowl:  9.7%

 If they played in a normal division, the Lions would be even safer than this, especially after the team's blowout win over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday -- albeit with New England missing quarterback Drake Maye for most of that contest . But Detroit's record has it on the verge of a playoff berth despite playing in a stacked NFC North and with the Seahawks and Rams looming as other wild-card threats. There's little doubt the Lions can score points. But the X factor down the stretch and in the postseason will be their defense, which ranks 23rd…

title: Ja'Marr Chase steps into 'SNF'  in style, leads NFL Week 10 arrivals
summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
Players across the NFL might want to look at the forecast before checking the mirror to finalize their Week 10 looks.

 

 Sunday's arrivals offer plenty of opportunities to layer up. Morning temperatures in the 30s in Green Bay and the 40s in Cleveland could make wool coats, chunky knits and beanies practical additions to the pregame rotation. The chill extends south, too: Atlanta and Nashville are forecast to start Sunday near freezing before warming into the 50s.

 Out West, sunglasses could be the accessory of choice. Mostly sunny skies and afternoon temperatures in the 70s in Glendale, Arizona, and upper 60s in Las Vegas favor lighter layers. Arlington, Texas, offers a different picture, with rain and temperatures hovering in the upper 40s -- another reason to give weather-ready outerwear a starring role.

 Here are the standout looks from Week 10.

 

 Sunday's best 
 Ja'Marr Chase fashionably mixed business with comfort ahead of a high-stakes night. The Bengals receiver paired a glossy beige jacket and matching snap-button pants with a white shirt and dark tie, carrying his cleats into Cincinnati's primetime showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers with the AFC North lead on the line.
 
 
 Fernando Mendoza kept his first-start look simple. Ahead of his debut as the Las Vegas Raiders ' starting quarterback, he arrived in a navy bomber jacket with a dark shirt and pants, adding white sneakers and a smile to complete the look.
 
 
 Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young paired a blue-and-white striped Kith polo over a white long-sleeve shirt with light-wash jeans and coordinating sneakers. Clear-frame glasses and a Louis Vuitton suitcase rounded out his look. 
 
 
 Thursday night's fashion 
 
 Cam Skattebo brought plenty of flair to his arrival, sporting a custom Giants -themed Iron Man mask. He paired the silver-and-blue headgear with a black sweatshirt, khaki pants and layered chains.

title: Chargers-Ravens odds, best bets: Tips, analysis and our favorite plays
summary: Odds, analysis and recommended plays to help you bet the Chargers-Ravens matchup on Monday night.
full_text:
Jim Harbaugh's Los Angeles Chargers are flying cross country to face his former protégé, Jesse Minter, as they search for their first win of the season Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens . Under center, embattled quarterback Justin Herbert will play through a finger injury on his non-throwing hand. Herbert is already the first quarterback in NFL history to start a season 0-8 immediately following a Pro Bowl and playoff appearance, and a loss in Baltimore would extend that unprecedented streak to 0-9.

 

 Meanwhile, the Ravens are looking to snap a four-game losing streak, during which Lamar Jackson played only one offensive snap. Baltimore will debut newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett , who already defeated the Chargers in Week 1 while starting for the Arizona Cardinals . The arrival of Brissett, known for locking onto his top targets ( Trey McBride and Michael Wilson rank first and fourth in targets, respectively, since Week 10 of 2025), should revive Zay Flowers , who has totaled just six receiving yards over his last two games.

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 

 

 Coming off a mini-bye and playing at home, the Ravens are unsurprising 4.5-point favorites. Minter will likely look to outmaneuver his former boss by controlling the clock. If Minter can keep Brissett from turning the ball over while leaning heavily on Derrick Henry (175 carries in nine games), Baltimore should find plenty of success against a Chargers defense that just surrendered 485 yards to the Houston Texans and ranks near the bottom of the league against the run (11 rushing TDs allowed).

 Both teams have been brutal against the spread. The 4-5 Ravens have covered just twice -- both on the road (Week 1 at Indianapolis and Week 5 at Atlanta) -- while the 0-8 Chargers haven't covered all season. Something has to give on Monday night, and since Los Angeles has yet to lose a game by fewer than six points, I'm comfortable laying the points with Baltimore .

 

 Notable player props, bets 
 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jacoby Brissett interceptions OVER 0.5 (-105) 

 Herbert is now infamously the only quarterback in the NFL to throw an interception in every game he has played in the 2026 season, tying Drake Maye with a league-high 11 picks. However, Brissett isn't far behind with seven interceptions. Adjusting to a new offense and facing a Chargers defense that is tied for sixth in the league with seven interceptions, Brissett seems likely to cough up at least one pick.

title: How Chargers' Harbaugh, Ravens' Minter can revive seasons
summary: Los Angeles stands at 0-8 on the season while Baltimore deals with its worst three-game stretch in team history.
full_text:
In January 2022, Jesse Minter was hot on the recruiting trail as the Vanderbilt defensive coordinator when his phone rang with an unfamiliar number.

 It was Jim Harbaugh, who was the head coach at Michigan.

 "Hey, I'm pretty sure my brother's hiring Mike [Macdonald]," Harbaugh told Minter. "You want to come to Michigan and be the DC?"

 Minter was stunned because he had never really spoken with Harbaugh. Their first real conversation started with a job offer. 

 There was an opening for the defensive coordinator job at Michigan because Macdonald was leaving to run the defense for John Harbaugh's Baltimore Ravens . Both Macdonald and John, Jim's older brother, knew Minter when he was a defensive assistant in Baltimore from 2017 to 2020. They strongly vouched for Minter, insisting that Jim should hire him. 

 "And Jim listened to them," Minter said.

 Minter was sure he had spoken with Jim because it sounded like him. But he wasn't certain that he landed the biggest break of his career. He knows there are some coaches who will call with an offer and you still need to go through the interview process.

 Minter quickly called Macdonald to ask if Jim had really just hired him as the next defensive coordinator at Michigan.

 

 "I'm telling you, this is real," Macdonald said.

 Jim Harbaugh and Jesse Minter formed one of the NFL's most successful coaching tandems over the previous four seasons. With Harbaugh as the head coach and Minter as his defensive coordinator, they won 50 of 63 games and captured a national championship at Michigan in 2023. And in 2024, Harbaugh and Minter were hired to be head coach and DC over the Los Angeles Chargers , where they earned playoff berths in each of their two seasons together, including last season.

 Minter feels Harbaugh set his path to becoming an NFL head coach by not only hiring him but empowering him. Harbaugh let Minter have full control of the defense while building him up with "ridiculous positivity," as Minter described it. "Dude, I believe in you," Harbaugh once told Minter. "You're going to be the best coach I've ever hired."

 In January, Minter was hired as the fourth head coach in Ravens history, replacing Jim's older brother. Jim Harbaugh then hired Western Michigan defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary to become the Chargers defensive coordinator.

 In their first season apart, both Harbaugh and Minter are dealing with once promising seasons that have gone terribly wrong by the NFL's midway point. Monday's game between the Chargers and Ravens ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN/ABC ) has become a commiseration reunion for Harbaugh and Minter, both of whom are looking to live up to their reputations as problem solvers who instill confidence during tough times.

 In Harbaugh's third season in Los Angeles, the Chargers (0-8) are the league's only winless team. In Minter's first season in Baltimore and his first as a head coach, the Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight to plummet into last place in the AFC North.

 "He's a leader through adversity," Minter said of Harbaugh last week. "When you go through [a bad] stretch, I was always just really impressed with his ability to keep the team intact, keep them motivated, find improvement, find little things to get better at every day and hold players accountable. I mean, that's what Jim's doing."

 The struggles for Harbaugh and Minter have reached historic proportions.

 With ankle and wrist injuries to quarterback Lamar Jackson , the Ravens have lost three consecutive games by more than 20 points for the first time in their 31-year history. The Chargers, meanwhile, are tied for the fourth-longest losing streak by a playoff team from the previous season.

 After starting the season with the third-best odds to win the Super Bowl, the Ravens currently have a 3.5% chance to make the playoffs, according to ESPN Analytics. The Chargers have gone from entering the season with a 68% chance to make the playoffs to now having a 74% chance of landing a top-5 pick in the 2027 NFL draft .

 Each week, Harbaugh is asked about offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job security and the expectations laid upon QB Justin Herbert . And, each week, Minter is asked about the defensive breakdowns in the second half, the kicking struggles and Jackson's timeline to return.

 On Monday night, the paths for Minter and Harbaugh converge again at a time when the questions outnumber their collective wins.

 "He just figures it out," Harbaugh said of Minter. "He has got a great ability to make things right."

 
 

 EIGHT DAYS AFTER the Chargers grabbed headlines for naming Harbaugh their new head coach, he touched down in Los Angeles on an atypical dark and rainy Southern California day.

 Chargers owner Dean Spanos warned Harbaugh about the untimely storm he'd be arriving to.

 Harbaugh's response? "Dean, we are the storm."

 Two and a half seasons later, the Chargers have transformed from a franchise once infused with confidence to the worst team in the NFL following the offseason firing of offensive coordinator Greg Roman and Minter's departure.

 After boasting the fifth-ranked defense in the NFL last season with Minter, Los Angeles has dropped to No. 21 at the midway point this season. The Chargers are coming off a loss to the Houston Texans in which they allowed a season-worst 44 points and 485 total yards.

 It's been a swift change from the previous two seasons, when Los Angeles made the playoffs with 11-6 records in 2024 and 2025. In losing their first eight games in 2026, the Chargers are in the midst of the longest losing streak in 15 years by a team that had made the playoffs the previous season.

 

  "There's fighting or there's slunking away," Harbaugh said this week. "That will never be a part of our culture, our organization. Any narrative that we're not hellbent on winning these games is completely wrong."

 This is uncharted territory for Harbaugh. Entering this season, he ranked ninth among NFL coaches with the ninth-best all-time winning percentage (66-31-1, .678).

 Before this disastrous start, Harbaugh had never had a losing season in six seasons as an NFL head coach. He had only lost eight games in a season once -- an 8-8 season in 2014 with the 49ers -- much less lose eight in a row.

 "He's literally been the same," safety Tony Jefferson said about Harbaugh through their winless start. "He's been -- sometimes a little snappy, which I like, but he hasn't changed as far as there's no -- as a leader, he's doing exactly what we would want, is to see a motivated, highly spirited coach every day, regardless of the result, just trying to get it fixed."

 While Harbaugh and Minter's on-field philosophies quickly produced results, Harbaugh and McDaniel have not experienced a similar dynamic.

 Harbaugh, 62, is the old-school coach known for his buttoned-up polo shirts. McDaniel, 43, is the eclectic playcaller with a joggers-only wardrobe. Their identities have clashed as much on the field as they do in a photo lineup, with the offense, ranking last in points per game (15.1) and touchdowns scored (11). In last week's loss to the Texans, a third-quarter touchdown ended a 37-drive touchdown drought.

 Herbert, a two-time Pro Bowl quarterback, ranks last in the league with a 29.8 Total QBR. He has thrown nearly twice as many interceptions (11) as touchdown passes and has been sacked 31 times, the second most in the NFL.

 "Just got to keep fighting," Herbert said. "As tough as it is, there's nothing else that we can do other than go out there and give our best effort throughout the week, understanding that it's only us in that locker room that can do anything about it. Obviously not where we want to be."  

 And, if there's any hope for salvaging the season, it seems to reside inside the locker room, where on a recent Friday afternoon, Mariah Carey blasted from linebacker Denzel Perryman 's DJ setup, as players milled jovially about and filled the adjacent barbershop in preparation for…

title: 49ers poke fun at Cowboys multiple times to headline NFL Week 10 trolls
summary: NFL teams kept it petty in Week 10, led by the San Francisco 49ers poking fun at the Dallas Cowboys.
full_text:
The NFL's oldest rivalries bring plenty of history, memories and gut-wrenching wins and losses. It's what makes the games more valuable -- and the trolls follow suit.

 

 The San Francisco 49ers put on an offensive show against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in a 46-40 victory.

 San Francisco had 584 total yards of offense, the most yards Dallas has allowed in a home game in franchise history, according to ESPN Research. 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey had 262 yards, plus three total touchdowns. He's the first 49ers player with at least 200 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns in a regular season game since Jerry Rice in 1995.

 The 49ers poked fun at the Cowboys multiple times with Texas- and Dallas-specific posts, including cowboy boots outside of AT&T Stadium with a 49ers cowboy hat on top of them. In one post, lyrics from country star Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" were in the caption, while another caption read: "Brought the star power."

 

 Here are the top trolls from Week 10.

 

 Buffalo Bills 31, New York Jets 12 
 The Buffalo Bills  have won five in a row after their victory over the New York Jets .

 Buffalo kept New York out of the end zone and scored four touchdowns -- three total from quarterback Josh Allen , and running back James Cook III had the other. The Bills' 8-1 record ties their second-best nine-game start in franchise history. Five of Buffalo's wins have come on the road, including Sunday.

 The Bills play in the western New York area, not far from Canada, and have embraced that region by including the Canadian national anthem at their home opener this season. Buffalo claimed more than a win after beating New York. It wrote on X after the game: "PSA: the Buffalo Bills are the only football team in New York." with a smiling face at the end.

 

 
 Carolina Panthers 20, New Orleans Saints 17 
 Divisional matchups tend to bring the best out of each team on and off the field. The Carolina Panthers epitomized that after a last-second win against the New Orleans Saints .

 With the score tied and 41 seconds left in the game, Panthers kicker Ryan Fitzgerald  nailed it from 54 yards to clinch the victory and snap Carolina's three-game losing streak.

 New Orleans is home to the French Quarter, which boasts Mardi Gras annually. The Panthers put their spin on the location with a graphic of their mascot dragging a parade boat through the location and the caption: "The Carolina Quarter."

 

 
 Los Angeles Rams 34, Arizona Cardinals 6 
 The Los Angeles Rams took care of business versus the Arizona Cardinals for a commanding road victory.

 Los Angeles held Arizona scoreless after the first quarter and outgained Arizona 436-123 in total yards in the win. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford had 249 passing yards and three touchdowns. Cardinals signal-caller Carson Beck struggled in his debut with 108 passing yards and two interceptions.

 Los Angeles utilized an Angry Birds-themed post to poke fun at its opponent.

 

 
 Seattle Seahawks 21, Las Vegas Raiders 13 
 The Seattle Seahawks  won their second straight after a road meeting with the Las Vegas Raiders .

 Seattle scored 14 points in the third quarter to go ahead for good after falling behind 10-7 heading into halftime. The Seahawks held the Raiders to just 163 yards and sacked quarterback Fernando Mendoza -- making his debut as starter -- six times.

 The city of Las Vegas has its unique quirks, including the "Welcome to Las Vegas" sign. The Seahawks put their spin on various Las Vegas elements to poke fun at the Raiders.

 

 
 Indianapolis Colts 24, Miami Dolphins 22 
 The Indianapolis Colts ' victory over the Miami Dolphins  ended Indianapolis' five-game losing streak.

 Miami received possession with 3:15 left in the game and a chance to take the lead. But Indianapolis forced a turnover on downs, then ran the clock down to clinch it.

 The big win came with a simple troll postgame, as the Colts referenced the Dolphins' "fins" nickname. They instead wrote "Phin" in their graphic.
