title: Who are the winningest NFL coaches of all time?
summary: From Belichick to Reid, there are many iconic coaches in NFL history. Who has the best career record? Check out the stat breakdown now.
full_text:
Only four head coaches in NFL history have won 300 career games across the regular season and postseason. Kansas City Chiefs  coach Andy Reid was the last to cross the 300-win plateau.

 Reid recorded his 300th career victory on Jan. 18, 2025, when his Chiefs defeated the Houston Texans 23-14 in the AFC divisional round.

 Reid, who signed a five-year, $100 million extension with the Chiefs in April 2024, entered the 2026 season looking to add to his career win total and close the gap between him and the NFL's all-time winningest head coach, Hall of Famer Don Shula.

 Let's take a look at which head coaches have the most career victories in NFL history (including both regular-season and postseason play):

 *Active NFL head coach 

 5. Tom Landry, 270 wins 

 Landry was the Dallas Cowboys' head coach for an NFL-record 29 years in a row and the team had 20 consecutive winning seasons, which is also a league record. Landry led Dallas to two Super Bowl wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI and the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII. He was named the NFL's Coach of the Year in 1966 and the UPI NFL Coach of the Year in 1975. Landry was an innovator, with the 4-3 defense among his creations. He was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

 *4. Andy Reid, 314 wins 

 Reid is the only head coach in NFL history who has won 100 games with two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles (coaching the team from 1999 through 2012) and the Chiefs (he has coached Kansas City since 2013). He led the Eagles on multiple deep playoff runs, including a Super Bowl in 2004 and three straight conference finals from 2001 to 2003. However, he wasn't able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy until he arrived in Kansas City. He has turned the Chiefs into a juggernaut, winning three Super Bowls. Reid is an offensive mastermind and quarterback whisperer. He'll likely continue to rack up wins moving forward with Patrick Mahomes , Travis Kelce & Co.

 

 3. George Halas, 324 wins 

 Halas was a co-founder of the NFL and creator of the Bears. For 10 years, he served as player-coach-executive for the Bears (which is how he earned the nickname "Mr. Everything"). In 1930, he retired as a player and focused on ownership, but he would later return to coach the Bears several times. Halas led the Bears to eight NFL championships, tying Belichick's number of titles. Halas coached the team for 40 years and had just six losing seasons. He helped create the T-formation system and used it to set an NFL record for the biggest blowout in league history: a 73-0 win over the Washington team in the 1940 NFL Championship Game. Halas was selected as the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1963 and 1965, and he was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

 2. Bill Belichick, 333 wins 

 Belichick is considered by some as the greatest coach in all of professional sports, as he has won an NFL-record eight Super Bowls (six as a head coach with the Patriots and two as an assistant coach with the Giants). He also ranks first among all NFL coaches in playoff wins with 31. Belichick was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 2003, 2007 and 2010. Many franchises have hired away Belichick's assistants and tried to replicate his "Patriot Way," but it hasn't been the same without him. If Belichick returns to NFL coaching, he is just 26 regular-season wins from surpassing Don Shula as the winningest regular-season coach of all time. 

 1. Don Shula, 347 wins 

 After playing in the NFL as a defensive back for seven seasons, Shula decided to retire and become a coach. He got his first head-coaching opportunity in 1963 with the Baltimore Colts, whom he led to the NFL championship in 1968. From 1970 through 1995, Shula had a legendary run as head coach of the Dolphins. Shula led the Dolphins to a pair of Super Bowl victories (in Super Bowl VII and Super Bowl VIII). Miami had a perfect season in 1972, making Shula the only coach in NFL history to go undefeated. He was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1964, 1967, 1968 and 1972. Whether you're just counting regular-season wins (328) or including playoff wins (347), Shula is the winningest coach in NFL history.

title: How an NFL ref crew worked two games in a day
summary: An inside look at the 14-hour day of four referees who worked an afternoon game in Indianapolis and the Sunday night game in Cincinnati.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- IT'S HARD  to tell when an NFL referee is actually in a hurry because they're always jogging from here to there.

 Jogging onto the field with a bag of footballs, jogging to take their position behind the quarterback, jogging over to the replay monitor to screen a review. But at 4:37 p.m. ET Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium, when referee Don Willard power-walks with his suitcase and bag through the concrete bowels of the stadium, led by a police officer and flanked by three other game officials and an NFL security staffer, it's clear that he is in a hurry.

 "Next stop: Beep! Beep!" umpire Terry Killens yells as the group walks out of the official's locker room in street clothes.

 Kickoff for their second NFL game of the day is less than four hours away, and Cincinnati is still two hours down the dark and construction-interrupted I-74. The crew has a police escort to the highway and then they'll be on their own. Willard, Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew hold their snack boxes in one hand and roll their small suitcases with the other. Willard totes a pink Pedialyte -- necessary for replenishing the 3 hours and 13 minutes of intense focus he had just put in during the Colts' 24-22 victory over the Dolphins. Larrew munches on a cookie while he walks and then accidentally drops it on the floor.

 

 Two stadium security workers wave goodbye and yell, "Drive safe!" But these four VIPs won't be driving themselves anywhere. A black sprinter van waits for the entourage, tucked just behind the Dolphins' team buses. Another stadium security worker escorts a CBS videographer into the area to capture their departure. He backpedals to get the perfect shot: four officials boarding a van that will take them from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Bengals' Sunday night game against the Steelers -- pulling double-duty to officiate two NFL games on the same day.

 The security worker tells another stadium worker, "Wow, this is really a big deal, huh?" He explains that the CBS camera he has shepherded into place is going to send its footage to NBC's "Sunday Night Football" broadcast (which will later highlight the feat).

 The NFL declined ESPN's request to speak to the four officials and Ramon George, the league's head of officiating training and development, who was responsible for sorting through the travel disaster created by the FAA's nationwide ground stop Friday.

 George worked through the night Friday to create new crews for each game based on geographic convenience so the game officials didn't need to use unreliable air travel. The result was flip-card changes for the game officials that were longer than the inactive players lists.

 Each of the four double-duty referees work on different crews. At the Sunday night game, the inactives sheet handed out to the media pregame featured an entirely different crew of the seven on-field officials than what had been previously slated, with the parenthetical "the instant replay official still is Chad Adams."

 The situation is likely unprecedented in NFL history because it's risky. The league intentionally arranges for officials to travel on the day before games (except in the case of international games, for which they travel further in advance), so they are settled and adjusted and can get good rest before they work.

 Former NFL vice president of officiating and current Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino told ESPN that when he was running the department, having a game official work two games on the same day "would be the last resort," which shows how extreme the circumstances were. Typically an emergency alternate scenario would impact one crew and two officials, not the entire 17-crew system.

 "I am sure they went through all the different iterations and exhausted every option," Blandino said.

 

 Blandino said officiating two games in one day is the last resort because "it would be like playing two football games back-to-back. There's the physical aspect of running and the mental exhaustion after a game because you are doing a pre-snap routine for every snap, and then the eight-second play, and then a post-snap routine.

 "The officials look like they are not exerting themselves the same way the players are, but they don't get breaks. They don't play one side of the ball. They are out there every snap and every kick. Then to say now I have to reset without any recovery time? That is a challenge."

 "It's exhausting because you're looking for something on every single play," said Russell Yurk, ESPN's rules analyst and former VP of replay for the league office. "You're analyzing every single play. You're watching your players. You're watching your keys, you're making judgment calls, and it doesn't really let up the entire game."

 

 1:03 p.m. 

 Kickoff in Indianapolis. Willard, normally a side judge, has never refereed a regular-season NFL game before, only preseason games and Big Ten conference matchups before he began working for the NFL in 2018. So when he first speaks into the microphone at Lucas Oil Stadium to announce the coin toss, it sounds weird, because his voice is totally unfamiliar.

 Following Willard's announcement of an illegal formation penalty that the Colts declined, CBS analyst Spero Dedes says, "I think we need to lower the volume on the officiating mic -- he is interfering with our call."

 Walker, the field judge, calls two Miami field goals wide left, and an extra point is no good.

 2:40 p.m. 

 Willard and Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley have a spirited conversation with a lot of hand gesturing on Miami's sideline before the second half kicks off.

 On the first play of the second half, Willard's instincts are tested. Colts cornerback Justin Walley hits Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord in the back of his throwing arm. McCord loses the ball with his arm drawn back, poised to throw. The Colts recover in the end zone for a touchdown. But is it a fumble or did he already start to move his arm forward? Willard throws his blue bean bag to mark the spot of the fumble and calls it a fumble recovery touchdown for Indianapolis.

 "This is a tough play, because Walley comes behind Kyle McCord and it's the defensive arm that really hits the ball and makes it go forward. As an official you think that ball is going forward because of the pass," said Gene Steratore, a retired official and CBS rules analyst. "But Don has fumble all the way, and it's a great job by him."

 Colts tight end Alec Ogletree gets to talking with Willard during a break. "Are you one of the ones going to Cincy after this?" he asks.

 Yep, that's us, Willard tells him.

 Ogletree knew there were going to be changes to the crew because on Friday, the Colts had gone over information about the officiating crew as a team, but it was all with an asterisk: it was only who they thought would be working the game.

 "But we didn't really know who was going to be out there till we got out here," Ogletree said.

 "I did ask [Willard], 'So how long you been the ref, like head ref?' He's like, 'First game.'" 

 3:07 p.m. 

 Miami cornerback Chris Johnson picks off Daniel Jones at the 59-yard line and runs it back for a touchdown. Willard is standing at the Indianapolis 42, behind the quarterback as he throws, then runs that same distance back to the end zone to keep the play in front of him.

 4:16 p.m. 

 The first game ends after three hours and 13 minutes -- a long one because Miami kept it close. The double-duty refs shower and change into street clothes for their trip to Cincinnati. They've all packed a second uniform, this one for an outdoor game. It will be much colder at Paycor Stadium.

 

 6:37 p.m. 

 The weary travelers arrive at Paycor Stadium and bring their luggage straight into the security meeting at the 100-minute mark before game time. Willard carries a massage gun with him, hinting that his focus on the bus ride was as much about recovery as anything else.

 "They're going to be tired…

title: Joe Burrow's 4-TD night puts QB in company of Tom Brady, Peyton Manning
summary: Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday night, becoming just the third player in NFL history after Tom Brady and Peyton Manning to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Even after a performance that was reminiscent of some of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history and enhanced his case as the current best in the league, Joe Burrow was not in the mood to bask in his latest achievement.
During the Cincinnati Bengals ' 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers , Burrow became the third player in NFL history to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span, according to ESPN Research. He joined Tom Brady and Peyton Manning.
Burrow let his guard down only a couple of times after the game, including when he was asked what kind of quarterback he was Sunday night at Paycor Stadium.
"A great one," Burrow said with one of the few smiles he offered after the game.
Despite Burrow being tight-lipped after Cincinnati's fifth consecutive win, the numbers said plenty: He was 35-of-44 passing for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Per Next Gen Stats, Burrow was perfect against the blitz (completed all 12 passes) and led Cincinnati to its fifth straight game scoring 30 or more points, the longest such streak in franchise history.
"I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people who aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "Because if you are, it's really hard to say this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."
The Bengals (7-2) bludgeoned the Steelers from the outset. Cincinnati scored on five of its first six drives, the lone exception coming on kicker Evan McPherson 's first missed field goal attempt of the season.
Against a Steelers defense that ranked fifth in fewest points allowed per drive entering Sunday (1.57), the Bengals had 337 yards by halftime and a 21-point advantage that partially illustrated Cincinnati's dominance Sunday night.
Burrow wasn't the only Bengal who had a big night. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with 11 catches for a season-high 231 yards. He came within 26 yards of breaking his franchise record, which he set as a rookie in a 2021 win over Kansas City .
Chase has played with Burrow since they led LSU to a national championship in 2019. It's easy for Chase to see why Burrow is playing so well.
"He's confident in his craft right now," Chase said. "He's confident his receivers will be open, and that's what you want in a quarterback."
Burrow threw two touchdown passes to running back Chase Brown , one to tight end Drew Sample and one to first-year player Dohnte Meyers , the former CFL star who caught his first career NFL TD on Sunday night.
The Bengals' win avenged a 30-27 loss to the Steelers (6-3) in Week 3, when Burrow was sacked and lost a fumble on the final offensive drive.
Cincinnati is in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but that didn't mean much to Burrow.
"Nobody's winning the division with seven wins," Burrow said. "Nobody is making the playoffs with seven wins. We certainly aren't satisfied."
Burrow knows that feeling well. Last season, he missed nine games because of a turf toe injury. Even after his return later in the year, Cincinnati still sputtered and finished with its worst record (6-11) since his rookie season.
Cincinnati is off to its best start in Taylor's eight years as coach, including the 2021 season, when the Bengals went to the Super Bowl, and the following season that ended in the AFC Championship Game.
After Sunday's win, Burrow can boast something he couldn't in either of those seasons. He leads the NFL in Total QBR (82.1) heading into Week 11. As Burrow walked off the field, he was serenaded with the same "M-V-P" chants he heard at various points during the game.
Burrow didn't put too much stock in that opinion after nine games. But when do those things start to be taken more seriously?
"We'll see," Burrow said with a smile.

title: Joe Burrow and Bengals dominate Steelers 38-18 to take AFC North lead alone
summary: — Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals didn't wither under the prime-time spotlight.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- — Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals didn't wither under the prime-time spotlight.
Instead, they played what could be their best game of the season.
Burrow passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns while Cincinnati's defense shut down Pittsburgh's Aaron Rodgers as the Bengals dominated the Steelers 38-18 on Sunday night to move into sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Cincinnati (7-2) has won five straight and is off to its best start since 2015, when it won its first eight games and was 8-1 after Week 10.
“It’s nice to give ourselves some leeway, but we certainly aren’t satisfied with where we’re at and want to keep getting better,” Burrow said.
Burrow completed 35 of 44 and had a 135.7 passer rating before he was lifted for Joe Flacco midway through the fourth quarter. It was the 10th 400-yard game of Burrow’s seven-year NFL career and his third this season.
Burrow is the 16th quarterback to throw for at least 400 yards against the Steelers. The last to do it was Buffalo's Josh Allen , who had 424 yards in a 2022 Week 5 game.
The Bengals jumped out to a 24-3 halftime lead and didn't show any jet lag after last week's 31-17 win over Atlanta in Spain. It was the first time in four opportunities that a team has played in Europe the week before and beaten an opponent coming off a bye.
“I thought that their time clocks were intact. They were getting the ball out on time, so you can see the effects of that on the quicker throws," Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said. "I thought Joe was playing extremely well. You know, as far as the ability to get through the checkdowns. You got to combat that with running hits on the ball. Those are things to look at.”
Ja’Marr Chase had 11 catches for 231 yards and running back Chase Brown had 82 scrimmage yards along with two touchdowns, both receiving.
Cincinnati’s defense sacked Rodgers three times as the 42-year-old quarterback had one of the worst games of his 22-year career. Rodgers did not have his first completion until his eighth attempt, a 5-yard throw to tight end Dwayne Washington off play-action with four minutes remaining in the first half.
Pittsburgh (6-3) struggled in all three phases until the fourth quarter. Rodgers was 15 of 29 for 129 yards with fourth-quarter TD passes to DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth .
Jaylen Warren , who came in sixth in the league in scrimmage yards, had only 41 yards. He was held to seven carries for 15 yards after rushing for 127 yards in the Steelers’ 30-27 victory over the Bengals in Week 3.
“We started really slow and couldn't get anything going until the fourth quarter, so that's disappointing,” said Rodgers, who had only 27 yards passing the first three quarters. “We kind of shot ourselves in the foot with a couple plays.”
Bengals get off to fast start
Burrow had a dominant first half for the second straight week as the Bengals were up by three touchdowns at halftime.
The seventh-year quarterback topped 300 yards in the first half for the second time in his NFL career as he completed 26 of 34 passes for 302 yards with touchdowns to Brown, Drew Sample and Dohnte Meyers .
The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions. The only time they didn't score was when Evan McPherson was wide right from 43 yards midway through the second quarter, ending his run of 25 straight field goals.
“I thought all three phases set the tone right away in a divisional game, to be able to jump on them quick. And second half, defense got a stop to start. Offense went down and scored seven points. I think that’s kind of where the game was at that point,” Bengals coach Zac Taylor said.
Burrow surgically picked apart the Steelers throughout the game as he moved freely in and around the pocket, often completing passes after stepping up when it appeared he might run.
His best throw came late in the first quarter when he rolled left and plenty of time to wait before Sample darted into the open and caught a 2-yard touchdown as Cam Heyward was ready to apply pressure. Burrow had 6.851 seconds to throw according to the NFL’s Next Gen stats.
“He's confident in his craft right now. He's confident his receivers will be open, and that's what you want for a quarterback,” said Chase, who had his third career game with at least 225 yards receiving.
Steelers: S DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warmups and was ruled inactive. LG Mason McCormick was carted off late in the second quarter with a right ankle injury.
Bengals: OG Dalton Risner went to the locker room with a left knee injury in the second quarter. LB Oren Burks (groin) was injured and ruled out in the second half.
Steelers: At Philadelphia next Sunday.
Bengals: At Washington next Monday night.

title: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 10: Playoff spin for Vikings, Pats, Browns, more
summary: Will Kirk Cousins be the difference in the NFC North? The Browns are going to the playoffs ... but not the Patriots? Patrick Mahomes for MVP and Kyle Shanahan for COY?
full_text:
We did not do post- trade deadline overreactions last week, preferring to see at least one weekend's worth of NFL games before rushing to judgment about the immediate impact of any of the completed deals.

 Now that we've seen the bulk of the Week 10 Sunday games, though? Well, as Dak Prescott would say if we hired him to introduce the weekly overreactions column: Here we gooooo ...

 Let's look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the end.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Cousins as the difference for the Vikings? 
 Mahomes to win MVP? 
 Browns going to the playoffs? 
 But Patriots missing the playoffs? 
 Shanahan to win COY? 
 Fantasy overreactions 

 
 

 

 The Kirk Cousins acquisition will win the NFC North for the Vikings 
 The biggest move at the deadline was Minnesota shipping a third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins, the former Vikings QB who was instantly installed as the starter to no one's surprise. Kyler Murray is still hurt (and wasn't playing well anyway), and Carson Wentz 's disastrous performance last Monday night was the main reason the Vikings decided they needed to make this deal. Fair to say the early returns are positive.

 Cousins was 21-for-31 for 207 yards, two touchdown passes and an interception in a 30-10 victory over the Packers on Sunday. Solid numbers, nothing eye-popping, but there is important context here about team confidence and vibes in general. This Vikings team looked energized by the return of Cousins, who ran the offense with a proficiency that has eluded all Vikings quarterbacks for the past two seasons. And he did it with just one week of practice.

 

 Minnesota scored the first 20 points of this game. The Vikings' all-world defense overwhelmed Packers quarterback Jordan Love , becoming the first NFL team in 11 years to record eight sacks and three takeaways in the first three quarters of a game. They finished with four takeaways for the game. On offense, star wideout Justin Jefferson set season highs in targets with 13 and catches with nine, finishing with 74 yards and the kind of smile he hasn't flashed since 2024.

 The Vikings completed the two-game season sweep of the division-rival Packers and moved into a three-way tie for first place in the historically awesome NFC North. Minnesota, Chicago and Detroit are all 7-2, and Green Bay is 6-4. The Vikings have a 3-1 record in division games, having beaten the Bears in Chicago and losing to the Lions in Detroit .

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 Yeah, you probably could have guessed where I was going with this answer just by reading the last two sentences of the last paragraph. There is no way to predict anything with confidence with four teams in one division playing this well. Sure, the Packers are 1-3 in division games and their offensive line is struggling, but they're also getting Micah Parsons back at some point. The Lions have won five in a row but might have lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a knee injury in Sunday's victory over the Patriots in Munich. The Bears are off this week, so there's not a ton new to say about them, but they've won four in a row and are obviously quite good.

 What we can say with confidence is that the acquisition of Cousins forces us to take the Vikings' chances very seriously, even in a division where everyone seems to be excellent. They just need a representative offense to pair with their elite defense, and Cousins right now appears to give them that.

 Will it last? No way to know. Cousins is 38 years old and certainly not all he used to be. But he's also clearly better than what the Vikings have been working with since they let Sam Darnold walk after the 2024 season. And the way they looked Sunday tells us his impact has already been felt beyond the white lines. It's a major move -- it's just way too soon to feel sure about anyone's chances to win this NFC North.

 

 
 

 Patrick Mahomes will win his third MVP award 
 Josh Downs  also had a fun debut after being  acquired by Kansas City , as the Chiefs cruised past the Falcons 35-13 . Running back Kenneth Walker III  has been the Chiefs' MVP so far this season, Kansas City's big free agent acquisition from the spring. But Walker missed this game because of a groin injury , which left the Chiefs to rely on rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who had 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, and of course Mahomes, who had a vintage game.

 The quarterback was 22-for-35 for 348 yards and five touchdown passes, including an 18-yarder to Downs that put the Chiefs up 14-3 just before halftime. Mahomes has 19 touchdown passes this season.

 

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 I think Mahomes is still the best player in the NFL, and he reminded us of that a bit Sunday. But he has also won this award twice. Based on how the voting tends to go, it will probably be harder for him to win again this year. Voters like to give it to someone new. (Before you ask: I am not an NFL MVP voter and never have been.)

 Mahomes has also taken a back seat on the hype train to Walker, and Mahomes's overall numbers, though very good, lag behind the performances of  Brock Purdy , Joe Burrow , Josh Allen , Trevor Lawrence , etc. Comeback Player of the Year might already be in the bag, and if he keeps throwing five touchdown passes every week, then yeah, MVP would be, too. But I think Mahomes and the Chiefs are very happy to build this season's offense around the running backs and focus on postseason success ahead of individual awards.

 

 
 

 The Patriots will miss the playoffs 
 Rough day in Munich for the Pats. Not only did they get smoked 35-10 by the Lions , but they lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury after the first series. Wide receiver A.J. Brown 's injury-plagued Patriots debut season continued, as he returned from his ankle injury but had to leave in the second half because of a hamstring injury. New England came into the game already banged up at running back and on the offensive line.

 Tommy DeVito relieved Maye and was ineffective, leading us to wonder if the offense can function if Maye has to miss much time -- especially if Brown also sits. New England is 5-5, 3½ games behind first-place Buffalo in the AFC East and a game behind Cleveland, which holds the final wild-card spot, in the AFC standings.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 Twelve of the past 26 teams to lose the Super Bowl have missed the playoffs the following season, and the Patriots are in danger of making that 13 of 27. After making it through last season as one of the healthiest teams in the league, the Patriots are feeling the sting of regression in that area. They have a bye next week, so maybe that gives Maye and/or Brown enough time to get back in the lineup. (It does sound like Maye will be out an extended period of time .) But the problems range beyond that, including a defense that has given up 80 points during the past two weeks and has suddenly developed a disturbing propensity for allowing explosive plays.

 It's not over yet, don't get me wrong. I'm not locking the Browns into that No. 7 spot just yet, and the Raiders, Ravens and Texans -- all of whom are in similar spots in the standings -- have plenty of issues. But it's absolutely possible that the Patriots miss the postseason, and if Maye is out for a while, it might even be likely at this point.

 

 

 
 

 The Browns will make the playoffs 
 After falling behind the Texans 17-0 in the second quarter and still being behind 24-20 in the final minutes of the game, the Browns stormed back for an improbable 27-24 victory and improved to 6-4. After missing last week's game , Deshaun Watson had 312 passing yards and 50 rushing yards, leading a winning fourth-quarter drive for the sixth time this season. The blitzing Browns defense of first-year coordinator Mike Rutenberg made life tough for C.J. Stroud , and Cleveland wore…

title: Betting buzz: How improbable is this Browns season? Here's what the numbers say
summary: Only 10 games into the season, the Cleveland Browns have already hit the over on their preseason win total, and that's just one of several notable numbers surrounding this team.
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have been an underdog going into every single one of their games this season except for one. They have trailed at some point in every game. Before the season, sportsbooks assigned them a win total of 5.5, tied for the third-lowest in the league, per DraftKings lines.

 And yet, against all odds, the Browns are 6-4 more than halfway through the 2026 NFL season, becoming the first team in the league to hit the over on their preseason win total in the process.

 Even more remarkably, all six of their wins have been in comeback fashion, with Sunday's victory over the Houston Texans serving as perhaps the finest example yet. Cleveland trailed 17-0 in the second quarter, at which point, their live odds to win the game lengthened all the way to +1480 on the live moneyline from a pregame closing line of +164, per DraftKings odds.

 The Browns' latest cardiac accomplishment put them into rare air: They are the first team in NFL history to win their first six games by four points or fewer, and the first team in the Super Bowl era to be underdogs and win their first four home games, according to ESPN Research.

 

 In each of those six wins, Cleveland has trailed at some point in the game, naturally forcing sportsbooks to lengthen their in-play odds and provide lucrative opportunities for bettors. Week 10's nearly 15-1 live line against Houston was the longest so far, but the Browns have been at least +365 at some point in every game, and were +1060 before coming back to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2, per DraftKings lines.

 "The Browns have turned live long shots into a weekly feature," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "Bettors are starting to recognize the pattern, and we have seen more interest in Cleveland when the Browns fall behind and their live price grows. There is still a little hesitation because repeatedly relying on fourth quarter comebacks is difficult, but bettors are becoming more willing to take a chance at the longer numbers."

 To that point, Hard Rock Bet said that Cleveland's early season wins against the Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers  attracted live ticket shares in only the 30% range, but Sunday's latest victory got an 89% share.

 The Browns are still a long shot to win the Super Bowl and AFC at 180-1 and 96-1, respectively, but other futures are starting to become more realistic, according to DraftKings odds movement. Cleveland entered the season at 21-1 to win the AFC North and have cut that almost in half to +1050, passing the preseason favorite Baltimore Ravens at 38-1.

 Feazel says that Caesars has some liability on the Browns to win the division due to some "handsome prices," and BetMGM reported them as their third-most bet division winner since Week 1 by tickets. At both books, though, more bettors focused on Cleveland's win total under, allowing for a nice win relatively early in the season for the house.

 Still, if the championship odds are any indication, bookmakers are not getting too ahead of themselves when approaching the Browns, noting that these miraculous wins, while entertaining, are not necessarily sustainable for long-term success.

 "While our rating and view of the team is certainly well improved from what it was going into the season (they've already exceeded their preseason win total), we still do not view this as a top 20 team in the NFL from a power rating perspective," a senior NFL trader at Hard Rock Bet said in an email. "While their ability to win close games has certainly been impressive thus far, we expect some variance to swing the other way going forward in these results."

 -- Doug Greenberg 

 

 Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds |  Sports betting home  |  DraftKings   

 
 Nov. 1: Cardinals lead charge for big underdogs yet again 
 

 It has been a banner season for big underdogs in the NFL, as underdogs of seven or more points have won at least one game outright in each of the first eight weeks -- the first time that has happened since 1971, according to ESPN Research. Underdogs of at least seven points are now 20-7-2 against the spread (ATS) with nine straight-up wins.

 Of all the big underdogs, though, one has stood above the rest: the Arizona Cardinals .

 With their dramatic, come-from-behind overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the Cardinals notched their third outright victory of the season ... all of which have come when they were underdogs of seven or more points.

 

 Arizona is the only team in the league to be 4-0 against the spread when coming in as an underdog of seven or more points and, oddly enough, their three ATS losses have come when they've been smaller underdogs (they have not been dubbed a favorite yet this season). They were responsible for the largest upset of the 2026 NFL season when they defeated the Los Angeles Rams as 13.5-point underdogs in Week 6.

 In general, the big underdogs' winning and covering has been a welcome development for bookmakers: It's a well-known axiom in sports betting that the public tends to back favorites, both on the spread and as featured in moneyline parlays.

 "Bettors still tend to be hesitant to trust big underdogs, which makes those occasional outright upsets especially valuable for the book," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football, Joey Feazel, told ESPN over email. "That has been a welcome change compared to 2024, when it often felt like the public's preferred teams continued to find a way home. Bettors are beginning to show more interest in taking the points with these underdogs, but we have not seen a widespread shift away from favorites on the moneyline just yet."

 Feazel said that "Arizona was comfortably the most important decision in the book's favor" on Sunday, and DraftKings noted that neither team was heavily backed either way.

 This most recent Cardinals win was particularly improbable. Down by 14 in the fourth quarter, Arizona was as long as 28-1 on DraftKings' live moneyline. Feazel said that some Caesars customers grabbed them in the 12-1 range, but not with significant enough money to cause too much of a problem for the sportsbook, while BetMGM called the Cardinals a "small loser" for the book due to live betting.

 Seven-point underdogs trailing by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter are now 5-977 since 2000, according to ESPN Research. The Cardinals are also the first team in the Super Bowl era to have three road wins as at least seven-point underdogs in their first eight games.

 Arizona began the season with the shortest odds to have the fewest regular-season wins (+250) and was tied with the Miami Dolphins with a preseason win total of 3.5, the lowest in the NFL since 2017. Less than halfway through the season, the Cardinals need just one more win to cash that futures ticket for faithful bettors.

 Their first chance to do so will be in Week 9 when they go on the road to face the  Seattle Seahawks  ... as 11.5-point underdogs, per DraftKings lines.

 - - Doug Greenberg 

 
 Oct. 23: Sportsbooks, bettors join the National Tight Ends Day frenzy 
 

 In 2018, the Supreme Court struck down the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, clearing the way for states to legalize sports betting nationwide. That same year marked the beginning of another momentous occasion that has become a stalwart of NFL betting every season.

 On the fourth Sunday in October -- Oct. 25 in 2026 -- the NFL celebrates National Tight Ends Day, a tongue-in-cheek commemoration of football's most underappreciated skill position. Since San Francisco 49ers tight ends Garrett Celek and George Kittle helped bring the honorary day to life eight years ago, it has become a staple of the betting world, with bookmakers taking extra notice and bettors staking extra cash backing players of the position.

 

 "National Tight Ends Day has become a fun day for football fans, and we've seen the excitement around it grow each year," DraftKings director of…

title: Schottenheimer 'very disappointed, very frustrated' with Cowboys' porous defense
summary: Brian Schottenheimer said the Cowboys' defensive performance in the second half was a first for him after it gave up nearly 600 yards to the 49ers.
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer levied his harshest criticism on his team's defense this season after Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .
Schottenheimer did not elaborate on what it could mean for first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker or the rest of the staff, but after giving up 584 yards -- the most allowed in a home game in team history -- and touchdowns of 74, 70 and 66 yards, he was at a breaking point.
"There's a lot of things we got to figure out because I haven't been around a situation like this where the defense was that poor in the second half," Schottenheimer said.
Trailing 17-16 at halftime, the Cowboys allowed 29 points and 340 yards in the second half.
Deebo Samuel Sr. was barely touched on a 70-yard reverse for a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey broke free for a 74-yard touchdown catch and he later went untouched on a 66-yard touchdown reception with 3:23 to play.
"It's something we've got to study. I mean, we got to look at the film, but very disappointed, very frustrated. I thought the first half we did some really good things. I think that's a very good offense, right? But what got us in the second half was the tackling, or the lack of tackling. You've got to get guys on the ground and, yeah, they're good players, but at the end of the day, we tackled like s--- in the second half."
Owner and general manager Jerry Jones was asked about his confidence level in Parker.
"It's what it is. He's a young coach that's in his first year of coordinating and basically calling the plays and so you would have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last [few] that we've lost," Jones said. "And I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."
After finishing with the 30th-ranked defense and allowing a franchise-record 511 points in 2025, the Cowboys fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus and all but one coach on the defensive staff.
Parker, who is the youngest defensive coordinator in team history at 34, came with a sterling reputation in his short time in the NFL with the Green Bay Packers , Denver Broncos and Philadelphia Eagles .
But the Cowboys have continued to struggle, despite the coaching change, schematic adjustments and personnel additions, including the largest free agent commitment in more than a decade for safety Jalen Thompson (three years, $33 million), who is on injured reserve because of a hamstring injury. Dallas also spent first-round picks on safety Caleb Downs and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence . Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was signed to a three-year, $105 million extension in training camp.
"I would have anticipated better results," Jones said. "I'm disappointed."
In the past three games, the Cowboys have given up six plays of 50-plus yards, which would still be the most in the NFL for the season. The Chicago Bears have allowed five such plays. This season, the Cowboys have allowed a league-high eight plays of 50 yards or more. Last season, the Cowboys allowed eight plays of 80 yards or more.
"Explosive plays are killing us," Schottenheimer said.
After closing to within 38-32 after the fourth of Dak Prescott 's five touchdown passes with 3:42 to play, the Cowboys needed one stop to potentially pull off the comeback. On second-and-10, Parker called for a "zero blitz," which had Von Miller , the oldest position player on the roster at 37, responsible for McCaffrey in coverage.
He slipped past Miller and ran untouched for the sealing touchdown.
"CP went with a call that he liked, and we got to look at it," Schottenheimer said. "But at the end of the day, it didn't work out very well for us."
Did Schottenheimer like the call?
"I want to see the film," he said.

title: Sources: Patriots fear Drake Maye has broken ankle, could miss rest of season
summary: The Patriots are concerned that Drake Maye fractured his ankle, sources told ESPN, an injury that could sideline the star QB for the rest of the season.
full_text:
MUNICH -- The New England Patriots are concerned that quarterback Drake Maye may have sustained a fractured ankle during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Maye will miss an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season, sources told Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Maye was knocked out in the first quarter of Sunday's 35-10 loss after he was sacked by Detroit defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , who suffered a serious knee injury while celebrating the play.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told WEEI radio in Boston that Maye stayed in Germany and did not travel home with the team.
"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back," Vrabel said Monday during an interview on "The Greg Hill Show."
"He'll be traveling back here shortly, but [we] just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. ... Just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel -- and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."
Maye, who wasn't in the locker room after the game when reporters were present, was replaced Sunday by backup Tommy DeVito .
The Patriots also have rookie quarterback Behren Morton , a seventh-round draft pick from Texas Tech, on the roster, and could look to add another quarterback to the team, potentially on the practice squad.
Maye's streak of 43 straight starts (including playoffs) is the third longest among NFL quarterbacks behind the Bills' Josh Allen (146) and Lions' Jared Goff (82).
Hutchinson sacked Maye on third down, ripping him down from behind with what appeared to be a possible hip-drop tackle. Hutchinson's right arm reached around Maye's right shoulder pad as he brought him down and landed on the quarterback's lower leg.
Sources told Rapoport that Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after initial tests revealed a torn ACL in his right knee. After leaping in the air to celebrate the sack, Hutchinson landed awkwardly and immediately clutched his knee.
On the Fox broadcast, rules analyst Mike Pereira said Hutchinson's tackle was "not a hip drop."
"Three things have to happen: you have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee," Pereira said. "This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse collar penalty."
Walt Anderson, the NFL's officiating rules analyst, confirmed Pereira's explanation through a league spokesman, noting it was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting.
It was also not a foul for a horse collar tackle, Pereira noted, because neither the collar nor the nameplate were grabbed. No penalty was called on the play by referee Clay Martin's crew.
Asked his view of the play, Vrabel said he wasn't going to assume there was any ill intent.
"However it happened, I don't think it was anything intentional. It's just part of the game," he said.
Maye was helped to his feet and limped to the sideline then later walked to the locker room for further evaluation as DeVito stepped in.
In other injury news, wide receiver A.J. Brown , who returned Sunday after missing two games with a knee injury, was ruled out in the fourth quarter after he sustained a hamstring injury.
"He wasn't able to finish. We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there," Vrabel said.
The Patriots are on a bye in Week 11.

title: Packers' NFC North title hopes in danger after Week 10 loss
summary: Rob Demovsky reports on the Packers following their 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

title: QB Jordan Love, Packers frustrated after blowout loss at home to Vikings
summary: Jordan Love and the Packers expressed their frustration after a 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The Green Bay Packers thought they had their issues protecting Jordan Love figured out. They thought wrong.
Just like in the season-opening loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Packers quarterback was hit, pressured and sacked from all directions Sunday. The only difference was they didn't blow a double-digit lead this time. This one, a 30-10 "butt whuppin" -- as coach Matt LaFleur called it -- was over from the moment the Packers showed they couldn't protect their quarterback.
"Definitely frustrated," Love said. "Everyone in that locker room is frustrated."
Love was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a game by a Packers quarterback in the last 40 years.
Love was pressured on 60% of his dropbacks (21-of-35), a career high, according to ESPN Analytics. Three times in his career, Love has been pressured on at least half of his dropbacks. All three times came this season. Two of those came against the Vikings, who got to Love 50% of the time in Week 1.
And just like in the opener, the Vikings went blitz crazy. Love was blitzed on 66% of his dropbacks on Sunday, the third-highest rate of his career. In Week 1, it was 72%, the highest of his career.
It left the Packers unable to come up with answers for what Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores keeps throwing at them, and worse yet it left them in last place in the NFC North despite still having a winning record (6-4).
"You have a game like that, where it just feels like we're not able to overcome, we're not able to play our game and do things that obviously in previous weeks we've been able to do," Love said. "So definitely frustrated, but it's one of those things we've got to look at it. We've got to see where we can improve."
The Packers can start with the offensive line, where they juggled things again.
Two weeks after left guard Aaron Banks returned to the starting lineup, the $77 million free agent signing last year was on the bench because the Packers thought street free agent Laken Tomlinson was a better option at left guard, and Banks couldn't beat out Travis Glover at right guard after a week of competition in practice.
Meanwhile, on the opening drive of the third quarter, fill-in center John Williams sent a snap sailing wide left and over the head of Love on a shotgun snap for a fumble that the Vikings recovered, one of four Packers turnovers on the day.
"We knew they were going to give us pressure pretty much the whole game, and that's what they did," Williams said. "So we need to be better sticking to our game plan, doing the stuff we're coached to do."
The Packers finished with a pass block win rate of just 19%, according to ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats, meaning they sustained their blocks for at least 2.5 seconds just 19% of the time. It was the Packers' third game with a PBWR under 20%, with two of them coming against the Vikings. All other teams in the NFL have combined for three such games this season.
When asked how frustrated Love was with the lack of protection, LaFleur said, "I think we're all frustrated."
That F-word was the catchphrase of the day in the losing locker room.
"I was frustrated myself," said receiver Christian Watson , who had three catches for 37 yards. "But I wasn't thinking about [Love] in that aspect too much or seeing that from him. But I wouldn't put it past him to be frustrated."
The Packers were coming off perhaps their best game of the season, a 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in which Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns while getting hit just five times. He took 12 hits Sunday after the Vikings clobbered him 15 times in the opener.
At one point in the third quarter, Love was slow to get up after taking a hit and reached for his lower back. By late in the fourth quarter, LaFleur had seen enough of his quarterback getting battered and took him out with 3:56 left in the game.
"I'm all right," Love said. "Took some shots, for sure.
"There was one I just got stepped on pretty good," Love added. "I was just kind of bruised, tried to get back up from that, but I'll be fine."

title: Browns' Deshaun Watson relishes 'special' win vs. Texans after engineering rally
summary: Deshaun Watson, who delivered his sixth game-winning drive of the season, called the 27-24 victory over the Texans, his former team, "definitely special."
full_text:
CLEVELAND -- Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson , who delivered his sixth game-winning drive of the season Sunday, called the 27-24 victory over the Houston Texans , his former team, "definitely special."
"People know the history behind it," he said. "Didn't leave on a good note, but it's all love for the city of Houston, the fans there, the players there, some of the staff there most definitely that I got to see today. And even the older ownership. So it was good to see a lot of people, familiar faces, but it's still love, but it's definitely a good win."
Watson played the first four years of his career in Houston but sat out the 2021 season amid a trade request and more than two dozen accusations against him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during massage sessions. He ultimately was traded to the Browns in March 2022.
Before Sunday's game, he had faced the Texans once in his career: when he made his Browns debut in Week 13 of the 2022 season following an 11-game suspension in the wake of the accusations.
On Sunday, Watson returned from a concussion that sidelined him in Week 9 and completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards. He also rushed for 49 yards and a touchdown.
Watson helped rally Cleveland from a 17-point first-half deficit, its first win after trailing by at least 17 points since Week 5 of the 2014 season. That ended a streak of 62 consecutive games when trailing by at least 17 points, including the playoffs.
Watson's sixth game-winning drive tied him with the Broncos ' Bo Nix for the most in the NFL this season. Cleveland became the first team in NFL history to have each of its first six wins come by four points or fewer.
"I wish collectively [Watson] and I together would play better early and coach better early, and we didn't have to get to this," Browns coach Todd Monken said. "And it's not just been then, it's been our team last week the same way. It's been a credit to our team, our guys up front. And like I said, we got a special group. It says a lot about Deshaun. And I'm happy for him.
"I don't care what he says. This meant a lot."
The win moved the Browns (6-4) into the AFC's seventh seed as they head into their bye week. They already have exceeded last season's win total with seven games remaining.
"What would that have been on FanDuel, right?" Monken said of the Browns' string of close wins. "And I don't gamble. I don't gamble. But there's no way. There's no way. But I'm done trying to plan out anything in all my years in the NFL. I'm done trying to plan out how games are going to go."

title: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: Snaps on offense, defense
summary: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver  Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. The Jaguars have followed through on that, making the 2025 No. 2 overall pick a starter on defense and mixing him in where designed on offense. 

 He has started every game at cornerback and has played at least four snaps on offense in all but one game (Week 4 at Cincinnati). He has made big plays on both sides of the ball and had the best game of his career in Week 6, when he clearly showed what kind of threat he can be. Head coach Liam Coen has been consistent in saying that Hunter's offensive usage is fluid.

 "You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches, then absolutely will."

 How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

 

 

 

 Week 10 at Tennessee Titans 
 Hunter came up with his highlight play of the season so far with a diving interception of a Cam Ward pass in the first quarter. Ward scrambled to his right on third-and-8 from the Jacksonville 35-yard line and threw back toward the left side of the field for receiver Elic Ayomanor near the sideline, but Hunter snagged the ball and cradled it to his body with his left hand as he hit the ground.

 "It was an unbelievable catch, unbelievable play," head coach Liam Coen said. "... Such a special play by obviously a special player."

 The Jaguars turned that into an eventual field goal and 10-3 lead early in the second quarter. Hunter, who is tied with cornerback Jourdan Lewis with a team-high three interceptions, played 56 snaps on defense, five on special teams, and five on offense against the Titans. He touched the ball on three of those offensive snaps: An end around that gained 3 yards and two catches for 16 yards.

 

 

 Week 9 at Baltimore Ravens 
 It was a quiet night for Hunter on defense -- five tackles on 44 snaps -- but a bad one on offense. Hunter played six snaps on offense and fumbled the only time he touched the ball. Hunter caught a receiver screen from Trevor Lawrence , and Ravens safety Malaki Starks knocked the ball loose 1 yard behind the line of scrimmage. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan recovered the ball at midfield, and the Ravens took over with 5:10 to play in the third quarter with the Jaguars ahead 20-3.

 The turnover didn't hurt the Jaguars, though, because the Ravens then turned the ball over on downs four plays later, with tight end Mark Andrews fumbling the snap on fourth-and-1. Hunter was officially credited with one catch for minus-1 yard.

 

 

 Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts 

 Coming off a Week 7 bye week, it was a relatively quiet day from Hunter -- in terms of stats, anyway. Hunter played 49 of the 60 total snaps on defense tallying four tackles. He played six snaps on offense with one rush for 5 yards and no catches on one target. A new wrinkle this week is that he played a season-high four snaps on special teams -- returning a punt for 1 yard and securing a fair catch on another.

 

 

 Week 6 vs. Houston Texans in London 
 Hunter had the best game of his career against the Texans at Wembley Stadium, catching four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and also intercepting C.J. Stroud in the end zone. He's just the fourth player since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a receiving touchdown and interception in the same game and the first to do it since Philadelphia's Brian Dawkins in 2002. The touchdown and interception came on consecutive drives.

 Per NFL Next Gen Stats, Hunter had 34 coverage snaps and limited the Texans to two catches on five targets. However, he also was hit with a questionable pass interference penalty in the end zone against Nico Collins that gave the Texans the ball at the 1-yard line late in the first half. Despite that, this was the first time Hunter has made a significant impact on both sides of the ball -- 58 snaps on defense and 9 on offense (season high) -- in the same game in his 13 career games. 

 

 

 Week 5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles in London 
 Hunter played every defensive snap (59) for the second week in a row and had six tackles (second-most on the team) and a pass breakup. He was penalized for defensive pass interference that wiped out a third-and-17 incompletion in the second quarter. It gave the Eagles the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line and Philadelphia running back Will Shipley scored two plays later.

 On offense, Hunter played five snaps and touched the ball for the first time since Week 1, catching a 9-yard pass on second-and-7 from the Jaguars' 40-yard line. Parker Washington scored on a 51-yard catch-and-run on the next play.

 

 

 Week 4 at  Cincinnati Bengals 
 Hunter played every defensive snap (71) in a 22-17 win against the Bengals and had four tackles and two pass breakups. It's the first time in his career he's played every defensive snap and it was necessary because the Jaguars were down cornerbacks Montaric Brown (hamstring) and Christian Braswell (knee) because of injury.

 "He played his ass off today," head coach Liam Coen said.

 Hunter, however, called his play "decent" and was disappointed that his interception got erased by a roughing the passer penalty on defensive tackle Arik Armstead .

 "I like to criticize myself a lot harder," Hunter said. "My wife does, too. I still give up a catch today, so she's going to be on me about that when I get home."

 Hunter didn't play at all on offense, the first time in his career that has happened. Coen said he didn't want to risk him getting hurt on that side of the ball because that would leave them down three cornerbacks. Hunter said he wasn't mad at that decision.

 

 

 Week 3 vs. New England Patriots 
 In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

 
 

 Week 2 at Denver Broncos 
 Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton . The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

 After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

 "We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

 "But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."

title: Five reasons why Chargers' offense, Justin Herbert have struggled in 2026 season
summary: Are injuries the biggest reason behind the Chargers' offensive struggles? Are Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton both taking steps back? We looked at the tape for answers.
full_text:
Could it get any worse than this for the Chargers? After nine weeks, they are the only winless team in the NFL. They're the first team in NFL history to start 0-8 after winning 11-plus games in the previous season, per ESPN Research. And they haven't won a game since Week 16 of last season -- 331 days ago.

 While last week's 44-22 loss to Houston  featured plenty of poor defensive play, new coordinator Mike McDaniel 's offense is 30th or worse in an alarming number of stats this season: points, touchdowns, turnovers, efficiency, Total QBR, pass block win rate, red zone drives and fourth-down conversion percentage. The Chargers went 37 straight drives without scoring a touchdown, a streak they finally broke in the fourth quarter against the Texans.

 So how did we get here after all the hype surrounding McDaniel, quarterback Justin Herbert and the rest of the Chargers' offense over the offseason? Ahead of their "Monday Night Football" matchup against the Ravens ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN ), I looked at the tape for some answers. Here are five reasons why Los Angeles' offense is off to such a horrific start.

 

 Injuries and subpar play on the offensive line 
 Yes, injuries have played a role here. Left tackle Rashawn Slater has been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury , right tackle Joe Alt missed two games with a neck injury, and center  Tyler Biadasz  went down with an ACL injury during camp  after signing a three-year deal .

 But the interior of the front wasn't corrected over the offseason, as  Cole Strange and Logan Taylor  both rank in the bottom half of all qualifying guards in run block win rate. And overall, the Chargers currently own a 37.7% pass block win rate, the third lowest in the league.

 Herbert must also take accountability in the pocket, but he has been sacked 31 times this season (second most in the league behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson ). Has the scheme clicked under McDaniel? No, and more on that later. But there is a general lack of execution on tape from the offensive line, which is devoid of quality talent in key spots.

 
 

 The turnovers in the passing game 
 Herbert's 11 interceptions, tied for the most in the league, show a regression in field vision. He has failed to identify second-level defenders in basic zone schemes. We're talking hook-to-curl drops and flat defenders, which has led to him to throw 10 interceptions and post a 17 QBR versus zone this season.

 Herbert has also forced the ball into too many contested windows while taking unnecessary risks down the field. I see too many examples of Herbert playing hero ball, relying on his physical tools instead of taking the available throw. And his 19 QBR on pocket throws ranks dead last in the league.

 
 A lack of playmakers on the perimeter 
 Ladd McConkey 's availability is a major issue for this team. He has missed time in 2026 with rib, foot and back injuries, as well as a concussion in Week 6 . He has played just one full game, recording 17 receptions for 286 yards in total.

 Besides McConkey, the Chargers don't have a receiver who alters defensive game plans.  Quentin Johnston  is an inconsistent straight-line speed target, while  Tre' Harris  would grade out as a No. 3 or No. 4 for most teams.

 I don't see the Chargers' wide receivers creating separation at a consistent rate versus man coverage, plus opposing defenses are playing more zone (66.2% of Herbert's dropbacks) to cap vertical routes and force Herbert to read it out with late rotation in the secondary. He has completed only eight passes of 20 or more air yards in 2026. This isn't an offense that can create explosive plays in the pass game.

 
 Limited run game production 
 This summer, I was all-in on  Omarion Hampton and the Chargers' run game under McDaniel. The use of 21 personnel (two RBs, one TE, two WRs) with fullback  Alec Ingold  and more motion/movement made perfect sense on paper. They had the tools to create advantages with numbers and blocking angles.

 However, Ingold was put on IR ahead of Week 6 with a shoulder injury. And Hampton is now part of a backfield rotation featuring Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal .

 The 2025 first-round pick is a volume runner who wins with short-area burst and contact balance when he can get on a downhill path. However, Hampton is averaging less than 4.0 yards per carry on outside and inside zone plays, which are core concepts in McDaniel's scheme. Based on the tape, Hampton isn't a great fit as a zone runner, as he lacks high-end vision as a ball carrier. And he doesn't display the one-cut ability to dart through creases of daylight.

 As a team, the Chargers are also averaging 1.9 yards before first contact, fifth fewest in the league. That puts L.A. behind the sticks, impacts McDaniel's ability to influence second-level defenders with play-action, and sets up more third-down throws for Herbert.

 

 
 The disconnect with OC Mike McDaniel's offense 
 Coaching does matter in this league. And I don't see the fit right now with McDaniel and Herbert.

 This system is built on timing and ball location. Yet, Herbert is completing 61.3% of his throws, and I don't see a rhythm-based pass game on tape. McDaniel has put Herbert in a position to use play-action (55 attempts), but he has an 11.6 QBR on those throws (31st in the league).

 What would I like to see? More boot off outside zone play-action. Let's move the pocket at a higher rate, as Herbert has just 18 attempts on designed rollouts in 2026. McDaniel could also use more schemed concepts that create leveled reads, especially on throws outside of the numbers. And the three-step passing game can improve with more defined reads for Herbert, using different formations and movement to clear the pre-snap picture.

 But until we see more consistent play from Herbert, and improvements up front, this system will continue to produce poor results.

title: Aaron Donald savors first sack in 1,050 days, but Rams' win 'felt even better'
summary: Aaron Donald recorded his first sack since New Year's Eve in 2023 and helped the Rams top the Cardinals for their fourth straight win.
full_text:
PHOENIX -- When Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald brought down Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck in the second quarter, the veteran notched his first sack in 1,050 days.
That stretch included two seasons Donald spent in retirement before returning to the Rams in late August. Donald finished the game with 1.5 sacks, snapping an eight-game streak without a sack, which had been the longest drought of his career.
Though Donald said it felt "good" to get his first sack since New Year's Eve in 2023, he noted that it "felt even better that we won."
After starting 2-4, the Rams have won four games in a row.
With his 1.5 sacks on Sunday, Donald passed Justin Houston and Chandler Jones (112.0) for 31st on the NFL's all-time list. Donald also became the first player in franchise history age 35 or older to record more than one sack in a game.
"I'm never surprised," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "He never ceases to amaze me. I think the term '1 of 1' is thrown around way too loosely this day and age, but it's not with him. He's 1 of 1.
McVay added: "He's had a tremendous impact on this team. And it is certainly not exclusive to just getting a sack today. He's just made a tremendous impact, and he's a guy that everyone looks at and they say, watching the way that he moves, 'If we just mimic and emulate that, we'll be in good shape.'"
Donald and the Rams' defense held the Cardinals to just 123 yards and six first downs, both the fewest by any team this season, according to ESPN Research. The Rams did not allow a third-down conversion (0-for-6).
Donald said he feels good physically going into the Week 11 bye, especially after the Rams' defense played so few snaps Sunday.
"Get back right, get myself feeling 100% and get ready for this run," Donald said.
The Rams play the Green Bay Packers after the bye.
