title: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza vows to learn from first NFL start, a loss to Seahawks
summary: Fernando Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards and had a passer rating of 71.5 in his first regular-season start for the Raiders.
full_text:
LAS VEGAS -- The beginning of Fernando Mendoza 's first career NFL start seemed like a fairy tale before the Seahawks ' defense turned it into a horror show.
On the Raiders ' first possession, Mendoza scrambled into the end zone for a 10-yard touchdown run -- a play that resembled one he had during Indiana's win over Miami in the CFP National Championship in January, his final college game.
But the Raiders then went stagnant on offense.
They punted seven straight times. Mike Macdonald-led defenses have made life difficult for rookie quarterbacks in the past, and Mendoza, who was pressured 19 times and sacked six, became another victim in Las Vegas' 21-13 loss to Seattle on Sunday.
"It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game," said Mendoza, who completed 17 of 29 passes (58.6%) for 143 yards and had a passer rating of 71.5.
Mendoza is the fourth straight No. 1 draft pick to be held under 150 passing yards in his first NFL start, joining Cam Ward , Caleb Williams and Bryce Young .
Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called Mendoza's debut start "good." He added that Mendoza was well prepared and began the game strongly as he orchestrated back-to-back scoring drives.
He was effective in play-action while he used his mobility to escape pressure and extend plays. He completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards while rushing for 21 yards on five carries in the first half as the Raiders took a 10-7 lead.
"[Mendoza] was poised in critical situations," Raiders left guard Spencer Burford told ESPN.
"That just shows how much maturity he has as a player, especially playing a defense like that for the first time in his first start."
After tight end Brock Bowers was ruled out at the start of the third quarter because of an ankle injury, the Raiders' offense fell apart. Mendoza and Kubiak couldn't keep up in the chess match against Macdonald as Seattle outscored the Raiders 14-3 in the second half, holding them to 27 total yards and keeping them without a third-down conversion.
"We have to play better," Kubiak said. "We've got to support him better. I've got to help him better in the second half. What happened in the second half to go 0-for-7 on third down is unacceptable. No reason that we should do that."
Mendoza was 6-of-16 for 53 yards and was sacked four times in the second half. He had just 15 passing yards until a 38-yard completion to running back Ashton Jeanty with under four minutes to go in the fourth quarter.
"Macdonald dialed it up and did great," Mendoza said. "He fooled me a couple of times."
Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon gave Mendoza his "Welcome to the NFL" moment, sacking him twice on three blitzes. Witherspoon sprinted into the pocket untouched on both sacks.
"A lot of sacks today were on me, not any on the offensive line," Mendoza said. "I thought they played great and displayed great leadership today. I need to be better, especially with those DB blitzes."
Despite the loss, Mendoza showed enough to have the Raiders hopeful moving forward. Fullback Connor Heyward said Mendoza is "going to be a hell of a quarterback in this league."
Burford said Mendoza's mobility will add a "whole different dynamic" to the offense because it will be able to incorporate quarterback reads into the game plan. Defensive end Maxx Crosby added that Mendoza will only get better and that the team is excited for the Heisman Trophy winner to be leading the way.
"He's a natural leader," Crosby said. "That's why he went No. 1 overall. Obviously, he's extremely talented and a great player, but as a quarterback, you've got to have those traits [to be] a great leader. And I think he definitely has every bit of those, and he's going to keep growing as a player and as a leader."

title: Patriots need to fix defensive effort -- especially if Drake Maye misses time
summary: New England has given up 80 points over last two games. The bye week will allow the team to reset.
full_text:
MUNICH -- If quarterback Drake Maye misses time with the ankle injury  he suffered on Sunday, the New England Patriots will likely need to rely more on defense to salvage the post-Week 11 bye part of their schedule.

 That's not a comforting thought after what's unfolded the past two weeks, with Sunday's 35-10 bludgeoning by the Detroit Lions in Munich coming after the defense was sliced up by the Green Bay Packers in a 45-27 defeat the week before.

 Yes, the Lions and Packers are two of the NFL's upper-echelon teams, playing in perhaps the best division, the NFC North. But that's no excuse for what the defense has produced in its past eight quarters. The unit hasn't met the most basic standard of what coach Mike Vrabel preaches as the No. 1 part of team identity. They aren't winning the "effort and finish" game.

 Veteran safety Kevin Byard , one of six team captains, didn't sugarcoat it when dissecting how the Lions took it to them.

 

 "They played harder than us. They played more physical than us," he said. "And as a defense, that feels like a slap in the face that we let them play harder."

 Byard noted Lions receivers blocking way down the field on screen plays, and offensive linemen pushing the pile into the end zone for a touchdown. The Patriots provided little resistance -- allowing a season-high 4.5 yards before contact per rush (not including kneel-downs), per ESPN Research. The previous high was 2.85 yards per rush.

 The Lions became the first team with 300 passing yards and 150 rushing yards in a game against the Patriots since the Chiefs did it in Week 1 of the 2017 season. It's part of a concerning trend: Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8  Tennessee Titans .

 "We're not doing anything besides disrespecting ourselves," veteran outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones said. "We come out here, we work hard, and then to get blown out -- it's ridiculous. We got to make the game competitive. It shouldn't be 35-10, especially how we played so well in the first half of the season."

 Christian Gonzalez , the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL, is among those on defense struggling recently. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, over the past two weeks, he has allowed 12 receptions for 271 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Gonzalez took responsibility for Amon-Ra St. Brown 's first touchdown, saying, "Obviously it starts with me. I can't miss that tackle."

 Jones still believes there's time to recover, and one theme among Vrabel and players was that they are 5-5 at the bye week and still have a lot to play for. There's a Week 12 road game against the currently winless Los Angeles Chargers , followed by home games against the 8-1 Buffalo Bills and 7-2 Minnesota Vikings , road contests vs. the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs and 2-8 New York Jets before finishing the year with back-to-back home games against the 7-2 Denver Broncos and 1-8 Miami Dolphins .

 "You have to go out there with the intention to do it. It has to be on the forefront of your mind to want to do more, want to give extra effort and show your identity," Jones said.

 "What you show on tape is your résumé, so if you're loafing around, looking like some B.S., it's going to show. ... What you saw [in Munich] was a team showing more tenacity, more effort, way more than we did."

 

 After the game, Vrabel was asked about the difference between execution breakdowns and not measuring up in the "effort and finish" category. He hinted there could be changes if he sees defenders not meeting what's required.

 "I tried to reiterate as many times as I could that they were going to chase the ball, and they were going to try to push the receiver into the end zone -- just like they did. And if we weren't there, again, that's a choice," he said.

 "I have to look at that and make sure that's something that's our standard. I'm not going to say that it was. That's what they were going to do, and it was no secret to anybody, especially me and to our team that got told that numerous times. Their first touchdown, the left guard's running 50 yards down the field and he's 5 yards behind the receiver, so give them a lot of credit."

 That's the way Vrabel implores his teams to play, going as far as to paint the words "push the pile" and "finish longer than the guy with the ball" on wooden sleds that players use at practice.

 The absence of it the past two weeks has been striking.

title: Giants QB J.J. McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers
summary: After only three starts and four games playing for New York, the quarterback's numbers are staggering.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Quarterback  J.J. McCarthy played "very well" in Thursday night's  24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders , according to coach John Harbaugh. He set a career high with 293 yards passing and had the New York Giants moving the ball the entire evening. 
 
 The night ended with McCarthy throwing his first interception since he entered the game in the fourth quarter last month against the New Orleans Saints . It still didn't come close to ruining the overall performance or change the impression that McCarthy has been impressive since becoming the team's starting quarterback. 
 
 It's not perfect, but it's promising. 
 
 "There were some plays made, he made some throws, scrambled. I thought J.J. played very well," Harbaugh said. 
 
 He later added that McCarthy "threw some dimes" and made some "great throws." McCarthy also seemed to be more comfortable in the pocket than last week against the Philadelphia Eagles , when he took five sacks, and did better getting through his progressions. In a lot of ways, he barely resembled the quarterback who struggled his first two seasons with the Minnesota Vikings , the first because of injury and then as he got acclimated to the NFL game. 
 
 
 
 McCarthy, the No. 10 pick for the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft, was traded to the Giants  in late September for a fifth-round pick. He was pleased but not blown away with his performance Thursday night. 
 
 "There's things I could've done better," he said afterward. 
 
 That just goes to show how far McCarthy has come in such a short time. He was the third-stringer in Minnesota just six weeks ago. 
 
 It may be only three starts and four games playing for the Giants, but the numbers are staggering. They suggest a much different quarterback than the one who started 10 games for the Vikings last season.   
 
 McCarthy's QBR has skyrocketed from 36.1 to 56.3 this season. His completion percentage has gone from second to last among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts at 57.6% to 63.5% with the Giants. His completion percentage over expectation has risen from an awful minus-5.2 with Minnesota (second worst only to Chicago's Caleb Williams last year) to plus-5.0, which puts him fifth among all quarterbacks this season. 
 
 His off-target throw percentage has dropped from 19.3% to 13.5% and his yards per dropback has gone from a bad 5.71 to 8.04 with the Giants, which is fourth in the NFL. Even McCarthy's precision passing percentage has gone from 45.3% (dead last) to a more than respectable 53.5%. 
 
 The improvement in his accuracy has been among the most noticeable differences. It was on display against the Commanders. Perhaps McCarthy's best throw came when he was under pressure with a blitzer in his face early in the fourth quarter. He hit tight end Isaiah Likely in stride with a laser through a tight window over the middle for a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown. 
 
 "That's probably as good a play as you're going to see in the National Football League all season, honestly," Harbaugh said. 
 
 It has McCarthy and the Giants feeling confident about this season and his future. The 23-year-old quarterback has been a good fit with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy's scheme and in New York. 
 
 
 At least so far. 
 
 "I just feel really good in terms of my preparation going into every week. They are very detailed in terms of what they want from me, what the intent is every single play. There is no gray area going into each play and I just really appreciate the heck out of that," he said. "It is all about building, constantly growing, and that is what we are focused on. Being in the league for a little over two years now, seeing defenses that I have seen before and running concepts that I have run before, everything seems to be slowing down for me. 
 
 "Just being able to keep stacking and keep growing 1% every single day and I am just so blessed to be in this offense and so blessed to be a part of this organization." 
 
 The spike in numbers is not all apples to apples. McCarthy is a year older, with more experience and in a completely different situation. But there clearly has been progress, especially in understanding the professional game. It has been apparent when he faces zone defenses. 
 
 McCarthy is averaging 10.9 yards per attempt against zone defenses through four games as a Giants quarterback. That's second best of any quarterback behind only Houston's C.J. Stroud since McCarthy entered the lineup. He was at a paltry 6.8 yards per attempt against zone defenses last season, which ranked him near the bottom of the league. 
 
 In fact, McCarthy's expected points added against zone defense of 0.22 is tops among all quarterbacks this season. It seems to be a sign that his understanding of the game is improving under the guidance of Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan and trending in the right direction with more playing time and experience. 
 
 "I think he's done a great job," Harbaugh said Friday.   
 
 It's still early, but maybe, just maybe, the Giants hit on something here.

title: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
summary: The Pittsburgh passer is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
full_text:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

 In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots . In Week 6 of 2026, he moved into a third-place tie with Peyton Manning with 539, and has since surpassed him this season with a total of 542 as of Week 10.

 "Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

 

 Rodgers supplanted Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025. But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

 Among the milestones for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 10 he has appeared in 296), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 10, he needs 1,712 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards . 

 This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

 
 Weeks: 
 Preseason | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 10 
 Remaining schedule 

 
 

 

 
 Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INT, 0 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

 

 Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

 
 

 Week 1:  Steelers 20, Falcons 13 
 Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard 
 Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth  for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the  Green Bay Packers , per ESPN Research.

 After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

 "No, keep doing it," Rodgers said, urging his coach to keep calling passes. "Keep doing it."

 And although Rodgers and the Steelers got the win, the quarterback struggled under the pressure from the Falcons' front. He completed 3 of 12 attempts under pressure and was sacked twice. And continuing the trend from last season, Rodgers was also 3-of-12 on throws of 15 or more air yards. Some of those incompletions, though, were the result of drops by his receivers.

 

 "I liked the plan from Mike," Rodgers said. "I liked the playcalling. We took some shots. I felt like we had really close to having one of those really good games. If we come down with a couple of those, it obviously looks a little different on the scoreboard and stat sheet and stuff, but love my guys, love  DK [Metcalf] .

 

 

 Week 2: Patriots 20, Steelers 3 
 Rodgers' stat line: 187 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT, 4 sacks, 1 rush for 5 yards 
 Rodgers set two personal Steelers milestones in the team's Week 2 loss -- and not in a good way. Rodgers was off target on 26% of his throws (nine attempts) in the loss, his worst as a Steeler. The Patriots frustrated Rodgers with heavy pressures and blitzed on 19 of 44 dropbacks (43%), the second-highest rate he has faced with Pittsburgh. Against the blitz, he was 8-of-17 for 42 yards with two sacks and an interception. And he had his first interception against the blitz as a member of the Steelers.

 

 "It's frustrating, for sure," Rodgers said of not getting into the end zone at New England on Sunday. "The defense has been playing great. They've been holding [opponents to] 13 points a game in two games, and offensively I think we're averaging like eight points a game. That's not winning football."

 

 

 Week 3: Steelers 30, Bengals 27 
 Rodgers' stat line: 292 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for 10 yards 
 It turns out Rodgers still has plenty left in the tank. A week after one of his worst performances as a Steeler, Rodgers bounced back with three passing touchdowns to help the offense put up a season-best 30 points and 411 yards in the win against the Cincinnati Bengals . Rodgers aired it out in the first quarter with two touchdown throws and 143 passing yards -- the most he has thrown in the first quarter since Week 6 of 2018 against the 49ers (170). Each of his touchdown passes traveled at least 20 air yards, marking his first time with multiple touchdowns of 20-plus air yards since he joined the Steelers. Entering Sunday's game, Rodgers was 0-of-9 on pass attempts of 20-plus air yards.

 "We definitely needed it because it was just uncharacteristic of us," Steelers wide receiver Ben Skowronek said of the offense's bounce-back performance. "Throughout camp, we felt really confident in what we were doing, moving the ball. And the first two weeks we just weren't us. So credit to the coaching staff, the guys in the building, we locked in this week and we knew we had to have it. We knew we could do it."

 

 After two weeks without much movement in the record books, Rodgers is starting to make some headway. Sunday's win marked the 165th of his career, tying him with Ben Roethlisberger for fifth most by a starting quarterback since positions were first tracked in 1950. With his first-quarter 38-yard touchdown throw to Roman Wilson , Rodgers also recorded his 233rd career game with at least one passing touchdown, tying Peyton Manning for the fourth most such games in NFL history.

 

 

 Week 4: Browns 27, Steelers 24 
 Rodgers' stat line: 299 yards, 3 TDs, 2 INTs, 5 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Rodgers spent a lot of time on the turf at Huntington Bank Field in what's scheduled to be his final Thursday night game (barring a late-season flex). Rodgers took 10 quarterback hits thanks to Cleveland's aggressive game plan, protection breakdowns and the quarterback's decisions to hold on to the ball as he looked for his pass catchers to get open against man coverage.

 

 All five of the sacks against Rodgers came as he faced man coverage, and on the season, he has been sacked an NFL-worst 12 times when facing man coverage -- seven more than any other quarterback. And while the offense largely stagnated through the second and third quarters, it came alive in the fourth as Rodgers aired it out with 43-, 28- and 22-yard completions to wide receiver DK Metcalf and a 21-yard touchdown throw threaded to Darnell Washington .

 Rodgers even tied the score at 24 with a quarterback sneak for a successful two-point conversion with less than two minutes to go.

 "I felt like there was no chance they'd be expecting that," Rodgers said. "So I just told them in the huddle, if I can this one, I'm going to sneak it.'"

 

 With the loss, Rodgers still has 13 wins on Thursdays and remains tied with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott for second most all time.

 

 

 Week 5: Steelers 34, Colts 22

title: Sources: Baker Mayfield's status uncertain for Bucs' Week 11 game vs. Lions
summary: Baker Mayfield's status against the Lions in Week 11 is in question because of an injury he suffered to his foot and ankle area, sources told NFL Network.
full_text:
Baker Mayfield 's status against the Detroit Lions in Week 11 is in question because of an injury that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback suffered to his foot and ankle area in last Sunday's loss to the Chicago Bears , sources told NFL Network.
Mayfield has been in and out of a walking boot in recent days as a way of rehabbing and resting the injury during Tampa Bay's bye week, which came at a fortunate time for him.
The injury is not considered a long-term issue, according to sources. Any missed playing time for Mayfield would be minimal, and injured reserve is not a consideration.
Mayfield was slow to get up after a few hits during the fourth quarter in Chicago. Before one sack, Bears defensive lineman Austin Booker briefly grabbed Mayfield by the helmet -- a play that resulted in a face mask penalty but not a fine from the league office.
Two plays later, Grady Jarrett and Jeffery Simmons combined to sack Mayfield and take him down in an awkward manner. Mayfield remained on the ground for a few moments.
But Mayfield never left the game and ran in a 2-point conversion to tie the game at 24-24 with 2:51 remaining. The Bears kicked a game-ending field goal on the next drive, so Mayfield and the Buccaneers' offense didn't return to the field after pulling even.
Mayfield missed three games last month after dislocating his right thumb in a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 27. Rookie undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels started the games Mayfield missed.
The Buccaneers (3-6), who enter Sunday only a half game out of first place in the NFC South, will monitor Mayfield's progress when they return to practice this week.
No one has ruled Mayfield out of next week's game in Detroit, and several sources have noted his willingness to play through injuries in the past. If it's a question of pain tolerance over functionality, according to sources, and Mayfield will do everything he can to take the field against the Lions.
